title: Aragog
paragraphs: Aragog (c. 1942 - 20 April 1997 ) was an Acromantula owned by Rubeus Hagrid .
Like the rest of his species, Aragog had a taste for human flesh and was able to communicate with humans vocally.
In his youth, he was the size of a Pekingese and near the end of his life was about the size of a small elephant with an eighteen-foot leg span.
Aragog had a wife, Mosag , and was the leader of a large Acromantula colony composed of all of his sons and daughters.
During his life, Aragog was accused of being Slytherin's Monster , although the monster was really a Basilisk .
Ironically, all spiders feared the Basilisk, as it was their mortal enemy.
After Aragog died, some of his venom was taken by Horace Slughorn .
Biography
Early life
Aragog was originally brought as an egg in a distant land and came to Great Britain in the pocket of a traveller .
Somehow, the egg came into possession of Rubeus Hagrid , who at the time was a student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
After Aragog hatched from it, Hagrid kept him in a cupboard in one of the school's dungeons , feeding him scraps.
1943 opening of the Chamber of Secrets
Aragog in his youth at Hogwarts

In the 1942-1943 school year , Tom Marvolo Riddle , a Slytherin prefect and the descendant of school founder Salazar Slytherin who would later become Lord Voldemort , opened the Chamber of Secrets and unleashed the resident monster, the Serpent of Slytherin , upon the castle to exterminate its Muggle-born population, those who were 'unworthy' to study magic.
Aragog was framed as being the monster and Hagrid was accused of being Slytherin's heir.
Several students were petrified in the school after the monster was unleashed, and after a student named Myrtle Warren died in a bathroom , the school's governors considered closing the school.

Tom, who considered Hogwarts his only home, found out about Aragog after discovering the young Hagrid tending to the Acromantula, and realised that he could use Aragog as a scapegoat for the monster's rampage.
Tom came to capture the creature, but Hagrid helped Aragog escape to the Forbidden Forest .
Hagrid was later punished with expulsion from the school for his alleged role in the attacks and for this course of action.
Aragog, meanwhile, was sent to live in the Forbidden Forest .

Hagrid, though expelled, was assigned the position of Gamekeeper at Hogwarts, by the intervention of Albus Dumbledore (who suspected and later knew his innocence), thus allowing him to stay in contact with Aragog.
Hagrid would visit Aragog now and then, bringing him food.
On one particular visit, Hagrid brought Aragog a female Acromantula he could hopefully mate with, Mosag .
The two Acromantulas started a large colony comprised of their children.
Sometime later, Aragog became blind .
1992-1993 Chamber reopening
In 1992 , Salazar Slytherin 's Basilisk was unleashed on the castle again.
This time, however, the rampage did not result in any deaths, only the petrification of several Muggle-born students.
Once again the governors considered closing the school due to the attacks.
Governors of the school once again accused Hagrid of being the Heir of Slytherin.

Hagrid vaguely told Ron Weasley and Harry Potter to 'follow the spiders ,' but couched this advice in a statement to Minister for Magic , Cornelius Fudge , as they were both hiding under Harry's invisibility cloak .
Though reluctantly, the two decided to continue their investigation of the monster, and follow the spiders like Hagrid had indirectly told them.
This led them into the Forbidden Forest .
Harry Potter , Ron Weasley and Fang encounter Aragog and his offspring in the Forbidden Forest
Arriving at Aragog's Lair , they encountered Aragog and his colony.

Aragog revealed to them his past, Hagrid's innocence, the discovery of Myrtle's body in the bathroom, and more of Riddle's scapegoating scheme, thus confirming that he was not the Chamber's resident monster.

While the ageing Acromantula revealed that all spider species such as his own feared the monster above other creatures and would never speak nor mention its name or anything about it, in no small part due to its malicious nature, he was able to give the boys a small clue: the monster was born in the castle and was an ancient creature that possessed such a terrifying ability and singular viciousness.
Aragog then warned the two that while he showed mercy to Hagrid, he would not deny his many children fresh meat if they were hungry-even if the boys were Hagrid's friends.
However, thanks to the Flying Ford Anglia , Aragog's children failed to eat the two boys, as they both escaped the forest by flying away in the enchanted car.
After this, Harry and Ron actually found the real monster was in fact a Basilisk , and the real heir was Tom Riddle , the true identity of the Dark Lord Voldemort.
Ron and Harry's encounter with Aragog and his colony made Ron's boggart manifest in the shape of Aragog, due to his arachnophobia and general fear of the Acromantula eating him.
Death and post-mortem

In 1996 , Harry and Hermione Granger , in an attempt to lure Dolores Umbridge into a trap in the Forbidden Forest , took the path towards Aragog's colony, but the immediate danger of running into Aragog's children was avoided when the local Centaurs intercepted them.
Horace Slughorn, Hagrid, Harry Potter , and Fang attend Aragog's funeral
That same year, Aragog contracted an unknown illness over the summer, and despite Hagrid's attempts to heal and comfort Aragog by feeding him giant grubs, he eventually died on 20 April 1997 .

Before this time, it had been dangerous for Hagrid to go and visit Aragog because, sensing the giant spider's weakness, his family was getting rather restive and were prepared to eat Aragog's corpse if they had to.

When Aragog died, Hagrid was able to get Aragog's corpse out of the colony before his children could attempt to cannibalise his corpse, though barely as they would no longer hold back in an attempt to devour Hagrid.
Aragog was buried in a deep pit near Hagrid's house the next evening.
Aragog's funeral was attended by Hagrid, Harry, and Professor Horace Slughorn , who took the opportunity to 'acquire' Aragog's highly valuable venom .

On 2 August 1998 , the Acromantula colony was forced out of the Forbidden Forest by Voldemort, his Death Eaters and his assembled army of Dark creatures , who then established their camp there as a prelude to the Battle of Hogwarts .
Aragog's children survived, however, and invaded Hogwarts, attacking both the Death Eaters and the defenders of Hogwarts.
It is unknown if the colony and its population survived following the conclusion of the battle, which was in favour of the Order of the Phoenix .
Physical description
In 1993, Aragog was described as being roughly the size of a small elephant , with a grey and black hairy body, with milky white eyes, as he was blind.
However, it was likely his eyes were formerly black, like most other Acromantulas.
Personality and traits
Aragog's eight-eyed stare
Aragog had a close friendship with his former owner, Hagrid.

He admitted that it would have been his instinct to try to attack humans, but he restrained himself out of respect and gratitude for Hagrid, and unlike the Basilisk herself, he never personally harmed a human in his life.
He was presumed to be a good father to his many children, understanding their taste for human flesh and allowing them to attack and eat anyone they wanted when they were hungry.
Hagrid was the only human that Aragog stopped his sons and daughters from attacking.
One such case of this was when Ron Weasley and Harry Potter found Aragog, however, this was more than likely an act of parental care as opposed to anger or hatred as Ron comes to think.
However, the two managed to escape by sheer luck, as the Weasleys' enchanted Ford Anglia emerged to extract them from the danger.

Aragog, like all spiders, feared Basilisks (though the personality of the Basilisk lurking in Hogwarts was most likely a contributing factor), and would not speak of one, not even to Hagrid himself, even though he had asked him about the creature many times.

The way that Aragog would not speak their name or of them was similar to the way that wizards and witches (amongst other creatures like house-elves and goblins ) would not speak Voldemort's name, or discuss him even obliquely any more than was absolutely necessary, which was appropriate since he himself commanded the creature in his youth.
Etymology
Notes and references

title: Berry Ocky Rot
paragraphs: Berry Ocky Rot was a fruit wine containing 17% alcohol .
It was made from berries, which the label boasted were picked and pressed by the "fair hands" of "our best house-elves ", and aged in oaken bungbarrels for a thousand years.
The beverage was sold at the Hog's Head pub in Hogsmeade , as well as the Leaky Cauldron .
Horace Slughorn and Rubeus Hagrid got drunk on a bottle of it after Aragog 's funeral in 1997 .
Etymology
Berry ocky is a Newfoundland English term for a drink made from wild berries (especially lingonberries ). "
Rot" may be related to rotgut , an English slang word for cheap, low-quality liquor. "
Rot" is also German for red .
Notes and references

title: Wine
paragraphs: Wine is an alcoholic beverage, typically made of fermented grape juice.
The natural chemical balance of grapes is such that they can ferment without the addition of sugars, acids, enzymes or other nutrients.
Wine is produced by fermenting crushed grapes using various types of yeast.
It was served often in both the wizarding and Muggle worlds.
Sherry is a known type of wine, along with many others.
Sixth-years learnt how to turn vinegar to wine in Charms class .
There existed a spell that could conjure a fountain of wine from the tip of a wand .
White wine was also an ingredient in The Famous French Method for the Bite of a Mad Dog .
History

In 1932 , during the Candidates' Dinner held at the German Ministry of Magic , Vicência Santos was served a glass of poisoned red wine by the server Karl , but Eulalie Hicks prevented her from drinking it and exposed its poison.
The Leaky Cauldron served bottles of red wine during the 1980s and 1990s .
The potion riddle in the Underground Chamber

During the 1991-1992 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Severus Snape placed two bottles of nettle wine amongst some potions in his chamber in the Underground Chambers , as part of the protections to guard the Philosopher's Stone .

On 25 December 1991 ( Christmas day), Rubeus Hagrid got somewhat drunk after drinking wine at the Christmas Feast in the Great Hall , which resulted in him kissing Minerva McGonagall on the cheek, which made the usually stern professor blush.
In 1993 , Harry Potter 's emotions caused Marjorie Dursley 's wineglass to shatter when the latter was cruelly insulting his late mother .

In 1994 , during the Wand Weighing ceremony at the start of the Triwizard Tournament that year, the Wandmaker Garrick Ollivander tested Harry Potter 's wand to ensure it was in good working condition, by successfully conjuring wine with his wand.
In 1996 Severus Snape served Narcissa Malfoy Elf-made wine at his home .
In 1997 , sixth-year Charms students at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry had to attempt to turn vinegar into wine during their N.E.W.T. lessons.
Hermione Granger was the only student who managed to successfully perform the charm , whereas Harry Potter turned his wine into ice and Ronald Weasley 's flask exploded.
Professor Filius Flitwick noted that they all needed to practise the charm for their homework.
Later during that year on 1 August , wine was amongst the various beverages that were served to the attendees of the wedding of William Weasley and Fleur Delacour .
Wine at the wedding of Bill and Fleur
A Muggle book on winemaking had been published by at least the 2010s .

Myra Curio , who considered winemaking the highest Muggle contribution to the world, sent a copy of this book to a Calamity Investigator working for the Statute of Secrecy Task Force , who studied the book and was reminded of the basics of soil, atmosphere, and magical energy, helping to increase the amount of time their Greenhouse Charm remained in effect.
Types
Notes and references

title: Refilling Charm
paragraphs: The Refilling Charm ( incantation unknown ) was a charm that was used to refill whatever the caster pointed at with the drink originally in the container.
This charm could be used verbally or non-verbally .
History

In 1997 it was used non-verbally by Harry Potter , even though he had " never pulled it off before ", when he noticed that Rubeus Hagrid and Horace Slughorn were running out of wine (at the time he was under the effects of Felix Felicis ).
It was later used to fill the up the glasses with champagne at the Wedding of William Weasley and Fleur Delacour .
It seems the Stone Basin had some form of a Refilling Charm placed on it, as it would refill itself with the Emerald Potion sometime after the contents were drunk.
Notes and references

title: Long Shouren
paragraphs: Long Shouren (Chinese: 龙守仁 ) was a Chinese pure-blood wizard and a dragonologist in the early 21st century .
Biography
Early life
Shouren grew up around dragons in a small mountain village in China , with a family who had pledged to protect them.
When he was growing up, he viewed caring for the dragons as a burden.
He loved dragons, but yearned to travel the world.
Shouren when he was a child
He left home when he was 17 and met a group of travellers who were impressed with his knowledge on dragons and he accepted their invite to join their group .
However, he soon learned they were actually wizard poachers who collected magical beasts.
Shouren was unhappy with this and wanted to leave but he was forced to help by his boss, Kellen Carrion , who told him he owed them.
Before he let Shouren leave, he demanded that he help steal a dragon egg .
Shouren managed to get the dragon egg but he couldn't bring himself to give it to the poachers.
When he tried to flee with the egg, his former partners chased him until the mother of the egg, a giant dragon , turned up.
They abandoned him for dead but when the dragon breathed fire on him, the egg absorbed most of it.
Even though he lost his arm, he survived the attack.
He considered it a fair price to pay after he had helped poachers and vowed never to let another dragon get hurt.
After this, he had to wear a prosthetic arm.
During his adventures, he had realised that dragons are a gift and chose to be a dragonologist .
He continued to travel the world to find dragons.
At some point, he met and befriended Rubeus Hagrid .
He thought that anyone who chose to fight a dragon had made a very bad choice.
Teaching at Hogwarts
In the early 2010s , Shouren visited Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry to help Hagrid teach classes about dragons, where they built a Dragon Paddock .
He stayed in a tent outside of Hagrid's Hut .
During his first lesson, he met a student who he recognised had an affinity for dragons.
He Apparated with the student to Diagon Alley where they observed two Dark wizards illegally trading three dragon eggs .
He put the Disillusionment Charm on them so they could rescue the eggs successfully, and Disapparated with them before being caught by a Dark wizard.
Shouren was grateful for their help but asked them not to tell anyone, even Hagrid, that they had the eggs.
He wanted the student to keep the eggs in their care and have them care for them until he could move them to a place where they would be safe.
The student took Shouren to the Room of Requirement where they thought the eggs would be hidden.
Shouren told them how to identify the eggs and that they should be cared for differently depending on their species.
After putting them in cauldrons , they kept them lit with the Fire-Making Spell .
However, after he left, Colby Frey revealed to the student that he overheard everything.
He told the student that they had actually taken the eggs illegally because the wizards in Diagon Alley were sanctioned by the Ministry of Magic to trade them.
They broke into Shouren's Tent to try and find out if Shouren was still a poacher.
Shouren returned while they were reading his journal.
He revealed that he was against even the Ministry-sanctioned trades and stole the eggs to protect them.
He told the student, who was worried that they had broken the law, that they had done nothing wrong.
They agreed with Colby to help care for the eggs until Shouren could take them somewhere else.
Shouren secured a home for two of the eggs before they hatched.
However, when he returned to the Room of Requirement, the egg containing a Chinese Fireball had hatched.
The hatchling was already being cared for by the student and Colby, but he told them baby dragons were a handful.
After telling them the dragon was a female, he told them it will be harder for him to find her home now that she had hatched and until he does, they would have to keep caring for her.
Colby wanted to keep her there for her safety, but Shouren told him they can't because she would grow and it would be too dangerous.
Shouren was later shocked to learn that his former boss, Kellen, was helping the Ministry investigate the theft of the dragon eggs.
Kellen told the student that Shouren was the real poacher but he denied it when they confronted him.
Shouren persuaded them to keep helping him and prepared to talk to Kellen, who suspected he was involved in the theft.
Shouren also temporarily filled in for Professor Filius Flitwick 's Charms class , as Flitwick was feeling ill after inspecting the Dragon Paddock.
He began teaching them the effects of the Mending Charm , intending to have them practise repairing a few small objects.

However, his class was interrupted by a Ravenclaw student informing him that Argus Filch needed his help repairing suits of armour that were damaged by Peeves , with the poltergeist even trapping Mrs Norris inside of one suit.
Shouren decided that the situation would be a perfect real-world opportunity for the students to practise the Mending Charm, allowing his students to help out with the repairs.
Becoming a fugitive
Shouren eventually sent a message to the student letting them know that he had found a home for the hatchling and to take her to the forest's edge that midnight.
Shouren encountered the student facing Kellen and talked to him about how he used to care about beasts.
Kellen replied to Shouren that, after everything he taught him, Shouren had betrayed him.

But Shouren told Kellen that he tried to save his life and he was left to die, claiming that Kellen had awoken Shouren's inner beast and he felt that it was devouring him for the worst, as it was doing to Kellen.
Kellen had enough of the conversation and duelled Shouren, who was assisted by the student.
After they bested Kellen, he ordered Qui LeBlanc to "get the little beast".
Qui was followed by the student, and, after they duelled, Qui set the forest on fire.
Shouren arrived to save the student from the fire and helped them face Kellen one more time.
The baby Chinese Fireball eventually attacked Kellen and made him lose his wand, but Shouren saved Kellen and told him that he believed "everyone could change", even him.
With the help of Colby, they escaped the forest .
Colby let them know that some Ministry types would be arriving soon, looking for Shouren.
Shouren decided to leave to avoid implicating the student and potentially losing the dragon hatchling.
He became a fugitive for doing what was right, but trusted that, while there were people who knew the truth, he might do it freely someday.
Shouren also told the student to care for the dragon for a little longer, as travelling with a dragon while being a fugitive would be difficult, and promised he'd return when it was safe.
After that he left Hogwarts.
Shouren returned as promised to take the dragon with him.
He met with Hagrid in secret, with only the student and Colby present.
Hagrid delivered the dragon to him and they saw them leave.
One morning, Hagrid received an owl from Shouren letting him know that a "certain something" was safely delivered "somewhere", which he told the student about in the Great Hall .
At some point after Shouren left Hogwarts, he was involved in an incident involving a poacher , an Erumpent , and a Muggle safari tour group.
Shouren later sent a letter to the Muggle-born student informing them of the status of the baby dragon.
He stated that the baby was growing well and that she had recently blown her first real fire breath.
Shouren expressed his wish that the student could see the dragon, but asserted that it was still too dangerous for all involved for him to share his and the dragon's location.
He stated that the baby dragon missed the student and that the both of them looked forward to the day they could be free to reunite with the student.
Personality and traits
Long was described as "charming, outspoken, driven, and friendly".
Magical abilities and skills
Possessions
Notes and references

title: Peruvian Vipertooth
paragraphs: The Peruvian Vipertooth was a copper-coloured dragon native to eastern and north-eastern Peru .
Description and traits
A Peruvian Vipertooth in flight
Its scales were smooth and copper-coloured with black ridge-markings and short horns on its head.
Like the Norwegian Ridgeback , its fangs were venomous.
It was the smallest and fastest known breed of dragon, about fifteen feet (five metres) long and able to conceal itself well from Muggles .
The Vipertooth fed mainly on goats and cows , but was notorious for its particular craving for humans .
Much like a snake , it ate by swallowing its food whole without chewing, though it may have chosen to tear off small chunks of its food as it went.
Like all dragons, the Peruvian Vipertooth was able to breathe fire .
Its flames were yellow and capable of burning and destroying a wooden barrel in under two seconds.
History
The egg of the Peruvian Vipertooth
In the late 19th century , Vipertooth numbers once went on an alarming increase and became a serious threat to wizards and Muggles alike.
The International Confederation of Wizards was forced to send an extermination squad in to reduce the Vipertooth population.
The dragonologist Harvey Ridgebit was the first person to catch a Peruvian Vipertooth.
The disease Dragon Pox was originally contracted by wizards working closely with Peruvian Vipertooths, before becoming a widespread wizarding disease.
Notes and references

title: Romanian Longhorn
paragraphs: The Romanian Longhorn was a dragon native to Romania .
Its habitat was the Carpathian mountains.
The dragon was dark green in colour.
History
The native territory of the Longhorn had become home to the world's largest and most important dragon reservation.
In recent years, the Longhorn had undergone an intensive breeding programme after its numbers plummeted due to the demand for its horn.
Description
The egg of the Romanian Longhorn
The Romanian Longhorn had dark green scales, and two long, glittering golden horns.
The Longhorn preferred to gore its prey with its horns before roasting it.
The horns of the Longhorn, when powdered, were highly prized as a potion ingredient, and was a Class B Tradeable Material .
The Longhorn was seen as being very bulky and large.
Despite being a fairly medium-sized species of dragon, they appeared to have larger muscles.
It was also the only dragon that had horns that go straight out like a bull.
These long horns and the small one just above its nose somewhat resembled the Triceratops , a dinosaur known and named for its three horns.
Notes and references

title: Baby Chinese Fireball
paragraphs: This Chinese Fireball was cared for by an unidentified student , Colby Frey and Long Shouren in the early 2010s .
She lived in the Room of Requirement after she hatched.
Biography
Before she hatched, she and two other dragon eggs were going to be traded legally when it was sanctioned by the British Ministry of Magic .
Long Shouren disagreed with even legal trade of eggs and persuaded a student of Hogwarts to help steal them.
After they Apparated to Diagon Alley , they stole the eggs and took them back to Hogwarts Castle .
The student suggested hiding the eggs in the Room of Requirement , where they were heard by Colby Frey .
Together, they cared for the eggs.
Shouren managed to secure homes for the other two eggs, but the Chinese Fireball hatched before he could get her to one.
The student was there when she hatched and told Colby.
While they discussed what to do with her, Shouren arrived.
He told them the hatchling was female and that baby dragons could be a handful.
He was going to try and find her a home, but it would be harder now that she had hatched.
They continued to care for her and Colby grew attached.
He tried to argue with Shouren that she would be safer at Hogwarts, but he pointed out she would grow and it would be very dangerous.
The eggs were stolen by a student
The hatchling often set things on fire when she burped sparks in her room, which they had to keep extinguishing.
The Room of Requirement also provided her a toy dragon which she liked gnawing on.
When Shouren found a new home for her, he asked the student to bring her to the Forbidden Forest at midnight.
They thought they had taken her there unnoticed, but Colby had followed them so he could say goodbye to her.
While they were talking, the dragon flew off to Rubeus Hagrid 's Hut .
Hagrid caught her standing outside, and, when he started asking questions, the student and Colby told Hagrid what they had been up to.
He decided to keep their secret when he heard they were helping Shouren get her away that night because she reminded him of the baby dragon, Norberta , that he once had.
However the Chinese Fireball spooked another dragon, an Antipodean Opaleye , that Hagrid was caring for.
When that dragon flew off, Hagrid and Colby chased her.
In their absence, a poacher , Kellen Carrion confronted the student and demanded they hand over the Chinese Fireball.
The student refused and pointed out the baby dragon, who was upset, didn't like him.
He responded that the feeling was mutual.
Fortunately, Hagrid returned to intervene.
They successfully defeated Kellen in a duel but the baby dragon flew off during the fight.
Hagrid stayed to fight off Kellen's poacher group to give the student time to catch the dragon and get her back to the castle.
They managed to get her but Kellen had also caught up with them.
They used the Stunning Spell on him which temporarily knocked him out but he didn't stayed down long enough.
The student ran with the dragon to Shouren who started duelling Kellen.
Qui LeBlanc , a member of Kellen's group, took the dragon during the fight.
The student chased them but Qui kept the dragon until she bit Qui, who called her a "nasty beast".
The dragon attacking Kellen
Qui trapped the student and the dragon in a wall of fire.
The student bested her in a duel and while trying to get out of the fire with the dragon, Shouren arrived and saved them.
Kellen was in pursuit but the baby dragon attacked him.
Shouren intervened and saved Kellen's life.
With the poachers gone, Shouren fled to avoid arrest for stealing her when she was an egg.
The student continued to care for her until Shouren sent for her.
He then took her to her new home.
Shouren later sent a letter to the Muggle-born student informing them of the status of the baby dragon.
He stated that the baby was growing well and that she had recently blown her first real fire breath.
Shouren expressed his wish that the student could see the dragon, but asserted that it was still too dangerous for all involved for him to share his and the dragon's location.
He stated that the baby dragon missed the student and that the both of them looked forward to the day they could be free to reunite with the student.
By September 2011 , a letter from Shouren let the student know that the dragon was " not so little anymore ".
Personality and traits
Shouren described her as "feisty".
Notes and references

title: Colby Frey
paragraphs: Colby Frey was a wizard who started attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in 2008 and was a member of Slytherin house.
He was the younger twin brother of Fischer Frey .
Biography
Early life
At an early age, his mother would read him rhyming poetry when he was unable to sleep, which he found comforting.
Hogwarts years
At the age of eleven, he and Fischer began attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in Slytherin house.
They befriended Cassandra Vole , and she led their group in bullying their fellow students including Daniel Page .
After their first Charms lesson, they challenged a fellow student to a duel.
Colby duelled them first in the Duelling Club and lost.
One day, the student caught Colby and Fischer with a Bombtastic Bomb Box in the Grand Staircase .
They were planning to use it to prank Argus Filch .
When they asked what it was, Colby tried to deny that there was a box but Fischer pointed out it was right in front of them.
He told them it was a collection of accessories.
The student lied that Filch was on the way and they should run.
They left the box behind to frame them so they'd get in trouble with Filch.
They later realised they had been tricked and tried to duel the student, only to lose when they used the box against them.
They went to the Library one night to find a newspaper article about Daniel.
Daniel, Ivy Warrington and their friend found out that they had broken curfew and went to find out why.
They watched the group at a distance, until Colby noticed and told Cassandra.
Colby and Fischer stayed at Hogwarts over the Christmas holidays.
They saw the student and Daniel talking in the Great Hall about being on their own for New Year's Eve.
They made fun of them for being "losers" and wondered if their friends realised they weren't worth it.
After they were called out for also being on their own, Fischer claimed they had a very exclusive party to go to.
Colby was confused and told him he thought they were just going to steal dessert in the Hogwarts kitchens because they didn't receive invites to anything.
Fischer "reminded" Colby that they did have an invite to a party, but then told him off at the side for revealing the truth.
Colby exclaimed that he did not want to be alone on New Year's Eve as it was "depressing".
The student then invited Fischer and Colby to be friends for the day and to go to Hogsmeade with them.
They agreed to "do them a favour" and help lessen their loneliness.
They spent the day in the village before they arranged a firework display.
After, Fischer told the student and Daniel that they had to go back to being "enemies" the next day.
Personality and traits
Colby had a mean-spirited personality and enjoyed bullying others with his friends.
He and Fisher were antagonistic and didn't consider friendship a priority as they preferred to duel people instead.
He was known to enjoy Herbology , handicraft, and poetry and disliked History of Magic , which he was not good at.
Magical abilities and skills
Possessions
Notes and references

title: Confoundable
paragraphs: The term Confoundable was used by the British Ministry of Magic to refer to a sort a piece of chaotic magic that, during the Calamity , stuck displaced wizards and witches , magical objects and artefacts, magical creatures or even memories somewhere very public in areas inhabited by Muggles , thus threatening to expose the wizarding world and in potential serious breach of the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy .

The Statute of Secrecy Task Force , created as a response to the Calamity, was tasked to investigate and contain this threat and prevent further breaches of the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy by banishing all Confoundables in order to retrieve all Foundables .
Notes and references

title: Alchemy
paragraphs: Using the Philosopher's Stone , Flamel achieved the transmutation of metals into pure gold

Alchemy was a branch of magic and an ancient science concerned with the study of the composition, structure and magical properties of the four basic elements, as well as the transmutation of substances; it was thus intimately connected with Potion-making , chemistry , and transformation magic.

Alchemy also concerned philosophy; one interpretation of alchemical literature, which was known to be dominated by mystical and metaphysical speculation, suggested that the study of alchemy was symbolic of a spiritual journey, leading the alchemist from ignorance (base metal) to enlightenment (gold).
Overview

The three goals of the alchemists were the transformation of common metals into gold (a phenomenon called chrysopoeia ) or silver , the creation of a panacea , a remedy that would cure all diseases and prolong life indefinitely, and the discovery of a universal solvent .
A less well known branch of the study of alchemy was Spagyric , or "plant alchemy", used for making herbal medicines.
The elements of fire , air , earth , and water were important in alchemy.

Through the centuries, alchemists' enjoyed great prestige and support, not for the pursuit of their three great goals, nor for their trademark mystic and metaphysical speculation that dominated their literature.

Rather, it was for their more mundane contributions to various chemical industries, such as ore testing and refining, metalworking, production of inks , dyes, paints and cosmetics, leather tanning, ceramics and glass manufacture, preparation of extracts and liquors, and the invention of gunpowder .
The preparation of Aqua Vitæ was also a popular "experiment" among European alchemists.

There was an Alchemy Room in St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries which was used by the resident Healers for the magical study of substances to help synthesise cures, along with the general brewing of healing potions for the hospital.
African and Chinese wizards had always been particularly skilled in alchemy and Astronomy .
Some scholars, like Kennilworthy Whisp , believed that Quidditch had been introduced in Africa by European witches and wizards travelling there in search of alchemical and astronomical information.
There was a Centre for Alchemical Studies in Egypt .
This may have been the largest centre in the world, although this is not clear.
A non-magical version of this study also existed, called Muggle alchemy.

While Muggles for the most part largely dismissed it as an outdated forerunner of modern chemistry , there were still wizards actively studying and practising it in the twentieth century and who held it to be some of the most difficult magic known to wizardkind.
Teaching
A book on the history of alchemy in Medieval Europe
Alchemy was an elective subject offered at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , though only when there was sufficient demand for it.
It was taught to sixth and seventh-years only.
To aid those few students who took alchemy, the Hogwarts Library contained a small section on alchemy, though Madam Pince noted that it was rarely accessed.

The sixth-year Potions curriculum at Hogwarts included enough details about alchemy to the point that Libatius Borage 's Advanced Potion-Making included a brief historical and scientific overview of alchemy.
According to Professor Horace Slughorn , the preparation of an antidote for a blended poison following Golpalott's Third Law was an almost alchemical process.
During the 1990-1991 school year at Hogwarts, Professor Cuthbert Binns taught his seventh-year History of Magic students about the history of alchemy in Medieval Europe .
History
Alchemy had been a field of study since antiquity.

As the time went on, the lack of common words for chemical concepts and processes, as well as the need for secrecy (presumably to avoid Muggle persecution) led alchemists to borrow the terms and symbols of biblical and pagan mythology, astrology , kabbalah and other esoteric fields.
This marked a progress in alchemical research, as it allowed the exchange of ideas between alchemists.
However, this also ended up making the plainest chemical recipe read like an abstruse magic incantation, probably confusing the learning and spreading of alchemy as a science .
Dzou Yen
Dzou Yen , widely considered one of the fathers of Chinese scientific thought, was an alchemist in the fourth century B.C. , during the final years of the Zhou Dynasty .

At least two of the three primary alchemical goals were achieved by the famed French alchemist Nicolas Flamel sometime in or after the 14th century , with his creation of the Philosopher's Stone and, by extension, the Elixir of Life .
Using the Elixir, Nicolas and his wife, Perenelle Flamel , extended their lifespans and would live for well over 600 years until the 1990s.
The stone could also perform Chrysopoeia , though it's unknown if Flamel used it for this purpose.

After Lord Voldemort nearly succeeded in stealing the stone for his own dark purposes during the 1991-1992 school year , Flamel and his old friend and colleague, Albus Dumbledore , decided that it would be best to destroy the stone to prevent its misuse.
After six centuries of life the Flamels were more than willing to accept death and passed peacefully after setting their affairs in order, when their supply of Elixir ran out.
Phillipus von Hohenheim
Phillipus von Hohenheim , apart from his important contributions to the field of medicine, was also a secretive alchemist in the sixteenth century .

According to an alchemical work , which original translation from Latin dated back to 1557 , the constituents of the perfect medicine were Vinegar , Salt , Urine , Sal Ammoniac and a particular Sulphur Vive .
During his world tour, Elphias Doge observed the experiments of Egyptian alchemists.
Known alchemists

title: Alchemy (class)
paragraphs: Alchemy was an elective subject taught at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
The course was open to sixth and seventh-years if there were enough students interested in taking the subject.
The ancient science of Alchemy focused on the study of nature's four basic elements ( fire , earth , air , and water ), as well as the transmutation of substances (such as base metals into gold ).
The subject was taught in the Alchemy Class located in the Dungeons of Hogwarts Castle .
It was also possibly taught in a pair of Alchemy rooms on the school's fourth floor .
It was not a very popular subject for Hogwarts students, with Madam Pince noting that no student had checked out a textbook on Alchemy since 1952 .
Despite this, the Hogwarts Library had a small archive on Alchemy, including some books which were handwritten and some which were written in Latin .
Graduates from Uagadou were known to be well versed in Alchemy, so presumably the subject formed a significant part of the school's curriculum, like it did for Beauxbatons .
Notes and references

title: Gold
paragraphs: A gold Galleon
Gold (chemical symbol: Au ) is a dense, soft shiny yellow metal, with a high value as money and is used in jewellery.
History
A Gringotts Wizarding Bank gold bar
The most common use for gold in the wizarding world was in the Galleon coin.
The Charlatan in the tale of Babbitty Rabbitty and her Cackling Stump was given a sack of gold for his services, and Babbitty Rabbitty herself was also erected as a gold statue .
The legendary Philosopher's Stone could be used to transform base metals into gold, implying that gold couldn't be produced by standard means of transfiguration , hence its value as currency.

In 2020 , Minister for Magic Hermione Granger confirmed that the Ministry had "plenty of gold in reserve", suggesting a stable and secure financial standing, or the potential existence of a gold reserve, depending on how one reads the phrase.
Notes and references

title: Transmutation
paragraphs: Transmutation was the conversion of one chemical element into another.
Chrysopoeia , the transmutation of common metals into gold or silver , was one of the best known goals of alchemists .
Advanced Potion-Making had a description about this.
Notes and references

title: Chemistry
paragraphs: Chemistry is the science concerned with the study of the composition, structure and properties of matter, with a particular emphasis on its chemical reactions and bonds.
The wizarding equivalents of chemistry were the arts of potion-making and alchemy .
History

During the the 1990-1991 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Arif Sikander had a conversation with Severus Snape, about Muggle chemistry in the Potions Classroom before they were interrupted by Jacob's sibling and Nymphadora Tonks .
Snape mentioned it in his introduction to Harry Potter 's first class on 1 September 1991 .
Severus Snape was known to like chemistry, and in his childhood he used to play with his chemistry set, according to Sirius Black .
Notes and references

title: Chrysopoeia
paragraphs: Using the Philosopher's Stone , Flamel achieved the transmutation of metals into pure gold
Chrysopoeia was a term used to refer to the transmutation of base metals into gold .

The transformation of common metals into gold or silver was among the best known goals of alchemists , along with the creation of a panacea (a remedy that would cure all diseases and prolong life indefinitely), and the discovery of a universal solvent .
History
The mythical King Midas gained the power of chrysopoeia from the Gods, but begged them to reverse it after he accidentally turned his daughter into gold.
Famed French alchemist Nicolas Flamel achieved at least two of these three primary goals with his creation of the Philosopher's Stone sometime in or after the 14th century .

The stone produced the Elixir of Life , a life extending potion that allowed him and his wife, Perenelle Flamel , to live for well over 600 years until sometime after the stone was destroyed in 1992 .
The stone could also perform chrysopoeia, although Flamel wasn't recorded as having used it for this purpose.
Merula Snyde turning to gold after picking up Sir Ribbithe

At some point before or during the 1990-1991 school year , Nicolas Flamel arrived at Hogwarts after giving a lecture at St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries where he used a Failed Stone as a teaching aid.
This stone was stolen by Merula Snyde and subsequently eaten by Sir Ribbithe , Liz Tuttle 's pet frog , who started turning everything he touched into gold.

Flamel was fascinated, as he had assumed that an individual having the power of chrysopoeia was impossible, however he also worked to help Merula, who had picked up Sir Ribbithe and had her hands turn to gold.
He and Penny Haywood created a potion which reversed the effects of chrysopoeia and administered it to Merula.
Afterwards, Flamel said he would be studying this incident for many years to come.
During a speech to the students of Hogwarts, Albus Dumbledore informed them that all items turned to gold would eventually revert back to their normal form, in about three to six months.
Notes and references

title: Silver
paragraphs: A silver Sickle
Silver (chemical symbol: Ag ) is a dense, soft shiny grey metal with a high value as money, second only to gold, and is used in jewelery in both Muggle and wizarding world.
The most common use for silver in the wizarding world was in the Sickle , though it was also used by goblins to create valuable armour and other items .
Overview
In the many Muggle myths and legends on the subject, werewolves can be killed by using a silver bullet.
This is false, but a mixture of powdered silver and dittany applied to a fresh bite would seal the wound and prevent the victim from bleeding to death.
The inner doors of Gringotts Wizarding Bank were made of silver and carried a poem warning of dire retribution to potential thieves.
Goblin-wrought silver never needed to be cleaned because it only took in that which made it stronger, and repelled anything else like dirt or rust, among other properties.
History
In 1926 , Newt Scamander anonymously gave Jacob Kowalski a suitcase full of silver occamy eggs to use as collateral for his bakery .
During his tenure as Headmaster of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Albus Dumbledore kept a number of curious and fragile instruments in his office which were made of silver.
These were repeatedly destroyed and repaired on numerous occasions.
The Deluminator he invented was, too, silver.
The Winged Key that matched the lock in the Underground Chambers in 1991 was also silver, like the handle of the door that it unlocked.
The Black family earned some silver goblets kept at 12 Grimmauld Place , embossed with their family crest.
During the summer holidays of 1995 , Mundungus Fletcher examined these and asked Sirius Black if they were solid silver.
He disgustedly agreed that they were, 15th-century goblin-wrought silver that was embossed with the Black family crest.
In late 1996 , Harry Potter discovered Mundungus Fletcher in Hogsmeade with some of these goblets, which he had stolen.
Lord Voldemort created Peter Pettigrew a hand to replace the one he sacrificed in his service.
It was made of solid silver, or appeared to be.
During the Duel in the Ministry Atrium , Voldemort also conjured a silver shield out of thin air in order to deflect a curse from Albus Dumbledore .
Silver as a colour
The colours of Slytherin were green and silver.
Unicorn blood , the Patronus Charm , Garrick Ollivander 's eyes were silver.
Dumbledore's hair was also silver, Rufus Scrimgeour 's was streaked with the colour, and Fleur and Gabrielle Delacour had "silver-blonde" hair.
Memories to be stored in a Pensieve resembled a silver liquid or gas, and could be mistaken for silver-coloured hair.
Notes and references

title: Panacea
paragraphs: Panacea was a remedy that supposedly would cure all diseases and prolong life indefinitely .
Its creation was one of the best known goals of the alchemists .

The Elixir of Life may have been considered the achievement of Panacea, as Lord Voldemort sought it out to regain a body after his original one was destroyed via a rebounded Killing Curse , and it can extend life indefinitely as long as it is drunk regularly.
At some point in or before 1990 , a rogue alchemist in Great Britain created and sold a fake panacea that was made of lard and corn starch , which gave the drinker boils instead of immortality.
Notes and references

title: Universal solvent
paragraphs: A universal solvent was a hypothetical substance that had the ability to dissolve any material.
Its discovery was one of the three goals of Alchemists .
Notes and references

title: Spagyric
paragraphs: A paragraph on Spagyric, on Libatius Borage 's Advanced Potion-Making
Spagyric (or plant alchemy ) was a less well-known branch of alchemy , with a focus on plants rather than metals.
It is the name given to the production of herbal medicines using alchemical procedures.
The Alchemy Room in St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries focused on the alchemy of plants, specifically healing herbs which were involved in cures.
Notes and references

title: Air
paragraphs: Ravenclaw , a House connecting to air
Air is an umbrella term used to refer to the various gaseous elements that make up the Earth 's atmosphere.
It is one of the four basic elements in Alchemy , along with fire , water , and earth .
Ravenclaw House was connected to the element of air.
Notes and references

title: Earth (element)
paragraphs: Hufflepuff , a House connecting to earth
Earth is one of the four basic elements in Alchemy , along with fire , water , and air .
It refers to the soil and mineral elements, the land itself, and in some cases, vegetation as well.
Hufflepuff House was connected to the element of earth.
Earth magic was a branch of elemental magic related to earth.
Notes and references

title: Ink
paragraphs: Ink is a liquid containing dye(s) or natural colouring(s).
When it is used, it produces images and texts on various surfaces and media.
Description
A quill with a bottle of ink
Ink was used in conjunction with quills to write on parchments by wizards and witches in the wizarding world , in place of the pens and pencils used in the Muggle world.

There were several types of inks, such as Azul Marino ink , various forms and types of Invisible Ink , Disappearing Ink , glow-in-the-dark ink, acidic ink, Self-Correcting Ink , Colour-Change Ink and Everlasting Ink .
Harry Potter seemed to prefer a scarlet-coloured ink.
In the wizarding world, ink was not permanent and smudges could easily be erased by using the a spell , with the possible exception of Everlasting Ink.
The feathers of the Augurey repelled ink, thus making them useless as quills.
Magical Regulation 572 is a rule issued by the British Ministry of Magic stating that the only ink to be used in examinations is Azul Marino ink .
History
Gilderoy Lockhart used Lilac Ink , his favourite colour.
Harry used this when he was helping Lockhart answer his fan mails as a detention in 1992 .
Tom Riddle's diary leaked ink when it was destroyed
As part of its abilities as a Horcrux , T. M. Riddle's Diary could absorb ink, and could interpret any messages written in it when it absorbed them.
It could also respond to these messages in ink, though it would reabsorb the ink used after a few moments.
When it was destroyed by Harry Potter in 1993 , it leaked a large quantity of ink, similarly to how a human would bleed .
Peeves would often shoot ink pellets at Hogwarts students.
This would usually only stop with the interruption of angry ghosts or teachers .
In 1995 , Dolores Umbridge had a quill which she made students use in detention , but it did not require any ink as it used the user's own blood and etched whatever was written into the skin.
Notes and references

title: Gunpowder
paragraphs: Gunpowder is a mixture of sulphur, charcoal and potassium nitrate.
Because of its burning properties and the amount of heat and gas volume that it generates, gunpowder has been widely used as a propellant in firearms and as a pyrotechnic composition in fireworks .
Gunpowder was one of the "mundane" contributions to science from which alchemists received prestige and support from the chemical industries of yore.
Notes and references

title: Aqua Vitæ
paragraphs: Aqua Vitæ (also spelt Aquavitæ ) is a term used to refer to distillates of alcoholic beverages.
The creation of Aqua Vitæ was a common alchemic experiment among European alchemists in the Middle Ages .
Aqua Vitæ is a known component of Belch Powder ; 3 gallons of the distillate is a required ingredient.
Notes and references

title: Alchemy Room
paragraphs: The Alchemy Room was a room in St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries used by the resident Healers to brew healing potions used at the hospital.
The room was also used by the Healers for alchemy , to study the magical properties of substances to help them synthesise their cures.
Notes and references

title: Africa
paragraphs: Africa is a continent in the eastern hemisphere.
The known wizarding nations that comprised it were Benin, Burkina Faso , Chad , Congo , Egypt , Ethiopia , Ivory Coast , Mauritius , Nigeria , Tanzania , Togo , Uganda , South Africa , and Zaire .
Magical community

The Beninese city of Bohicon , the Burkinabé capital city of Ouagadougou , the Egyptian capital city of Cairo , the Ethiopian city of Gimbi , the Tanzanian city of Sumbawanga , the Togolese city of Tchamba , and the Ugandan city of Patonga along with the Mountains of the Moon were known locations of wizarding communities.
Magical government
The only known magical government body in the continent was the Burkinabé Ministry of Magic .
Magical education
Uagadou , one of the eleven major wizarding schools of the world, was located in the Mountains of the Moon in Uganda .
It was the largest of all wizarding schools, and it took students from all over the continent.
It was known that other smaller schools in Africa had come and gone.

title: China
paragraphs: China is the third or fourth largest country in the world by size, and the largest by population.
Stretching across a large swath of eastern Asia , its capital of Beijing is located in the northeastern corner of the country.
The autonomous region of Tibet is also located within China.
Magical government
Liu Tao, the Chinese Minister for Magic in 1932
A Ministry of Magic existed in China.
Liu Tao was the Minister for Magic in 1932 .
Non-magic world
In July 1996 , The Guardian reported that the current Dalai Lama was given the Congressional Gold Medal of Honor by the United States , which China objected to strongly.
Wizarding world
Many different wand woods were from China.
For instance, redwood trees grew here, as well as in North America .
Jixi may have had a community of note in the wizarding world , as the Daily Prophet reported on its weather in its international section.
Sleekeazy's Hair Potion was manufactured in China.
Credence Barebone , Vinda Rosier and Carrow in China
In 1932 , Newton Scamander visited the Tianzi Mountains outside of Kweilin where he wanted to catalogue information on a Qilin .
There, he witnessed a Qilin mother birth a child; right afterwards, acolytes of Gellert Grindelwald came in and cast a spell on the mother, taking the child Qilin, and escaped.
Newt sat beside the mother Qilin, only to find a twin of the baby Qilin; he put the Qilin in the suitcase and left.
In 2010 , the Chinese National Quidditch team participated in the 2010 Quidditch World Cup .
The final was between China and Moldova , with Moldova winning 750 to 640.
The match lasted three days, and it was widely held to have produced some of the finest Quidditch seen this century.

In 2019 , members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force accompanied a team of Magizoologists from the Calamity World Centre in England to China, where they spent several days in stillness trying to safely see and capture a Demiguise , which benefited them as a test of patience, perseverance, and focus.
Education
There was possibly a Chinese wizarding school, which was attended by Robyn Thistlethwaite's mother .
Individuals
Long Shouren leaves his village in China
Cho Chang , a love interest of Harry Potter , as well as her grandfather , were presumably of Chinese heritage.
Long Shouren grew up in a small moutain village in China where his family protected dragons.
He left when he was seventeen to travel the world.
Robyn Thistlethwaite 's mother was of Chinese heritage, with Robyn being half-Chinese on her mother's side and half- British on her father 's side.
Other famous wizards hailing from China included the alchemist Dzou Yen , the dragonologist Quong Po and the Minister for Magic Liu Tao .

title: Astronomy (class)
paragraphs: Astronomy was a subject and core class and taught at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry and Uagadou .
Astronomy was the branch of magic and science that studied stars and the movement of planets.
Students would also use their wands with an Orrery to predict the next eclipse, the only known practical form of magic used in the class.
Uagadou students were known to be skilled in astronomy, implying the teaching that was provided at Uagadou was excellent.
Class information
The study of the stars
Astronomy lessons were spent observing the night skies with telescopes , as well as gaining an understanding of the various phenomena that go on in space, such as Lunar phases and Space weather .
Known assignments included learning the names of stars, constellations and planets, as well as charting their locations, movements, and environments.
It was a required class from year one until year five , and became an optional subject for the final two years.
Astronomy was not to be confused with the divination practice of astrology .
One was concerned with mysteries stellar and lunar, the other was referred to as "mere lunacy".
It is currently unclear exactly how this subject was relevant to the education of witches and wizards, but according to Professor Shah , there was much that could be gleaned from the stars.
She believed that people were like blank star charts , empty canvasses waiting to be inscribed by all that the universe had to offer.
Professor Shah found it increasingly rare to find a student who sought after things celestial (of their own accord).
Although, some students, like Amit Thakkar , were fascinated by the concept of infinity and limitless potential, as there was always something new being discovered in space.
In the fifth year , the Ordinary Wizarding Level examinations were taken.
During the exam, students had to fill in a blank star chart.
Wiseacre's Wizarding Equipment in Diagon Alley sold telescopes and other equipment needed for Astronomy.
Aurora Sinistra was the Astronomy professor at Hogwarts during Harry Potter 's time as a student.
She was also teaching during Jacob's sibling 's time at Hogwarts.
Location and time
Classrooms
The Astronomy Tower, where this class was held

Astronomy classes took place in the highest level of the Astronomy Tower , the tallest tower in Hogwarts Castle and included sky observation sessions with telescopes (each student had to buy one of their own).
Lesson times
Curriculum
First year

During the first year of studies at Hogwarts, students studied the night skies through their telescopes every Wednesday at midnight and learn the different names of the stars and the movements of the planets.
Towards the end of the 1991-1992 school year , Hermione Granger was quizzing Ron on Astronomy for preparation for their first year exams .
Their studying included using a map of Jupiter .
It was noted that the studies on Jupiter continued into later years, when Harry tried to learn the names of Jupiter's moons in his fifth year of study at Hogwarts.
Third year
In the 1993-1994 school year , one of the homework assignments included drawing a star chart which probably meant they studied stars that year, and they took a midnight exam at the end of the year.
Fifth year
Hogwarts students studied Jupiter's moons and wrote an essay for their homework containing facts such as Europa being covered by ice and Io having many volcanoes.
They filled in blank star charts and the homework during this year became intensive enough that some students had to organise a meeting to help each other get through it.
For the Astronomy O.W.L. exam in their fifth year, the written exam contained a section on Jupiter.
In 1996 , it was held on Wednesday morning.
The practical exam took place in the evening at eleven o'clock, and each student had to " fill in a blank star chart " based on a few hours of observing the night sky.

When Harry Potter was taking the Astronomy O.W.L. in 1996, Rubeus Hagrid was confronted by Dolores Umbridge and a team of corrupt Aurors in what was an attempted sacking, which was also the night that Minerva McGonagall took " no less than four Stunners to the chest. "

title: Kennilworthy Whisp
paragraphs: Kennilworthy Whisp was an English wizard , author and Quidditch expert/fanatic, known for having written a number of Quidditch -related works, including the best-selling book Quidditch Through the Ages .
Whisp resided in Nottinghamshire in England , and divided his time between his home and "wherever the Wigtown Wanderers were playing".
His hobbies included playing backgammon , vegetarian cookery , and collecting vintage broomsticks .
Despite liking vegetarian cookery, he was not a vegetarian.
Biography
During the Calamity in the late 2010s or early 2020s , Kennilworthy wrote an article in the Daily Prophet regarding which broomstick was most historically important in Quidditch .
The article received a massive, vitriolic response from Quidditch fans, reminding a Calamity Investigator working for the Statute of Secrecy Task Force of the power of sport.
Published works
Etymology
The author's surname may be derived from the Old English word "Wisp", meaning a small bundle of straw (such as might be found at the end of a broom). "
Kenilworth " is also the name of a town in Warwickshire, England .
Notes and references

title: Egyptian Centre for Alchemical Studies
paragraphs: The Egyptian Centre for Alchemical Studies was a centre where Alchemy was studied in Egypt .
There is a possibility this was the world's largest centre for Alchemical Studies.
Notes and references

title: Egypt
paragraphs: Egypt is a country in north-east Africa .
The capital of Egypt is Cairo and the Nile River runs through the country.
The main language is Arabic .
History
Ancient Egyptian depictions of wizardkind, holding wands and staffs
Egypt was the earliest place where magic had been recorded.
During the times of ancient Egyptian society, wizards and witches were held in high esteem.
Ancient Egyptian wizards had a tendency to place curses on tombs, which Gringotts Curse Breakers try to break.

In the year following the summer of 1899 , during his tour of the world, Elphias Doge wrote to Albus Dumbledore of the experiments of the Egyptian alchemists , which Albus was unable to attend due to the death of his mother .
Bill Weasley worked in Egypt for several years as a Curse-Breaker .
Molly and Arthur Weasley visited him there during the Christmas holidays in 1992 .
The entire Weasley family visited him there for a month in the summer of 1993 and also toured some of the Egyptian tombs after winning the Daily Prophet Grand Prize Galleon Draw .
One of the pyramids that the family toured was full of skeletons of Muggles who had broken in and had "grown extra heads and stuff".
Quidditch referee for the 1994 Quidditch World Cup Hassan Mostafa was from Egypt.
In 2002 , Egypt defeated Bulgaria 450 to 300 at the 2002 Quidditch World Cup .
Magical education
Egyptian witches and wizards had the option to attend Uagadou as it accepted students from all over Africa.
Magical games and sports
Egypt had its own national Quidditch team .
