title: Bilton Bilmes
paragraphs: Bilton Bilmes was a British or Irish wizard who, during the 1980s , was living in the Highlands of Scotland , having taken up both residence and employment in the picturesque little all-wizarding village of Hogsmeade as the proprietor of Zonko's Joke Shop .
Biography
Early life
Bilton Bilmes attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , where he was Sorted into Hufflepuff House .
During his school career, he was well known for his sense of humour.
He was an infamous prankster at Hogwarts during a time when the school had strict discipline policies.
However, his antics, according to Rolanda Hooch , introduced a balance between students and the faculty, with Bilmes protecting many students from the worst of the faculty's punishments.
During his school years, he poured Bulbadox powder in Horace Slughorn 's mead as a prank, which prevented Rita Skeeter from joining the Slug Club .
Despite this, he was a member of the Slug Club himself, and was still well-liked by Slughorn after Slughorn retired.
It took him three years to graduate the seventh year .
Later life

He once accidentally set off some Stink Pellets in the closet in his home and, unable to get the smell out, resolved to burn every piece of clothing he owned and buy new ones, only to accidentally burn his home to the ground in the process.
He spent the next several days drowning his sorrows in candy from Honeydukes , and his mistake would haunt him for many years to come.
By the 1980s , Bilton had settled down in Hogsmeade and took up a job at the local joke shop.

Loud and affable, and with a childlike fondness and enthusiasm for pranks and mischief, Bilton was always happy to accommodate the young scoundrels of Hogwarts Castle with the latest within classical trouble-making whenever they came to his shop looking for prank devices, actively encouraging their practical jokes.
Bilton would be visited many times by Jacob's sibling and their friends during their time at Hogwarts, where he would be instrumental in helping them with various problems.
Bilton participated in the Hogwarts Trivia contest that was held during the 1986-1987 school year , where he participated on the side of the former student team and represented Hufflepuff House.
After the contest was over, he would be presented with a Hogwarts Trivia sweatshirt by Gwenog Jones and Nymphadora Tonks as thanks for participating.
Bilmes on the floor of Zonko's during his depressive slump

During the 1987-1988 school year , Rita Skeeter published a review of the town of Hogsmeade which included a particularly hateful review of both Zonko's and Bilmes due to her personal vendetta against him.

This review, combined with several other coincidental events, caused Bilmes to think he wasn't funny anymore and sent him down into a depressive spiral that caused him to announce he was closing Zonko's.
When Jacob's sibling , Nymphadora Tonks , and Tulip Karasu learnt about this, they worked to helped Bilmes overcome his depression and re-open Zonko's.
Bilmes in St Mungo's with a Nose-Biting Teacup stuck to his nose
During the 1990-1991 school year , Bilmes got a Nose-Biting Teacup stuck to his nose, for which he had to go to St Mungo's to get it removed.
As part of their assignments as seventh-years , Jacob's sibling and Jae Kim attended to him in his hospital bed.
On 2 May 1998 , it is most likely that, as a former Hogwarts student, Bilmes participated in the Battle of Hogwarts alongside hs fellow Hogsmeade residents.
In the 2010-2011 school year , Bilmes was still working at Zonko's.
He was talking to Robyn Thistlethwaite when she accidentally set off Dungbombs and created a mess.
One of the shop's employees, Hrithvi Sharma , temporarily barred her from the shop for the incident.
Personality and traits
Bilmes's sense of humour was legendary, according to Rolanda Hooch , and he was well liked by much of the wizarding world.
During his time at Hogwarts , he acted as a shield to younger students from a much stricter faculty, which earned him respect even amongst the faculty he opposed.
Horace Slughorn liked him enough to invite him to become a member of the Slug Club , which Bilmes accepted.
Even Severus Snape respected him for his humour, though he himself didn't think Bilmes was that funny.
Bilmes was able to defuse many situations with his humour that would otherwise have caused him to get into trouble.

Professor Snape once recounted a story where he saw Bilmes get into a confrontation with a particularly large Slytherin Beater , during which he was able to defuse the situation with his good sense of humour.

As proprietor of Zonko's Joke Shop , Bilmes was so well loved by the inhabitants of Hogsmeade that, when news of Zonko's closing reached the community, many people were incredibly disheartened and stopped going to many of the local establishments out of sadness.
Bilmes was well loved by the students of Hogwarts too, with his shop being a popular stop for many of them during their Hogsmeade weekend trips .

He had a thick skin for criticism, not particularly caring about how well a light reviews painted him in, and did not care if people considered him a joke, as he only wished to make people happy with his humour.
When he wasn't able to make people happy with his jokes, he fell into a depressive slump, gorging himself on sweets and being too apathetic to bring himself to do anything.
Magical abilities and skills
Bilton wasn't a particularly gifted magical wizard, however he was still skilled enough to run Zonko's and invent new prank items from time to time.
Etymology

Bilton is the name of several towns in England whose names are alternatively derived either from the Anglo-Saxon Beolatun meaning Beola's town or the old English Billeton meaning the the farmstead of Billa or Bilo .
Bilmes is an obscure surname of Hebrew origin, most of whom are living in Argentina or New York .
Bilmes's name in French is Jussien Turlupin, which comes from the French comedic actor Henri Legrand who was a well known actor in the 16th and 17th centuries.
He was considered one of the best jokers in French theatre.

title: Fanged Frisbee
paragraphs: A Fanged Frisbee was similar to a Muggle frisbee , but it had teeth and 'snarls'.
They were forbidden at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
History

Fanged Frisbees could be purchased at a variety of joke shops in the wizarding world , including Zonko's Joke Shop in Hogsmeade near Hogwarts, and in Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes , the popular joke shop run by Fred and George Weasley in Diagon Alley, London.
1988-1989 school year
Fanged Frisbees unleashed in Zonko's

During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Jacob's sibling , Nymphadora Tonks and Tulip Karasu visited Zonko's Joke Shop in Hogsmeade in order to speak to owner Bilton Bilmes about Duncan Ashe .

During their visit, Bilton opened a new box of Fanged Frisbees in the store, but the Frisbees went out-of-control and started flying all over the shop, resulting in Jacob's sibling having to destroy them with the Bombardment Spell .
1989-1990 school year
Again during this school year, Bilton accidentally released several Fanged Frisbees in Zonko's when Jacob's sibling and Nymphadora Tonks entered.
Jacob's sibling again destroyed them with the Bombardment Spell.
These Frisbees were added to Filch 's list of forbidden objects in the 1994-1995 school year .
A brand of Fanged Frisbees, Fanged Flyers , was sold at Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes .
Using her Prefect duties, Hermione Granger took a Fanged Frisbee from a fourth year student in 1996 .
Ron Weasley quickly took it from her, saying he had always wanted one.
Harry Potter found a Frisbee in the Room of Requirement when hiding his copy of Advanced Potion Making .

paragraphs: This wizard was a shop assistant in Zonko's Joke Shop , Hogsmeade in the 2010s .
He was also attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry at the same time.
Biography
In December 2010 , he attended a rally led by Renka , an anti- werewolf activist, and listened to her hold the werewolves responsible for the break-ins of several shops in Hogsmeade .
Upon returning to work at Zonko's Joke Shop , he was approached by a Hogwarts student while he surveyed the damage that the thief had done to his shop.
He complained that he didn't have time to clean up after "hairy hooligans".
Later on, Robyn Thistlethwaite set off dungbombs in Zonko's.
He was overheard telling his friend about the mess it had caused.

title: Robyn Thistlethwaite
paragraphs: Robyn Huang Thistlethwaite was a witch who started attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in 2008 and was sorted into Gryffindor .
Biography
Early life
Robyn was born to a British father and a Chinese mother .
When Robyn was young, her family celebrated Chinese New Year .
After Robyn began attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , her mother wanted her to celebrate the festival as usual and sent her a recipe for Singing Hot Pot .
She also used to fend off gnomes in her family's garden.
Hogwarts years
At the start of the 2008-2009 school year , Robyn sat with Kevin Farrell on the Hogwarts Express .
She was Sorted into Gryffindor house.
After their first Charms lesson, Robyn was talking to Kevin and Lottie Turner in a corridor.
She approached a fellow first-year student and introduced herself.
She asked if they knew when Flying lessons started and that she couldn't wait to view the castle on a broomstick.
They asked her if she was nervous to be that high but she was very excited.
Kevin asked if they knew where the library was but they didn't know because they hadn't been there yet.
Kevin was worried it had moved because he was sure he had found it once.
Robyn told him only the stairs move but the classrooms stay where they are which he was pleased to hear.
Lottie thought the paintings and statues were wonderful and thought Hogwarts was like an art museum.
Robyn told her she hated museums because they were boring and filled with old stuff.
When Lottie told her about the Troll Tapestry , Robyn thought it was weird but admitted it was interesting.
When the student was challenged to a Duo Duel by Cassandra Vole , Robyn offered to help them.
Together, they beat Cassandra and her friend, Fischer Frey .
At one point, she taught Kevin how to fly on a broomstick .
One day, she was in the Great Hall looking for "flying buddies" and the student was interested.
While she couldn't wait for flying lessons, the student told her that they didn't know anything about broomsticks or flying.
She offered to show them, inviting them to fly around the castle.
She took them on a flying tour, where she was impressed with their flying skills.
Robyn attended Dance Club and forced Kevin to go with her.
While they were dancing, she kept stepping on him.
The student talked to them and Kevin whinged about Robyn, but she claimed he was having a great time there.
He told her he was until she had stepped on him, but she told him he didn't feel a thing.
He told her that he didn't at first so she shouted he should find someone else to dance with next time.
Robyn suggested the student find Daniel or Ivy to dance with.
Robyn received an owl from Lottie who was putting together a search party for Ivy in the library after curfew.
She snuck out and run into the student in a corridor who was also looking for her.
They went to the library together and found Kevin and Daniel already there.
Robyn was surprised that Daniel was reading books there to study so early in the school year.
Daniel told her if trying to learn at school is mad, then he was.
The student told them Ivy had to be lost in the castle.
Kevin was unsure if it was safe and when Daniel told him it wouldn't be, Robyn disagreed to encourage Kevin to stay and help.
After Daniel decided to leave, she goes with the student and Kevin to search the Potions Classroom where she released acromantulas by accident.
After they dispatched of the spiders, they left to search another part of the castle.
Robyn thought the corridors went on forever and understood how Ivy could get lost.
While they were talking, the portrait of William de Cognac asked them to put out their light so he could sleep.
Kevin asked if he happened to notice Ivy walking past.
He told them he hadn't and threatened to tell Filch they were there.
They were then spotted by Peeves who took great delight in finding the missing first-years before realising there was only supposed to be one.
They told Peeves they weren't lost but they were also looking for Ivy.
He decided to test their mettle.
After they defeated Peeves, the student and Robyn discovered Kevin had disappeared.
Daniel decided to help out after all and reappeared in the corridor to make sure they didn't lose House points .
When they heard Filch heading their way, they had to flee into the nearby Charms Classroom with a sign on the door reading "KEEP OUT".
Daniel was annoyed they ignored they sign and led him in there anyway but they were sure nothing dangerous was in there.
Daniel and Robyn saw a Monster Book of Monsters moving around in there.
The student couldn't spot it so Robyn enlarged it which made it angry.
After subduing it, Robyn had run away.
After she left, the student and Daniel found Ivy.
During a Quidditch game, Robyn missed a Bludger , which caused their Chaser to drop the Quaffle .
They were about to score a goal, which would have given their team a 150-point lead.
Their team-mate tried to help by cutting across the pitch, which knocked their own Seeker off course.
This prevented the Seeker from catching the Golden Snitch , causing the other team to win.
Robyn was very upset, holding herself responsible for their loss.
She wanted Rubeus Hagrid to feed her to a Blast-Ended Skrewt .
The student took her to Hagrid's Hut , where they hoped he would cheer her up.
Instead, they fought gnomes that were eating his pumpkins , which helped Robyn to let out her frustration.
In the 2010-2011 school year , Robyn made the house Quidditch team .

Nearly a century after Miranda Goshawk's spell journal was written and stolen, at some point between the 2008-2009 and 2010-2011 school year , Robyn, Kevin, and their friend followed a gone-astray Chocolate Frog , which brought them to find the notebook which was hidden on a quiet bookshelf in the Hogwarts Library.
When the three students realised it belonged to the famous witch who authored the The Standard Book of Spells , they were amazed and surprised.
Personality and traits
Robyn was a very determined girl who was obsessed with Quidditch and loved adventures.
Magical abilities and skills
Possessions

title: Dungbomb
paragraphs: A Dungbomb was a magical stink bomb that gave off a putrid odour.
Dungbombs were invented in the 1800s by Alberic Grunnion .
When handled, Dungbombs left a person's hands dirty.
They were sold at Gambol and Japes Wizarding Joke Shop , priced at one Sickle and twenty-one Knuts each.
Known uses
In 1891 , Dungbombs were available for purchase at Zonko's Joke Shop in Hogsmeade .

In or around the 1910s , Leta Lestrange , whilst a student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , let off a Dungbomb under the desk of Prendergast , a Hogwarts employee, so she could join her friend Newton Scamander in detention .

In the late 20th century , students at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry were constantly reminded by Professor Dumbledore that Dungbombs were banned items at the school, though only at the request of Argus Filch .
Despite (or perhaps due to) Filch's dislike of them, students often used them at school.
They were a particular favourite of Tulip Karasu , who frequently used them in her many pranks at Hogwarts in the 1980s .
She also owned a special Dungbomb on a necklace that she later gave to her friend, Jacob's sibling .
During the 1980s or 1990s , Zonko's sold a special extra smelly variant of a Dungbomb.
During a Christmas holiday in the 1980s , Jacob's sibling gave a Dungbomb to Charlie Weasley as a present along with a pair of Sugar Quills .
Fred and George Weasley once set a Dungbomb off under their Auntie Muriel 's chair, leading her to never visit again, and she subsequently wrote them out of her will.
In their first year at Hogwarts, the twins set off a Dungbomb and incurred Filch's wrath.
Sent to his office, they discovered the Marauder's Map , and George caused a distraction by dropping a second Dungbomb so that Fred could nick the map.
A poster advertising Dungbombs sold at Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes

During the 1990-1991 school year , Jacob's sibling used a Dungbomb to drive Dolores Umbridge out of her office so that they could properly search it to find out the information that Rita Skeeter wanted them to acquire.
In 1995 , Nymphadora Tonks also taught Ginny Weasley to test a door for an Imperturbable Charm , by checking if Dungbombs bounced away after being flicked at the door in question.

Later that same year, Filch accused Harry Potter of using an owl to order Dungbombs, when he was actually sending a secret letter to Sirius Black , and Harry truthfully denied it, with the backing of Cho Chang .

In 1996 , as the tyranny of Dolores Umbridge reached a new level with her becoming Headmistress , the students of Hogwarts revolted en masse, and Dungbombs and Stink Pellets were dropped in the halls with such frequency that it became the new fashion for students to use the Bubble-Head Charm just to ensure that they had a supply of fresh, clean air.

This increase in the use was partly in honour of Fred and George Weasley , with students continuing Weasley twins' campaign of harassment against Umbridge in the aftermath of their departure from Hogwarts .
The twins later sold Dungbombs among the many joke products at their shop, Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes .
Ron Weasley once expressed his fondness for Dungbombs by writing "Dungbombs rule" in Harry Potter 's copy of Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them by Newt Scamander .
In the 2010-2011 school year , Robyn Thistlethwaite accidentally set off Dungbombs in Zonko's Joke Shop and created a mess.
Notes and references

title: Stink Pellets
paragraphs: Stink Pellets were a joke product made of small pellets of dung , that released a burst of stinking green smoke.
In 1992 , they could be purchased in Diagon Alley at Gambol and Japes Wizarding Joke Shop for 20 Knuts each, or four Sickles for a pack of ten.
They were also sold in Hogsmeade at Zonko's Joke Shop .
They were not tolerated by Argus Filch .
History
Early in the 1993-1994 school year , Fred Weasley was running low on these and wanted to get some in Hogsmeade.
Their usage was similar to that of a Dungbomb , another item not tolerated by the Hogwarts caretaker.

In 1996 , as the tyranny of Dolores Umbridge reached a new level with her becoming Headmistress , the students of Hogwarts revolted en masse, and Dungbombs and Stink Pellets were dropped in the halls with such frequency that it became the new fashion for students to use the Bubble-Head Charm just to ensure that they had a supply of fresh, clean air.
In December 2010 , Robyn Thistlethwaite asked her friend to buy 17 Stink Pellets for her in Zonko's after she was barred.

In 2020 , Hermione Granger told Ron Weasley (actually Albus Potter with the use of Polyjuice Potion ) that if he had left another stink pellet in her office, then he would be in big trouble (" Merlin won't help you ").
Notes and references

title: Trick wand
paragraphs: Trick wands , also known as fake wands , were magical joke objects that were created by Fred and George Weasley , and sold in the shop they founded, Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes .
These wands appeared normal in every way, but when used to cast a spell , they turned into random objects (e.g. rubber mice or chickens).
A more expensive version beat the user around the head and neck.
As of 2010 , they were also sold in Zonko's Joke Shop .
History
A trick wand
In August 1994 , Molly Weasley got very frustrated when she picked a stray one of these up even though she had banned them from their house, The Burrow .
At the 1994 Quidditch World Cup , Ludo Bagman found the wands very amusing and offered to pay Fred and George Weasley five Galleons for one.

Just before Professor McGonagall announced the Yule Ball at Hogwarts in December 1994, Harry Potter and Ron Weasley were having a sword fight with a couple of trick wands in Transfiguration class , where Ron's turned into a tin parrot , with Harry's becoming a rubber haddock .
After Ron began to help his brother George managing Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes , he introduced trick wands to a visiting student and recalled he and Harry's sword fight.
In December 2010 , Robyn Thistlethwaite asked her friend to buy her 22 trick wands from Zonko's Joke Shop after she was barred.
Notes and references

title: Boxing telescope
paragraphs: Boxing telescopes were magical joke products first invented before the 1890s .
During the 1990s , Fred and George Weasley invented their own version for Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes .
When held up to the eye, a small fist would extend and punch the individual in the face.
Between 1890 and 2010 , they were sold at Zonko's Joke Shop .
Effects
Fred and George Weasley invented a version that, when squeezed, produced a tiny fist on a spring from its end, landing a punch, accompanied by a puff of black smoke and a loud bang.
The purple bruise caused by the telescope did not fade by itself, and could not be healed with standard remedies such as could be found in The Healer's Helpmate .
The only known means to remove was another Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes product, a bruise removal paste .
History
Boxing telescopes were available in Zonko's Joke Shop during the 1890s and 1980s .
Hermione's black eye after a boxing telescope hit her in the face
Fred and George stored boxing telescopes among the products in their old bedroom.
When Hermione Granger went rummaging in their boxes she accidentally activated one which gave her a black eye that Molly Weasley was unable to remove.
When Hermione, Harry Potter , and the Weasleys went to Diagon Alley shortly afterwards, Draco Malfoy noticed Hermione's black eye and said he wanted to buy flowers for whoever did it.
The group then went to the twins' joke shop, where Fred gave Hermione a thick yellow paste , which removed the bruise within an hour.
In December 2010 , Robyn Thistlethwaite asked her friend to get her two boxing telescopes in Zonko's Joke Shop after she was barred.
Notes and references

title: Disillusionment Charm
paragraphs: The Disillusionment Charm ( incantation unknown ) was a charm that disguised a target as its surroundings by making it take on the exact colour and texture of its environment, effectively turning it into a chameleon .
Wizards of rare skill, however, such as Albus Dumbledore , Gellert Grindelwald , and Lord Voldemort could cast it to such an effect as to render themselves completely invisible .
Casting
It is presumed that there were two methods of casting.
It seemed that if one was using the charm on themselves, they must twirl their wand around themselves as though they were wrapping themselves in rope.
If, however, they were using it on an external target, they must merely tap on the target with their wand.
This then produced a sensation that a raw egg had been cracked onto the person's head as the charm travelled down them, granting them invisibility.
History

Hippogriffs and winged horses may have been kept by wizards , as long as they performed a Disillusionment Charm on them daily (as their effects were apt to wear off) so that Muggles would not notice anything strange about them.
It was also noted that one of the ways to create an Invisibility Cloak was to imbue a travelling cloak with a Disillusionment Charm, although the charms on these cloaks wore off with time.
During the 1987-1988 school year , R sent a messenger to confront Jacob's sibling about the student's quest for the Cursed Vaults .
This messenger's face was concealed by a red hooded cloak and a Disillusionment Charm.
After Patricia Rakepick defeated the messenger with the Blasting Curse , Jacob's sibling used a General Counter-Spell to remove the charm, revealing their identity .

During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , fifth-year Charms class students were taught about this charm by Professor Filius Flitwick for the Ordinary Wizarding Levels in the subject.
In December 1997 , Hermione Granger suggested using a Disillusionment Charm when she and Harry Potter were planning the visit to Godric's Hollow .
Known uses
Known practitioners
Notes and references

title: Ever-Bashing Boomerang
paragraphs: An Ever-Bashing Boomerang was a magical joke product that swung back to repeatedly hit the thrower.
Argus Filch added these Boomerangs to the list of items banned at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry at the beginning of the 1994-1995 school year .
History

During the 1988-1989 school year , Jacob's sibling and Jae Kim got a box of a jinxed version of Ever-Bashing Boomerangs from Mundungus Fletcher , which would fly everywhere once released instead of flying back to the thrower.
They later released them in the Great Hall with Tulip Karasu and Nymphadora Tonks which drove nearly everyone out of the Hall.
In December 2010 , Zonko's Joke Shop sold Ever-Bashing Boomerangs.
Robyn Thistlethwaite snuck into the shop when she was barred under the Disillusionment Charm .
She knocked the Boomerangs and they sprung to life, drawing the attention of Hrithvi .
Notes and references

title: Zonko's Joke Shop (The Wizarding World of Harry Potter)
paragraphs: The exterior concept art of Zonko's shop for The Wizarding World of Harry Potter theme park
A recreation of Zonko's Joke Shop in Hogsmeade is located in The Wizarding World of Harry Potter in the Islands of Adventure in Orlando.
Visitors are able to buy various wizard joke articles from this shop.

In a conference call on 28 January 2010 with Thierry Coup, vice president of creative development for Universal Creative, it was revealed that Zonko's shop is the largest shop in The Wizarding World of Harry Potter theme park.
Products
Notes and references

title: Dagenham
paragraphs: Dagenham is a town in East London , England .
History
During the time of the Calamity in the 21st century , George Weasley accidentally shrank several teashops in Dagenham into miniature form, while testing his new joke product, a Tea Snug .
Members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force were sent by Hermione Granger to help solve the problem.
Notes and references

title: 21st century
paragraphs: Times

title: Tea Snug
paragraphs: A Tea Snug was a joke product created by George Weasley and intended for sale at Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes .
History
During the Calamity in the late 2010s and early 2020s , George Weasley attempted to test a Tea Snug, but he accidentally shrank several teashops in Dagenham into miniature form instead.
Members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force were sent by Hermione Granger to help solve the problem.
Notes and references

title: Fire-breathing chicken
paragraphs: A fire-breathing chicken was a magical breed of chicken that possessed the ability to breathe fire , very similar to the dragon .
History

During the 1890s , a hybrid between a chicken and a Common Welsh Green called a Dricken was rumoured to exist, and prompted the British Ministry of Magic to launch an investigation into experimental breeding.
Bob holding one of these creatures in a cardboard box
One of these creatures was confiscated by Ministry employee Bob in 1995 , as the creature was considered a major violation of the Ban on Experimental Breeding .
The chicken was put inside a large cardboard box, whose air holes would frequently light up due to the bird 's fiery exhalations.
The box was most likely enchanted to prevent it from catching fire.
The box and the chicken were taken by Bob to the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures .
Several fire-breathing chickens appeared throughout the Wizarding world during the Calamity in the 2010s , in which they acted as Confoundable guards to certain Foundables , such as Kneazles .
Volunteer members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force had to cast the Ebublio Jinx to trap these chickens in large bubbles, allowing the Foundables to return to their rightful places.

In the 2010s , Rubeus Hagrid , after undergoing hours of positive reinforcement through the use of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans , was able to train fire-breathing chickens to hold their fire at a consistent temperature and to change the flames' temperature on command, enabling them to heat up cauldrons much quicker, with only the occasional burn risk.
This technique helped enable members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force to increase the duration of the Baruffio's Brain Elixir brewed within these cauldrons.
A Calamity Investigator working for the task force later found a large number of fire-breathing chickens underneath an inn in Brondby , Denmark .
As the creatures had become a delicacy after being revealed to actually exist to wizardkind at large, the Calamity Investigator brought the chickens back to the British Ministry of Magic .
As a reward for their efforts, Minister for Magic Hermione Granger secured higher-energy meals at wizarding bed and breakfast inns for the Calamity Investigator.
Notes and references

title: Chicken (bird)
paragraphs: A chicken is a type of domesticated fowl and one of the most common and widespread domestic animals, commonly consumed as food .
Description
Chickens were kept as pets by the wizarding community.
The Weasley family kept chickens in a large chicken coop at the Burrow .
Fleur Delacour once stated that there isn't much to do at the Burrow, "unless you like cooking and chickens".
Rubeus Hagrid kept chickens and roosters beside his hut , some of which were killed during the 1992-1993 school year by Ginny Weasley while she was under the control of Tom Riddle .
The meat of the chicken was a popular ingredient in both Muggle and wizarding cuisine.
Although chickens did not harness any magical ability, they could be altered by magic to become magical creatures .
For instance, Bob confiscated a fire-breathing chicken due to breaches of the Ban on Experimental Breeding , and Babayaga , a Russian hag , lived in a house standing on giant chicken legs.
A chicken egg hatched under a toad would produce a Basilisk , King of the Serpents, however, the cry of a rooster was fatal to the Basilisk.
This was why Tom Riddle ordered Ginny Weasley to kill all the roosters surrounding Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , as to ensure the welfare of his Basilisk .
A baby dragon must be fed a bucket of brandy mixed with chicken blood every half an hour.

The Weasley twins created two products with a chicken theme, Rubby O' Chicken , a rubber chicken bewitched to perform an Irish stepdance, and trick wands , some of which were bewitched to transform into a rubber chicken whenever touched.
The spell Pullus transfigured Erklings and other creatures/objects into either chickens or geese.
The cockatrice was extremely similar to a rooster, however, instead of a feathered tail, it had the tail of a lizard.
Known chickens

title: Common Welsh Green
paragraphs: The Common Welsh Green , or just Welsh Green , was a dragon native to Wales .
It nested in the higher mountain regions, where a reservation had been set up for it.
It was a green dragon with a distinctive, musical roar.
Description
The Common Welsh Green dragon
The Common Welsh Green dragon was a relatively subdued breed (except for the rare exception of the Ilfracombe Incident ).
It preferred to prey mainly on sheep and other small mammals and to avoid human contact altogether.
That being said, the Common Welsh Green was known to do what it had to in order to survive in a time of crisis, including taking refuge in a human inhabited area and even feeding on fruits .
The Welsh Green's roar was rather distinctive and somewhat melodious, and it issued its fire in narrow jets.
The eggs of the Common Welsh Green were earthy brown, flecked with green.
History
17th century
It was possible that a young Common Welsh Green may have been the actual cause of the Great Fire of London in 1666 .
19th century
At some point in 1890 or 1891 , it was illegally captured by poachers and held in captivity at Horntail Hall .
20th century
The Ilfracombe Incident occurred in 1932 , when a rogue Common Welsh Green dragon attacked a group of sunbathers at Ilfracombe, in Devon , England.
The attack was thwarted by the Toke wizarding family, who proceeded to cast the largest group of Memory Charms seen in the twentieth century.
The Toke family were subsequently awarded the Order of Merlin First Class, for their heroism and quick thinking.
The Common Welsh Green at the Magical Creatures Reserve
There existed a Common Welsh Green at the Magical Creatures Reserve during the 1980s .
Jacob's sibling and Penny Haywood bonded with it and collected dragon dung for fertiliser .
A Common Welsh Green attacked several Muggles in Kenilworth in Southwest England during the 1990-1991 school year .
Jacob's sibling investigated this case with the Ministry , and the dragon was eventually captured and sent to its new home.
Fleur Delacour faced this breed of dragon for the First Task of the Triwizard Tournament in 1994 .
She enchanted the creature into a magical slumber to retrieve her golden egg .
The spell was only partly successful and the dragon attacked, setting Fleur's skirt on fire.
Notes and references

title: Dricken
paragraphs: The Dricken was a fire-breathing chicken that was allegedly a hybrid between a chicken and a Common Welsh Green dragon .
This creature was bred by a Cornish wizard .
History
The Dricken was bred by a Cornish wizard in 1890 , supposedly by crossing a chicken with a Common Welsh Green dragon .

Although technically legal at the time, the British Ministry of Magic started to look into confirming the existence of the creature, along with some of the wizard's other rumoured cross-breeds, in order to ensure that none of them caused any harm to the wizarding or Muggle communities nearby if they did exist.

Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures employee Belinda Brown commented on the rumoured creature in an interview in the Daily Prophet by claiming that the Ministry's concerns would be greater if the supposed "Dricken" was a dragon-sized chicken rather than a chicken-sized dragon.
The Dricken was eventually located and captured in the town of Newquay .

Belinda Brown commented that the British Ministry of Magic had ensured the safety of both the creature and the citizens of Newquay and was looking into the rumours of the Dricken's origin through experimental breeding, with Belinda asserting that such experimental breeding should be made illegal.
The Cornish wizard would later only comment that the "little bird" shouldn't be "locked up in London " just because it could breathe fire.
Notes and references

title: Bob
paragraphs: Bob was a British wizard who worked for the British Ministry of Magic , under the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures .
He was described as big and bearded.
Biography
Arthur Weasley and Harry Potter ran into Bob while waiting for a lift in the Ministry lobby on the 12 August 1995 , the day of Harry's disciplinary hearing .
He was carrying a large cardboard box that contained a fire-breathing chicken that he strongly suspected was a serious violation of the Ban on Experimental Breeding .
When the lift arrived, he got on with Arthur and Harry, and exited at the floor of the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures , the department in which he worked.
Magical abilities and skills
Notes and references

title: Ban on Experimental Breeding
paragraphs: Newt Scamander , the law's writer
The Ban on Experimental Breeding was a law enacted in 1965 to prevent the creation of new species of creatures within Great Britain , out of the fear that they may be dangerous and untameable.
History

There was initial support for a ban on experimental breeding in the 1890s when a " Dricken ", a cross between a chicken and dragon , was rumoured to have been bred, and an investigation was carried out by the Ministry of Magic on magical cross-breeds.

Belinda Brown , an employee for the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures , spoke to the Daily Prophet about her concerns on experimental breeding, but believed not many people were paying attention to it.
By 1925 , a similar ban had come into place in America .
The law was eventually written by the Magizoologist Newt Scamander some decades later, and was enforced by the Ministry of Magic's Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures.
Scamander personally regarded the implementation of the law as his greatest achievement.
The punishment for violations of this law were handed down by the Wizengamot .
Possible breaches
Blast-Ended Skrewts
A young Blast-Ended Skrewt on a leash
The Blast-Ended Skrewt was a cross between a Manticore and a Fire Crab that was bred by Rubeus Hagrid in the autumn of 1994 .
They looked like large, deformed, shell-less lobsters with legs sticking out at odd angles.
They were able to produce small explosions which propelled themselves forward, and the males had stingers and the females had suckers to suck blood.
Eventually Skrewts grew to be about 10 feet long and were highly dangerous, with spell-resistant armour and a weak, soft underbelly.
Despite their creation having breaching this ban, their creator, Hagrid, was never punished for their creation.
Fire-breathing chickens
A fire breathing chicken
Fire breathing chickens were a breed of chicken which possessed the ability to breathe fire, much like a dragon .
In 1995 , Bob confiscated one of these creatures, remarking to Arthur Weasley that it "looked like a serious breach of the ban on experimental breeding".
By the 21st century , there were many more of these creatures in the world, particularly in Denmark where they had become a delicacy.

Rubeus Hagrid had managed to train several of these chickens to hold their fire at a constant temperature and increase the temperature of their flames at will, which aided Calamity Investigators in brewing potions.
Pygmy Puffs
Pygmy puffs
Pygmy Puffs were a miniature variation of the regular Puffskein that came in colours such as pink and purple.
They were bred by Fred and George Weasley , the proprietors of Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes , who created them for their WonderWitch line.
Eventually, Pygmy Puffs were available to buy at other retailers as well, such as the Magical Menagerie .
Fanged Puffskeins
A fanged puffskein
Fanged Puffskeins were a variation of the normal Puffskein that possessed fangs.
Notes and references

title: Ebublio Jinx
paragraphs: The Ebublio Jinx or Bubble Jinx ( Ebublio ) was a jinx that entrapped the target in a very large bubble that could not be popped by physical force or seen through by the individual trapped inside.
Filius Flitwick invented a modified version of this jinx which the target could see out of, which he used during the House Points Scramble .
History
Hogwarts students in the 1980s often cast the Elublio Jinx against their opponents whilst duelling at the Duelling Club .
When trying to rehome the Flying Sparks , Ben Copper , Penny Haywood , and their fellow student used the jinx to safely trap the Firedrakes in order to move them.
Albus Dumbledore later cast it to move a noble oak tree .
This jinx was used heavily amongst volunteer members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force during the Calamity in the 2010s .

This spell was particularly useful when containing gnomes , fire-breathing chickens , trolls and even other wizards in large bubbles of water , in the form of Confoundables which were guarding various Foundables throughout the wizarding world .
Known practitioners
Notes and references

title: Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans
paragraphs: Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans were one of the most popular sweets in the wizarding world .
Invented by Bertie Bott , they were almost the same as Muggle jelly beans , except the range encompassed every possible flavour imaginable.
There was also no way of telling for sure what flavour any given bean was without tasting it, although you could try and guess by the colour.
There were ordinary flavours like chocolate , peppermint , and marmalade , but also less fanciable ones like spinach , liver , and tripe .
There were also strange and unusual flavours that were not actual foods like grass, farm dirt, vomit , earwax , paper, and bogeys.
At Sugarplum's Sweets Shop , they were priced at 6 Sickles per box.
History
A box of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans
The inventor of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans was the eponymous Bertie Bott , who created them in the mid- 20th century by mistake.
He was planning on making tasty sweets from food, but accidentally made one taste like a dirty sock.
He immediately recognised the sales potential of " a risk with every mouthful!"
According to Ron Weasley , there are ordinary flavours like chocolate and peppermint and marmalade, but also more adventuresome ones like spinach and liver and tripe.
George Weasley said he had a bogey-flavoured bean once.
Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans
In late June 1992 , while Harry was in the Hospital Wing , he offered one to Professor Dumbledore .
Dumbledore told him that he had been unfortunate enough to have come across a vomit-flavoured one in his youth, and since that occasion, he had not cared for them.

In spite of this, he decided to give them another chance and carefully selected a golden brown-coloured one that he assumed would be toffee-flavoured, but it turned out to be an earwax-flavoured bean.
They were advertised at the 422nd Quidditch World Cup on a large sign, showing how famous and popular they are.
The advertisement at the cup stated: "Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans--A Risk with Every Mouthful!"

During the Calamity in the 2010s , Rubeus Hagrid , after undergoing hours of positive reinforcement through the use of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans, was able to train fire-breathing chickens to hold their fire at a consistent temperature and to change the flames' temperature on command, enabling them to heat up cauldrons much quicker, with only the occasional burn risk.
This technique helped enable members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force to increase the duration of the Baruffio's Brain Elixir brewed within these cauldrons.
Popularity
Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans were a popular sweet for students at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
They bought them from the lunch trolley on the Hogwarts Express and from Honeydukes in Hogsmeade.
They gave them for Christmas gifts and as gifts when someone was ill and in the Hospital Wing .
Bertie Bott's Beans were sold in bags or in small striped boxes.
Known flavours
Notes and references

title: Baruffio's Brain Elixir
paragraphs: Baruffio's Brain Elixir was a potion that supposedly increased the drinker's brain power.
According to Gethsemane Prickle , British Ministry of Magic Herbologist and Potioneer , Baruffio's Brain Elixir did not work and posed a serious health hazard if improperly brewed.
History
A phial containing Astor Bellchant 's failed attempt at Baruffio's Brain Elixir

In June 1996 , Harry Potter and Ron Weasley were offered some by Eddie Carmichael , who swore it was responsible for his achievement of nine Outstandings in his Ordinary Wizarding Levels the previous year.
Before they could buy it from him, Hermione Granger , a Prefect at the time, confiscated it and poured it down the toilet.

After receiving a letter from Hogwarts School informing him that his son Albert was failing Transfiguration , Charms , and Herbology , Astor Bellchant blackmailed Bilius Finbok , with whom he had attended Hogwarts, into brewing an illegal mental acuity potion.

When Finbok was badly hurt while handing a Runespoor whose eggs he intended to use for the potion, Bellchant tried to use Finbok's potions lab to brew it himself; his attempt at brewing the potion was duly confiscated by Ministry investigators Mathilda Grimblehawk and her partner , and expert potioneer Gethsemane Prickle labelled it a "seriously incompetent" brew, likely to melt the brain of whoever would take it.
Notes and references

title: Brondby
paragraphs: Brondby is a municipality in eastern Denmark .
History
By at least the 2010s , a Calamity Investigator working for the Statute of Secrecy Task Force found a large number of fire-breathing chickens underneath an inn in Brondby.
As the creatures had become a delicacy after being revealed to actually exist to wizardkind at large, the Calamity Investigator brought the chickens back to the British Ministry of Magic .
As a reward for their efforts, Minister for Magic Hermione Granger secured higher-energy meals at wizarding bed and breakfast inns for the Calamity Investigator.
Notes and references

title: Denmark
paragraphs: Denmark is a Nordic country, the southernmost country in Scandinavia ; it is located southwest of Sweden and south of Norway , and bordered to the south by Germany .
Greenland is a part of Denmark as an autonomous territory.
History
In 1926 , The New York Ghost reported that Apparition by under-seventeens had been legalised in Denmark.
By at least the 2010s , a Calamity Investigator working for the Statute of Secrecy Task Force found a large number of fire-breathing chickens underneath an inn in Brondby , Denmark.
As the creatures had become a delicacy after being revealed to actually exist to wizardkind at large, the Calamity Investigator brought the chickens back to the British Ministry of Magic .
As a reward for their efforts, Minister for Magic Hermione Granger secured higher-energy meals at wizarding bed and breakfast inns for the Calamity Investigator.
Notes and references

title: Greenhouse Charm
paragraphs: The Greenhouse Charm ( Celescere ) was a charm that helped the growth of plant-based potion ingredients in greenhouses.
History
The Greenhouse Charm was created as the culmination of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force 's research into the Gemino Curse and Herbivicus Charm .
The Herbologist Neville Longbottom later provided improvements to the incantation and stance used when casting it.
A Calamity Investigator working for the Statute of Secrecy Task Force also discovered that moisture and general weather conditions could affect the duration of the charm.
The charm was taught to the Statute of Secrecy Task Force to help them with the Calamity .
Etymology
Celescere is possibly a portmanteau of two words, celerare (Latin for "to quicken or accelerate") and crescere ("to thrive; to multiply" in Latin, and "to grow or cultivate" in Italian).
Put together, the resulting incantation can mean to grow (plants) quickly, or to accelerate the growth of the plants, much like the effect of the Herbivicus Charm.
Notes and references

title: Herbivicus Charm
paragraphs: The Herbivicus Charm , also known as the Herbivicus Spell or Gardening Charm , ( Herbivicus ) was a charm used to rapidly increase the growth rate of plants and cause flowers to bloom.
Herbivicus Duo was a stronger version of this charm.
Effects
Upon casting, a twisting jet of brilliant green light would shoot from the wand .
A crackling ball of emerald-green energy would appear at the tip of the wand, with an identical one appearing at the plant one was charming , with a thick jet of green light connected them.
The plant would rapidly begin blooming.
If a plant's situation was delicate, then the use of the Herbivicus Charm wasn't recommended, as in certain cases it could do more harm than good.
Use of the Herbivicus Charm would leave certain marks on the plant it was used on, and a skilled herbologist would be able to recognise these signs.
History
Red roses bloomed with the Herbivicus Charm in Herbology

Around Valentine's Day in 1988 , to celebrate the holiday, classes at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry provided subject-related lessons, and this charm was taught in fourth-year Herbology class for the special occasion by Professor Pomona Sprout .
She specifically taught them how to grow red roses with the charm.
Harry Potter using this charm to bloom a plant in a Hogwarts greenhouse

A spellbook which detailed how to cast this charm was owned by Professor Sprout, which she used to help teach the charm to her Herbology students, from the fourth year onward, the year this spell was taught.
This spellbook could be found in the Hogwarts greenhouses .
Volunteers of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force were advised on using this charm by Constance Pickering to help accelerate the growth of plants they grew in Greenhouses, for usage in potion -making.

A Calamity Investigator working for the task force also used this charm repeatedly to increase the growth rate of cabbages in several patches to produce nearly a million cabbage hearts , which they gave to the chef Wulf Kauendessen , who needed them for his "legendary" sweet und sauerkraut .

title: Herbologist
paragraphs: Herbologist Pomona Sprout tending to her plants in Greenhouse Three
A Herbologist was a wizard or witch who specialised in the field of Herbology , the study of plants and fungi, both magical and mundane.

Pomona Sprout , Herbert Beery and Neville Longbottom were Professors of Herbology at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , while Tilden Toots was a celebrity herbologist in the wizarding world .
History
Phyllida Spore was a 15th century witch who was a celebrated Herbologist.
She was the author of the textbook One Thousand Magical Herbs and Fungi and Healing at Home with Herbs .
One Thousand Magical Herbs and Fungi was one of the required texts for first-year students.
The textbook was also used in Potions and Herbology classes at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
Mirabel Garlick teaching students Herbology at Hogwarts
At some point in the late 1800s, Mirabel Garlick became the Professor of Herbology at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
Her sunny demeanour and flowery language charmed colleagues and students alike, prompting some students to worry she might one day leave them for another greenhouse.
The Sunday edition of The New York Ghost published on 28 November 1926 reported a Mandrake attack on a Herbologist.
Herbert Beery was the Herbology Professor sometime during Armando Dippet's tenure as Headmaster.
Miranda Goshawk was very knowledgeable of Herbology and herself a Herbologist.
She wrote an expansive encyclopedia on the subject, titled Goshawk's Guide to Herbology .
Herbologists supplied various healing herbs to St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries so the Healers there could use them to brew various healing potions .

In the 1990-1991 school year , Herbologists mixed up the hospital's order, resulting in Healer Miriam Strout assigning Jacob's sibling with the collection of various herbs to the hospital to fix the problem.
Eventually, the Herbologists corrected the hospital's order.
Professor Sprout teaching Hogwarts students about Mandrakes
Pomona Sprout was a Herbologist who taught Herbology at Hogwarts.
In the greenhouses, Sprout had to deal with a wide variety of magical plants, some of which were very strange and even dangerous.
She handled them all with aplomb, even the Venomous Tentacula .
Sprout was kind and nurturing to the students, and surely encouraged Neville's penchant for Herbology because he was anxious to show her his Mimbulus mimbletonia .
Her favourite brand of fertiliser was Dragon dung .
Sprout used bandages to fashion slings for a number of the Hogwarts Whomping Willow 's branches after Harry and Ron crashed the Flying Ford Anglia into it.
Neville Longbottom teaching Herbology at Hogwarts
Tilden Toots was Herbologist with "three green thumbs" who hosted a Wizarding Wireless radio show on Herbology.
This show was called Toots, Shoots 'n' Roots.
He also produced his own line of plant-related potions , such as Rejuicer and Regerminator .
After the Second Wizarding War , Neville Longbottom became a Herbologist, specifically the Herbology professor at Hogwarts.

title: Gareth Greengrass
paragraphs: Minister Gareth Greengrass was a British wizard who worked as a Senior Unspeakable in the Department of Mysteries and later Head of the Department of Mysteries at the British Ministry of Magic .
He was also a member of the Unforgivable , an insidious organisation of Dark wizards .
Biography
Early life
Gareth was born into the Greengrass family , one of the oldest pure-blooded families in Britain .
In his adulthood, Gareth joined the British Ministry of Magic .
Career
Gareth successfully landed a job as a research assistant and eventually worked his way up to the point where he earned a place as a Unspeakable in the Department of Mysteries .
He eventually became a Senior Unspeakable.
Gareth married Aquila Greengrass and they had a daughter, Cereus Greengrass .
By 2019 , Aquila had died .
Cereus had a blood malediction for which Gareth was desperate to find a cure.
The Calamity
Greengrass as "Edward Scot"
At an unknown date, Gareth joined the Unforgivable .
By 2015 , he had stolen the appearance of Kensington Millbottom and taken on the persona of 'Edward Scot'.
He lived a double life, being both Gareth and 'Edward' when needed, deceiving everyone. '
Edward' joined the Department of International Magical Co-operation , working up to be the Lead Liaison Minister .
Gareth joined a council that oversaw the investigation into the disappearance of Grim Fawley 's wife Penelope and four other people known as the London Five .
He promised Grim that he would do everything in his power to find Penelope, and that no cost would be spared.
However, the council called off the investigation before she was found and recommended Grim take time off work to recover and care for his children .
Grim had a grudge against Gareth's persona 'Edward Scot' and suspected he was involved in the failed London Five investigation.
However, Gareth was in fact behind Penelope's disapperance, as he had cursed her to remain trapped inside a portrait in her Ministry office.

Gareth met with a Calamity Investigator working for the Statute of Secrecy Task Force over tea and provided them a documented list of 700 instances of spells cast in anger, including Grim Fawley's Calamity Spell as example 628, explaining that all of them were more powerful than the caster imagined possible.
He later took the same Calamity Investigator to watch Muggles playing rugby at Wembley .
Although the investigator was confused by the sport, Gareth helped them better appreciate the sheer violence of the spectacle, broadening their understanding of the sporting mind.
Gareth also led a meditation retreat for a select group of task force members, including the same Calamity Investigator.

As a result of his guidance, the investigator only fell asleep once and gained greater focus and mindfulness, with these effects being further enhanced when they consumed their Baruffio's Brain Elixir .
Gareth later travelled to Nepal to return Foundables , discovering a new powerful mental technique in the process.
He showed this technique to the same Calamity Investigator, who found that the technique immediately helped them better utilise their Trace Charm .
Around January of 2021 , Gareth's persona 'Edward Scot' received word from the French Ministry of Magic of a large breach in the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy .
Muggle reporter, Brice Badeaux , documented Calamity activity and released his findings.
He had even successfully photographed a local agent of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force in the process of returning Foundables , causing non-magical news to begin reporting a series of exposés. '
Edward' was serving the Calamity World Centre and notified the Calamity Management Team and the local SOS Task Force, to help the French Ministry.
Capture
Greengrass was later suspected to be a member of The Unforgivable , an organisation suspected of causing the Calamity.
Hermione Granger slipped Greengrass Veritaserum , causing him to say he was in the Unforgivable, so he was taken into custody.
However, confession under Veritaserum did not count in court, so Harry Potter began questioning Greengrass who kept claiming he was innocent.
Constance Pickering found evidence that he was involved in Ron's kidnapping.
In that time, Greengrass had obtained a wand , and used the Imperius Curse to get out.
He took Polyjuice Potion and transformed into 'Edward'.
Hermione and Constance worked out he was going to try and escape, and Harry saw and stopped 'Edward' running away.
He denied being Greengrass until the effect of the Polyjuice Potion ceased.
Greengrass wouldn't divulge the secrets of the Unforgivable until Harry vowed to find a way to save his daughter and open a case into his brother's imprisonment.
He began cooperating, but only to tell Harry about himself and what he had done.
When Harry took an Unbreakable Vow to help Cereus, he led Harry to a journal which contained everything he knew about the Unforgivable and the Calamity.
When Harry began reading the journal, Greengrass was killed due to an Unbreakable Vow he had broken not to tell anyone about the Unforgivable.

title: Eldred Worple
paragraphs: Eldred Worple (fl.
1970 - 1997 ) was a wizard and writer who was once a favourite student of Horace Slughorn .
He studied and lived with vampires , even becoming friends with one named Sanguini , and wrote Blood Brothers: My Life Amongst the Vampires .
Biography
Worple attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in his youth, where he became a favourite student of Professor Horace Slughorn , who made him a member of his elite Slug Club .
On 20 December 1996 , Worple attended a Slug Club Christmas party at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry and brought Sanguini as a guest.
There, Professor Slughorn introduced them to Harry Potter .

Worple tried to convince Harry to let him write his biography citing the money to be made, but Harry who was not fond of fame and already had money, declined, and quickly went to speak to his friend Hermione Granger .
Worple also tried to distract Sanguini from some young women's necks by shoving a pasty in his hand.
Physical appearance
Worple was described as "small, stout, and bespectacled".
Etymology
The name "Eldred" is from an English surname which was derived from EALDRÆD.
The name itself means "Old Advisor".

paragraphs: Helen Elizabeth McCrory ( 17 August 1968 - 16 April 2021 ) was a British actress who portrayed Narcissa Malfoy in the films Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince and Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1 and Part 2 .

McCrory lived with her husband, actor Damian Lewis , and their two children, Manon and Gulliver, in Tufnell Park , London .

title: Harry Potter and the Cursed Child(play)
paragraphs: Harry Potter and the Cursed Child is an original Harry Potter franchise play, authored by J. K. Rowling , John Tiffany , and Jack Thorne .

Despite much assumption to the contrary, J. K. Rowling had insisted that the story of the play was not a prequel to the story of Harry Potter , and eventually revealed that the Cursed Child would follow Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows .
As such, she considers the story of the play to be part of the official Harry Potter canon .
Official summary
It was always difficult being Harry Potter and it isn't much easier now that he is an overworked employee of the Ministry of Magic, a husband and father of three school-age children.
While Harry grapples with a past that refuses to stay where it belongs, his youngest son Albus must struggle with the weight of a family legacy he never wanted.
As past and present fuse ominously, both father and son learn the uncomfortable truth: sometimes, darkness comes from unexpected places.
History
On 23 October 2015 , it was revealed that Harry Potter and the Cursed Child would be the official sequel to Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows as the eighth Harry Potter story of the series.
On 10 February 2016 , it was announced that the script would be published in book form on 31 July 2016 .
On 4 May 2017 , Pottermore announced that the play would be opening on Broadway on 22 April 2018 at the Lyric Theatre .
In 2024, it was expanded to a North America Tour.
It was also expanded to Brazil, in 2025, and the Netherlands, in 2026.
Overview
Creative team

Productions
West End
The original West End production of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child is a play performance based on the script.
It premiered on 30 July 2016 .
The play was shown in two parts.
On 30 March 2017, Pottermore announced that the cast would be changing on 24 May of that year.
The original cast performed for the final time on 21 May 2017.
The West End Run will conclude on 15 February 2026 .
The eighth year ends on 20 September 2026 .
The ninth year starts in October 2026, with the two part show being changed to a 1 part show.

An early review for the play from USA Today reviewer Elysa Gardner was glowingly positive, giving the play 3 1/2 out of 4 stars.
Gardner stated that the "smashing storytelling and layered but accessible emotional life that always fueled Harry's saga" has remained.

Entertainment Weekly also gave the play a strong review, with an overall grade of A-, stating the play is one that "doesn't play it safe with the Potter canon and will change how fans see certain favourite characters forever."

Reviews across the board have generally been very favourable, though most reviews have been kept largely spoiler-free, as attendees are handed badges reading "Keep the Secrets" upon exiting the theatre.
