title: Cassandra Vole's wand
paragraphs: Cassandra Vole 's wand was 10 inches in length, made of holly with a Veela hair core .
Notes and references

title: Discipline at Hogwarts
paragraphs: In Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , the many underage wizards and witches were kept under control by the teachers through the many rules set there.
Any miscreants were usually punished by the teachers or the Ministry of Magic , and the form of punishment depended on the severity of the mischief.
These punishments could also be used in combination as the ones who handed them out saw fit.

During the 1995-1996 school year , when Educational Decree Number Twenty-Five was activated, Dolores Umbridge had the right to override the punishments given by other teachers, and alter them to her own wishes.
Types of discipline
House point deduction
The House point hourglasses , stationed in the Entrance Hall , represented the House points possessed by each house at any time
This was one of the most common forms of punishment in Hogwarts.
Students who performed well in class were awarded points for their house, and the house that had the most points at the end of the school year would be awarded the House Cup .
However, when a student had committed some minor mischief, they would usually lose House points .
As the House Cup competition was a sign of pride for each House, losing points would set them back from winning that pride.
This form of punishment could seem a little unfair, as one student could drag the entire House down with them.
However, this also showed why this form of discipline was so effective - peer pressure to behave.
All teachers, prefects , and the Head Boy and Girl had the authority to dock House points from students.
However, prefects had no authority to dock points from other prefects.
During the reign of the Inquisitorial Squad , the members were given special permission to dock points from anyone they desired, even prefects.
Strict disciplinarians, such as Professor McGonagall, had no qualms about deducting points from their own House, if they believed such action was warranted.
Other teachers, such as Professor Snape, were biased toward their own House.
Detention
This was another common form of punishment at the school.
When a student caused a certain level of mayhem, they were usually given detention.
This punishment was the most varied form, as there were many ways for the students to serve it.
The length of the detention could also be determined by the teacher providing it.

Some detentions could (and sometimes intentionally would) overlap with student events, such as Quidditch matches, Hogsmeade weekend trips , or even dinner, forcing the student to forgo partaking in said events.
Harry Potter served his fair share of detentions during his years at Hogwarts, most of which were administered by either Minerva McGonagall , Severus Snape , or Dolores Umbridge .
Such examples could include doing something dangerous (such as entering the Forbidden Forest to help Rubeus Hagrid ) or doing physical labour and other tasks without magic.
Hagrid believed that simply writing lines was not enough to instil the lesson in the offending student.
A popular form of detention was making wrongdoers polish the school's many ornate candelabra.
Detentions were usually held in a teacher's office, but the Detention Chamber was a known room in Hogwarts that was likely to be used.
The Marauders pointed out a Detention Escape Route in their Marauder's Map .

Severus Snape placed Vincent Crabbe and Gregory Goyle in detention during their sixth year because they failed to do acceptable work the second time around after failing Defence Against the Dark Arts O.W.L.s .

In the same way Horace Slughorn threatened several of his favourite students with detention if they did not complete their homework assignments; Draco Malfoy was given such a punishment by Minerva McGonagall after he failed to hand in his Transfiguration homework twice, which took place on a Saturday, thus depriving him of a chance to visit Hogsmeade (though this actually served to cover up his botched attempt to murder Dumbledore , as McGonagall stood up for him based on the detention).
When Gilderoy Lockhart was a professor, he requested Harry Potter to assist him in answering his fan mail, and considered this to be a treat, preferrable to any other detention he could receive.
Contrary to Lockhart's misguided belief, Harry found the detention to be dull and irritating, his hands aching while having to endure Lockhart's constant bombardment of unsolicited advices to fame.
Indeed, Lockhart's choice of detention was more to show off his fan mail to Harry, because Hagrid had told him that Harry was more famous than him without needing to try.
Snape was known to give harsh and demoralising detentions to students.

This included having Ron clean the Hospital Wing 's bedpans without the use of magic, having the latter and Harry pickle rats' brains in the dungeon, and forcing Neville Longbottom to disembowel a barrelful of horned toads, causing him to almost faint afterwards out of nervousness and sickness.
Harry forced to scar his own hand by Umbridge as detention
When Dolores Umbridge became a professor, she utilised a very cruel method of punishment for her detentions, which was more akin to actual torture.

She forced students to spend hours a day for a week at her office, using a Black Quill to write lines, which caused the words to cut into their hands to draw blood as ink; in time, the student's hand would be scarred with the sentence on the back of their hand.
This detention usually started at 5 pm, so the students did not have much time for dinner, and lasted until over midnight, leaving a lack of time for sleep and homework.
Professor McGonagall considered this a "medieval method" and tried, unsuccessfully, to argue against Umbridge for utilising it.
Being a teacher, Umbridge had the privilege to hand out detentions to her students, no matter how unfair they were, thus Minerva could not circumvent it.

As Umbridge was restrained by the laws of the wizarding world (though the actual legality of her actions at the time is unclear), her punishments paled in comparison to those of the Carrows during Severus Snape 's headmastership following the Fall of the Ministry of Magic .
This included torture and physical punishment, such as the use of the Cruciatus Curse on students, or shackling them to the dungeons.
Prefects may also have been able to place fellow students in detention.
Ron once threatened Seamus Finnigan with this punishment when he questioned Harry's sanity, and the twins Fred and George Weasley once suggested that Hermione might do this to them.
When Harry unintentionally injured Draco with the Sectumsempra curse, Professor Snape gave him detention for every Saturday morning until the end of term.

Professor McGonagall considered detentions of even such magnitude to be a very lenient punishment for such a heinous act (despite Harry's lack of knowledge of the curse's effects beforehand) as Harry could have easily been expelled for bringing harm to another student (in spite of the fact that Draco had attacked first, and was about to use the Cruciatus Curse on Harry).
Confiscation of possessions
Professor McGonagall confiscating Harry's new broom
The caretaker , prefects and teachers could confiscate students' possessions when they were on the list of prohibited objects, or they believed they may be dangerous.
In at least one instance this was done as a punishment.
In Harry's third year , Professor McGonagall confiscated his Firebolt , because she believed that Sirius Black sent it with a jinx or hex to harm him.
She returned it to him intact after stripping it down to search for any jinxes or hexes.
In Harry's fifth year , Dolores Umbridge confiscated brooms as punishment from Harry, Fred Weasley and George Weasley after they attacked (or attempted to attack) Draco Malfoy .
The twins recovered theirs against her will when they quit school; Harry's was returned to him upon Umbridge's departure from Hogwarts .
Removal of privileges
Teachers could sometimes suspend or remove certain privileges of students, such as Quidditch and visits to Hogsmeade .
The Hogwarts librarian could also ban students from the Library .
In Harry's second year , Snape suggested suspending Harry from Quidditch during the opening of the Chamber of Secrets , but Professor McGonagall rejected that.
Three years later, Professor McGonagall threatened Angelina Johnson with the loss of her position as Captain of the team if she shouted loudly again in the Great Hall .
Later that year, when Harry and George Weasley attacked Draco Malfoy for insulting their families, Umbridge stripped them of their privilege to play Quidditch and confiscated their broomsticks .
Fred Weasley also lost his permission because he would have attacked Malfoy too, if Angelina Johnson, Katie Bell, and Alicia Spinnet had not restrained him.
Although Fred and George retrieved their brooms and escaped Hogwarts, Harry was given his privilege and Firebolt back when Umbridge was sacked.

In his third year, Neville Longbottom lost his privilege to go to Hogsmeade when his list of Gryffindor Tower 's passwords was stolen by Crookshanks , which allowed Sirius Black to enter the third year boys' dormitory.
Harry also lost his privilege by Umbridge two years later after his interview with Rita Skeeter about Lord Voldemort 's return.
Both of them regained their privileges at the end of their respective years.
In her sixth year, Ginny Weasley lost her privilege to go to Hogsmeade after reforming Dumbledore's Army .

When, in 2020, Albus Potter and Scorpius Malfoy were found using the "true" Time-Turner illegally in an attempt to prevent Cedric Diggory 's death, which led to disastrous alterations that they just barely managed to fix, Headmistress McGonagall punished the two boys by removing their rights to visit Hogsmeade for the rest of their education at school, along with their Christmas and Easter holidays .
They were also given detentions for the remainder of the school year .
It is also noted that Professor McGonagall considered expelling the culprits, but decided it would be safer for them to stay.
Parent or guardian notification
A Howler, a type of message used by parents to reprimand their children
Serious offences, or perhaps repeat offences, warranted sending a letter to the family of the student in addition to other punishments.

In some cases the reply from the family was a Howler (a red envelope that would burst into flames and spoke its message in a highly-magnified voice of the writer) sent to the offending student, which was especially embarrassing if it arrived in front of other students.

In Harry's and Ron's second year , the Headmaster, Albus Dumbledore , wrote to both their families regarding them operating a flying car that was seen by Muggles , in violation of The International Statute of Secrecy .
While Harry saw this as nothing, since his legal guardians would only be disappointed that he was not killed by the incident, Ron's mother sent him a Howler .

In Neville's third year , his Head of House, Professor McGonagall, wrote to his grandmother after Sirius Black gained admittance to Gryffindor Tower by getting the list of passwords Neville had written on parchment.
Neville's grandmother sent him a Howler.
When Hermione Granger caught Fred and George Weasley testing Fainting Fancies on some first-years, she ordered them to stop it at once and threatened to write to their mother if they did it again.

In stark contrast to before, when the twins had mocked her other threats of punishment, this one actually had a marked effect on the usually laid-back and carefree duo, in that they recoiled in fear and took her threat seriously enough that they did not use first-years as test subjects from then on.
Suspension
To be suspended from school was to be removed from participation in school life for a certain amount of time.
Although this practice was not very usual, some professors, like Severus Snape , frequently suggested that Harry Potter be suspended for reasons that they thought were justified.
Expulsion
Harry receiving a letter claiming that he is expelled, before it was retracted
Expulsion from Hogwarts was the final and worst punishment given to a student.
The rule-breaking they committed was usually severe enough to have injured others.
The student would be removed permanently from school, and the Ministry of Magic would confiscate one's wand and destroy it.
From that point on, the youth in question would be forbidden from practising any more magic.
As they had technically already graduated , many jobs in the wizarding community only listed O.W.L. requirements and hence were employable once they came of age at 17.

however, the expellee in question could, on a case-by-case basis, be deemed responsible enough to learn from their mistakes and still function as law-abiding citizen in wizarding Britain, as were the case with the famed Magizoologist Newt Scamander .
Having been expelled in his sixth year after he had accidentally " endangered another human life with a beast ", he was still permitted to keep his wand and allowed to use magic afterwards.

This luxury was not given to everyone, however, as another student that was later expelled, Jacob , was eligible to have his wand snapped despite being expelled in his final year , when he "admitted" to Ministry officials that he was guilty of pressuring his classmate into reckless experimenting with a dangerous potion that ended up killing him.
There were other reasons for expulsion.

Under the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy and Decree for the Reasonable Restriction of Underage Sorcery , for underage wizards and witches , if they performed magic outside of school, especially in front of Muggles , they were given one warning letter.
A second offence may result in a disciplinary hearing or expulsion.

There were exceptions, though: if the situation was serious enough to threaten the student in question or anyone within the vicinity, or if granted permission by a high-authority figure, he or she had permission to perform magic.

The Ministry did not have the authority to punish students for misdemeanours within school unless it directly transgressed any Educational Decrees , nor could it expel any students and confiscate wands unless charges were successfully proven.

Under the tenure of Professor Dolores Umbridge as High Inquisitor , Educational Decrees Number Twenty-Four and Twenty-Seven were passed, which would lead to students being expelled if they dared start an unauthorised organisation or carry The Quibbler inside school, respectively.
Sebastian Sallow was potentially expelled for the murder of his uncle, Solomon Sallow , in the 1890-1891 school year .
It was up to his friend whether they wanted to turn Sebastian in or not.
Tom Riddle falsely framing Hagrid, which led to his expulsion
Rubeus Hagrid was expelled, in his third year, after being falsely accused by Tom Riddle of owning Aragog , the "monster" that resulted in the death of Myrtle Warren .
However, Tom Riddle was the true owner of the monster, the Serpent of Slytherin .
Over fifty years later, his name was cleared by Harry Potter , Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger , who uncovered the whole truth about the Chamber of Secrets .
However, his access to the privileges of practising magic and receiving magical education were not restored.
Harry Potter was many times close to being expelled, mainly by Professors Severus Snape and Dolores Umbridge .
However, thanks to quick thinking and help from fairer teachers, he was saved from these situations.

Once, when Harry produced a Patronus out of school, to save his life and that of his cousin, Dudley Dursley , from a pair of Dementors sent by Umbridge, Harry received an expulsion notice for performing underage magic , and in front of a Muggle, stating that his wand would be confiscated and destroyed.
However, this expulsion was later retracted and changed to a disciplinary hearing , at which Harry was found not guilty.

In 1996, Harry came within an ace of being expelled for forming Dumbledore's Army without the High Inquisitor's permission, in violation of Educational Decree Number Twenty-Four; Dumbledore used the group's name to take credit for its founding, thus saving Harry from expulsion.

When Harry critically injured Draco Malfoy with the Sectumsempra curse, it was actually enough to have him expelled, as Professor Minerva McGonagall stated Harry was lucky not to have been, due to Snape giving lenience to prevent others from finding out that he was the one who invented the curse.

Severus Snape once claimed to Bellatrix Lestrange that he had done his utmost to have Harry thrown out of Hogwarts, " where [Snape] believe [d] he scarcely belong [ed]", though to what degree this was actually true is uncertain, given his secret loyalty to Albus Dumbledore .
Draco Malfoy once risked his own expulsion when he made a botched attempt at killing Dumbledore , in which he inflicted a severe injury upon Katie Bell instead.
Snape warned him he was already suspected of being responsible for the incident, and only lack of evidence saved him from expulsion.
Later however, Dumbledore confirmed that he allowed Draco to remain at Hogwarts to keep him safe from Lord Voldemort's wrath, despite knowing he nearly killed both Katie and Ron Weasley .
Draco was allowed to remain a student at Hogwarts partly because neither Ronald nor Katie suffered any lasting injury.
Other forms of discipline
Corporal punishment

Corporal punishment had been in place since the school's founding, and given the existence of a disused torture room in the ramparts at Hogwarts Castle , and taking into account that the Hospital Wing could comfortably deal with the most severe physical injuries, it was heavily implied that the discipline at the school were harshly disciplinarian throughout most of its history, and used severe physical punishments to both correct and deter rule-breakers.

As Argus Filch stated that it was " a pity they let the old punishments die out ", however, such as hanging students from their thumbs and/or wrists for days on end and severely whipping them, yet Arthur Weasley , whom then-caretaker Apollyon Pringle gave a less severe (but still brutal) caning, a then more conventionally acceptable form of corporal punishment, it was further implied that the severity of such punishments gradually died down over time, despite having continued well into the 20th century , during the tenure of Armando Dippet as Head of the school, gradually decreased.

In his first year, after he had made unauthorised use of a broomstick to retrieve Neville's Remembrall , Harry feared that Professor McGonagall would use a cane to discipline him, due to his confusion about the surname of Gryffindor Quidditch captain, Oliver Wood .

While Albus Dumbledore was headmaster, however, inflicting pain on students was strictly prohibited, with the then Deputy Headmistress and Head of Gryffindor House, Minerva McGonagall , viewing it as a barbaric and outdated way to handle unruly students, and more than once reminded fellow teachers about the prescribed disciplinary practices of the day.

Upon seeing Dolores Umbridge shake Marietta Edgecombe very hard, Dumbledore was visibly angry and magically forced Umbridge to release her saying, " I cannot allow you to manhandle my students, Dolores. "
Immediately thereafter, Fudge threatened him with arrest, forcing him to depart his office (and likely the school) temporarily.
Previously, some of Umbridge's detentions had students write lines with a blood quill that cut the back of their own hand and used their blood as ink.
Upon discovering Harry was being subjected to this, Ron said, "Go to McGonagall, say something!"
but Harry did not.
Lee Jordan also experienced the blood quill after angering Umbridge.

In 1996 , despite being a Ministry-appointed Headmistress, Umbridge might still have not been authorised to inflict pain as a punishment, perhaps due to rules set down by the Hogwarts Board of Governors , which could only be overridden by the Ministry's educational decrees.

Filch said to Harry, " You filthy little beasts would never have dropped Stink Pellets if you'd known I had it in my power to whip you raw,... if I could've strung you up by the ankles in my office, would they?
But when Educational Decree Number Twenty-Nine comes in,... I'll be allowed to do them things... "
Soon thereafter, Argus Filch was seen entering Umbridge's office to get forms to allow him to administer whipping as a punishment.
Filch attempted to administer this punishment on Fred and George Weasley, but they flew away before he could do so.

He later prowled the corridors of the school with his whip in hand, but there were so many miscreants that he did not know which way to turn, so it is uncertain if he was able to ever administer this punishment.
Educational Decree Number Twenty-Nine would have possibly allowed even more gruesome punishments, but it was never actually passed.
Upon Umbridge's removal and Dumbledore's return, these punishments or threats of punishments ceased.

During the Death Eaters ' takeover of the school in the 1997-1998 school year , the Cruciatus Curse was used on students placed in detention and other severe forms of punishment were used, mainly by Amycus and Alecto Carrow , who were placed in charge of all discipline; their cruelty made Umbridge look tame.
Transfiguration

Bartemius Crouch Junior , impersonating Alastor Moody , once transfigured Draco Malfoy into a ferret , though the transfiguration was quickly undone by Minerva McGonagall , who warned him that " we never use Transfiguration as a punishment. "
Disciplinary authority
Discipline at Hogwarts was enforced by a variety of people.
Depending on their position within the hierarchy, they could hand out different kinds of punishment.

The Ministry of Magic had no right to punish students for their wrongdoings in school, nor did they have the right to expel students and confiscate wands unless charges had been successfully validated and the student accused of them convicted.
It is unknown what, if any, disciplinary authority the Board of Governors or its members had.
Notes and references

title: Evanesce
paragraphs: Evanesce was the incantation for a transfiguration spell that vanished objects.
Etymology
Evanesce in English means "to disappear into vapour"; in Latin , it is a conjugated form of evanesco , meaning "I vanish".
Notes and references

title: Warrington sisters' grandmother
paragraphs: This witch was the maternal grandmother of Ivy and Winifred Warrington .
Biography
When her granddaughters were growing up, Winifred accidentally vanished herself.
In an effort to help Ivy forget what happened, she put a Memory Charm on her.
Unfortunately, it caused Ivy to wholly forget about Winifred.
Ivy eventually discovered the truth a year later and her grandmother regrettably confessed what had happened.
Physical description
By the late 2000s , she was an elderly witch with grey hair , purple eyes and a large hooked nose, who wore elegant purple robes and a traditional purple pointed hat .
Personality and traits
She was a caring, loving woman who couldn't bear to see those she loved in pain, but she believed she knew better than others, and sometimes couldn't hide her comtempt.
Magical abilities and skills
Behind the scene
Concept art
Notes and references

title: Flask-conjuring spell
paragraphs: This unidentified spell ( incantation unknown ) conjured a glass flask out of thin air.
On 1 May , 1998 , Hermione Granger used this spell to collect the memories of a dying Severus Snape .
History
Creation
On the night of 1 May , 1998 at approximately eleven o'clock, Harry Potter , Ronald Weasley and Hermione Granger met Professor Severus Snape in the Shrieking Shack .
The latter had been sliced apart by Tom Riddle 's snake Nagini .
He was quickly dying , and urged Harry to take the memories that flew from him as his life drained away.
Hermione , her hands shaking slightly, conjured this flask to capture the memories in.
Use and post-use
Harry took the flask with trembling hands and carefully retrieved his late Professor 's memories at the latter's urging.
When the last of Snape 's life had left him, Harry returned to the castle where he viewed Snape's memories in Albus Dumbledore's Pensieve .
It is unknown what happened to the flask; it presumably ceased to exist as all conjured objects tend to over time.
Notes and references

title: Human Transfiguration
paragraphs: Human Transfiguration was a sub-branch of Transfiguration and a form of transformation in which one transfigured human body parts or an entire human being into another form.

Human Transfiguration was more difficult and dangerous than any other form of Transfiguration, including Cross-Species Transfiguration and was therefore N.E.W.T. -level, taught only to sixth-years and above at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
The malicious casting of a human Transfiguration spell was a highly serious matter, and would result in severe punishment from Hogwarts if an individual was caught.
Students of Uagadou School of Magic were especially skilled in human Transfiguration.
Nature
Horace Slughorn disguised by the use of Human Transfiguration

Human Transfiguration could be used to essentially replicate the natural abilities of Metamorphmagi , allowing the practitioner or the subject to take on an entirely different form or make various individual changes to their appearance, such as growing or changing the colour, style or pattern of one's hair or taking on individual animal body parts.

However, while human Transfiguration could presumably be performed by any wizard who was skilled enough, on themselves as well as on others, a Metamorphmagus was born with the ability to make such changes to their own bodies with little to no effort and without the use of a wand.

Although it was possible to transfigure humans into inanimate objects, it is unknown how someone who had himself transfigured into an object would be able to untransfigure without the intervention of another witch or wizard .
Emeric Switch contributed an article on the scientific aspects of human Transfiguration to a 1926 issue of Transfiguration Today .
Dangers
It had been stated many times that human Transfiguration could go badly wrong when performed poorly.
The user had the risk of getting stuck in their transfigured state.
Another matter that complicated human Transfiguration was the reversing of the changes.

Although it was possible for a different witch or wizard to reverse the changes using Reparifarge , this was best done carefully as even a small mistake could permanently damage the transfigured individual.
This effect was compounded when the transfiguration was badly cast.
The best way to undo a human transfiguration was to have the original caster perform the spell.
Known instances
Prior to 1991
After 1998
Known practitioners
Notes and references

title: Crinus Muto
paragraphs: Crinus Muto was the incantation of a transfiguration spell that could be used to transform the colour and style of the caster's hair .
History
During the 1987-1988 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , before Jacob's sibling 's first date, Andre Egwu possibly used a variation of this spell on them to grow facial hair.
In December 1996 , sixth-year students in Transfiguration class at Hogwarts practised this spell.
Known practitioners
Etymology
From crinis , the Latin word for "hair", and muto , which means "to change".
Notes and references

title: Untransfiguration
paragraphs: Untransfiguration was a branch of Transfiguration magic and a type of counter-spell , which involved returning something to its proper form, reversing the effects of a Transfiguration.
Untransfiguration was covered in beginner-level spellbooks such as A Beginner's Guide to Transfiguration .
Learning Untransfiguration was mandatory at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry from 1926 onward.
Failure to at least attempt to Untransfigure a wrongly-done Transfiguration was considered irresponsible.
Methods
Professor McGonagall Untransfiguring Draco Malfoy in 1994
Reparifarge was a general Untransfigurative spell used to counter the effects of a Transformation spell that was poorly performed and only partially Transfigured the object in question.
The spell was located in A Beginner's Guide to Transfiguration by Emeric Switch .

However, like all things involving Human Transfiguration , simply using Reparifarge could do more harm than good, and so in cases of total human transfigurations needing reversing, the solution was often more complicated.
There existed a spell which could change Animagi wizards and witches back into their human form from their animal form.
The Revelio Charm could be used to Untransfigure a Transfigured human.
Aurors working for the British Ministry of Magic often had to Untransfigure transformed objects in their line of work.
Known instances

During the 1890-1891 school year , fifth-year students were taught a transformation spell which an unidentified student was able to use against Animagus poachers in order to revert them into their original form, even in the midst of a battle.

In the aftermath of the arrest of Percival Graves in the New York subway in 1926 , Newton Scamander used the Revelio Charm to reveal that it was actually the Dark wizard Gellert Grindelwald , who had used Human Transfiguration to take the appearance of the MACUSA official.
In Harry Potter 's first Transfiguration class in 1991 , Professor Minerva McGonagall Transfigured her desk into a pig , and the pig back to a desk .
In 1994 , Remus Lupin and Sirius Black changed Peter Pettigrew from a rat back into his usual human appearance, during the Encounter at the Shrieking Shack .

At the start of the 1994-1995 school year at Hogwarts, when the new Defence Against the Dark Arts professor Barty Crouch Jnr ( disguised as Alastor Moody ) Transfigured Draco Malfoy into a ferret on the Marble Staircase , Minerva McGonagall Transfigured him back into a human.

In 1996 , Albus Dumbledore had to Untransfigure Horace Slughorn after Slughorn had transformed himself into an armchair, whilst he was hiding in a Muggle house in Budleigh Babberton from the Death Eaters .
Known practitioners
Notes and references

title: Emeric Switch
paragraphs: Professor Emeric Switch was a wizard , author and expert on Transfiguration .
Biography
Switch was the author of A Beginner's Guide to Transfiguration .
This book was a required textbook for first-year and second-year Transfiguration classes at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
He also contributed an article on the scientific aspects of Human Transfiguration to Transfiguration Today in 1926 .
A portrait of him hung at Hogwarts Castle .
Magical abilities and skills
Etymology
Emeric is a variant of Emmerich , which means "whole, universal".
This could relate to him being able to do transfiguration, as he can wholly turn something into something universally else.
To switch is to exchange one thing with another; could be extended to transfiguration, changing one form into another.
Notes and references

title: Transfiguration Today
paragraphs: Transfiguration Today was a scholarly journal focusing on the latest news on developments in the magical field of Transfiguration .
It published articles as well as papers submitted by prominent and knowledgeable figures in the subject.
The magazine was also known for awarding the Transfiguration Today Most Promising Newcomer award to accomplished Hogwarts School students who extraordinarily excelled in Transfiguration .
History
During his student years at Hogwarts School in the 1890s , Albus Dumbledore wrote some papers to the magazine, at least one of which on Trans-Species Transformation .
Bathilda Bagshot was favourably impressed with the paper, leading to her acquaintance with him and the Dumbledore family .
Around 30 years later, Dumbledore was a contributing columnist by 29 November , 1926 , being " enraptured " at the honour.
In her student years, Minerva McGonagall was awarded with the Transfiguration Today Most Promising Newcomer award .
In her adult years, McGonagall became Transfiguration teacher at Hogwarts School , and, in her spare time, she made a scientific revision of the articles in the magazine.
Porpentina and Queenie Goldstein owned a copy of this periodical.
Almost a century later, in 1991 , Dumbledore was still an attentive reader of this periodical.
Minerva McGonagall also kept at least one issue in her office .
In December 1992 , the magazine ran an advertisement on the Daily Prophet , which included a coupon entitling the bearer to a free Muggle Guard .

In the summer of 1993 , during Harry Potter 's stay at the Leaky Cauldron in London , he noticed some venerable-looking wizards arguing over the latest article in Transfiguration Today over breakfast.
Known editions
Notes and references

title: Reparifarge
paragraphs: Reparifarge was the incantation of an untransfiguration spell.
It appeared to be a general spell used to counter the effects of a Transformation spell that was poorly performed and only partially Transfigured the object in question.

This spell was covered in A Beginner's Guide to Transfiguration , which stressed the importance of at least attempting this spell when necessary, as the products of incomplete Transfigurations could be dangerous.
History
Minerva McGonagall reversing a badly done Felifors Spell with Reparifarge
This spell was covered in second-year Transfiguration classes at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry during the 1985-1986 school year .
After retrieving a Black Quill from another House common room , Jacob's sibling used this spell to Untransfigure it, which turned out to be a roll of parchment with more instructions.

During the 1986-1987 school year , as Rowan Khanna and Jacob's sibling helped Rubeus Hagrid finding Fang in the Transfiguration Classroom , Jacob's sibling was inspired by Rowan's line of thought, and wondered if someone had Transfigured Fang into a cauldron , therefore casting Reparifarge on a nearby cauldron, which turned out to not be Fang, but a cat.

After helping out Madam Rosmerta by serving at the Three Broomsticks Inn and retrieving ingredients for Rosmerta's special concoction of Butterbeer , so the landlady could take to time to search for a Black Quill Jacob had left behind, Madam Rosmerta kept her word and gave the object to Jacob's sibling, who Untransfigure it, revealing it to be Jacob's notebook , which Madam Rosmerta had mentioned seeing him scribbling in.
The notebook was then unfortunately immediately confiscated by Argus Filch .
During the hunt for Chocolate Frog Cards at Hogwarts that same year, Jacob's sibling, Penny Haywood , and Andre Egwu came across a card in the Transfiguration classroom .
However, after noticing several errors on the card, they realised that Merula Snyde had transfigured an object into a card to fool Jacob's sibling's team.
Jacob's sibling reversed the card's transfiguration with Reparifarge , turning the card back into a frog .
During the 1989-1990 school year , Jacob's sibling used it to revert a transfigured black quill into a letter written to them by their brother in the Boathouse .
Also during this year, Jacob's sibling used the spell to revert a bag of Thunderbird tail feathers disguised as leaves by Todd Cribb in the Forest Lake .
During the 1990-1991 school year , Jacob's sibling used it to revert a transfigured black quill into a hand mirror in the Forest Grove .
In the 2010s on 4 October , a student asked Professor Minerva McGonagall to help them with their Untransfiguration , as they were unable to revert a cauldron back to its previous form.

Before she could show them how to cast Reparifarge , the student asked her if she always wanted to be a teacher, so she told them about how she wanted to be a professional Quidditch player and about her time at the Ministry of Magic before becoming a Hogwarts professor.
She then proceeded to cast the spell and revealed a birthday cake, with other students in the classroom joining to congratulate Professor McGonagall on her birthday.
She mentioned that they reminded her of Harry Potter and his friends and that watching them all together brought back memories of old friends of hers.
She then went out on a walk to think of them for a while.
Etymology
The incantation comes from the Latin word reparo meaning "to renew" or "repair", plus the suffix - farge (or fors ) which means "shape".
Notes and references

title: Circe
paragraphs: Circe , or Circe of Aeaea , was a witch who lived in ancient Greece , on the island of Aeaea , and enjoyed transfiguring lost sailors into animals .
She was immortalised on a Chocolate Frog Card .
Biography
Legacy
Circe was featured on a Chocolate Frog Card .
Harry Potter obtained this card from a Chocolate Frog on his first trip to Hogwarts in 1991 .
There was a portrait of Circe at Hogwarts Castle , guarding a secret shortcut between the fourth-floor landing of the Grand Staircase and the Entrance Hall side room.
The password required to gain access to said shortcut was Piggywiggy .
Magical abilities and skills
Notes and references

title: Mirabella Plunkett
paragraphs: Mirabella Plunkett (b. 1839 ) was a British witch famous for falling in love with a merman in Loch Lomond while on holiday.
After her parents forbade her to marry him, she transfigured herself into a haddock and was never seen again.
She was featured on a Chocolate Frog Card and on a portrait hung at Hogwarts Castle .
Biography
Early life
Mirabella Plunkett was born in 1839 to Mr and Mrs Plunkett .
Finding love
At some point in her life, Mirabella travelled to Loch Lomond on holiday, where she met and fell in love with a merman .
Mirabella and the merman decided to marry .
However, Mirabella's parents objected strongly, and forbade her to marry him.
In response, Mirabella transfigured herself into a haddock , never to be seen again.
It is unknown if she ever returned to her merman lover once she became a haddock.
Legacy
After her disappearance, Mirabella was not forgotten.
She was eventually immortalised on a Chocolate Frog Card .
There was also a portrait of her hung at Hogwarts Castle , which guarded a secret shortcut between the first-floor landing of the Grand Staircase and the Entrance Hall side room.
The password required to gain access to said shortcut was haddock .
Magical abilities and skills
Etymology
The name "Mirabella" is derived from Latin mirabilis, "wonderful".
Notes and references

title: Thaddeus Thurkell
paragraphs: Thaddeus Thurkell ( 1632 - 1692 ) was a wizard who fathered seven sons who were all Squibs .
He transfigured them into hedgehogs out of disgust.
The birth of a single Squib to a magical parent was known to be a rare event.
This would seem to indicate that the case of the Thurkell family was quite exceptional, especially as it merited mention on a Chocolate Frog Card .
Magical abilities and skills
Etymology
The name "Thaddeus" comes from Θαδδαιος (Thaddaios), the Greek form of the Aramaic name Thaddai.
It is possibly derived from a word, meaning "heart", but it may in fact be an Aramaic form of a Greek name such as Theodoros.
Notes and references

title: Todd Cribb
paragraphs: Todd Cribb was a wizard who used the alias Prospero , after the character of the same name from the William Shakespeare play The Tempest .
Biography
Early life
He attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in his youth, holding fond memories of it despite his criminal ways.
It was during his Hogwarts days that he met Corrine Cribb , and the two fell in love.
During their time at Hogwarts, the pair discovered a hidden location within the Forbidden Forest and would sneak out from school to meet there.
At some point, he married Corrine, and the pair started to engage in illegal enterprises.
He regarded her as his "dear wife" and feared displeasing her.
Adulthood

During this year, Todd and Corrine Cribb tried to kidnap Fang from Rubeus Hagrid as revenge for Hagrid stopping their poaching activities, however they were unable determine which pets belonged to Hagrid, so kidnapped all pets in the vicinity .
The Cribbs did this under an Invisibility Cloak so they wouldn't be followed, but they were able to be followed by the trail of birdseed , tung oil , and Demiguise hair that they left.
Jacob's sibling and Merula Snyde confronted the pair and defeated them in a duel, after which they Disapparated to an unknown location.
Todd Cribb conjuring a storm at the Forest Lake

During the 1989-1990 school year , Cribb travelled to the Forest Lake in the Forbidden Forest , where he provoked a Thunderbird high in the sky with Metelojinx , creating storms which caused its tail feathers to fall.
He intended to use the tail feathers to make counterfeit Shikoba Wolfe wands and make a good fortune from them.

However, Jacob's sibling and the MACUSA employee Holly Blackbird confronted him at the lake in the midst of him conjuring storms, where he reacted angrily towards them and demanded they refer to him "Prospero" and grovel before them.
He challenged the both of them to a duel , and Jacob's sibling had to face him, as Holly's wand stopped working properly in the presence of Thunderbird tail feathers.
Jacob's sibling defeated him, and he attempted to run away, but was stopped by Rubeus Hagrid .
Upon interrogation by Jacob's sibling, he revealed his true identity and wife and his intention with the tail feathers.
Jacob's sibling also exposed his bag of tail feathers disguised as leaves with Reparifarge , which reverted them to their true form.
Afterwards, he was handed over to the authorities.
After being handed over to the British Ministry of Magic by Blackbird, they punished him by making him use his weather magic to water the Ministry's gardens for some time.
After this encounter, he returned to Hogwarts to exact revenge on Jacob's sibling , and to steal the blood from their Salamanders .

When he attempted to freeze them, Barnaby Lee and Rubeus Hagrid at the Great Lake during their Salamander bonfire , his spell backfired, leaving him frozen in thick ice, as his broken wand was improperly repaired with Spellotape .
It was afterwards their decision to leave him frozen, make him leave, or allow him to join their bonfire.
Things between Todd and Corrine eventually began to get rocky, and Todd wanted a special surprise for their anniversary.
He stole various objects from the shopkeepers of Hogsmeade and Diagon Alley , such as wine and butterbeer , in order to surprise her.
However, he was so focused on this that he didn't speak to his wife for days, causing her to resent him.
He was discovered by Jacob's sibling, who had been given a map by Corrine.
After attempting to flee, he gave up and confessed everything, returning the items.
He and Corrine were possibly invited to the celebration of Fawkes by Jacobs' sibling, but were also possibly turned over to the Ministry.
Todd got the idea to disguise himself as a vampire called 'The Count' and steal from the people of Hogsmeade .

During Hallowe'en that year, he used his weather-making skills to cast a thick fog around the townsfolk, and used the Confundus Charm to manipulate people into being his thralls and give him their valuables, then used the Memory Charm to make them forget.
He successfully managed to steal lots of valuables, but was caught by Jacob's sibling and Merula Snyde who were trying to find a real vampire.
He duelled Jacob's sibling, but lost when he tried to surprise Jacob's sibling with physical violence and the latter hit him with the Full Body-Bind Curse .
He was then turned in to Albus Dumbledore , who dealt with him.
Unbeknownst to him, he was also being hunted by a real, unidentified vampire who eventually decided to let Jacob's sibling deal with him.
Physical description
Cribb had long black hair , moustache and goatee, grey eyes and light skin.
He wore long blue robes adorned with celestial imagery.
Personality and traits
Cribb seemed to be an arrogant wizard , given how he identified with an alias to make himself seem more fearsome to others, as he thought that his real name was unimpressive.
According to Holly Blackbird , Todd was not an inherently bad person, only one who was eager to impress his wife .
Magical abilities and skills
Possessions
Todd's wand
Notes and references

title: Demetrius Prod
paragraphs: Demetrius J. Prod (d. 27 November 1998 ) was a English wizard who lived in Didsbury , England in late 1992 .
He died on 27 November 1998 after an argument with his wife, Elsie , over the washing-up.
His obituary in the Daily Prophet mentioned that he died "noisily".
Biography
Little is known of Demetrius' early life; he was trained (albeit not well) in the magical arts and could perform weak enchantments .
Sometime in his life, he met Elsie ; the two would later marry, although they did not get along very well.

Sometime prior to January 1992 , Demetrius wrote to Kwikspell Company , and a month thereafter managed to turn Elsie into a yak ; he wrote an advertisement for the Kwikspell Company, proud of this feat.
Harry Potter and Argus Filch would later read about this.
On the eve of 27 November 1998 after supper, Demetrius and Elsie got into an argument over the washing-up.
He died that night, and was described by the Daily Prophet to have died "noisily".
Magical abilities and skills
Relationships
Elsie Prod
Demetrius and his wife didn't seem to get along too well; she sneered at his feeble charms , and he once turned her into a yak .
They frequently argued, and it was during one argument over the washing-up that Demetrius met his death.
Etymology
The name "Demetrius" is the Latinised form of the Greek name Δημήτριος (Demetrios), which was derived from the name of the Greek goddess Demeter.
Kings of Macedon and the Seleucid kingdom have had this name.
This was also the name of several early saints, including a Saint Demetrius who was martyred in the 4th century.
Notes and references

title: McClivert clan
paragraphs: The MacClivert clan was a wizarding family led by Dugald McClivert .
History
They lived on the Isle of Drear , and were engaged in a feud with their neighbours, the MacBoon clan .
According to legend, after Dugald was killed by Quintius MacBoon in a drunken duel, the clan attacked the MacBoons and Transfigured the entire family into Quintapeds .
Realising too late that they had now made the MacBoons more dangerous than ever, the entire McClivert clan was wiped out by the carnivorous beasts.
Whether or not the legend was true is unclear.
Notes and references

title: Lapifors Spell
paragraphs: The Lapifors Spell ( Lapifors ) was a transforming spell that could be used to transform the target into a rabbit ; it worked best on smaller targets such as statues , salamanders or cats .
The spell could be viewed as a jinx when used to transform creatures into rabbits .
History
This spell was learned in third-year Transfiguration class at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , taught by Professor Minerva McGonagall .
This spell was covered in third-year exams at the end of the school year.
Effects
Once performed, the caster had an option to control the rabbit in question, directing its movements.
Known practitioners
Etymology
From Latin " lepus ", meaning " hare ", with the -fors suffix attached as with most transforming spells.
Alternatively, Lapi- could be derived from Latin Lapis , meaning "stone", in reference to the statues Lapifors can transform.
Notes and references

title: Rabbit
paragraphs: A rabbit , also colloquially known as a bunny , is a small mammal in the family Leporidae of the order Lagomorpha, found in several parts of the world.
Rabbits, if needed to be dispatched by magic , were particularly vulnerable to Vermillious , as well as the Fire-Making Spell .
Overview
Babbitty Rabbity in Babbitty Rabbitty and her Cackling Stump
The Lapifors Spell could be used to transform small objects and creatures into rabbits.
It was taught to third year students in Transfiguration class at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
If conjuration was not performed correctly, mistakes such as Frog-Rabbit hybrids could occur, explainable by the Principle of Artificianimate Quasi-Dominance .
The rabbit was a possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm , including the Wild Rabbit .
Helen Thistlewood had her Patronus assume rabbit form.
The fictitious Babbitty Rabbity in Babbitty Rabbitty and her Cackling Stump from The Tales of Beedle the Bard was a witch and Animagus who could transform into a Rabbit at will.
History
The Fat Friar was executed by senior churchmen, in part because they were suspicious of his habit of pulling rabbits out of the communion cup, sometime during the Middle Ages .

Shortly after the disappearance of French sorceress Lisette de Lapin in 1422 , a large white rabbit was seen crossing the English Channel in a cauldron with a sail fitted to it, and a similar rabbit later became a trusted advisor at the court of King Henry VI .
Although it was never proven, it was likely that Lisette had been an Animagus and slipped through the bars of her prison cell window the night before her execution.
One of the rabbits on Hogwarts ground

In a 1913 Defence Against the Dark Arts lesson on the Boggart at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , an unidentified student used the Boggart-Banishing Spell to turn the Boggart taking the form of a vampire Boggart into a buck-toothed rabbit.

In the 1930s , a young Tom Riddle , killed the pet rabbit of another boy, Billy Stubbs , after Stubbs had insulted him, and hung it from the rafters of the building of Wool's Orphanage where they lived.
James Potter sometimes referred to Remus Lupin 's condition of being a werewolf as his "furry little problem."
Because of this, many came to believe that Lupin was the owner of a rather badly behaved rabbit.

When Harry Potter first witnessed the Sorting Hat during the Sorting Ceremony on 1 September 1991 when he first came to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Harry thought that his and the other new students' task might be to pull a rabbit out of it, thinking of the Muggle magic trick.
The Keeper of Keys and Grounds of Hogwarts Rubeus Hagrid sometimes wore gloves made of rabbit fur.
In the 1991-1992 school year , Harry Potter 's Transfiguration class turned a lit candle into a Purple Rabbit , which escaped from class and around in the Hogwarts Castle .
Harry was entrusted by Professor McGonagall to capture it.
He was awarded 25 House points for this.
Harry struggling with casting Rabbit Slippers

In 1992 , after being bitten while trying to help Hagrid care for the Norwegian Ridgeback dragon Norbert , Ron Weasley proclaimed "I tell you, that dragon's the most horrible animal I've ever met, but the way Hagrid goes on about it, you'd think it was a fluffy little bunny rabbit."
In 1993 , Harry Potter's Transfiguration class had to transform rabbits into Rabbit Slippers , given to Professor McGonagall.
Harry and Ron Weasley had problems with this spell .

In August 1993, Harry Potter, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger came across a Transforming rabbit , a peculiar creature capable of turning itself into a top hat and back, in the Magical Menagerie in Diagon Alley .
Lavender Brown owned a male rabbit called Binky as a pet.
Sometime in late 1993, he was killed by a fox , which devastated her.
The exterior of Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes in Diagon Alley depicted a rabbit underneath a top hat lifted and lowered repeatedly on the head of one of the proprietors .
In 1996 Fred and George Weasley ran a product called Repeating Rabbit in their shop Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes in Diagon Alley .
Known rabbits
Notes and references

title: Statues
paragraphs: For all known statues, including individuals who had statues made in their likenesses.

title: -fors suffix
paragraphs: The -fors suffix was a modifier added to certain Latin words to create the incantations for individual transfiguration spells .
Transfiguration spells using the -fors suffix
Etymology

" -fors " is most likely from Latin " forma ", meaning " shape ", " figure ", or " appearance ", although there is another Latin word, " fors ", meaning " fortune " or " luck ", which may be a hint towards the difficulty of transfiguration and the luck needed to perform it correctly.
Notes and references

title: Frog-Rabbit
paragraphs: Frog-Rabbit was the name given to the result of a half- frog , half- rabbit mutant hybrid creature created by magical means.
It could be a by-product of incorrectly-performed Conjuring Spells , a fact explained by the Principle of Artificianimate Quasi-Dominance .
Notes and references

title: Draconifors Spell
paragraphs: The Draconifors Spell ( Draconifors ) was a transfiguration spell used to transform objects into small dragons .
History
This spell was taught in third-year Transfiguration class by Professor Minerva McGonagall , during the 1993-1994 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
Hermione Granger easily mastered how to cast this spell in class.
There was also a spellbook which contained information on the casting of this spell.
Effects
The Draconifors Spell transformed the target into a dragon .
However, it was only a very small transfigured dragon, around the size of an infant, significantly limiting its potential for violence and breathing fire .
Known practitioners
Etymology
From Latin " draco ", meaning " dragon ", with the -fors suffix attached.
Notes and references

title: Draconiforsspellbook
paragraphs: The Draconifors spellbook was a book containing information and instructions on the Draconifors Transfiguration spell .
History
One copy was owned by Cuthbert Binns , and he kept it, like his other books , in Classroom 4F , where he taught History of Magic , though in a locked side-room.
Notes and references

title: Model dragon
paragraphs: Model dragons were magical , realistic models of various types of dragons such as; Hungarian Horntails , Chinese Fireballs , Swedish Short-Snouts , and Common Welsh Greens .
Uses
A model dragon
These models had various usages, such as roasting chestnuts and presumably other foods.
Most notably, they were used by the Triwizard Tournament champions who each drew small model dragons out of a silk bag prior to the first task .
The type of model indicated which dragon they had to face.
A long time after the second task, the miniature figurine of Viktor Krum was seen trying to fight Harry Potter 's dragon model at the Gryffindor Boys' Dormitory .
In Diagon Alley in August 1996 , there was a dragon model in the roast chestnuts sale machine.
In the 2010s , dragonologist Long Shouren would gift Professor Rubeus Hagrid model dragons every time he visited, one of them being of a Portuguese Long-Snout .
Notes and references

title: Snufflifors Spell
paragraphs: The Snufflifors Spell ( Snufflifors ) was a transforming spell used to turn objects into mice , with flying books being particularly vulnerable to this spell .
History

In the 1993-1994 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Hermione Granger learnt this spell from a spellbook , which she had bought from Fred and George Weasley in their shop on the sixth floor of Hogwarts Castle .
Known practitioners
Etymology
From English " snuffle ", probably compared to sniffling mouse, with the -fors suffix attached.
Notes and references

title: Flying book
paragraphs: A flying book was any book that had been bewitched to fly , as well as to attack and bite anyone nearby.
Some of them might throw projectiles.
Description
Several flying books were found in the Hogwarts Library , particularly the Restricted Section .
There were multiple ways to defend against a flying book.
They could be stunned using a Knockback Jinx , burned with a Fire-Making Spell or transfigured into a mouse using the Snufflifors Spell .
History
The Hogwarts Library had a number of copies by September 1991 .
More books were imported from the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1993 in large wooden crates that were held in a freight compartment of the train.
They were then moved into the Glanmore Peakes' Corridor .
Notes and references

title: Snuffliforsspellbook
paragraphs: The Snufflifors Spellbook was a book containing information and instructions on the casting of the Snufflifors Spell , a transforming spell used to transform objects into mice .
History

It was owned by Fred and George Weasley , and sold at their "shop" in the disused sixth floor bathroom to Hermione Granger during the 1993-1994 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
Notes and references

title: Disused sixth-floor bathroom
paragraphs: This disused bathroom was located on the sixth floor of Hogwarts Castle .
History
Early history
The bathroom was found in Glanmore Peakes' Corridor .
At some point, the bathroom fell into disuse and was no longer used.
However, two Chocolate Frog Cards were found in the toilets and a number of school robes remained on a coat peg by a bookshelf.
One of the toilets was broken and another was covered in a pool of water .
Items and products
The items sold in the bathroom included:
Notes and references

title: Ducklifors
paragraphs: Ducklifors was the incantation of a transfiguration jinx that transformed an organism into a duck .
Fourth-years and above were able to cast the spell , meaning it was likely taught in Transfiguration class during or before the fourth year.
Casting and effects

The caster would slash their wand downward to point at the target; a banana-yellow jet of light would shoot from the tip, with what appeared to be a duck made entirely of brilliant yellow light soaring in front.
When it hit the target, there was a burst of yellow light and when said light faded, the target was in the shape of a duck.
Etymology
From the English noun " duck ", with the -fors suffix attached.
Notes and references

title: Duck
paragraphs: A duck is a species of bird that mostly lives in water .
Description
Ducklifors was the incantation for a transfiguration spell used to turn other living creatures into ducks, in particular Erklings and Blast-Ended Skrewts .

A rubber duck was a type of bathtub toy, shaped in the likeness of a duck, that was fairly common in Muggle society , but may have been rare in the wizarding world , as Arthur Weasley inquired of Harry Potter as to its purpose.
History
In 1927 , an Animagus was involved with an incident involving a duck, as reported by Le Cri de la Gargouille .

When Herbert Chorley was placed under an ill-performed Imperius Curse , he acted like a duck due to his mind being damaged, and as a result, he had to be removed from the Muggle society while he recovered at St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries .

During the infiltration of the British Ministry of Magic , Harry Potter overheard an employee of the Muggle-Born Registration Commission mention an episode involving a poisonous duck apparently created by the Committee on Experimental Charms .
Notes and references

title: Avifors Spell
paragraphs: The Avifors Spell ( Avifors ) was a transfiguration spell that transformed small objects and creatures into birds .
The spell was viewed as a jinx when used to transform certain creatures into birds.
Nature
A Dugbog being transformed into birds with this spell
The Avifors Spell could, at times, be a very complicated spell and some beginning Hogwarts students were known to struggle with it.
One student nearly failed the class when he proved unable to transform objects into anything more than eggs .
His cousin bragged about this.
This spell could also transform certain creatures into birds, like Dugbogs or Blast-Ended Skrewts .
Teaching
The Avifors Spell in action

The Avifors Spell was learned in first-year and revised in second-year Transfiguration class with Professor Minerva McGonagall , and was included in The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 2 by Miranda Goshawk .
Known uses
Known practitioners
Etymology
From Latin " avis ", meaning " bird ", with the -fors suffix attached.
Notes and references

title: Pullus
paragraphs: Pullus was the incantation of a transforming jinx used to transfigure the target into a chicken ; in particular, Erklings were rather vulnerable to this spell .
History
This jinx was used in 1754 by an unknown wizard on Silvio Astolfi , an Italian broom racer.
Known practitioners
Etymology
Pullus is Latin for the young of animals, particularly chickens (i.e. chicks).
Notes and references

title: 1750s
paragraphs: Muggles in the 1750s
The following events happened in the 1750s :
Events
Quidditch
Births
Deaths
Notes and references

title: Silvio Astolfi
paragraphs: Silvio Astolfi was an Italian wizard who was one of the most revered broom flyers in Europe in the mid- 18th century .
Biography
In 1754 , Astolfi agreed to participate in a broom race from Aberdeen to Rome with the Scottish Torquil McTavish , his bitter rival.
The race took place at night so as to avoid attracting the attention of Muggles .
Reaching Rome at daybreak, Astolfi and McTavish were seen racing toward the finish line at the Colosseum , but at that point, a violent clash broke out between rival fans that had gathered there.
During the course of the fight, Astolfi was turned into a chicken , and McTavish was hit with a hex that left his knees back-to-front .
The conflict culminated in an explosion that reduced the Colosseum to rubble.

Thanks to Orabella Nuttley , who came forward and proceeded to fix a few columns with a spell of her own invention , the Mending Charm , the damage to the Colosseum had been undone by the time that Muggles roused from their beds by the sound of the explosion finally arrived up at the scene.
All they found was a few strangely-dressed men attempting to quell Astolfi, who was obviously enraged, and still stuck in the form of a chicken.
It can be presumed afterwards, that after the Muggle observers had left, Silvio was untransfigured back into a human.
Magical abilities and skills
Notes and references

title: Italy
paragraphs: Italy is a country on the Mediterranean coast of Europe , consisting of a boot-shaped peninsula (the boot shape being caused by the Gulf of Taranto ) and a number of islands, the largest of which are Sicily and Sardinia .
Its commune of Mirto may have contained a wizarding community of note, as the Daily Prophet reported on this community's weather in its International section.
History

In A.D. 79 , the Ancient Roman warlock Zaccaria Innocenti cast the Dancing Feet Spell on Mount Vesuvius , triggering its eruption, destroying the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum , and killing at least 1500 people.
A sub-committee of sorcerers from the island of Sardinia did something of note in September of 1289 .
Professor Cuthbert Binns mentioned this during a lecture on the International Warlock Convention of 1289 he gave to his second-year History of Magic students in 1992 .
Culture
The flag of Italy hanging in the all-night café on Tottenham Court Road
Italian cuisine is popular around the world.

There was an all-night café on Tottenham Court Road in London which served hot panini , where Harry Potter , Ron Weasley , and Hermione Granger sought refuge after fleeing the wedding of Bill Weasley and Fleur Delacour in 1997 .
Italian Vermouth Bianco , a brand of vermouth , was made in Italy, but was specially tailored toward British consumers.
Wizarding world
Government
Italy was governed by a Ministry of Magic .
Games and sports
Luciano Volpi was a known Seeker for the Italian National Quidditch team .
Magical creatures
The following creatures were all found worldwide:
Known locations
Notes and references

title: Vermiculus
paragraphs: Vermiculus was the incantation of a transforming jinx used to transfigure things into worms .
Effect
Vampyr Mosps were especially susceptible to this spell, and any spell cast on them whilst they were in their transformed state would cause them to explode in a flash of bright colours.
Known practitioners
Etymology
From Latin " vermiculus " meaning " little worm ".

title: Worm
paragraphs: The worm is an invertebrate animal consisting of a tube-like body with no legs.
History
Known events involving worms in the wizarding world :
Types of worm
