title: Vampyr Mosp
paragraphs: A Vampyr Mosp was a fanged wasp-moth magical hybrid.
Description
Vampyr Mosps were giant, aggressive insects who would try to sting any individual they came into close contact with; the effect of these stings could be quite painful to the victim.
They were very attracted by the smell of certain flowers.
There were two known kinds of Vampyr Mosps, the Purple Vampyr Mosp and the Red Vampyre Mosp.
The Purple variants were usually less aggressive than Red variants.
They may have been native to Scotland , in wet places; Hogwarts had a reasonable amount of them in the sewers and pipes, and in the Herbology Greenhouses .
Many also inhabited large hives in the Forbidden Forest .
History

In the 1990-1991 school year , while doing research on magical creatures to try to identify the creature that had attacked Dolores Umbridge and Ismelda Murk in Hogsmeade , Jacob's sibling and Liz Tuttle read about Vampyr Mosps.
The Detective Files of Conebush and Persimmons contained a case where Copper Conebush and Kit Persimmons were attacked by Vampyr Mosps controlled by Dr Goosander .
Notes and references

title: Human to worm spell
paragraphs: This spell ( incantation unknown ) could transfigure a human into a worm .
Known uses
A student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry named Hilda used this spell on her classmate, Astoria Crickett , during the late 19th century .
Notes and references

title: Squiggle Quill
paragraphs: Squiggle Quill ( incantation unknown ) was a transforming spell that transfigured writing quills into worms .
Notes and references

title: Dark charm
paragraphs: Dark charms were charms that drew their power from Dark magic .
Like all charms, a Dark charm would provoke a magical effect on a target, but in a malicious and harmful manner.
The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 1 didn't carry instructions for such spells .
Classification
Dark charms were classified into three groups based on their level of severity.
The higher one ascended up the hierarchy, the more powerful, wicked, and longer lasting the spells became.
The three types of Dark charms in order of increasing severity were jinxes , hexes , and curses .
Notes and references

title: Leg-Locker Curse
paragraphs: The Leg-Locker Curse ( Locomotor Mortis ), also known as the Leg Locking Spell was a curse that bound the legs of the victim together.
History
It was most often used by experienced witches and wizards in duels , or in friendly wizard races.
This curse was one of the dark charms found in the Dark Arts spellbook Curses and Counter-Curses by Vindictus Viridian .
There existed a counter-curse of unknown incantation; Hermione Granger used it to reverse the usage of the curse Draco Malfoy used on Neville Longbottom .

During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , this spell was taught to fifth-year students in Charms class by Professor Filius Flitwick , in preparation for their upcoming Ordinary Wizarding Levels .
Hermione Granger and Ronald Weasley learned this spell in their first year , to use on Severus Snape if he tried to harm Harry Potter at an upcoming Quidditch match.
They did not need to use it, however, as Professor Dumbledore was watching, they found it unlikely Snape would try to hurt Harry.
Known uses
Successful
Unsuccessful
Known practitioners
Etymology
This spell's incantation is derived from the English word locomotor , meaning "of or relating to locomotion" and the Latin word mortis , meaning " death ".
Overall, the incantation roughly means "killing locomotion" or in other words, stopping someone from moving normally.
Notes and references

title: Jinx on the post of Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher
paragraphs: This jinx ( incantation unknown ) was cast by Tom Marvolo Riddle , who was by the time known exclusively as Lord Voldemort, to curse Hogwarts 's Defence Against the Dark Arts class to ensure that none of its teachers could hold their post for more than one year.
It is unknown what the requirements and incantation of this jinx were, or if it could be used for other school subjects or other establishments and careers.
The jinx could only be lifted once the caster had died .
History
Tom Riddle's request

Upon his graduation from Hogwarts, Tom Riddle asked the then Headmaster , Armando Dippet , for the post as Professor for the Defence Against the Dark Arts class due to his love for Hogwarts and passion for the Dark Arts .
Professor Dippet cordially rejected Riddle's application because Riddle was too young at eighteen years old but offered him to reapply after a few years if he was still interested.
Over two decades later, when Riddle resurfaced as the mysterious Lord Voldemort, he returned to Hogwarts to ask for the job once again.
At this time, Albus Dumbledore had taken over as Headmaster and, knowing of Voldemort's dark intentions, rejected his application.

Although Voldemort was merely using the application as an excuse to return to Hogwarts to do research into dark magic, recruit more followers , and hide his diadem Horcrux , he was still infuriated that his return to the school had been denied despite also knowing that Dumbledore would never hire him.
In revenge, Voldemort jinxed the position to ensure that no applicant of the Defence Against the Dark Arts post could keep it for more than one year.
A secondary and more strategic reason for jinxing the post could be Voldemort's wish to reduce the quality of the teaching of the subject, as its purpose was directly opposed to his personal goals.
Disrupting the teaching by an annual change of staff would make future students less capable of self-defence, thus mitigating chances of facing too many future enemies who excelled in the subject.

After a certain amount of times of this jinx's effects, the subject has fewer willing applicants as many came to fear of being jinxed, resulting in the necessity of Dumbledore going out to seek for a new teacher and give them offers to persuade them to take the job.
In 1995, Dumbledore actually failed to find a replacement due to the jinx's reputation, enabling the Ministry of Magic to implant their own teacher, Dolores Umbridge .
Throughout the time between Voldemort's career interview and death, the jinx continuously claimed a teacher every year.
The reasons for their no longer being able to hold the job were varied, but the end result was always that the school needed a new D.A.D.A. teacher.
The potency of the jinx was so great that nobody seemed to be able to remove it, not even Albus Dumbledore with the Elder Wand , until the caster's demise.
Known victims of the jinx
Once Voldemort placed his jinx on the post, around the end of each school year, the teachers of the class were forced to leave due to one reason or another from the effects of the jinx.
The jinx lifted
After Voldemort's downfall , the jinx was broken and Hogwarts was able to keep a permanent Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher .
Notes and references

title: Stinging Jinx
paragraphs: The Stinging Jinx ( incantation unknown ), also known as the Stinging Hex , was a Dark charm that could be used to sting the victim's flesh, producing a red brand like a scorch mark and causing swelling.
The Death Eater Antoine Grimalkin created a highly powerful variation of this jinx called the Frequensting , which he and his wife used to terrorise Great Britain during the First Wizarding War .
History
When under assault by Severus Snape 's Legilimency , Harry Potter found it almost impossible to resist the intrusion until Snape happened upon the memory of Harry's kiss with Cho Chang .
The resistance he felt to Snape viewing this memory translated into a Stinging Hex that broke Snape's spell .
Harry had not consciously decided to perform that spell, so it seems unlikely that that he actually spoke any words .
It would seem instead that this hex was purely an extension of his intention to fight Snape off.
Hermione Granger used it on Harry as a means of disguising his face when they were caught by Snatchers after inadvertently triggering the Taboo on Voldemort 's name in 1998 .
Effects
Harry Potter under the effects
When cast, the Stinging Jinx was a burst of white light.
Immediately upon hitting the target, it caused agony and rendered the target unable to see.
It was also excruciatingly painful when the target was hit in the face, making that area feel unrecognisable to the owner.
The skin was tight, swollen, and puffy, as though they had suffered some violent allergic reaction.
The eyes were reduced to slits through which a person could barely see.
It also produced welts on the skin if used on other parts of the body.
Known practitioners
Notes and references

title: Antoine Grimalkin
paragraphs: Antoine Grimalkin was a powerful Dark wizard and Death Eater who fought during the First Wizarding War alongside his wife, Bedilia Grimalkin .
He was the inventor of a powerful curse , the Frequensting .
Biography
Antoine lived in Godric's Hollow with his wife, Bedilia .
He briefly worked for the British Ministry of Magic , but left when they wouldn't allow him to purse his research.
During the First Wizarding War , he and his wife announced their support of Lord Voldemort and joined the Death Eaters .

At some point during the war, Antoine invented the Frequensting , a variation of the Stinging Jinx which caused everyone affected by it to be constantly afflicted with an ever more painful stinging in their mind.
During the war, the couple, based in Godric's Hollow, would travel to wizarding settlements and cast the curse over all the inhabitants, rendering them almost incapable of fighting.
The curse was so widespread that almost everyone who survived the war had been affected by it.

Despite their success with using the curse, Voldemort and the other Death Eaters didn't approve of the curse due to its use of the gramophone , a Muggle invention, as one of the key parts to casting it.
The pair were ostracised from the Death Eaters, barely escaping with their lives.
At the end of the war, Antoine was captured by the British Ministry of Magic , with the help of information given to them by Albus Dumbledore , and placed into Azkaban .
Although Bedilia believed her husband might have died in Azkaban, by the late 1980s , he was still alive.
Notes and references

title: Frequensting
paragraphs: The Frequensting ( incantation unknown ) was a curse and modified version of the Stinging Hex which was invented by the Death Eater Antoine Grimalkin during the First Wizarding War .
Later, his wife, Bedilia Grimalkin , managed to recreate and modify the spell, which she used to attack the wizarding world during the late 1980s .
Effects
The effects of the curse were complex, and varied based on several factors.
At its weakest level, the curse would cause a constant low-level stinging sensation, akin to the Stinging Hex it was derived from.
Although annoying, at this stage the curse wouldn't be strong enough in incapacitate someone, only annoy them.
As the curse increased in strength, the effects would become more severe.
The victim would uncontrollably spasm in response to the curse, the pain could be enough to cause someone to fall unconscious.
At its most severe, the pain would be enough to permanently injure the victim.
Bedilia Grimalkin's modifications allowed her to individually control the intensity of the curse for a specific individual.
It allowed her to, in her words, 'turn up the volume'.
Such a sharp increase in the pain would incapacitate the victim, and Bedilia appeared to be able to do this wandlessly and nonverbally , giving her immense power.
However, although the curse could be directly removed from individuals, the caster could not directly curse somebody with the curse.
The curse required constant concentration and a constantly playing piece of music in order to work, which led Antoine to create a cursed gramophone .
Whenever the music on the gramophone looped, the curse would increase in intensity, and the song the gramophone was playing would be stuck in the head of anyone who had been cursed by it.
However, if an individual couldn't hear the music (such as by wearing earmuffs like those used to harvest Mandrakes ), they wouldn't be afflicted with the curse.
History
Antoine invented this curse during the First Wizarding War , in experiments that the British Ministry of Magic wouldn't have allowed.
He taught it to his wife, Bedilia Grimalkin , and the pair joined Lord Voldemort and his Death Eaters .
During the First Wizarding War, they were feared due to the power of the Frequensting .
However, Voldemort and the other Death Eaters didn't approve of the Muggle technology involved in its function and nearly killed them, with the pair able to escape.
They continued to use the Frequensting even after the war ended, but Antoine was captured by the British Ministry of Magic and sent to Azkaban .
The curse became dormant for years afterwards.
Bedilia fled Great Britain and began to work on controlling the curse using Antoine's theories.
She eventually discovered the key to controlling the curse and was even able to modify the spell beyond its original capabilities.

With revenge against the Order of the Phoenix , the British Ministry of Magic, and the Death Eaters in mind, she activated the curse again during the late 1980s , afflicting large swathes of people with it.
Jacob's sibling eventually managed to figure out what and who was behind the curse and tracked Bedilia to St Jerome's graveyard in Godric's Hollow .
However, they were nearly killed by Bedilia before she was caught by Albus Dumbledore , Severus Snape , and Minerva McGonagall and sent to Azkaban.
Jacob's sibling and Dumbledore then broke the curse on the gramophone with the General Counter-Spell .
Victims
Notes and references

title: Bedilia Grimalkin
paragraphs: Bedilia Grimalkin was a powerful Dark witch and Death Eater who fought during the First Wizarding War alongside her husband, Antoine Grimalkin .
However, she had to flee Great Britain after the Death Eaters discovered the couple weren't as fanatical about wizarding supremacy as the rest of the Death Eaters.
Biography
Bedilia lived in Godric's Hollow with her husband, Antoine.
During the First Wizarding War , they announced their support of Lord Voldemort and joined the Death Eaters .

At some point during the war, Antoine invented the Frequensting , a variation of the Stinging Jinx which caused everyone affected by it to be constantly afflicted with an ever more painful stinging in their mind.
During the war, the couple, based in Godric's Hollow, would travel to wizarding settlements and cast the curse over all the inhabitants, rendering them almost incapable of fighting.
The curse was so widespread that almost everyone who survived the war had been affected by it.
Antoine taught Bedilia how to cast the curse, which required constant attention.
However, Voldemort and the other Death Eaters didn't approve of the curse due to its use of the gramophone , a Muggle invention, as one of the key parts to casting it.
The pair were ostracised from the Death Eaters, barely escaping with their lives.

At the end of the war, Antoine was captured by the British Ministry of Magic , with the help of information given to them by Albus Dumbledore , and placed into Azkaban , while Bedilia fled the country.
Whilst in hiding, Bedilia spent years learning about her husband's curse and how to amplify its power.

Finally succeeding years later, Bedilia returned to Godric's Hollow and began to cast the Frequensting again, which caused the curse to activate in those that had been cursed with it before as well as spread to new people.
Jacob's sibling began to investigate, getting afflicted with the curse themselves.

They eventually encountered Bedilia, who told them of her plan to attack her old enemies as well as her former Death Eater allies and invited Jacob's sibling to join them after being defeated in a duel by them.
Jacob's sibling refused, and Bedilia left.
Aware of who she was, the Ministry sent a squad of Hit Wizards to comb the village, but Bedilia easily defeated them.
She encountered Jacob's sibling again, this time with their friend Penny Haywood by their side, however she chose not to fight them.
Jacob's sibling secretly followed her to the hiding spot of Antoine's cursed gramophone , St Jerome's graveyard , but Bedilia discovered them.
She gave them one last chance to surrender, but Jacob's sibling refused.
At precisely that moment, Jacob's sibling was afflicted with the curse and was left vulnerable.
Bedilia used this opportunity to attempt to kill Jacob's sibling, and was mid way through casting the Killing Curse when she was stopped by Severus Snape , Albus Dumbledore, and Minerva McGonagall .

Snape took her to the Ministry, where she was imprisoned in Azkaban , and Dumbledore and Jacob's sibling broke the protective enchantments on the cursed gramophone, which allowed them to stop the curse altogether.
Magical abilities and skills
Possessions
Relationships
Lord Voldemort and the Death Eaters
Lord Voldemort , Bedilia's former master
Bedilia's relationship with Lord Voldemort and the other Death Eaters was a complicated one.
Neither she, nor her husband, was as fanatical about wizarding supremacy as the rest of the organisation.
Although she clearly saw Muggles as inferior, unlike most other Death Eaters and indeed most other wizards, she acknowledged that Muggles had created some worthwhile inventions.

She claimed that her husband had managed to perfectly merge Muggle science with magic, something which she was clearly proud of but which the other Death Eaters presumably took as a sign of weakness and inferiority.

Although they had been formidable members of the Death Eaters, and were two of the most feared by the wizarding population for their use of the Frequensting , their acceptance of Muggle inventions was enough to turn the Death Eaters against them.
Bedilia claimed they were ostracised, then forced to flee for their lives after Voldemort discovered how their invention worked.

Although still a supporter of the Death Eater ideals and continuing to perform attacks with the Frequensting even after the war ended, Bedilia eventually renounced the Death Eaters and began to target them as well as the members of the Order of the Phoenix for revenge when she returned to Great Britain .
Etymology
Bedilia is likely a variation of Bedelia, which is an Irish name connected to Brigid and means 'strength'.
Grimalkin or greymalkin is an archaic word for a cat, stemming from the words 'grey' and 'malkin'.
Scottish legends talk about a fairy cat called Greymalkin, and the two words became bynames for witch in the early modern period.
Notes and references

title: Legilimency Spell
paragraphs: The Legilimency Spell ( Legilimens ) was a charm that allowed the caster to perform Legilimency ; in other words, to delve into the mind of the victim, permitting the caster to see memories, emotions and thoughts.
Skilled Legilimens (such as Tom Riddle ) was able to perform Legilimency without using the incantation or a wand .
Highly skilled Legilimens were able to control their victims and create realistic visions.
History
During the 1989-1990 school year , Professor Severus Snape performed this spell on Beatrice Haywood in the Potions Classroom to help navigate and understand her thoughts and emotions.

In the 1990-1991 school year at St Mungo's , Jacob's sibling used this spell to perform Legilimency on Zenith Xeep in the Janus Thickey Ward , so they could read her mind to see who was behind the curses at St Mungo's.
Reading her thoughts, she learnt she was thinking about a Dark wizard called Burke .
Harry Potter using the spell Legilimens to look into Snape's mind
Professor Snape used this spell on Harry Potter while attempting to train him in Occlumency in the 1995-1996 school year .
He also used it nonverbally and wandlessly in 1997 to find out where Harry learned the Sectumsempra spell.
Voldemort had used this spell extensively, both wandlessly and nonverbally, to enter the minds of those he wished to interrogate.
Due to the link between himself and Harry, both could access each other's thoughts if Voldemort did not block it with Occlumency.
Albus Dumbledore used this spell to find out Kreacher 's plot to lure Harry to the Department of Mysteries ; whether he used his wand and incantation or not is unknown.
Known practitioners
Etymology
Latin legere , "to read", and mens , "mind".
Notes and references

title: Gwendoline Babcocke
paragraphs: Gwendoline Babcocke was a Scottish witch that worked as a shop assistant at The Magic Neep in Hogsmeade .
Biography

She received several notes and gifts such as chocolates and lavender perfume from an anonymous admirer, including an night-time invitation to the Boathouse at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry which caught fire just as she arrived.
Enamoured with dragons , she owned a copy of Dragon Breeding for Pleasure and Profit but would never leave Hogsmeade to work with them as it would break her mum 's heart.
In addition to her interest in magical beasts , she said she was a natural at the Stinging Jinx .
Notes and references

title: Insect Hex
paragraphs: The Insect Hex ( Entomorphis ), also known as the Insect Jinx , was a dark charm that could be used to induce insect-like qualities upon a victim for a short period of time.
It deprived them of their ability to speak, forcing them to crawl about and endowing them with feelers .
History
In the 1980s and 1990s at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , students often used this spell against their opponents in the Duelling Club .

On 2 August , 1995 , when Dudley Dursley insulted Harry Potter for his nightmares about the death of Cedric Diggory , Harry considered using the spell on Dudley, although the arrival of two Dementors prevented him from using it.
Etymology
The Greek word "έντομο" (" entomo ") means " insect " or " hopper ", and "μορφή" (" morfi ") means " form ", " shape " or " figure ".
Notes and references

title: Bee-Sting Jinx
paragraphs: The Bee-Sting Jinx ( incantation unknown ) was a jinx that caused the target's skin to swell and turn pink, similar to the effect of a bee sting.
History
In the 1980s and 1990s , this jinx was used by members of the Hogwarts Duelling Club against their opponents in duels .
Notes and references

title: Severus Snape's copy ofAdvanced Potion-Making
paragraphs: A personally-annotated copy of Advanced Potion-Making belonged to Severus Snape while he attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
Snape's nickname for himself was the "Half-Blood Prince", and so he signed this nickname along the bottom of the back cover of the book.
Advanced Potion-Making was a Potions textbook used by Hogwarts for N.E.W.T level Potions classes and authored by Libatius Borage .
It contained a variety of recipes for various potions, many of which Snape improved by means of amending procedures and scribbling notes in the margins.
History
Under Severus Snape's possession
The first known owner of this copy of Advanced Potion-Making was Eileen Prince , mother of Severus Snape.
The book became second-hand when it was passed down to Snape when he went to Hogwarts.
A teenage Severus Snape

When Snape attended Hogwarts as a student, he had acquired this textbook for N.E.W.T.-level Potions with Horace Slughorn and then signed it with his own self-proclaimed nickname and signature, the "Half-Blood Prince".
Snape, being a talented potioneer even at a young age, had made alterations to the many recipes within the book for even better effects.
He also made notes in the margins of several spells that he had invented himself, including Sectumsempra , Levicorpus , Langlock , and Muffliato .
When Severus left Hogwarts, he fell in league with the Death Eaters , though he never lost his old copy of Advanced Potion-Making .

When he eventually returned to Hogwarts to work as Potions Master , he kept the book in a cupboard in his classroom (perhaps to use its annotations for his own teaching, as it was obviously not meant to be used by students).
When he changed teaching positions and Horace Slughorn gained the classroom, he left the book there.
Under Harry Potter's possession
Harry Potter brewing a potion with the aid of the Half-Blood Prince's book
In the 1996-1997 school year , Harry Potter took a N.E.W.T. Potions class under the newly reinstated Slughorn.

Harry had not bought his own textbook prior to arriving at Hogwarts, as he believed that he failed to qualify for advancement; Snape had stated that he would only accept students who had received ' Outstanding ' in their O.W.L.s, but Slughorn was quite content with the ' Exceeds Expectations ' that Harry had received.
As such, Slughorn loaned one of the older books left behind by previous students.
Harry, by chance, received this book.
While initially annoyed by the scribbles that made it difficult to read the original instructions, when Harry tried Snape's methods, he achieved better results than even Hermione Granger .

When Harry got a new book from Flourish and Blotts , he then swapped the front covers and gave Slughorn the new one with a combination of the Severing and Mending Charms , while keeping this one for himself, much to Hermione's displeasure.
Harry showed his lack of academic integrity by choosing to follow the revised formulae over the regular instructions, in order to acquire unearned success in the course without any effort on his own.

As a result, for the rest of his sixth year at Hogwarts, Harry became better at potions than he had ever been in his time with Snape and even managed to save Ronald Weasley 's life with a bezoar when the latter had been poisoned .
This book also helped Harry to win a bottle of Felix Felicis during his first class, which later proved essential in helping him acquire a memory from Slughorn about Tom Riddle and Horcruxes .
Harry also read through the notes within out of sheer interest, and his friends suggested that he went as far as to sleep with it.
Over the course of the year, Harry began trying the Half-Blood Prince's self-invented spells written in the textbook.
However, when he used Sectumsempra on Draco Malfoy , he was unaware of its effects and Malfoy was critically injured.
Although they were bitter rivals, Harry was shocked when he saw the deadliness of the curse .
Harry reading the Half-Blood Prince's copy of Advanced Potion-Making in the Gryffindor common room
When Madam Pince saw the book with its graffiti-covered pages, she flew into a rage, despite Harry insisting that it was not the library's .
She clawed the air for it, and throwing angry claims at Harry for defiling a book with writing.
During one of Professor Slughorn's Slug Club parties, Snape was told of Harry's sudden improvement in the art of potion-making.
Snape then suspected that his old textbook may have fallen into Harry's hands.

When Harry used Sectumsempra on Draco, Snape was able to confirm his suspicions, but was unable to get his hands on the book, as Harry had stashed it inside the Room of Requirement and used Ron's book as a decoy.
As a result, Snape (correctly) accused Harry of being a liar and cheater, and punished him with a multitude of detentions for injuring Malfoy and cheating in potions.
Despite knowing Harry's source for the curse, Snape chose not to outright turn Harry in for a harsher punishment, as he feared it would connect himself to being the inventor of the curse.

Using this curse greatly shocked Harry, as he did not expect the Prince would have added something so vicious into the notes, and even reprimanded the Prince within his own mind of doing so; nevertheless, he intended on retrieving the book if he had a chance to.
As a result of hiding the book from Snape, Harry's potions grade declined sharply from thereon, though Slughorn attributed this to Harry's newfound love with Ginny Weasley .
Harry hiding the book would later prove to be a fortuitous move as he inadvertently discovered Ravenclaw's Diadem while doing so which was one of Lord Voldemort's Horcruxes .

After learning the story behind the diadem's theft from the Grey Lady , Harry realised that he had seen the diadem while hiding his old potions book which proved to be crucial in that Horcrux's eventual destruction.
Hermione Granger resented the book, for it did not follow the "official instructions."
She did some research on possible candidates for the Prince's identity, but the only information she found pertained to Eileen Prince , although Harry remained certain that the writer was male.
Later, Snape revealed that he was the Half-Blood Prince, and that he owned the book before.

This came as a major shock to Harry, when he learned that the Half-Blood Prince, who had taught him so much over the year, happened to be the person he hated the most (especially after Snape killed Albus Dumbledore ).
Ginny Weasley was also displeased when she heard Harry was following instructions from an unknown individual's book, something she had personally experienced .

It is unknown if Harry removed the book from the Room of Requirement after hiding it there, but if not, then it was possibly destroyed when Vincent Crabbe released Fiendfyre in the room during the Battle of Hogwarts .

However, since Lottie Turner and her friend were able to retrieve some furniture that had been placed there since the 1820s about ten years after Crabbe set the room on fire, the book itself may have been unharmed or restored.
Altered potion formula
The Half-Blood Prince's many annotations and corrections
The books many pages with annotations and corrections
Invented spells
Notes and references

title: Dangling Jinx
paragraphs: The Dangling Jinx ( Levicorpus ) was a jinx , which was intended to be cast nonverbally but the incantation could also be spoken aloud, caused the victim to be hoisted into the air by their ankle; the counter-jinx for this jinx was Liberacorpus .
History
An individual under the effects of this jinx
This jinx was invented by Severus Snape and recorded under his pseudonym the " Half-Blood Prince " during his time as a student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .

According to Remus Lupin this spell became quite popular during his school times and students could barely move about without being hoisted up in the air by their ankle, apparently unaware that Snape had invented it.
It is unclear when Severus Snape invented this jinx , as James Potter knew it in his fifth year , whereas it was noted in Snape's NEWT -level textbook.
Furthermore, according to Sirius Black , Snape " knew more curses when he arrived at school than half the kids in seventh year ."
During the 1986-1987 school year , Cecil Lee put on a sock which had been bewitched with this spell.
He was eventually freed from it by Jacob's sibling and Merula Snyde .
Known uses
Successful
Unsuccessful
Known practitioners
Etymology
The incantation can be divided into two separate Latin words; levare means "lift", and corpus is translated to "body".
It could also be translated as "Light Body".
Notes and references

title: Muffliato Charm
paragraphs: The Muffliato Charm ( Muffliato ) was a charm used to fill the ears of any person in the vicinity of the caster with an unidentifiable buzzing sound so as to allow for conversation without being overheard, similar to the Imperturbable Charm .
History
The charm was invented by Severus Snape and recorded during his time as a student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , meaning it would have been created sometime between 1971 and 1978 .
It is unknown when Severus Snape invented this and many of his other spells as according to Sirius Black "he knew more curses when he arrived at school than half the kids in seventh year ".
During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts, this charm was taught by Professor Filius Flitwick to his fifth-year Charms students.
Harry Potter used this spell multiple times during the 1996-1997 school year after discovering the Half-Blood Prince 's copy of Advanced Potion-Making .
Hermione Granger originally disapproved of using the spell, but came to use it herself when it was needed.
On 15 October 1996 , Ron Weasley suggested that Harry Potter should have cast Muffliato during Herbology class, to have prevented Professor Pomona Sprout from overhearing their conversation.

On 2 September 1997 , during the infiltration of the Ministry , Harry Potter realised that in the corridors near Dolores Umbridge's office was such silence as the Muffliato Charm was cast on the entire floor .
He was also thinking about throwing Muffliato in the courtroom on Dolores Umbridge and Corban Yaxley , but he said that saying the incantation would cause a violent reaction from Hermione Granger .
Known uses
Known practitioners
Etymology
Notes and references

title: Bezoar
paragraphs: A bezoar was a stone-like mass taken from the stomach of a goat , that acted as an antidote to most poisons , with Basilisk venom being one notable exception.
This was the reason why bezoars were used in the preparation of the Antidote to Common Poisons .
This object was usually made of hair, plant fibre, or similar indigestible matter that stayed in the gut of an animal and formed a hard ball or "stone".
Bezoars were also notably rare, according to Horace Slughorn, who cited this as the reason why it was still worth knowing how to mix antidotes.
History
There was a small stock of bezoars that could be found in the Potions Classroom store cupboard, as well as at least two in the Hospital Wing .

In 1991 , Severus Snape asked Harry Potter where one would to find a bezoar in Harry's first ever Potions class , in order for him to chastise Harry for supposedly not paying attention during his class.

In late 1994 , in a Potions exam, Harry forgot to add a bezoar to his potion, because he was too focused on thinking about asking Cho Chang to the Yule Ball , which subsequently earned him bottom marks in this class for his dismal performance.
As a student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Severus Snape, under his alias "The Half Blood Prince", wrote " Just shove a bezoar down their throats. "
across the list of antidotes in his copy of Advanced Potion-Making .

In the 1996-1997 school year , during one of Harry's sixth-year N.E.W.T. classes about antidotes, Harry, who was unable to understand Golpalott's Third Law , fetched a bezoar from the cupboard and showed it to Professor Horace Slughorn as the answer to the poison he was supposed to be analysing.
This gained Harry Slughorn's admiration and ten points to Gryffindor for " sheer cheek ".
Known users
Harry Potter shoving a bezoar down Ron Weasley 's throat
On 1994 , during a fourth-year Potions class exam, the bezoar was used as an ingredient for antidotes.
Harry, being distracted by the Yule Ball, forgot to add one and subsequently got bottom marks.
On 1 March 1997 , Ron Weasley was poisoned when he drank some poisoned oak-matured mead that was intended for Albus Dumbledore .
Harry, remembering the above mentioned incident in Potions class, quickly found the bezoar he had given Professor Slughorn and shoved it down Ron's throat, saving his life.
Etymology
Bezoars are undigested clumps of matter that accumulate inside a digestive system, similar to a cat 's hairballs.
They are used in Chinese Herbology , and are claimed to remove toxins from the body.
The word "bezoar" may come from the Persian pâdzahr (پادزهر), which literally means "protection from poison ".
Notes and references

title: Lottie Turner
paragraphs: Lottie Turner was a witch who began attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in 2008 , where she was Sorted into an unknown House .
Biography
Early life
Lottie was born in 1997 to Ambrose Turner and a South American witch .
During her youth, Lottie and her father would often travel together to paint.
One of these travels was to the Swedish dragon reservation , but they didn't have the chance to paint at all because the annual broom race was taking place.
Lottie also regularly was asked by her father to double check their teapot before pouring in hot water to ensure an Occamy wasn't hiding inside.
In winters, they would build snowmen and decorate them with scarves and hats, and after they went home, Ambrose would prepare hot cocoa with mint , and they would bake cookies .
Hogwarts years (2008-)
Lottie started attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in 2008 .
She sat on her own on the Hogwarts Express .
Her paint in her bag spilled out all over her table.
When a fellow student asked if they could sit with her, they told her they couldn't because there was paint everywhere.
Lottie sorted into the same House they were, as well as Daniel Page and Ivy Warrington .
She greeted the student in their dormitory in the morning, telling them to hurry up and get ready before they were late to their first lesson, Charms .
In the Grand Staircase , Lottie told them the moving staircases were so dizzying and that not every portrait had the patience to guide them to their classroom if they got lost.
After their lesson, Lottie talked with the student, Kevin Farrell and Robyn Thistlethwaite in a corridor.
She told them she loved Hogwarts because it was like a museum with interesting paintings and statues everywhere.
Robyn disagreed because it was filled with old, boring stuff.
When Lottie told her about the Troll Tapestry , she admitted that did sound weird and interesting.
One evening, Lottie sent an owl to Robyn, Kevin and Daniel to gather in the library after curfew to help find Ivy.
However, Lottie didn't show up.
Personality and traits
Lottie was very creative and loved art, and liked to capture the moment by drawing it.

title: Sopophorous Bean
paragraphs: The Sopophorous Bean was the fruit of the Sopophorous plant ; it was a shrivelled pearly-white bean which resembled an overgrown Mistletoe berry .
It had many magical properties and was used as an ingredient in potion -making.
Uses
A Sopophorous Bean
The Sopophorous Bean contained a thick silver juice that would remove the drinker's memory if drunk neat.
If used in potion-making, it did not seem to retain this power.
The Sopophorous Bean was used as an ingredient in the Draught of Living Death .
The potion's written instructions, as featured in Advanced Potion-Making by Libatius Borage , said to cut the bean in order to release the juice within.
However, this could prove very difficult, and the bean often bounced when punctured with the blade of a knife.

However, crushing the bean with the flat side of a silver knife was a more simple and effective method of obtaining the juice, as suggested by Severus Snape in his personal copy of Advanced Potion-Making .

Professor Pomona Sprout taught sixth-year Herbology students how to cultivate the Sopophorous plant, including their beans, in the 1989-1990 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
She later taught seventh-year Herbology students specifically how to handle Sopophorous Beans during the 1990-1991 school year in preparation for their upcoming N.E.W.T. exams.
Etymology
The prefix "Sopo-" most likely comes from the Latin sopor meaning "deep sleep".

The suffix "-phorous" is more elusive, though it could quite possibly have the same etymological roots as the "-phorus" in "phosphorus" (a chemical element) - in this case "phos-" and "-phorus" come from the Greek φως ( fo̱s in the Latin script, meaning light) and φέρω (féro̱ in the Latin script, meaning bringer or carrier) respectively.
Hence, "Sopophorus" would read as "bringer of deep sleep", which is appropriate given its use as an ingredient in the Draught of Living Death .
Also, it is a possible allusion to the plant historically used by the Native American shamans of the ancient Southwest, the mescal bean (Sophora Secundiflora).
These beans also have a very hard shell and were split open and made into various concoctions that were then imbibed by the user in spiritual ceremonies.
The sophora beans were described to put the user into a coma-like trance where the other elements of the magic ceremony could be carried out.

title: Elixir to Induce Euphoria
paragraphs: The Elixir to Induce Euphoria was a sunshine-yellow potion that induced a sense of inexplicable, irrational happiness upon the drinker.
It served as the cure for uncontrollable sobbing.
History
Penny Haywood had fond memories of brewing this potion with her grandmother before she started at Hogwarts.

During the 1990-1991 school year at St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries , several patients were admitted to the hospital with uncontrollable sobbing after consuming faulty Calming Draughts , that had to be cured with the Elixir to Induce Euphoria.
Jacob's sibling brewed this potion in the Alchemy Room to cure the patients, following Healer Miriam Strout 's instruction.
In 1997 , Harry Potter brewed this potion in his sixth year , whilst most of his fellow sixth-year classmates were attending Apparition lessons in the Great Hall .
Professor Slughorn set his remaining students the task of creating "something amusing".

Harry prepared the potion with the hope that, if he could persuade the professor to taste the potion, Slughorn would be in "such a good mood that he would be prepared to hand over" the memory about young Voldemort and his search for information about Horcruxes .
However, Slughorn swiftly left when he saw that he and Harry were alone, thus a disappointed Harry cleaned up his workstation.
According to the Half-Blood Prince 's instructions , the potion recipe was heavily altered.
Brewing instructions
This potion being brewed during Potions class
To brew this potion, follow these steps:
NOTE: A sprig of peppermint , when added to the brew, counteracts certain side-effects.
Effects

As the name implies, this potion induced sudden euphoria in the drinker - excessive singing and nose-tweaking were possible side-effects (a sprig of peppermint added to the potion during preparation helped to counterbalance these).
The addition of a sprig of peppermint to counteract excessive singing and nose-tweaking was considered to be unorthodox, but a stroke of inspiration.
Notes and references

title: Liberacorpus
paragraphs: Liberacorpus was the incantation for the counter-jinx to the Dangling Jinx ( Levicorpus ).
Both spells were invented by Severus Snape .
History
It is unknown when Severus Snape invented this and many of his other spells as according to Sirius Black "he knew more curses when he arrived at school than half the kids in seventh year".
In June 1976 , James Potter cast Liberacorpus to reverse the Dangling Jinx he had cast on Snape earlier, due to Lily 's request for him to do so.
James's son, Harry Potter , used the spell in 1996 to counteract the Dangling Jinx he inadvertently cast on Ron Weasley .
Harry used the spell again in 1998 to counteract the Dangling Jinx Hermione Granger cast on him once he took hold of the Hufflepuff's Cup during the trio's Gringott's raid.
Known practitioners
Etymology
Liberacorpus name comes from the Latin words liberare , "to free", and corpus , "body".
Notes and references

title: Counter-jinx
paragraphs: A counter-jinx was a type of counter-spell that ended the effect of a jinx .
Effects
It differed from an anti-jinx in that an anti-jinx was intended to prevent those effects rather than remove them.
Hermione Granger once had to look up the counter-jinx for the Jelly-Legs Jinx in June 1995 .
History
During the 1988-1989 school year , Professor Patricia Rakepick would often ask her fifth year Defence Against the Dark Arts students to use counter-jinxes.

Wilbert Slinkhard said that the term "counter-jinx" was a misnomer, implying that they were intended with just as much harm as the spells they countered, though Hermione Granger disagreed with this assessment, much to the disapproval of Dolores Umbridge in a fifth year Defence Against the Dark Arts class in late 1995 .
Practical Defensive Magic and Its Use Against the Dark Arts contained moving colour illustrations of the various counter-jinxes and hexes that it illustrated.
Fifth years were expected to preform counter-jinxes as apart of their Defence Against the Dark Arts practical O.W.L. exam .
Known counter-jinxes

title: Toenail-growing hex
paragraphs: This hex ( incantation unknown ) was used to cause the victim's toenails to grow at an alarmingly fast rate.
History
This hex was invented by Severus Snape and recorded in his copy of Advanced Potion-Making during his school years at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
Therefore, it had not been approved by the British Ministry of Magic .
It is unknown when Severus Snape invented this and many of his other spells, as according to Sirius Black "he knew more curses when he arrived at school than half the kids in seventh year".
In 1996 , Harry Potter used this hex on Vincent Crabbe in the corridor, with "very entertaining results".
Ron Weasley also recommended trying it on Cormac McLaggen .

title: Nigel Wolpert
paragraphs: Nigel Wolpert (c. 1983 ) was a wizard and a student who attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , during the 1990s .
He was sorted into Gryffindor House in 1994.
Nigel was an avid fan and friend of the famous Harry Potter and was a member of Dumbledore's Army , an organisation taught and led by Harry.
Nigel fought in the 1998 Battle of Hogwarts , despite being underage at the time.
He fought alongside his friends and presumably survived to see Harry defeat Lord Voldemort once and for all.
Biography
Early life
Nigel was born between circa 1982 and 1983 in Great Britain or Ireland .
Hogwarts years (1994-1998)
Nigel after being sorted into Gryffindor House
Nigel Wolpert began attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in 1994.
He started when famous student Harry Potter was in his fourth year of schooling and Nigel was sorted into Gryffindor house.
Nigel also appeared to have a great deal of respect for the school headmaster.
During Dumbledore 's welcoming speech, Nigel seemed completely captivated.
This was in contrast with the other students who were getting distracted by friends, floating candles, and the Great Hall's enchanted ceiling.
Nigel trying to get Harry Potter's autograph
Nigel had also shown an interest in Harry Potter (who was dubbed the 'Boy Who Lived') and had asked Ron Weasley if he could get him Harry's autograph.
Ron agreed to get him Harry's autograph in exchange for Nigel bringing Ron his mail that day, which Nigel did.
It is unknown if he ever got Harry's autograph.
Ron dismissed him after getting his mail and said they would talk about it later.
Nigel then left looking very disappointed.
Nigel was seen supporting champion Harry Potter throughout the Triwizard Tournament .
For instance, when Nigel was cheering for Harry after he emerged from the lake, Draco Malfoy hit Nigel over the head and pulled his hat down over his face in irritation.
Also, despite being only a first year Nigel attended the Yule Ball .
This means he must have been asked by someone much older than him, as third year Ginny Weasley accepted Neville Longbottom 's offer.
Ginny doubted she had to be asked by anyone else and being so young she would not have been allowed to attend otherwise.
Only fourth years or older could attend the ball.
Nigel and Ron supporting Harry during the third task of the Triwizard Tournament

At the end of the year Nigel was supposed to have his first ever Leaving Feast , but due to the circumstances surrounding the Triwizard Tournament and them resulting in the murder of Cedric Diggory , this feast was cancelled and instead a memorial feast was held by Albus Dumbledore for students and staff to pay their respects to the late Diggory and grieve the loss.
At the end of this year Dumbledore had declared, based on Harry Potter's word, that Lord Voldemort had returned to power.
Nigel was amongst the students to believe this claim and not be persuaded otherwise by the Ministry of Magic and the Daily Prophet which in later months would slate Harry and Dumbledore as liars.
The following year, Hogwarts would be put under the watchful eyes of Dolores Umbridge , the newly Ministry-appointed Hogwarts High Inquisitor and Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher.
Umbridge was making the students' lives a misery and was refusing to teach them any practical forms of Defence Against the Dark Arts.
When Harry Potter and Hermione Granger set up an organisation against this Nigel joined and became a part of Dumbledore's Army.
Nigel standing next to Harry during a Dumbledore's Army meeting
When attending the D.A. 's meetings Nigel would often stay close to Harry, whom he looked up to.
With Nigel's enthusiasm in lessons Harry would often use him as a 'test dummy', such as to demonstrate the Stunning Spell.
He also assisted Harry by acting as a look-out as the students left the Room of Requirement at the end of the meetings.
When Dolores Umbridge and her Inquisitorial Squad discovered the D.A. meetings, Nigel was at the front of the class along with Harry.
He was among the students to serve one of Umbridge 's 'medieval' detentions as punishment for being a member of Dumbledore's Army .

Towards the end of the year Fred and George Weasley put their plans of escape into action and Nigel was amongst the crowd of students and staff to witness their departure and cheered them off after they turned a school corridor into a swamp.
Nigel at Quidditch tryouts standing next to Seamus Finnigan and Dean Thomas
During Nigel's third year, his idol Harry Potter became the new Captain for the Gryffindor Quidditch team .
Nigel was present at the Quidditch tryouts that year but did not make the team, however he did not take the news badly and was quite happy with the selected students.
Nigel was later shown to be very supportive of the team.
He was seen cheering loudly for Ron Weasley when he won his first Quidditch match.

He also witnessed Ron and Lavender Brown passionately kissing for the first time in the Gryffindor common room, something which he showed disgust in by poking his tongue out and covering his face with his woolly hat to block his view.
Nigel with Luna Lovegood and Madam Pomfrey raising their wands to the late Professor Dumbledore
Nigel was also still present at Hogwarts when Professor Severus Snape killed the school's current headmaster Albus Dumbledore .

After hearing the news and seeing the Dark Mark floating above the school he and a large group of students and staff gathered around Dumbledore's body, which had fallen from the Astronomy Tower , Nigel arrived at the place with Luna Lovegood and stood with her and Madam Pomfrey whilst the crowd looked on at Harry who had crouched down to Dumbledore.
When the time came, Nigel followed Professor McGonagall 's sign of respect and lit his wand and raised his arm in the air with the crowd of students to show their respects to the late headmaster.
In doing so the combined faculty and students of Hogwarts managed to rid the sky of the over-looking Dark Mark.
It is more than likely that Nigel attended the funeral service that followed afterwards unless his parents pulled him out of school before the year had finished, like some others had done.
Nigel announcing Harry's arrival at Hogwarts
In Nigel's fourth year, he was still at Hogwarts and was a member of Dumbledore's Army.
He was seen on the train ride on 1 September with Seamus Finnigan .
Nigel with D.A. members defending the Wooden Bridge during the battle
On 2 May , he greeted Harry when the latter arrived in the Room of Requirement prior to the Battle of Hogwarts , and also served as a communicator to members of the Order of the Phoenix .
Nigel participated in the battle alongside his friends against the Death Eaters and Voldemort's army of Dark creatures.
Nigel was not listed among the 50 casualties, and presumably survived to witness Harry's final defeat of Lord Voldemort and the end of the Second Wizarding War.

title: Mandrake
paragraphs: A Mandrake , also known as Mandragora , was a magical and sentient plant which had a root that looked like a human (like a baby when the plant is young, but maturing as the plant grows).
When matured, its cry could be fatal to any person who heard it.
The Mandrake was a part of the Solanaceae family of plants.
Description and traits
A baby Mandrake
Whenever unearthed, the root screamed.

The scream of a mature Mandrake when it was unearthed was powerful enough to break glass and would kill any person who hears it, but a young Mandrake's screams would usually only knock a person out for several hours.
They stopped screaming once they were replanted in the soil.
When Hogwarts students studied Mandrakes in Herbology class, Professor Pomona Sprout had her students wear earmuffs to protect their ears from the Mandrake's cries.
Professor Mirabel Garlick had her students put cotton in their ears in the late 19th century .
Mandrakes had to be yanked out of their pots by the leaves and replanted in larger pots as they matured.
According to Professor Garlick, when tucking them into the new pot, the soil should have enveloped the root like a warm, dirty blanket, putting the Mandrake right at ease.
The life stages of the Mandrake
Mandrakes not only resembled humans , but also had similar behaviours to them.
In the 1992-1993 school year at Hogwarts, the school's Mandrakes, at one point of time, became moody and secretive, which indicated that they were reaching adolescence.
Later on, they threw a loud and raucous party, which was comparable to humans when they are teenagers, which made Professor Sprout very happy indeed.
Madam Pomfrey also mentioned the Mandrakes having acne .
Mandrakes were fully matured when they started moving into each others' pots.

Once matured, Mandrake Roots could be cut up to serve as a prime ingredient for the Mandrake Restorative Draught , which was used to return those who have been transfigured , cursed or Petrified back to their rightful state.
Stewed Mandrake was used in potion-making , forming an essential part of most antidotes .
Their leaves were also used in potions as well, including the potion used in the process of becoming an Animagus .
The Dugbog 's favourite food was Mandrake, which led to Mandrake-growers finding nothing but a bloody mess when pulling their plants out of the ground.
Flesh-Eating Slugs were known to favour eating Mandrakes as well.
History
Several deaths have occurred through exposure to Mandrakes.
Before 1890 , someone died in Dogweed and Deathcap after knocking over a Mandrake.
A couple of decades later, Minister for Magic Venusia Crickerly died in 1912 , following a freak Mandrake-related gardening accident.
Furthermore, the Sunday edition of The New York Ghost published on 28 November 1926 reported a Mandrake attack on a Herbologist .
Professor Sprout teaching students how to repot young Mandrakes in Herbology class
Mandrakes were part of the second and third-year Herbology curriculum at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , taught by Professor Pomona Sprout .
Mandrakes were revised again in the fifth year for students' Ordinary Wizarding Levels .
During the 1986-1987 school year at Hogwarts, Professor Sprout taught third year students in Herbology how to handle Mandrakes.

Also during the 1986-1987 school year, Jacob's sibling and Penny Haywood found a hidden Chocolate Frog Card buried in the soil of a potted baby Mandrake in the Herbology Classroom , which Penny uprooted after borrowing some earmuffs from Professor Sprout, with Jacob's sibling collecting the card.
During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts, Jacob's sibling and Liz Tuttle helped Professor Sprout spraying Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent on Mandrakes to prevent slugs from eating them.

Later in the school year, first-year students learnt about Mandrakes presumably in Herbology class, but some of them neglected to use their earmuffs, making it necessary for them to be treated by Madam Pomfrey in the Hospital Wing .
Jacob's sibling helped her take care of them.
Harry and Ron replanting Mandrakes in Herbology
At the start of the 1992-1993 school year , Professor Sprout taught second-year Gryffindor and Hufflepuff students in class how to properly repot baby Mandrakes.
Hermione Granger impressed Professor Sprout with her knowledge of the Mandrake's properties, earning her house points for her house Gryffindor.

During this school year, the school's growth of Mandrakes served the additional purpose of making the Mandrake Restorative Draught , in order to revive all those who had been petrified during the Chamber of Secrets openings.
During the Battle of Hogwarts , Professor Sprout , Neville Longbottom and other students lobbed Mandrakes over the Castle's battlements to attack the Death Eaters .

During the Calamity which affected the wizarding world in the 2010s , Mandrakes were amongst the various magical items caught up as Foundables which had to be dealt with by members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force .
Etymology
Mandrake is from late Old English mandragora , that had the dragon -related description replaced with native drake .
Mandragora , other than referring to the plant, could also mean "a kind of tiny dragon immune to fire ".
It is from the Latin mandragorās , which is from Ancient Greek μανδραγόρας (translit.
mandragóras ), associating with the Old Persian word merdum gija meaning "plant of humans ".
Notes and references

title: Mandrake Root
paragraphs: A Mandrake Root was the root of a Mandrake .
It was a powerful potion ingredient, that was the subject of many Muggle superstitions.
Stewed mandrakes that had matured beyond adolescence were the primary ingredient of the potent Mandrake Restorative Draught , a healing potion capable of curing petrification .

title: Solanaceae
paragraphs: A mandrake , a plant in the nightshade family.

Solanaceae , also known as the Nightshade family, is a family of flowering plants that include over two-thousand seven-hundred individual species, including some of the most commonly eaten foods as well as common potion ingredients.
The plants from this family were well-known for their highly specific soil needs.

title: Cotton
paragraphs: Cotton is a soft, fluffy fibre from the cotton plant, used to make textiles .
History
Professor Mirabel Garlick had her Herbology students put cotton in their ears to protect them from Mandrake cries in the late 19th century .
By the 1986-1987 school year , these cotton balls were replaced in favour of earmuffs .
Notes and references

title: Flesh-Eating Slug
paragraphs: A Flesh-Eating Slug was a dark magical creature very similar to its namesake, the common garden slug.
Description
The spittle of the Flesh-Eating Slug had a corrosive effect on both skin and plants.
History

During the 1989-1990 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Bill Weasley taught a group of sixth-year students about Flesh-Eating Slugs and instructed them on how to defend themselves from the creatures in one of his Defence Against the Dark Arts tutoring sessions.
A Flesh-Eating Slug as depicted on a label of Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent
It was a garden pest, and in 1992 , the Hogwarts gamekeeper Rubeus Hagrid explained to Harry Potter that Flesh-Eating Slugs were ruining all of the school cabbages.
The only known way to get rid of these slugs was by using a specific repellent that could be bought in Knockturn Alley .
The Flesh-Eating Slug was apparently a fairly frightening creature to some, since a Hogwarts student was scared enough of them to turn a Boggart into one.
Flesh-Eating Slugs on a pumpkin
Around Hallowe'en 2010 , Flesh-Eating Slugs appeared in Hagrid's pumpkin patch and ruined some of the newly planted pumpkins .
During the Calamity which occurred in the late 2010s , several Flesh-Eating Slug Foundables were found being guarded by Troll Confoundables .
Volunteer wizards and witches had to overcome these small obstacles by using the Knockback Jinx to knock the Trolls over and allow the slug Foundables to return to the Hogwarts vegetable patches.
Notes and references

title: Individual who died in Dogweed and Deathcap
paragraphs: This individual died after knocking over a Mandrake in Dogweed and Deathcap in Hogsmeade prior to 1890 , while Beatrice Green worked there.
Beatrice took every effort to tell customers not to knock over Mandrakes after that point, including to a student of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry who entered her shop.

title: Dogweed and Deathcap
paragraphs: Dogweed and Deathcap was a shop in Hogsmeade that sold exotic plants and flowers, presumably including the Death-Cap .
History
Originally, Dogweed and Death-Cap was located slightly apart from Hogsmeade, built into a mountainside with its interior supported by the branches of a large tree .
The shop was operated by Beatrice Green in the 1890s .
During her tenure, a customer accidentally knocked over a Mandrake , which resulted in their death .
From that time onward, Beatrice consistently warned visitors never to disturb the Mandrakes.

title: Venusia Crickerly
paragraphs: Minister Venusia Crickerly was a British witch who served as the twenty-first Minister for Magic of the British Ministry of Magic , in office from 1903 to 1912 , being elected at least twice.
Biography
A former Auror , Minister Crickerly was considered both competent and likeable.
She died in office, however, following a Mandrake -related freak gardening accident.
Etymology
Venusia might be a reference to Venus, who was the Roman goddess of love, beauty, desire, fertility and prosperity.

title: The New York Ghost
paragraphs: The New York Ghost was an American wizarding newspaper based in New York .

It had been published daily from at least 1863 and offered an early Sunrise Edition and an evening Sunset Edition, as well as a West Coast Supplement every Thursday and a Divination Supplement every Friday.
In 1926 , a single issue cost 0.03 dragots , while a 12 month subscription cost 5 dragots and was delivered by owl .
Its slogan was "Enchanted Dispatches to the American Wizard".
History
In the 1920s , The New York Ghost reported extensively on claimed sightings and Wizard Hunt for Gellert Grindelwald around the world, including Bratislava , Paris , London , New York , and Caxambu .
It covered local incidents, such as a havoc caused by a Poltergeist in a Nashville diner, as well as international changes, such as the legal Apparition age in Denmark .
It covered varying degrees of entertainment and academic subject matters, from listing Top Apparition locations in Canada to discussing Korean Master Aurologists views on aura .

title: Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent
paragraphs: Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent was a pesticide potion used to get rid of Flesh-Eating Slugs .
It can be purchased in Knockturn Alley , and its slogan was "with slugs out, mandrakes sprout."
History

During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Jacob's sibling and Liz Tuttle helped Professor Pomona Sprout spraying Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent on Mandrakes to prevent slugs from eating them.

During the 1989-1990 school year , Bill Weasley taught a group of sixth-years how to defend themselves from Flesh-Eating Slugs by wielding this particular pesticide against the creatures in one of his evening Defence Against the Dark Arts classes.
A green can of this potion
In the summer of 1992 , Rubeus Hagrid went to Knockturn Alley to buy this product, as Flesh-Eating Slugs were destroying the cabbage crop at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .

While there, he ran into Harry Potter , who had gotten lost after a Floo powder -related accident, and escorted him out of Knockturn Alley back to the Weasley family in Diagon Alley from whom he had become separated.
Another time, when Harry, Ron , and Hermione were discussing that Hagrid might be the heir of Slytherin , Hagrid showed up behind them in the courtyard carrying a can of Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent.

title: Iran
paragraphs: Iran , historically known as Persia , is a country in southwestern Asia , located between Turkey , Turkmenistan , Iraq , Afghanistan , Azerbaijan , Armenia , and Pakistan .
Wizarding world
History
The alchemist Calid and his father Jasichus were from Persia.
Government
Iran was governed by a Ministry of Magic .
Games and sports
Quidditch never caught on there, due to their preference for flying carpets .
Notes and references

title: Banshee
paragraphs: The banshee was a dark creature which could be found in Ireland .
Banshees were Dark spirits that had the appearance of women and their cries were fatal to anyone that heard them.
Drinking the Laughing Potion was an effective defence against them.
The sound of laughter was known to weaken them and ward them off.
The exact reason for their aversion to laughter is unknown, but Cobb theorised that the sound of laughter may simply be intolerable to them, as they are considered creatures of tragedy in folklore.
Biology and description
Banshees had the appearance of a woman with floor length black hair, a skeletal face, and green skin.
They also sported dark clothing that turned lighter in colour as they aged.
A banshee's scream was fatal to the ears, in a manner similar to fully grown Mandrakes .
Most banshees could be presumed to be hostile, as at least one wizard had a Boggart that was a banshee.
However, at least one individual, Duncan Hobhouse , had a Boggart of a creature that was otherwise considered harmless.
Additionally, some banshees were able to communicate with other beings and were willing to uphold their end of a bargain .
There is much that wizarding society does not know about banshees; such as if they are good or evil, or if it's possible to communicate with them.
History
The Bandon Banshee was supposedly defeated by Gilderoy Lockhart , which he described in his book Break with a Banshee ; though he later admitted to stealing credit for his books.
The only thing known about the actual witch who defeated the Bandon Banshee was that she had a hairy chin.
The singer Celestina Warbeck was known to perform some of her shows with a backing group of banshees.
She once had to cancel a Hallowe'en concert one year with Banshees as backup singers.
In 1985 , a swarm of banshees attacked Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry to retrieve the black comb that their leader traded with a maiden centuries ago.
Jacob's sibling and Penny Haywood managed to return the comb to the banshees, allowing them to leave Hogwarts in peace.
Bill Weasley showing fellow sixth-years a banshee in Defence Against the Dark Arts

During the 1989-1990 school year at Hogwarts, Bill Weasley taught his sixth-year friends about banshees and instructed them on how to defend themselves from the creatures in one of his Defence Against the Dark Arts tutoring sessions.
Bill even brought an actual banshee into the classroom to study, with him and his classmates wearing protective earmuffs to prevent them hearing its deadly scream.
Jacob's sibling banished the banshee with the Laughing Potion .

On 31 July 1992 , Mrs Mason "screamed like a banshee" when the owl post letter warning Harry Potter about his supposed underage magic transgression (actually committed by Dobby ) was dropped on her head at 4 Privet Drive , as she suffered from ornithophobia (the fear of birds ).
Seamus Finnigan was afraid of banshees, as his Boggart demonstrated in 1993 .
Seamus also mentioned it when Harry Potter opened the golden egg and heard a screeching sound.

Another possible banshee was the bogle-banshee , mentioned by a student on the " Second Year Essential Knowledge Test " that Gilderoy Lockhart gave his second-year Defence Against the Dark Arts class in 1992 .
During the Wizarding Schools Potions Championship , a banshee drove the Uagadou potions champion mad.

Banshees appeared throughout the wizarding world during the Calamity in the 2010s , in which they acted as Confoundable guards to certain Foundables , such as a portrait of Salazar Slytherin , which belonged at Hogwarts Castle .
Volunteer members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force had to cast the Bombardment Spell in order to repel them, allowing the Foundables to return to their rightful place.
Notes and references

title: Mandrake Mufflers
paragraphs: Mandrake Mufflers was a store at Diagon Alley which presumably sold earmuffs serving as Mandrake mufflers.
A pair of pink earmuffs were placed close to the shop sign.
It shared the same building with Gaberlunzie Garments , Grandma Gramercy's Grandiloquent Gramophones , and Shrew & Scold's Bridal Wear , next to Nell's Bells .
Notes and references

title: Diagon Alley North Side
paragraphs: Diagon Alley North Side was the northern part of Diagon Alley , comprised of the area closest to the Leaky Cauldron and, thus, closest to Charing Cross Road and Muggle London .
Commercial buildings lined the two sides of the cobbled street, and among them stood an archway into the nearby Knockturn Alley .
Several objects on display lined the shopfronts, such as cauldrons, broomsticks and barrels, and hanging above them were signs bearing the names of the shops.
Walking along Diagon Alley North led to the tall white main offices of Gringotts Wizarding Bank , and turning to the left led to Diagon Alley South .
Locations
