title: Modifier
paragraphs: A modifier was a word attached to an incantation to alter the effects of the spell that incantation was used in.
Most frequently, this was in order to increase the raw power of a spell, however it was also frequently used to make the spell target a specific type of person or object.
Known modifiers
Diabolica
The Diabolica modifier was only known to be used in conjunction with the Shield Charm .
Its exact effect was unknown, however Protego Diabolica created a protective ring of black fire that incinerated the caster's enemies whilst leaving their allies unharmed.
Duo
The Duo modifier could be attached to a spell in order to increase its power and sometimes change the appearance of the spell case.
Known Duo spells include:
Homenum

The Homenum modifier appeared to modify a spell to in some way relate to humans , as the Human-presence-revealing Spell , Homenum Revelio , revealed humans in the vicinity and was a modification of the Revealing Charm .
Horribilis
The Horribilis modifier was only known to be used in conjunction with the Shield Charm .
Its exact effect was unknown, however Protego Horribilis , when combined with other spells, could almost completely protect an area from Dark Magic .
Maxima
The Maxima modifier increased the strength of a spell, possibly to its highest intensity.
Mortis
The Mortis modifier, when used in conjunction with the Locomotion Charm , created a curse called the Leg-Locker Curse , which caused the target's legs to lock together.
Mucus
The Mucus modifier appeared to cause spells to specifically affect one's mucus, as in the case of the incantation for the Curse of the Bogies , Mucus ad Nauseam and the spell Mucus Projectum .
Oculus
The Oculus modifier, when used in conjunction with the Mending Charm , Reparo , caused the spell to specifically repair eyeglasses .
Papyrus
The Papyrus modifier, when conjunction with the Mending Charm , Reparo , caused the spell to specifically repair torn pieces of paper.
Piertotum
The Piertotum modifier, when used in conjunction with the Locomotion Charm , Locomotor , created the Animation Charm , Piertotum Locomotor , which could be used to animate non-living objects.
Skullus
The Skullus modifier appeared to cause a spell to only affect a target's head, as when combined with the Engorgement Charm , the spell Engorgio Skullus could be used to swell the head of a victim.
Similarly, the spell Mutatio Skullus likely caused the target's head to mutate in some way.
Solem
The Solem modifier was only known to be used in conjunction with the Wand-Lighting Charm , where it resulted in the Sunlight Charm which could be used to create a blinding flash of sunlight.
Specialis
The Specialis modifier, when used in conjunction with the Revealing Charm , created a spell which revealed any spells that had been performed on objects or potions .
Totalum
The Totalum modifier, when applied to the Shield Charm , created a protective enchantment which provided a certain degree of protection for an area.
When applied to the middle of the Snake-Vanishing Spell , it created a spell which banished snakes in a large area.
Tria
The Tria modifier could be attached to a spell in order to increase its power, more so than could be achieved with Duo , and sometimes change the appearance of the spell cast.
Known Tria spells include:
Virga
The Virga modifier, when used in conjunction with the Revealing Charm , created a spell which revealed any hidden tree branches.
Wibbly
The Wibbly modifier, when used in conjunction with the Locomotion Charm , created a curse called the Jelly-Legs Curse , which caused the target's legs to collapse.
Possible modifiers
Lacarnum
The spell belonging to the incantation Lacarnum Inflamari could be used to set clothing on fire .

It may have been a modified version of the Ignition Spell , Inflamare , as Inflamari appears to be a passive counterpart to Inflamare , however Inflamari is not a Latin word whereas Inflamare is, albeit spell differently.
Muggletum and Inimicum

These were likely modifiers of an unknown repelling charm with the incantation Repello , as the Muggle-Repelling Charm , Repello Muggletum , and Repello Inimicum both prevented certain people or objects from entering an area.
Recanto
The incantation for the Counter-curse to Metelojinx is Meteolojinx recanto .
It is unknown if this means that Meteolojinx recanto is a modified version of Meteolojinx , or if it's simply following a standard form for counter-curses.
Totalus
The word Totalus was possibly a modifier as it has the appearance of being a masculine adjective for the neuter adjective Totalum , which is a known modifier.
In this case, the Full Body-Bind Curse , Petrificus Totalus , would be a modified spell.
Known modified spells with unknown incantations
The Frequensting was a curse and modified version of the Stinging Jinx invented by the Death Eater Antoine Grimalkin .
It was later refined and improved by Antoine's wife and fellow Death Eater Bedilia Grimalkin after she fled the country following Antoine's capture by Ministry forces.
Bill Weasley created a modified version of the Cursed barrier .
Unlike the regular Cursed Barrier, which prevented anyone without a Dark Mark from passing through, Bill's version prevented anyone with a Dark Mark from passing through.
Filius Flitwick invented a modified version of the Ebublio Jinx for the House Points Scramble .
Unlike the regular Ebublio Jinx, this modified version could be looked out of by the individual trapped inside.

Flitwick also modified the Bubble Spell , which normally produced a harmless stream of bubbles, into a version which produced golden bubbles that exploded, throwing a blinding substance into the eyes of the opponent.
There existed a mask which had been cursed with a modified version of the Imperius Curse .
Anyone who looked into the eyes of the mask would fall under its spell and be unable to resist.
Similarly, there was a bottle which was cursed with a modified version of the Bat-Bogey Hex .
Whenever the bottle was opened, a black bat-bogey would chase whoever opened the bottle unless the bottle was recorked.
Notes and references

title: Protego Diabolica
paragraphs: Protego Diabolica was the incantation of a powerful and dangerous protective dark charm that encircled the caster with a protective ring of black fire that incinerated the caster's enemies while leaving their allies unharmed.
The black fire also took the appearance of winged creatures that spread rapidly and were capable of great destruction.
It was similar to, but different from the Fiendfyre Curse .
Description and effects
Krall being incinerated by the fire, due to his disloyalty to Grindelwald

When conjured, the black fire produced by Protego Diabolica followed the caster's control, and could be directed to create a ring of protective fire around the caster and their allies that incinerated any enemy of the caster.

The caster could also control it to attack specific targets in the form of tendrils of fire that extended from the ring, along with having the flames take the form of winged creatures that spread rapidly, and were capable of incinerating an entire city or large area if not extinguished.
The black fire also protected the caster from certain offensive spells from outside of the protective circle.
Vinda Rosier crossing the fire, due to her loyalty to Grindelwald
Krall , having had recently reserved himself from Gellert Grindelwald 's side due to his disloyalty, was incinerated to ash immediately upon entering the black fire created by Grindelwald.

Leta Lestrange was initially allowed to cross through Grindelwald's protective fire by appearing to show loyalty to him, however as she immediately turned on him and Vinda Rosier and destroyed his skull-hookah when she entered, Grindelwald had the flames engulf and incinerate her.
Counter and treatment
Jacob recovering from the effects of this spell in St Mungo's

It was a very rare occurrence for a victim to survive being burned by the flames of Protego Diabolica , requiring the injured victim to undertake proper medical treatment afterwards in order to improve their health and recovery, if the wounds were not instantly fatal to them.
Burn-Healing Paste was insufficient in treating these burns.
The General Counter-Spell could extinguish the black fire.
The flames could also be deflected with the Shield Charm .
History
Grindelwald controlling the fire to separate his enemies from his allies

In early September 1927 , Gellert Grindelwald cast this spell in the Lestrange Mausoleum in Paris to test the loyalty of his followers and kill a number of his enemies, most of whom were Aurors trying to arrest him.
Because they were loyal, Vinda Rosier , Abernathy , Nagel , MacDuff , Carrow , Krafft , Credence Barebone and Queenie Goldstein all passed through the fire into the circle.
Krall , who considered turning against Grindelwald, failed to enter.
Several victims who never attempted to cross either escaped the ring or fell to its wrath.

The black flames were eventually dispelled by the combined efforts of Theseus and Newt Scamander , Porpentina Goldstein , Yusuf Kama , and Nicolas Flamel following Leta Lestrange 's self-sacrifice, effectively saving the entire city of Paris from Grindelwald's fury and destruction.
During the 1990-1991 school year , Jacob travelled to Japan , believing R was after a legendary artefact after he gathered evidence from different captured R members.
He discovered half of the Dark Scroll in a mountaintop cave and was severely burned with Protego Diabolica , with which the Dark Scroll was protected .
Jacob was then sent to St Mungo's back in England , where he was treated for his injuries.

After Healer Miriam Strout healed his burns and saved his life after adjusting his treatments accordingly to the helpful advice by Albus Dumbledore , Jacob told his sibling about his venturing in the cave and that he had deduced that " R " had already been there and took the other half of the scroll in order to brew Dai Ryusaki's mind-enhancing potion , as he only found one torn half of it.

title: Knockback Jinx Duo
paragraphs: The Knockback Jinx Duo ( Flipendo ) was a more powerful version of the Knockback Jinx .
It was twice as powerful as the standard Knockback Jinx, but it was not as powerful as Flipendo Tria .

title: Fumos Duo
paragraphs: Fumos Duo was the incantation for the most powerful version of the Smokescreen Spell .
It could conjure multiple clouds of dark red smoke.
This spell was quite useful in duelling , as the thick smoke hid the target, making it difficult for an opponent to accurately aim their spells through the smoke.

title: Glacius Duo
paragraphs: Glacius Duo was a charm used offensively in duelling to freeze a target enemy in ice.
It was a more powerful version of Glacius , but was not as powerful as Glacius Tria .

title: Incendio Duo Spell
paragraphs: The Incendio Duo Spell ( Incendio ) was a charm that conjured green flames .
It was a stronger variation of the Fire-Making Spell , but not as strong as Incendio Tria .
Overview
This charm was covered in second-year Herbology classes at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , and was useful for burning through cobwebs and incinerating Flesh-Eating Slugs .
Notes and references

title: Lumos Duo
paragraphs: Lumos Duo was a variation of the Wand-Lighting Charm .
It created a focused beam of light from the end of the wand .
Effect
Casting this charm caused an extremely bright, intense beam of light to emit from the tip of the wand , which could be used for a variety of purposes.
For instance, the spell 's light forced ghouls to retreat and hinkypunks to solidify, and therefore could be used as a defensive measure.
The light could also be used to attract Chizpurfles , which were attracted to magic .
History
1993-1994 school year
During the 1993-1994 school year , a spellbook detailing the use of this spell could be found in a storeroom near the Muggle Studies Classroom in Hogwarts Castle for unknown reasons.
During that year, third-year Gryffindor student Ronald Weasley found Professor Burbage 's spellbook and took it.
He then proceeded to read the book and learn this Lumos Duo spell , and used it against several hinkypunks .
He also used it to free Neville Longbottom from the ghoul in the classroom , who was harassing him.
Etymology
The incantation derives from Latin " lumen ", which means " light ", and " duo ", which means " two "; therefore, the incantation comes together to mean " two light " or " light two ".
Notes and references

title: Mucus ad Nauseam Duo
paragraphs: Mucus ad Nauseam Duo was the incantation of a curse that gave the recipient a very nasty cold and runny nose.
It was a more powerful version of the Curse of the Bogies .
The Duo variant of the Curse of the Bogies was also more effective than a single cast of Mucus ad Nauseam Tria .
Effects
Successive casts of Mucus ad Nauseam Duo on the same target would have no further effects.

Casting Mucus ad Nauseam Tria on a target already affected by the Duo variant would intensify the target's cold, while casting Mucus ad Nauseam Uno on a target already affected by the Duo variant would reduce the effects of the cold.
Notes and references

title: Petrificus Totalus Duo
paragraphs: Petrificus Totalus Duo was the incantation of a curse that could be used to temporarily paralyse an enemy target.
It was a more powerful version of the Full Body-Bind Curse , but was not as powerful as Petrificus Totalus Tria .
Notes and references

title: Protego Duo
paragraphs: Protego Duo was the incantation of a charm used to protect the caster from physical and magical attacks alike, and was fully capable of deflecting spells cast at the shield to their original source.
It was a more powerful version of the traditional Shield Charm , although it was not as powerful as Protego horribilis , Protego totalum or Protego Maxima .
Notes and references

title: Stupefy Duo
paragraphs: Stupefy Duo was the incantation of a more powerful version of the Stunning Spell .
Notes and references

title: Ventus Duo
paragraphs: Ventus Duo was the incantation of a stronger variant of the the spell Ventus .
The spell created a stronger jet of spiralling wind than the standard version, which could cause more damage to an opponent in a wizard's duel .
Notes and references

title: Vermillious Duo
paragraphs: Vermillious Duo was the incantation of a charm that produced a jet of red sparks that could be used offensively in duelling .
It was a more powerful version of Red Sparks , but it was not as powerful as Vermillious Tria .
Etymology
The incantation is derived from the English word " vermillion ", a shade of red.
The modifier " duo " applied to the spell means " two ", referring to its higher power than Vermillious Uno .
Notes and references

title: Verdimillious Duo Spell
paragraphs: The Verdimillious Duo Spell ( Verdimillious ) was a charm that emitted green sparks from the tip of the wand .
It was a more powerful version of the Verdimillious Charm .
It held a number of useful purposes and was rather easy to cast.
History
Professor Quirinus Quirrell taught this charm to his first-year Defence Against the Dark Arts class in the 1991-1992 school year along with the Verdimillious Charm and Verdimillious Tria .
Professor Gilderoy Lockhart later revised it with his second-year Defence Against the Dark Arts class the next year .
Effects
The Verdimillious Duo Spell created green sparks that had multiple uses.
One such use was to do damage to an opponent, hence proving very useful in duelling .
These green sparks could also be used reveal objects hidden by Dark Magic in a blinding flash of white light, thereby illuminating the entire room for a short time.
Unlike its precursor, objects revealed by The Verdimillious Duo Spell remained tangible and visible even after the light faded.
Nonetheless, green sparks would still be floating around the enchanted objects for a while after the light disappeared.
Practitioners
Etymology
This incantation is most likely derived from Latin " viridis ", meaning " green " and French " mille ", meaning " a thousand ".
The modifier " duo " means " two " and is common in incantations of increasing power.
Notes and references

title: Wingardium Leviosa Duo
paragraphs: "Diffindo!"
Wingardium Leviosa Duo was the incantation of a stronger variation of the Levitation Charm , a spell which induces levitation in objects.
Known practitioners
Notes and references

title: Human-presence-revealing Spell
paragraphs: The Human-presence-revealing Spell ( Homenum Revelio ) was a charm which revealed the presence of other humans in the surrounding environment.
The spell indicated a body by a marker.
It was also a variation of the Revelio Charm .
Effect
This spell created no flash of light when cast.
When this spell was cast on a person it created an odd sensation.
According to Harry Potter , it felt like " something was swooping low over him, immersing his body in its shadow ".
History
This charm in action
During a conversation after losing a game of Gobstones in the 1986-1987 school year , Talbott Winger realised that he and Jacob's sibling were not alone in the Courtyard .
Talbott then used the spell to reveal the presence of Merula Snyde , who was spying on them under a Disillusionment Charm .

During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Professor Patricia Rakepick taught her fifth-year students this charm in Defence Against the Dark Arts , in preparation for their Ordinary Wizarding Levels that year.
It was used in 1991 and 1993 by Dumbledore , nonverbally , to detect Harry and Ron under the former's Cloak of Invisibility .
On 1 August 1997 , Hermione Granger used this spell at 12 Grimmauld Place after escaping pursuing Death Eaters Antonin Dolohov and Thorfinn Rowle .
On 30 December 1997 , Death Eaters Selwyn and Travers ambushed Lovegood House and Travers used this spell to locate Harry Potter .
It is possible that it was related to the spell Specialis Revelio , and it is very likely that the spell couldn't detect magical creatures such as house-elves , goblins , etc.
Known practitioners
Etymology
Hominum is the genitive, plural form of the Latin word homo , which means "person".
Also in Latin, revelo means "I unveil or reveal" .
Notes and references

title: Protego horribilis
paragraphs: Protego horribilis was the incantation of a powerful protective charm .
Description

It was probably the most powerful version of the Shield Charm , which was used as a protective enchantment against anything approaching the protected area, and against any dark magic , except the Killing Curse , which was unblockable with any Shield Charm and passed through it, presumably leaving holes into the magical shield.
By extended use of a spell , the magical shield could eventually be broken down.
History

This spell was cast by Charms Master Filius Flitwick to protect the boundaries of Hogwarts Castle from the Death Eater 's forces in the late hours of 1 May 1998 , prior to the Battle of Hogwarts that started the next day .
This may have been the spell that the professors cast around Hogwarts Castle to protect it from Dementors and other dark creatures before the Siege of Hogwarts in the 2010-2011 school year .
Known practitioners
Etymology
Latin Protego , "protect", and Horribilis , "horrible, frightful, dreadful"; altogether the charm means "Protect against the horrible".
Notes and references

title: Maxima
paragraphs: Maxima was a magical modifier attached to the end of a spell's incantation used to increase the power of the relevant spell , most likely to its maximum intensity.
However, some spells were different when Maxima was added to the end of the incantation.
Maxima spells were invented separately from the original spell.
List of Maxima Spells
Notes and references

title: Aguamenti Maxima
paragraphs: Aguamenti Maxima was a variation of the Water-Making Spell .
It conjured a powerful jet of water from the tip of the caster's wand .
History
This modified spell was created by Hogwarts Professor and duelling champion Filius Flitwick prior to the 1986-1987 school year .
It was considered to be magic beyond the curriculum of Hogwarts.
It was possibly used by Flitwick during the 1986-1987 Toothill Duelling Club Invitational Tournament to defeat Evelyn Starling .
Known practitioners
Etymology
The incantation is derived from the incantation for its predecessor, " Aguamenti ", and the Latin word " maxima ", which means " very great " or " greatest ".
Notes and references

title: Bombarda Maxima
paragraphs: Bombarda Maxima was the incantation used for the strongest variation of the Bombardment Spell .
It provoked large, violent explosions capable of demolishing entire walls.
History

During the 1990-1991 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , the then Defence Against the Dark Arts Professor , Olivia Green , taught her seventh-years how to use this spell in class, as part of her curriculum focused on both theoretical and practical defensive magic .
Known practitioners
Etymology
See the page for Bombarda . "
Maxima " in Latin means " the largest ".
Notes and references

title: Flipendo Maxima
paragraphs: Flipendo Maxima was the incantation for a more powerful variation of the Knockback Jinx , which threw the target back further and with greater force than the original spell .
History

It was invented by Badeea Ali , with the help of Ben Copper , in the 1989-1990 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , after Ben had asked her to invent a more powerful variation of the Knockback Jinx .
After the spell was finished, Badeea Ali taught Jacob's sibling and Merula Snyde how to cast it in Classroom 3C .
Ben Copper cast this jinx against Patricia Rakepick in the Forest Grove during their duel in an attempt to harm her, but she was able to swiftly block his spell.
During the summer break just before the 1990-1991 school year , Jacob's sibling used this spell to stun a Doxy which was flying around Andre Egwu 's head.
Known practitioners
Notes and references

title: Glacius Maxima
paragraphs: Glacius Maxima was the incantation of a charm capable of deep freezing a target.
It was a more powerful version of Glacius .
Notes and references

title: Lumos Maxima
paragraphs: Lumos Maxima was the incantation to a charm that could be used to produce a blinding flash of bright white light from the tip of the wand , a modified version of the Wand-Lighting Charm .
Casting
This charm creating a large burst of light from the wand tip

To cast this light-creation spell , one had to flick their wand , then draw it back and flick it a second time, after which it would light, as noted in chapter thirty-two of Extreme Incantations by Violeta Stitch .
The spellbook also included a diagram depicting the proper casting of this spell.
History

During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Professor Filius Flitwick taught his fifth-year Charms students this charm in preparation for their upcoming Ordinary Wizarding Levels .
In the summer of 1993 , Harry Potter practised this charm while reading the instructions from Extreme Incantations under his bed covers at 4 Privet Drive .
Known practitioners
Etymology
The incantation is derived from the incantation for its predecessor, " Lumos ", and the Latin word " maxima ", which means " very great " or " greatest ".
Notes and references

title: Snowfall Spell
paragraphs: The Snowfall Spell , also known as the Maxima Snowflake-Making Spell ( incantation unknown ), was a stronger version of the Snowflake-Making Spell that created snowstorms.
History

This spell was invented by Jacob's sibling before Christmas in 1985 , who intended to give the original spell a wider range so they could make it snow at The Burrow , but accidentally ended up creating a snowstorm that almost completely buried both Hogsmeade and Hogwarts Castle under the snow.
Notes and references

title: Snowflake-Making Spell
paragraphs: The Snowflake-Making Spell ( incantation unknown ) was a Weather-Modifying Charm that created snow .
History
Merula Snyde had fond memories of this spell, as it was the only spell her aunt had taught her that couldn't be used to harm someone.
They would cast the spell every Christmas , a tradition which Merula kept up when she attended Hogwarts.
During the 1984-1985 school year Christmas holidays , Merula taught Jacob's sibling this spell so they could put on a show for Molly and Arthur Weasley in the Great Hall .
Later that day, Jacob's sibling performed the spell, with everyone finding it quite lovely.

Just before the 1985 Christmas holidays , Jacob's sibling attempted an amplified version of this spell and inadvertently caused a blizzard that shut down the Hogwarts Express , almost disrupting the holiday plans of the entire school .
When they confessed this to Professor Flitwick , he taught them the counter-spell , which the student successfully cast.
This spell was used unintentionally by Ronald Weasley in 1996 .
He used it whilst practising the spell to turn vinegar into wine in Charms , due to his being distracted by talking to Harry Potter .
Known practitioners
Notes and references

title: Curse of the Bogies
paragraphs: The Curse of the Bogies ( Mucus ad Nauseam ), was a curse that gave the recipient a nasty cold and an extremely runny nose that could cause the victim to collapse if it were not treated.
The cold was accompanied with constant sneezing.
No further casts of this curse had any additional effect on the target, unless the Duo or Tria modifiers were used.
There existed a counter-curse of unknown incantation covered in the Updated Counter-Curse Handbook , Second Revised Edition .
Presumably the Pepperup Potion would cure the effects as well, though the Antidote to Common Poisons was notably reported to work.
History
Harry Potter using this spell against Draco Malfoy in a duel

During the 1988-1989 school year , the Slytherin student Ismelda Murk taught this unpleasant curse to Jacob's sibling on the Hogwarts grounds, in order for her to show her appreciation towards them, for having taught her how to cast various spells beforehand.
Quirinus Quirrell mentioned it to his first-year class in 1991 .

Ron Weasley threatened to learn this curse, then use it on Hermione Granger and Neville Longbottom if they got him and Harry Potter caught roaming the school at night on their way to a duel with Draco Malfoy .
In the same school year, Harry Potter fell ill when Peeves used this curse on him.
Harry had to look for Updated Counter-Curse Handbook in the library to perform the Counter-curse .
Known practitioners
Etymology
" Ad Nauseam " is a Latin term meaning "to the point of nausea".
This implies that the curse makes one produce mucus to the point of them feeling physically ill.
Bogies is plural of "bogy", which in turn is an alternative spelling of "bogey" (plural: "bogeys").
It is British slang for a piece of nasal mucus, booger.
Notes and references

title: Mucus Projectum
paragraphs: "Diffindo!"
Mucus Projectum was the incantation of a spell which had an unclear effect, though, given its name, it possibly involved discharging mucus from the caster's wand .
Notes and references

title: Oculus Reparo
paragraphs: Oculus Reparo was the incantation of a charm that repaired broken eyeglasses .
It was a variant of the Mending Charm .
History

Arthur Weasley used this spell in Diagon Alley in 1992 to repair Harry Potter 's spectacles after Harry broke them when tumbling out of the Floo Network connected to the fireplace in Borgin and Burkes respectively.
Percy Weasley used this spell or a similar one on his own glasses during the final of the 1994 Quidditch World Cup .
Known practitioners
Etymology
The word reparo is the first person singular form of the first conjugation verb ( -are ) reparare , meaning "to renew" or "to revive" in Latin.
The word oculus is the nominative singular form of the word meaning "eye".
Thus, the spell Oculus Reparo roughly means "I renew the eye".

Unfortunately, from a grammatical point of view, this statement is incorrect, because although it follows the common SOV word order, the word oculus is in the nominative singular case, when it should be accusative singular, as it is the object of the sentence.
Note: in Brazilian Portuguese "óculos" [ˈɔ.ku.lʊs] means glasses.
Notes and references

title: Spectacles
paragraphs: Spectacles (also called eyeglasses or glasses ) are composed of two lenses set inside of a frame.
They are worn in front of the eyes in order to correct vision disorders.
Glasses in the wizarding world
Albus Dumbledore , who wore half-moon spectacles
Apart from using spellotape , the charm Oculus Reparo (a variation of the Mending Charm ) could be used to fix broken spectacles.
Harry Potter wore round spectacles, like his father, James
Animagi who wore glasses might have distinctive markings in the same shape as the glasses they wore in human form.

The physical location of these markings seemed to depend on the type of animal one's Animagus form took: Minerva McGonagall , a cat Animagus, had markings around the eyes, and Rita Skeeter , a beetle Animagus, had markings around the antennae.

Wearing glasses would not protect a person from the fatal effect of the Basilisk 's stare, because glasses still allowed one's line of vision to connect directly and clearly with the serpent 's eyes, unlike looking in a mirror or through a camera .
Spectrespecs were a magical type of spectacles that allowed the wearer to see wrackspurts .
Goblins at Gringotts Wizarding Bank examined precious stones through glasses.
Known wearers
Minerva McGonagall wearing glasses
Rita Skeeter wearing glasses
Notes and references

title: Papyrus Reparo
paragraphs: Papyrus Reparo was the incantation of a charm that could be used to mend torn pieces of paper.
It was a variant of the Mending Charm .
History
This spell was used by Newt Scamander in 1927 to restore a torn postcard from Tina Goldstein addressed to Queenie Goldstein .
This informed Newt of Tina's whereabouts in Paris.

During the 1986-1987 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Nymphadora Tonks , Jacob's sibling and Ismelda Murk all tried this spell on pieces of paper torn from a copy of Have Yourself a Fiesta in a Bottle!
by Squawk , but they failed due to the rest of the book being missing.
Later, after the students found the rest of the pages and the cover, Jacob's sibling used this spell again and succeeded in mending the book.
Etymology
Papyrus may refer to a paper-like material made from the papyrus plant ; a term also used to refer to documents written on such material.
Papyrus is one of the oldest forms of "paper" known, dating back to ancient Egypt .
Reparo is the incantation of the Mending Charm , derived from the Latin verb "I restore, or repair".
Notes and references

title: Specialis Revelio
paragraphs: The Specialised Revealing Charm ( Specialis Revelio ) was a charm that revealed any spells performed on objects or potions.
It was a variation of the Revelio Charm .
History
Possibly used nonverbally by Dumbledore when he poked his wand into the purple armchair at Horace Slughorn's house to reveal that the wizard had transfigured himself into the armchair.
Known uses
Practitioners
Etymology
Latin specialis , "particular; individual" and revelare (present tense revelo ), "unveil".
Altogether the incantation may read as "[to] reveal the particulars [of]".
Notes and references

title: Vipera Totalum Evanesca
paragraphs: Vipera Totalum Evanesca was the incantation of a stronger variation of the Snake-Vanishing Spell , a spell which vanished snakes .
The spell was modified, possibly by Salazar Slytherin himself, to be able to vanish large groups of snakes at once.
The spell was written on the scroll he used to hide the snakewood tree branch .
Known practicioners
Notes and references

title: Flipendo Tria
paragraphs: Flipendo Tria was a jinx that threw the target longer than its less powerful Flipendo and Flipendo Duo .
It resembled a small tornado.
The spell targeted multiple opponents.
Notes and references

title: Glacius Tria
paragraphs: Glacius Tria was a charm used offensively in duelling to freeze a target enemy.
It was the most effective version of Glacius , being more powerful than Glacius and Glacius Duo .
Notes and references

title: Incendio Tria
paragraphs: Incendio Tria was the incantation of a charm that conjured blue flames ; the average first or second-year Hogwarts student could perform this spell .
This charm was an improvement over both Incendio and Incendio Duo , and consequently created larger flames than either spell.
Notes and references

title: Mucus ad Nauseam Tria
paragraphs: Mucus ad Nauseam Tria was the incantation of a curse used to give a target a head cold that increased in severity with each successive cast.
It was the most powerful version of the Curse of the Bogies , though not when cast by itself.
Effects
When this version of the Curse of the Bogies was cast once on a target by itself, it appeared identical to Mucus ad Nauseam Uno .
However, if the recipient was already affected by any variation of the curse, including Tria , then each successive cast of Mucus ad Nauseam Tria would intensify the recipient's cold.
After Mucus ad Nauseam Tria had been cast on a target, casting the Duo or Uno variations would reduce the cold's intensity, as if the Tria version was never cast.
Mucus ad Nauseam Tria was the most powerful version of the Curse of the Bogies, because it was the only variant that intensified the effects with each consecutive cast.

Because of the way these variants worked, in order to give the target the worst cold in the shortest amount of time, one must cast Mucus ad Nauseam Duo on the target , followed by Mucus ad Nauseam Tria successively from then on.
Notes and references

title: Petrificus Totalus Tria
paragraphs: Petrificus Totalus Tria was a curse that could be used to paralyse up to at least three targets.
It was the most powerful version of the Full Body-Bind Curse , being more effective than Petrificus Totalus and Petrificus Totalus Duo .
Notes and references

title: Ventus Tria
paragraphs: Ventus Tria was the incantation of a stronger variant of the spell Ventus .
The spell created a stronger jet of spiralling wind than either the standard version or Ventus Duo , which could cause more damage to an opponent in a wizard's duel .
Notes and references

title: Vermillious Tria
paragraphs: Vermillious Tria was the incantation of a charm that produced a jet of red sparks that could be used offensively in duelling .
It was the most powerful version of Red Sparks .
Etymology
The incantation is derived from the English word " vermillion ", a shade of red.
The modifier " tria " applied to the spell means " three ", referring to its higher power than Vermillious Duo .
Notes and references

title: Verdimillious Tria
paragraphs: Verdimillious Tria was the incantation of a charm that emited green sparks from the end of the wand.
It was the most powerful version of the Verdimillious Charm .
These sparks could be used offensively in duelling to harm an opponent.
As it was stronger than both Verdimillious and Verdimillious Duo , the green sparks would go a further distance than its precursors.
History
Professor Quirinus Quirrell taught his first-year Defence Against the Dark Arts class this spell along with the Verdimillious Charm and Verdimillious Duo Spell .
Professor Gilderoy Lockhart later revised it with his second-year class of the same subject.
Practitioners
Etymology
This incantation is most likely derived from Latin " viridis ", meaning " green " and French " mille ", meaning " a thousand ".
The modifier " tria " means " three ".
Notes and references

title: Virga Revelio
paragraphs: Virga Revelio was the incantation of a variation of the Revelio Charm , a spell which caused hidden things to appear.
The spell was modified, possibly by Salazar Slytherin himself, to be able to reveal tree branches, specifically the snakewood tree branch that he had hidden.
The spell was written on the scroll he used to hide the snakewood tree branch .
Known practicioners
Notes and references

title: Ignition Spell
paragraphs: The Ignition Spell ( Inflamare ) was used to light a target via a small fireball .
Notes and references

title: Muggle-Repelling Charm
paragraphs: The Muggle-Repelling Charm ( Repello Muggletum ) was a charm that prevented Muggles from seeing or entering an area.
Any non-magic person that would get close to the vicinity of the enchantment would remember something urgent to do and leave.
Known uses
Every inch of the Quidditch Trillenium Stadium was covered in Muggle-Repelling Charms for the 1994 Quidditch World Cup in Dartmoor .
Hermione suggested that Durmstrang Castle might be protected by Muggle-Repelling Charms.
According to Newton Scamander in Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them , Muggle-Repelling Charms were used on the habitats of some magical creatures.

Also according to him, the powers of certain magical creatures - such as the kelpie or Pogrebin - could negate the effects of the Muggle-Repelling Charm, due to their own innate powers existing to attract humans.
Hermione Granger and Harry Potter used this spell to protect their campsite from 1997 to 1998 while hunting Horcruxes .
Known practitioners
Notes and references

title: Repello Inimicum
paragraphs: Repello Inimicum was the incantation of a charm that, when cast in combination with Protego Maxima and Fianto Duri , conjured up a barrier of magical protection around the place the caster is trying to protect.
Effect
Bodies crossing the boundaries of the barrier of this spell disintegrated on the spot and spells cast at it if they are unable to break the barrier, create large, resonating explosions.
History of use

This spell was cast by Charms Master Filius Flitwick to protect the boundaries of Hogwarts Castle from the Death Eater forces in the late hours of 1 May 1998 , prior to the Battle of Hogwarts that started at midnight the next day .
The Death Eaters , on Voldemort 's command, started bombarding the magical protection with spells, and they were ultimately brought down by a spell cast by Voldemort .
Etymology
Notes and references

title: Metelojinx
paragraphs: Metelojinx was the incantation of a Weather-Modifying Charm that created a small, localised thunderstorm within an area.
Known uses
Known practitioners
Etymology
It most likely comes from a portmanteau of the study of weather, meteorology , and jinx , a dark charm.
Notes and references

title: Meteolojinx recanto
paragraphs: Meteolojinx recanto was the incantation to a counter-charm that caused weather effects caused by Weather-Modifying Charms such as the Atmospheric Charm to cease.
History

In 1997 , Arthur Weasley suggested that Reginald Cattermole (actually his son Ron in disguise) use this spell to stop the raining in the office of Yaxley , who was the head of the Department of Magical Law Enforcement while Lord Voldemort was in control of the British Ministry of Magic .
He commented that it had worked previously for Bletchley .
It is unknown if Ron tried it or if he succeeded in stopping the rain.
During the Calamity , the Welsh witch Wendy Wunderwind taught this spell to members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force so they could use it in greenhouses.
Known uses
Known practitioners
Etymology

The incantation for this spell is likely a portmanteau of meteorology , the study of weather, which originates from the Greek word metéōron , "high in the sky", and jinx , which is a charm, as well as the English verb recant (from the Latin recantare , of which the first person singular present indicative active is recanto ), "to withdraw or retract".
Notes and references

title: Cursed barrier
paragraphs: The cursed barrier ( incantation unknown ) was a curse that formed a barrier which prevented anyone without a Dark Mark from passing.
This curse was used by an unknown Death Eater during the fight against Order of the Phoenix around the Astronomy Tower .
History
Bill Weasley picked up this curse from a Dark wizard he fought during one of his Gringotts assignments.
He modified it into a version that instead blocked anyone with a Dark Mark .
It was used to prevent the members of the Order from interfering with Draco Malfoy 's attempt to assassinate Albus Dumbledore .
This curse could not be broken with the Reductor Curse .
The curse created a barrier around a certain area, preventing anyone from passing through it and throwing them backwards on contact.
Only Death Eaters with a Dark Mark on their arm could pass through the barrier unhindered.
If the area around the barrier collapsed, the barrier would be dispelled.
Severus Snape , though secretly a loyal member of the Order of the Phoenix, was able to pass through because he had been branded with the Dark Mark.
Notes and references

title: House Points Scramble
paragraphs: Head of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
The House Points Scramble competition was held during the 1986-1987 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry to challenge the students in the four house values.
Each student who completed a trial would be awarded house points , and thus the competition was considered to be able to upset the existing house point leaderboard.
History
Headmaster Albus Dumbledore announced the tournament to the school in the Great Hall .
He explained that each Head of House would organise a trial, and that students could complete the trials in any order they wish, or only complete some of the trials.
He also mentioned that the student who completed all the trials the fastest would win bonus house points.
Jacob's sibling and Nymphadora Tonks held a bet between the two of them that whoever was fastest would win bragging rights.
Jacob's sibling won this bet, as they completed all the trials and were the fastest overall.
McGonagall's trial
McGonagall with the caged pixies
Professor Minerva McGonagall 's trial consisted of the students having to dodge a pack of pixies whilst flying on a broomstick , for which they would earn fifty points.
This was made difficult by the fact that McGonagall had enchanted the pixies with the Oppugno Jinx , which made them more deadly and aggressive.
Additionally, the students couldn't use magic to defend themselves, and if a pixie touched them, they would have to start the whole trial over again.
Jacob's sibling and Tonks both passed first try, and Penny passed as well, but Merula never managed to complete this trial and got frustrated, eventually quitting the trial.
As a bonus reward, McGonagall also gave the winning student an insight into one of the other trials, although they could only pick one trial to get an insight for.
Flitwick's trial
Jacob's sibling trapped in a modified Ebublio Jinx
Professor Filius Flitwick 's trial involved the students simply having to answer a riddle for fifty house points.
However, there were many factors which made this more difficult.
Flitwick trapped the students with the Ebublio Jinx , though he modified it to be see-through, as he didn't think students would like being trapped in a dark bubble.

Secondly, each student only got three guesses and, if they got the answer wrong, then they would lose ten house points, meaning if the student used up all three of their guesses but still got the answer right, they would only be able to get thirty house points.
The riddle was:
A single glance will make me change, so no-one knows my true face.
And even though you want to hide, I know the corners of your mind.
What am I?
The correct answer was a Boggart , as no-one knows its true face and it can peer into one's mind to see one's worst fears.
Jacob's sibling, Tonks, and Penny all passed the trial, though it is unknown if they all managed to get the maximum point amount or not.
Sprout's trial
Professor Pomona Sprout 's trial was different to the others, as it required the students to be paired up to complete the trial.
Jacob's sibling paired up with Penny, who had been waiting for a partner.
Each person in the pair had to answer a question, however they could choose to let the other person answer their question for them.

If they did so, and the other student got the answer right, they would earn fifty points, however if they chose to answer it themselves instead and got it right they would only earn twenty-five points.
It is unknown if Jacob's sibling and Penny chose to trust each other with their answers or not, and equally it's unknown if they got the answers right.
The first question they were asked was: 'The mandrake is part of which family of plants?'
The correct answer was the Solanaceae family, also known as the nightshade family.
The second question was: 'What's another name asphodel goes by?'
The correct answer was 'Royal Staff'.
Snape's trial
Three of the Sleeping Draughts

Professor Severus Snape 's trial initially seemed simple, as he presented the students with several different Sleeping Draughts of various concentrations and asked them to identify which one was safe to drink.
If they succeded, they would get fifty points, and if they failed they would sleep until the effect of the potion they had chosen wore off.
This was, however, a trick question.
Although one could identify the concentration, and therefore the strength, of a Sleeping Draught based off of its consistency and the shade of purple, that wasn't what the question was asking.

Instead, Snape was asking which potion was safe to drink, and the correct answer was all of them, as Sleeping Draughts are not harmful, as even at higher strengths, they only put the drinker to sleep for longer.
It was for the same reason that a student couldn't answer 'none of them'.
Jacob's sibling, Tonks, and Penny all guessed correctly, however Tulip Karasu failed this trial.
Notes and references

title: Bubble Spell
paragraphs: The Bubble Spell ( incantation unknown ) was used to conjure a stream of bubbles from the tip of the wand .
History
Flitwick's conjured bubbles
Professor Filius Flitwick created a variation of this spell that produced golden bubbles prior to the 1986-1987 school year , which was considered to be magic beyond the curriculum of Hogwarts .
It was possibly used by Flitwick during the 1986-1987 Toothill Duelling Club Invitational Tournament to defeat Evelyn Starling .
He later used this variant of the spell to conjure decorations for a Christmas tree in the Great Hall in December 1991 .
In early 1993 , Ron Weasley 's broken wand was emitting large purple bubbles at one point, but from his dismayed reaction it would seem that this was a malfunction rather than a spell he was casting.

title: Imperius mask
paragraphs: This mask had been cursed with a modified version of the Imperius Curse .
Anyone who looked at the mask's eyes would fall under its spell and be unable to resist.
Simply breaking line of sight with the mask would prevent the curse from activating, however.
History
The mask's curse had been rendered dormant by the late 1980s , and it was stored in Classroom 3C along with a number of other cursed artefacts.
During the 1980s, a Gryffindor girl stole a number of these artefacts and reactivated the curses on them in a misguided effort to create an interesting Defence Against the Dark Arts lesson.
The Hogwarts Diary became aware of this and informed its keeper , Jacob's sibling , of the issue.
Jacob's sibling managed to track this mask to the Astronomy Tower , where they encountered Professor Severus Snape , who had tracked the mask with a Dark Detector .
Together they managed to place a box over the mask, preventing either of them from falling under its spell.
Snape then took the mask back to Classroom 3C and once again neutralised the curse.

title: Curses and Counter-Curses
paragraphs: Curses and Counter-Curses was a book written by Professor Vindictus Viridian , which explained how to cast various dark charms , including jinxes , hexes , and curses , as well as their counter-curses .
History
Harry Potter saw a copy for sale at Flourish and Blotts on 31 July 1991 , and was intrigued by the thought that it might help him to curse his cousin, Dudley Dursley .
Rubeus Hagrid dragged him away from it, telling him that he was not allowed to perform magic around Muggles , and that he was still too young to pull off such advanced spells.
A copy was seen on a bench in the Great Hall during the 1991 Christmas feast .

title: Disarming Charm
paragraphs: The Disarming Charm ( Expelliarmus ) was a charm that forced whatever an opponent was holding to fly out of their hand.
It was common to see this spell used in duels to make an opponent lose their wand .
History
An individual being deprived of their wand with this charm
It is not known precisely who created the Disarming Charm.
Some wizarding historians claimed that it may have been invented by Merlin himself, while others claimed that its first widespread use was in Madagascar in the 11th century .

Even if any of this is true, the fact remains that it was not very popular until 1379 , when Elizabeth Smudgling - the most likely inventor , in the opinion of Miranda Goshawk - used it in a duelling contest in Dartmoor .

The Disarming Charm became Harry Potter 's signature spell , and it notably caused the final defeat of Lord Voldemort during the Battle of Hogwarts by rebounding his Killing Curse , because the Elder Wand recognised Harry as its master through the spell connection, and thus strengthened the Disarming Charm to the point that Voldemort's Killing Curse backfired onto himself.
Effects
Harry casting a powerful disarming charm indicated by the scarlet jet of light
The Disarming Charm caused whatever an opponent was holding at the time, usually a wand , to fly high out of their hand.
A single Disarming Charm could also disarm multiple opponents if they were all in close proximity to one another.
Multiple or exceptionally powerful Disarming Charms were even able to send a target flying, sometimes to the extent of knocking them unconscious.
Known uses
Successful
Unsuccessful
Known practitioners
Etymology
Latin expellere (ex = out, pellere = to drive), meaning "to drive out" and "arma" meaning "weapon".
Expelliarmus actually means "to drive out the weapon".

title: Madagascar
paragraphs: Madagascar is an island country in the Indian Ocean , off the southeastern coast of Africa .
History

Although the origins of the Disarming Charm were obscure, some wizarding historians suggested that the charm originated in Madagascar, claiming that it was in widespread use there in the 11th century .
However, others claimed that Merlin was the spell's inventor, while yet others (such as Miranda Goshawk ) found it much more likely that it was invented by Elizabeth Smudgling in 1379 .
Magical education
Malagasy wizards and witches may have had the option to attend Uagadou in Uganda, as it accepted students from all over Africa.
Magical games and sports
The Malagasy National Quidditch team faced off against the Syrian National Quidditch team in the final of the 1974 Quidditch World Cup .

When Royston Idlewind , the International Director of the International Confederation of Wizards Quidditch Committee , appeared in the private box reserved for dignitaries and officials, the audience protested his highly unpopular wand ban by making their Dissimulators produce loud raspberry noises, then transforming them back into wands from which they had been transfigured .
Idlewind resigned on the spot, and thus although Madagascar ultimately lost, their fans still celebrated that night.
Notes and references

title: Elizabeth Smudgling
paragraphs: Elizabeth Smudgling was an English witch who lived in the late 14th century .
An accomplished duellist , she was, in the opinion of Miranda Goshawk , the most likely inventor of the Disarming Charm .
Biography
Smudgling was born in England in the mid-to-late 14th century .
In 1379 , she entered a duelling competition held in Dartmoor , in which wizards and witches from across Europe came to partake.
According to contemporary reports, the contest (which was held at night, so as to avoid attracting the attention of Muggles ) featured duelling of a level of skill that was almost unprecedented.
Eventually, only four competitors remained, including Smudgling and three wizards.

The judges of the competition - distinguished warlocks and wizards from several different countries - delivered rousing speeches to the contestants before the final three duels commenced, telling them, " Think big!
Think bigger than you have ever thought before!
Let us see this night magic on such a scale, that future generations will envy us for having witnessed such greatness! "
The first semi-finalists then moved in front of the crowd.
Keeping in mind the judges' advice to think big, the first wizard transformed himself into a bull and charged the second , who escaped death by quickly turning himself into a viper .
The second wizard bit the first on the leg, sending him crashing to the ground in pain.
Next, the second wizard faced the third , and brought a great storm cloud down from the sky, drenching his opponent in freezing-cold rain and forcing him to evade bolts of lightning.
The third wizard then got the idea to call a powerful cyclone, which not only blew away the storm, but also the judges, most of the spectators and several trees.
Elizabeth Smudgling disarms the third semi-finalist
It took several hours for everyone to regroup.

Frightened of what the third wizard might do for his encore, the judges attempted to talk Smudgling out of challenging him, telling her that it might be easier if they simply gave him the cup before anyone else got hurt, but she refused.
The judges award Elizabeth Smudgling the title of " Supreme Dueller "
Smudgling and the third wizard then went up against each other.

On the count of three, the wizard began a long, complex incantation that would have caused a mountain to break out of the ground and fall upon Smudgling's head had he been given the opportunity to complete it.
However, Smudgling beat him to the punch, quickly murmuring the incantation for the Disarming Charm and sending his wand flying out of his hand.
She was awarded the title of " Supreme Dueller " and the Disarming Charm became one of the most useful combative spells in any duellist's repertoire.

title: 1974 Quidditch World Cup
paragraphs: The 1974 Quidditch World Cup was an international Quidditch sporting event that took place in the summer of 1974 .
It was the 417th edition of the World Cup.
It was won by the Syrian Quidditch team .
History

At the time of the World Cup, the International Director of the ICWQC was Royston Idlewind , a former Chaser who was part of the Australian Quidditch team when they won the Quidditch World Cup in 1966 .

Since he had been appointed to the post, he had been introducing a series of draconian regulations regarding crowd control, the worst of which was the ban of all wands from the stadium except those carried by ICWQC officials, something that earned him the wizarding world 's dislike and distrust.
Many fans threatened to boycott the 1974 World Cup in protest, but seeing as empty stands were Idlewind's secret ambition, their strategy was not effective.

The World Cup duly commenced and the crowds that attended carried with them not their wands , but a new style of musical instrument called a Dissimulator : a tube-like object that issued bright lights and colourful puffs of smoke in national colours and emitted loud cheers for the teams being supported.
For the first few matches of the tournament, very few wizards showed up, but those that did brought along Dissimulators, enlivening the match considerably.
The Dissimulator craze grew, as did the crowds.
On the day of the final match between Syria and Madagascar , the stands were packed with a record crowd of wizards, each carrying his own Dissimulator.
When Royston Idlewind appeared in the Top Box , a hundred thousand Dissimulators emitted loud raspberries turned back instantly into the wands they had been concealing all along.
Humiliated by the mass flouting of his pet law, Royston Idlewind resigned immediately, amid celebrations.

title: Royston Idlewind
paragraphs: Royston Idlewind was a former star Chaser of the Australian team in the 1960s .

In 1971 , he was appointed International Director of the International Confederation of Wizards Quidditch Committee , but later resigned after the draconian regulations regarding crowd control he imposed were flouted en masse by the spectators of the final of the Quidditch World Cup in 1974 .
Biography
Quidditch career
Royston Idlewind was born in Australia , sometime before 1949 .
In the 1960s , he was "Australia's star Chaser " - in which capacity, he was noted to have endured many jinxes , something that fuelled his dislike of spectator crowds later in his life.
He was also part of the winning Australian squad during the 1966 Quidditch World Cup .
As International Director of the ICWQC
In 1971 , Royston Idlewind was named International Director of the International Confederation of Wizards Quidditch Committee .

Upon his contentious appointment, he immediately issued the statement that the only thing he disliked about Quidditch was the crowds, thus gaining the wizarding world 's dislike and distrust - this petty dislike soon turned into outright hostility when Idlewind passed a number of draconian regulations on crowd control, the worst of which was the ban of all wands from the stadium except those carried by ICWQC officials.
Many fans threatened to boycott the 1974 Quidditch World Cup in protest, but seeing as empty stands were Idlewind's secret ambition, their strategy was not effective.

The World Cup duly commenced and the crowds that attended carried with them not their wands , but a new style of musical instrument called a Dissimulator : a tube-like object that issued bright lights and colourful puffs of smoke in national colours and emitted loud cheers for the teams being supported.
For the first few matches of the tournament, very few wizards showed up, but those that did brought along Dissimulators, enlivening the match considerably.
The Dissimulator craze grew, as did the crowds.
On the day of the final match between Syria and Madagascar , the stands were packed with a record crowd of wizards, each carrying their own Dissimulator.
When Royston Idlewind appeared in the Top Box , a hundred thousand Dissimulators emitted loud raspberries turned back instantly into the wands they had been concealing all along.
Humiliated by the mass flouting of his pet law, Royston Idlewind resigned immediately, among celebrations.
Later life
Idlewind seemed to have retired from public life sometime after that.

After the incident of the Reappearance of the Dark Mark , shortly after the final of the 1994 Quidditch World Cup , he re-emerged briefly to give a statement to the Daily Prophet about how the latest goings-on proved him right about how wands should be confiscated during international Quidditch matches.

title: International Director
paragraphs: International Director was the title given to the chairman of the International Confederation of Wizards' Quidditch Committee .
It was an appointed office.
History
The International Director of the ICWQC between 1971 and 1974 was Royston Idlewind , a former Chaser who was part of the Australian Quidditch team when they won the Quidditch World Cup in 1966 .
He introduced a series of draconian regulations regarding crowd control, the worst of which was the ban of all wands from the stadium except those carried by ICWQC officials.
Idlewind's pet law was humiliatingly flouted en masse during the final of the 1974 Quidditch World Cup , which led to his resignation.

title: International Confederation of Wizards Quidditch Committee
paragraphs: The International Confederation of Wizards Quidditch Committee ( ICWQC ) was an international regulatory body, subject to the International Confederation of Wizards , that oversaw international Quidditch competitions, such as the World Cup .
Namely, it located suitable venues, arranged transportation for spectators, and provided policing for the games themselves.
It was also the ICWQC that chose the referees for World Cup matches.
History

The ICWQC was created following the implementation of the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy in 1692 , which made the Quidditch World Cup a security risk, as the mass congregation of so many wizards entailed exposure to Muggles .
Following mass protests and threats to the International Confederation of Wizards , this committee was set up to deal with the most problematic logistical issues.
Regulations on the size and nature of national team mascots in the World Cups had long been a source of debate at the highest levels of the ICWQC.

In 1995 , a motion to restrict mascots to " herbivores, creatures smaller than a cow and nothing that breathes fire " was defeated by an overwhelming majority, and Quidditch supporters have been resistant to any meddling as far as team mascots are concerned.
The Committee frowned upon the ceremonial burning of their broomsticks by Japanese teams following a defeat as a waste of good wood.

title: Dissimulator
paragraphs: A Dissimulator was a wizarding musical instrument which first appeared at the 1974 Quidditch World Cup .

Taking the form of multicoloured tubes, these devices emitted loud cheers and puffs of smoke in national colours, and were used by audience members to show support for their preferred teams during matches.
History

They started to be used during the 1974 Quidditch World Cup , after Royston Idlewind , International Director of the International Confederation of Wizards Quidditch Committee , passed a number of draconian regulations on crowd control, the worst of which was the ban of all wands from the stadium except those carried by ICWQC officials.

When Royston Idlewind appeared in the Top Box during the final between Syria and Madagascar , the hundred-thousand witches and wizards in the audience made their Dissimulators produce loud raspberry noises and then turned them back into the wands from which they had secretly been Transfigured .
Idlewind resigned on the spot and the wizarding world rejoiced.
As of 2014 , leaving unattended wands in the form of Dissimulators in any house common room at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry was sufficient grounds to have said Dissimulator confiscated.

title: 1379 duelling contest
paragraphs: This duelling contest was held in 1379 , in Dartmoor , Devon , England .
Witches and wizards from across Europe came to partake, and featured duelling of a level of skill that was almost unprecedented.

An English witch, Elizabeth Smudgling , won this contest with a single Disarming Charm (a charm that, in the opinion of magical theoretician Miranda Goshawk , was of Smudgling's own making) and was subsequently awarded the title of " Supreme Dueller ".
History
This contest was called together on Dartmoor , in Devon , in the year 1379 .
It was held at night, so as to avoid attracting the attention of Muggles , and gathered master duellists from all over Europe .
The judges of the competition were distinguished warlocks and sorcerers from several nations.
After the wizards arrived, the duelling competition duly commenced.
The duelling was noted, by witnesses, to have been of a standard that few had ever seen before.
As the contest progressed, only four contestants remained: the English witch, Elizabeth Smudgling , and three wizards.
The first semi-finalist facing the second semi-finalist
Before the four semi-finalists began their duels, the judges intervened with rousing speeches, telling them to think big and to display great magical prowess in the three duels that would follow.
The first semi-finalists then moved in front of the crowd.
Keeping in mind the judges' advice to think big, the first wizard transformed himself into a bull and charged the second, who escaped death by quickly turning himself into a viper .
The second wizard bit the first on the leg, sending him crashing to the ground in pain.
The second semi-finalist facing the third semi-finalist
Next, the second wizard faced the third , and brought a great storm cloud down from the sky, drenching his opponent in freezing-cold rain and forcing him to evade bolts of lightning.
The third wizard then got the idea to call a powerful cyclone, which not only blew away the storm, but also the judges , most of the spectators and several trees.
It took several hours for everyone to regroup.

Frightened of what the third wizard might do for his encore, the judges attempted to talk Elizabeth Smudgling out of duelling him, telling her that it might be easier if they simply gave him the cup before anyone else got hurt, but she refused.
Elizabeth Smudgling disarming the third semi-finalist
Smudgling and the third wizard then went up against each other.

On the count of three, the wizard began a long, complex incantation that would have caused a mountain to break out of the ground and fall upon Smudgling's head had he been given the opportunity to complete it.
However, Smudgling beat him to the punch, quickly murmuring the incantation for the Disarming Charm and sending his wand flying out of his hand.
She was awarded the title of " Supreme Dueller " and the Disarming Charm became one of the most useful spells in any dueller's repertoire.

title: Warlock
paragraphs: Albus Dumbledore - Former Chief Warlock of the Wizengamot
Warlock was a very old term that had two meanings: to describe a wizard of unusually fierce appearance, or as a title denoting particular skill or achievement.
It originally denoted one learned in duelling and all martial magic or was given as a title to a wizard who had performed feats of bravery (as Muggles were sometimes knighted ).
It was sometimes incorrectly used as interchangeable with the term "wizard".
There also existed the position of "High Warlock", though it is unknown if this was an official title or merely a popular designation.
History

In The Tales of Beedle the Bard , Albus Dumbledore mentioned an old magazine called Warlock at War - this was written by Brutus Malfoy and was essentially concerning the war he felt was between pure-bloods and Muggles .
The term here may have been used to draw on the fact that warlocks were skilled in warrior magic, as well as it being used synonymously with wizard.
Also in the book, there was a story called The Warlock's Hairy Heart , which concerned a warlock engaging in Dark Magic .
Dumbledore claimed this was to show that he was an accomplished wizard regardless of his darker inclinations.
The Sunday edition of The New York Ghost published on 28 November 1926 reported a dispute by warlocks due to the Crystal Ball Regulation at the time.
The Sunrise Early Edition of The New York Ghost published on 30 May 1927 had an article located on page 3, column 2 regarding Alaskan warlocks being suspected of contraband .
Harry Potter saw some "wild-looking" warlocks in the Leaky Cauldron in 1993 .
Known warlocks
Fictional warlocks
Etymology
The Anglo- Saxon waerloga or "oathbreaker", which passed through a Middle English form of warloghe or warlach to become warlock , has two components, waer "covenant", and loga "betrayal".
The latter is derived from leogan "to lie", and may consequently have commonalities with Loge/Loki, the Norse God of Mischief and betrayer of Asgard.
The word could possibly derive from the Norse word vardlokkur, meaning "Wise Man" or "Wise Wizard".

More specifically, a man with the power of binding spirits by channelling or using tools such as runes and knot-magic, as well as a label for the Gate Keepers or Guardians who protected spiritual knowledge and wisdom.

title: Human to bull spell
paragraphs: This spell ( incantation unknown ) was a Human Transfiguration , that turned a human into a bull.
History
During the international duelling contest in 1379 , the first semi-finalist used this spell on himself in his duel against the second semi-finalist .
Once transformed into a bull, he proceeded to charge his opponent, who only managed to escape death by turning into a viper and biting the first wizard-turned-into-bull.
If a wizard turned himself into an animal, he was endowed with the animal's brain, and started thinking like the animal, the only exception being Animagi .

title: Cattle
paragraphs: Cattle , commonly referred to as cows (female) and bull (male), are the most common type of large domesticated ungulates and are domestically raised as livestock for meat, dairy animals for milk and other dairy products, and as draft animals used in drawing heavy loads.
History

During a duelling competition in 1379 , a wizard transformed himself into a bull, but was defeated by another wizard , who changed himself into a viper and bit the first wizard, thereby causing the bull-wizard to lose.
A cow was mentioned in the famous French play Hélas, Je me suis Transfiguré Les Pieds by the French wizard Malecrit .
In the play, the character Grenouille says to the character Crapaud that he cannot help him as he is to play Keeper in an upcoming Quidditch match that same day.
The Hogwarts Express passes fields full of cows during its trip from London to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
In 1995 Rubeus Hagrid brought half a dead cow to feed to the Hogwarts Thestral herd during his Care of Magical Creatures class.
Dragons such as the Peruvian Vipertooth have been known to feed on cows, and Hebridean Blacks have been known to carry off cattle.
