title: Fat Friar
paragraphs: The Fat Friar was a wizard , who attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in his youth, and was Sorted into Hufflepuff .
He was a jolly man and very forgiving.
He devoted his life to religion and, after his death, returned to the school as the house ghost of Hufflepuff House .
Biography
Lifetime
The Friar was born no earlier than 982 , presumably somewhere in the British Isles .
At the age of eleven, the Friar became a student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in Scotland .
He was Sorted into Hufflepuff House and was taught by Helga Hufflepuff in the magical arts the seven years that followed.
At some point in his life, he joined the clergy as part of a mendicant religious order, meaning that he spent his life begging in the name of charity.
Apparently, given his physically large appearance, he indulged in the pleasures of food and drink.
The Fat Friar's kindness was to be his undoing.
He was executed because senior churchmen grew suspicious of his ability to cure the pox merely by poking peasants with a stick, and his ill-advised habit of pulling rabbits out of the communion cup.
Post-mortem
The Fat Friar after his death
The Friar returned from the dead as a ghost , and returned to Hogwarts Castle , where he became the house ghost of his former House, Hufflepuff .
He has thus far spent the majority of his afterlife within the castle walls along with the other Hogwarts ghosts.
After his death, the Fat Friar retained his kind and joyful demeanour.
He eagerly welcomed new students to the school and offered assistance whenever needed.
The Fat Friar participated in planning Sir Nicholas's 493rd deathday party when Erling the Great , a friend of his, visited Hogwarts.
Knowing that Sir Nicholas and Erling shared the same deathday, he eagerly suggested that the two hold a joint party, but Erling rejected the idea.
Nevertheless, the Friar guided Erling on a tour of Hogwarts, including the Charms Classroom and the dungeons .
During their respective parties, when he saw that neither was going well, he gathered them together and again proposed a merged celebration, to which they finally agreed.
During the 1988-1989 school year , Penny Haywood and her friend consulted with the Fat Friar in the Great Hall to inquire if he knew anything about Duncan Ashe or the Marauder's Map .
He recommended they seek Sir Nicholas for help finding the map, as he himself was unaware.
Later during that same school year, Penny's friend and Merula Snyde spoke to him in the Hufflepuff common room to ask if he had seen Peeves .
He offered to assist but unfortunately could not provide much help in locating Peeves, commenting that he would know more about curing peasants of the pox.

Shortly before the Start-of-Term Feast on 1 September 1991 , the ghosts came across the first years waiting for Professor McGonagall , while discussing whether Peeves should be allowed to attend the Feast (for he had given the house elves quite a bit of trouble, throwing food and breaking dishes).
The Friar was excited to see the new students, and smiled around at them.
He later attended the Feast, and waved merrily at students being Sorted into Hufflepuff , notably Hannah Abbott .
On 2 September , the Friar haunted the Charms corridor , chanting aloud as he hovered around.
Fat Friar at Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington 's five-hundredth Deathday Party

In the evening of 31 October 1992 , the Friar attended Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington's five-hundredth Deathday Party , where he engaged in conversation with a knight with an arrow sticking out of his forehead.
This year, the Friar could be usually seen strolling around the Grand Staircase .
The House ghosts of Hogwarts
In the afternoon of 1 September 1994 , the Hogwarts ghosts gathered to decide whether Peeves should be allowed to attend the Start-of-Term Feast.

The Fat Friar wanted to give him another chance, but both Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington and the Bloody Baron decided against it, as it was Peeves and he could not and did not want to change, and therefore did not deserve a second chance.
As a result, Peeves wreaked havoc in the kitchens, spilling soup all over the place and scattering pots and pans everywhere, scaring the house-elves that were present.
The Friar around the First-floor corridor
By 1995 , there was a tetraptych of the Friar hung in the first-floor corridor.
He would frequently haunt this area during this school year.
It is unknown what he did with the rest of his time.

After the Educational Decree Number Twenty-Eight was passed on 21 April 1996 , the Fat Friar saw Dolores Umbridge fruitlessly trying to get access to the Headmaster's Tower , as the tower had sealed itself against her and later told Ernie Macmillan about it.
It is safe to assume that like all other residents of Hogwarts that the Friar did not like Umbridges's presence in the school.
The ghosts of Hogwarts at Albus Dumbledore's funeral
The Fat Friar was present in the castle on 30 June 1997 when Death Eaters invaded the school.
It is unknown if he assisted in the ensuing battle or not.
Albus Dumbledore , Headmaster of Hogwarts , was killed at the hands of Severus Snape in the former's plan on top of the Astronomy Tower.
The Hogwarts ghosts were some of the known attendees of his funeral in early July, which most likely included the Friar.
On 1 August 1997 , the Ministry of Magic was taken over by Lord Voldemort and his Death Eaters .

By 1 September 1997, Severus Snape was made Headmaster of Hogwarts while two of his fellow Death Eaters , siblings Alecto Carrow and Amycus Carrow became the Muggle Studies and Defence Against the Dark Arts teachers respectively.
The Carrows were put in charge of all discipline and punishments, which were violent.
Many students had bruises, cuts, scars, or other forms of injuries from the two evil siblings.
It is likely the Friar, as did the Heads of House , tried to protect the pupils from Alecto and Amycus.
Harry Potter's final defeat of Lord Voldemort and the end of the Second Wizarding War
On 2 May 1998 , the Battle of Hogwarts ensued after Lord Voldemort learned Harry Potter was in the premises.

The ghosts, likely including the Friar, attended a gathering in the Great Hall , in which Professor McGonagall gave instructions on evacuation of underage students and Kingsley Shacklebolt organised the participants for battle.
Later on, the ghosts gathered at the Great Hall, joining the mass mourning over the dead.
When the Second Wizarding War came to an end, it is possible that the ghosts (including the Friar) celebrated Harry's victory and Voldemort's demise .

During a Calamity surge in December 2020 focused on Grim Fawley 's memories of Christmases spent at Hogwarts with ghosts and portraits of the Hogwarts founders , the Fat Friar became a Foundable , with members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force managing to return him to his original time.
After his Foundable was returned, the Friar suddenly developed a clear memory of Grim advising him to "mind the portraits ".

Believing that he had just had this conversation with Grim in the present due to the clearness of the memory, the Friar informed Professor Minerva McGonagall , although she informed him that there was no sign of Grim or any other intruder at Hogwarts despite his insistence that the conversation had just taken place.
Minister for Magic Hermione Granger theorised that Grim had attached a false memory to the Friar's Foundable, realising that the target didn't need to be alive to receive such messages.
Physical description
Fat Friar laughing
As a ghost, the Friar was pearly-white and slightly transparent, like all other ghosts.
He had short brown hair, which he wore with a small tonsure.
At first sight a monk, he was dressed in a habit held by a rope belt.
He was fat and short, and usually carried a mug with him.
Personality and traits
The Friar was very cheerful and welcoming, and happily greeted new students at Hogwarts.
He also tended to find something to value in anyone and look past their faults, as he always insisted with the other ghosts to let Peeves attend the Start-of-Term Feasts despite his many wrongdoings.
He also appeared to be quite sociable, meeting and engaging in conversation with fellow ghosts during Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington 's five-hundredth Deathday Party .
He also seems to have some House pride, as he happily reminisced about his "old House" when welcoming first-years .
Despite this, he was always resentful of the fact that he was never made a cardinal .

His overly kindness has proven to be his undoing, as he would heal the pox simply by poking with a stick, and pull rabbits out of the communion cup, showing recklessness in terms of concealing his wizardry.

title: Bloody Baron
paragraphs: The Bloody Baron (d. 11th century ) was a wizard who attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in the Founders ' time and was Sorted into Slytherin House .
After Hogwarts, he fell in love with Helena Ravenclaw , but she did not love him in return.
He was sent by Rowena Ravenclaw to find Helena in Albania , but Helena refused to return with him and so he killed her in a rage.
When he realised what he had done, the Baron committed suicide with the same knife.
After his death , he became one of the ghosts that haunts Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , and the house ghost of Slytherin House.
Covered in Helena Ravenclaw's blood to this day, he earned himself the moniker of "Bloody Baron".
Biography
Early life
The Baron was born into nobility, no earlier than 982 .

At the age of eleven, the Baron became part of one of the first generations of students at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in Scotland , which, at that time, was still being run by its original Founders.
He was Sorted into Slytherin House and was educated in the magical arts by Salazar Slytherin for the seven years that followed.
Sometime around this time the Baron met Helena Ravenclaw , daughter of Rowena Ravenclaw , whom he fell in love with, though she always rejected his advances.
Death
Later on in his life, Helena, after stealing a diadem belonging to her mother that increased the intelligence of the wearer, ran away to Albania .
Around this same time, Rowena fell fatally ill, although legend has it that it was a broken heart, possibly caused by her daughter abandoning her.
Rowena ordered the Baron to go after her, which he did, eventually finding her hiding in a forest.
After he had found her, the Baron tried to compel her to return with him, but she refused, and, in a fit of rage, he killed her.
Overcome with grief, he proceeded to take his own life with the same weapon he used to stab Helena.
Post-mortem
The Bloody Baron in his blood-stained clothes standing next to the other House ghosts

The Baron, as well as Helena, now known as the Grey Lady , both returned from the dead as ghosts, and returned to Hogwarts Castle , where they became the house ghosts of their former Houses, Slytherin and Ravenclaw respectively.
The Baron had been remorseful of his actions ever since, and carried heavy chains as a sign of penance.
Nobody else seemed to know why he was covered in blood, not even the other two Hogwarts ghosts .

For unspecified reasons, presumably related to his apparently violent, dangerous nature, the Baron had gained Peeves 's respect and was the only one, besides Professor Dumbledore, who could give him orders.
According to Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington , groaning and clanking in the Astronomy Tower was a favourite pastime of the Baron's.
Also according to Sir Nicholas, the Bloody Baron had many times frightened a young Slytherin student in the Slytherin common room .
The Bloody Baron speaking to several Slytherin students in the Potions Classroom

In their search for the Marauder's Map , Jacob's sibling , along with Slytherin students Merula Snyde , Ismelda Murk , Barnaby Lee and Liz Tuttle , went to the Potions Classroom to ask the Bloody Baron about Duncan Ashe .
The Baron revealed that Duncan was a ghost.
Later during the year, Merula and Jacob's sibling spoke to him in the Slytherin common room to ask if he had seen Peeves .
However, he refused to part with any information about Peeves and was not much help to them.
The Baron at the 1991 Start-of-Term Feast
On 1 September 1991 , the Baron attended the Start-of-Term Feast, where he sat next to first year Draco Malfoy , who did not look too pleased with the seating arrangements.

A while before midnight on 12 September 1991, the Bloody Baron passed twice by the Fat Lady's Corridor, frightening Neville Longbottom , who was sleeping in the corridor because he had forgotten the new password to get into Gryffindor Tower .
Shortly prior the Hallowe'en feast on 31 October , the Baron haunted the Dungeons .

In the evening of 4 June during their quest to save the Philosopher's Stone from Lord Voldemort, Harry Potter , Ronald Weasley , and Hermione Granger , all under the Cloak of Invisibility , were intercepted by Peeves who threatened to call Argus Filch if whoever that was there did not show themselves.
Harry Potter, in a hoarse whisper, proceeded to impersonate the Baron.
The Bloody Baron attending Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington's five-hundredth Deathday Party
It can be assumed that the Baron attended the Start-of-Term Feast with the other ghosts, as they seem to do every year.
On the evening of 31 October 1992 , the Baron attended Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington 's five-hundredth Deathday Party .
The other ghosts appeared to avoid him during the celebration.
This was most likely due to his ghoulish blood-stained appearance and the shackles he wore.
He spent Christmas day strolling the dungeons by the Slytherin Dungeon .
In the afternoon of 1 September 1994 , the Hogwarts ghosts gathered to decide whether Peeves should be allowed to attend the Start-of-Term Feast .
The Fat Friar wanted to give him another chance, but both Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington and the Bloody Baron decided against it.
As a result, Peeves wreaked havoc in the kitchens , spilling soup all over the place and scattering pots and pans everywhere.
Later in the year, the Baron encountered Harry Potter and Ron Weasley in the North Tower , while they were talking about Sybill Trelawney 's alleged predictions of Harry's death.
The Bloody Baron in the Potions dungeon
By 1995 , there was a tetraptych of the Baron hung in the dungeon cupboard .
He would frequently haunt this area of the Dungeons during this school year.

During the Start-of-Term Feast , on 1 September 1995 , Ronald Weasley managed to inadvertently insult Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington , by saying the ghost was afraid of the Bloody Baron when he said he would never dream of seeking an argument with the Baron.

A week later, on 7 September , Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington looked for the Baron to see if he could dissuade Peeves from dropping a bust of Paracelsus on top of anyone who passed the corridor in which the bust stood.

In the early hours of 22 April , 1997 , the Bloody Baron saw Albus Dumbledore return to the Castle from one of his missions to find Lord Voldemort 's Horcruxes , and reported it to Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington .
He later retreated to the Astronomy Tower where he liked to groan and clank.
On 2 May 1998 , the Battle of Hogwarts ensued after Lord Voldemort learned Harry Potter was in the premises.

The ghosts, likely including the Baron, attended a gathering in the Great Hall , in which Professor McGonagall gave instructions on evacuation of underage students and Kingsley Shacklebolt organised the participants for battle.
Later on, the ghosts gathered at the Great Hall , joining the mass mourning over the dead.
In December 2020 , during the Calamity , the Bloody Baron suddenly developed a clear memory of Grim Fawley after the return of the Baron's Foundable to his original time.
He grumbled that Grim had "invaded his mind", being overheard by Neville Longbottom , who sent an owl to Harry Potter regarding the situation.
However, the Baron refused to speak any further about the issue when questioned by Harry.
Physical description
The Bloody Baron's ghoulish appearance, bound in his chains
As a ghost, the Baron was very pale, pearly-white and slightly transparent.
He had wide, staring, black eyes and a gaunt face.
He dressed in robes covered in silver bloodstains, and carried chains in a final act of penitence for having murdered Helena Ravenclaw .
He sported a curly powdered wig, fashions closer to the 17th century than the 10th, and carried his sword.
He spoke in a hoarse whisper.
Personality and traits
During his lifetime, the Baron was described by Helena Ravenclaw as a " hot-tempered man ".
He insisted on having his way in interactions, responding with violent uncontrolled anger when contradicted.
As a ghost, he was frightening and most people did not seem to enjoy his presence, not even his fellow ghosts .

However, he seemed to have a cordial, if not friendly, relationship with the ghost of Sir Nicholas de Mimsy Porpington , despite Ronald Weasley 's allegations of the latter being " terrified " of him.

The Baron seemed to be intolerant towards Peeves , who was scared of him, and could not bear his lack of civilisation, putting " his foot down " over the Poltergeist 's potential presence at the 1994 Start-of-Term Feast .

He also seemed to have a great deal of House pride; before Harry Potter 's arrival at Hogwarts, Slytherin had won the House Cup for six years in a row, and the Baron had become " unbearable " according to Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington .
Notes and references

title: Theophilus Harlow
paragraphs: Theophilus Harlow (fl.
1890s ) was a Dark wizard and Victor Rookwood 's right-hand man in the Rookwood Gang in the late 19th century .
Biography
On 2 September 1890 , Harlow accompanied Victor Rookwood at his meeting with Ranrok , the goblin leader of a rebellion .
He later tried to back Victor's attempts to abduct the new fifth-year student from the Three Broomsticks Inn , but was dissuaded by the owner Sirona Ryan with the support of her patrons.
Harlow was torturing Hippogriffs , including Highwing , when he again encountered the fifth-year and the Gryffindor student, Natsai Onai , who began an independent investigation into the criminal.
The duo rode off on the backs of two Hippogriffs while Harlow unleashed two bolts of the Killing Curse targeting them, much to their surprise and horror.
Theophilus Harlow blackmailed numerous denizens of Hogsmeade.
Harlow walked into Gladrags Wizardwear and asked employee Otto Dibble for a non-existent order.
With the employee distracted, he stole Dibble's letter about his engagement to the owner's daughter, Rosie .

He blackmailed him into letting him steal luxurious clothing every now and then for his " lady friend " or else he would tell Mr Hill about Dibble's engagement, putting his employment and relationship in jeopardy.
He also attacked Agabus Philbert for speaking out against the Rookwood Gang.
He petrified and stole his late wife's ornately bound book of poetry, laughing while the widower helplessly watched.
Harlow kidnapped the husband of Daisy Rabe after she refused to use her position as a Gringotts Wizarding Bank security guard to extort her colleagues for treasure within the vaults.
Mr Bickle had grown tired of Harlow's schemes and sought to help Daisy and all those the criminal had hurt.
Harlow had become aware that the Bickle family were conspiring against him.
He confronted Mr Bickle and murdered him in front of his son .
Archie attempted to run away but was captured by Harlow and his Ashwinders .
The Dark wizard ordered that the boy be executed for what he had witnessed but his henchmen were too disturbed at the thought of murdering a child.
The Ashwinders guarding Archie wasted enough time deliberating who would kill him that the fifth-year and Natty rescued him.
Theophilus Harlow sent a fake letter to Natty claiming to be from Mrs Bickle, which stated they could find evidence on Harlow at Cape Manor .
Natty and the fifth-year quickly deduced that this letter was fake and ran to confront Harlow at the manor.
The Dark wizard explained his respect for them, despite how they interfered in his business operations.
Harlow boasted of his "problem-solving skills" before he duelled them.
The duel concluded with Harlow casting the Killing Curse and the student firing a spell back, and their spells interlocked.
The fifth-year triumphed and the Dark wizard was defeated.
A nearly incapacitated Harlow rose from the ground and cast the Cruciatus Curse in a last effort to kill the fifth-year.
However, Natty transformed into her gazelle Animagus form and jumped into the path of the curse .
She writhed in pain as her mother, Mudiwa Onai , comforted her, while Officer Ruth Singer subdued the Dark wizard.
Theophilus Harlow was sent to Azkaban for his many crimes.
Personality and traits
Theophilus was Rookwood's murderous, solicitous right-hand man, an unapologetic bully who thrived on cruelty.
He was arrogant, condescending, and entirely devoid of compassion, even for children.

title: Highwing
paragraphs: Highwing was a female Hippogriff that lived in the 19th century .
Inhabiting the Highlands of Scotland in the 19th century , she regularly found herself the target of wizard poachers , though she was ultimately saved and tamed by an unidentified student .
Biography
Between 1886 and 1890 , Highwing was rescued from poachers by Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry student Poppy Sweeting .
Afterwards, she resided in the area around Hogwarts, where Poppy cared for her and thought of her as her best friend.
Poppy introduced Highwing to her friend .
Poppy Sweeting was very concerned about her, telling the student she wanted Highwing to be as far away from whatever the poachers were up to as possible.
In 1890 , Highwing was restrained by poachers and kept in Falbarton Castle .
She and another Hippogriff were rescued by Natsai Onai and her friend , after which Highwing became that friend's mount.
Notes and references

title: Natsai Onai
paragraphs: Natsai "Natty" Onai (b. 1874 / 1875 ) was an African witch who lived during the late 19th century .

She originally attended Uagadou , but later transferred to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , where she was sorted into Gryffindor house , following her mother Mudiwa 's appointment as a professor of Divination at the school.

Since September 1890 , she, as a fifth-year student, became determined to overthrow a criminal activity in the Scottish Highlands led by Victor Rookwood by collecting evidence to expose Theophilus Harlow , a Dark wizard heavily involved in the operation, and delivering it to Officer Singer , an authority figure, much to the concern of many.
Biography
Early life
Natsai was born in Africa in 1874 or 1875 to Mudiwa Onai and her husband .
As an only child, she was raised in Matabeleland , among a tribe, often wandering the Matobo Hills with her father, who was a giraffe Animagus .
She also observed her mother, a skilled Divination practitioner, using her abilities to protect their tribe from hostile neighbours.
Uagadou School of Magic, where Natsai first enrolled and Mudiwa taught Divination
When Natsai was nine years old, her father was killed by local bandits while protecting her.
Following his death , Natsai and her mother relocated to Uganda , where she began her magical education at Uagadou and Mudiwa became the Professor of Divination there.
During her time at the school, Natsai learned to become an Animagus , taking the form of a gazelle .
Her mother believed her Animagus form manifested as a gazelle because, like the animal, Natsai adapted well.
Natsai, however, believed it was because she could sense danger and always kept her wits about her.
The first transformation was unnerving for her, as she experienced a searing pain and a strong double heartbeat.
However, with each subsequent transformation, the process became easier.
Eventually, she no longer felt any pain and found comfort in her animal form, having fully mastered the ability to become an Animagus.
Fourth year
Just before her fourth year , she transferred to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry when her mother took up a role as professor of Divination .
She had to learn how to use a wand at Hogwarts, as hardly anyone at Uagadou used one, and Natsai still found wandless magic to be more instinctive and convenient.
It took her weeks to get anything right when she transferred but it kept getting easier.

In terms of adaptability to the new school, Natsai found herself becoming more accustomed to and adjusting to the environment by walking around the school and surrounding areas, exploring and wandering about.
She became knowledgeable of the school grounds, with Professor Weasley remarking in the following school year that she knew the region well, despite having only been there for a year.
However, she was still not fully adjusted to a few things, such as snowfall , as snow was uncommon in her homeland of Matabeleland.
Fifth year
During the 1890-1891 school year , Natsai took Ancient Runes as an elective class, which her mother had chosen for her.
On 2 September 1890 , the first lesson day of the school year, when the new fifth-year student arrived at their Charms class , Natsai invited them to sit beside her, where a seat was available.

At the beginning of the class, Professor Ronen asked a warm-up question, and Natsai handed the new student the study book for an answer, which the professor briefly confiscated before returning it to them.
He then led the class outside for a refreshing activity: a game of Summoner's Court .
Natsai and the new student played the game together.
At the end of the lesson, they spoke briefly, and she told the student she was impressed with their skills.
However, Professor Ronen noted that she had seemed somewhat distracted recently.
Natsai and her friend being provoked in Hogsmeade
Later that day, Natsai was a possible combatant during the troll attack on Hogsmeade , had she been invited by the student to visit Hogsmeade .
However, it was also possible that they could have invited Sebastian Sallow instead.
If it was indeed her and not Sebastian, then later after the fight, she brought the new student to the Three Broomsticks Inn for Butterbeer .
The inn was soon entered by the leaders of the Ashwinders - a criminal gang , Victor Rookwood and Theophilus Harlow .
The two came specifically to provoke and intimidate the new student.
Sirona Ryan , the bartender and owner of the Three Broomsticks, intervened to protect Natsai and the student, and firmly forced Rookwood and Harlow to leave the inn.
Not long into the school year, Natsai realised the harm the Ashwinders had inflicted upon the wizarding community , especially through their alliance with Ranrok , a goblin rebel.
Determined to take action and become part of the solution, she resolved to stand against their operations.

She and the new fifth-year snuck into Falbarton Castle , one of the headquarters of the Poacher Pack and the Ashwinders, where she intended to find evidence of Harlow's criminal activities so that she could report him to Officer Singer .
She succeeded, Summoning a letter outlining illicit plans straight from Harlow's hands before fleeing.
Highwing and another hippogriff , freshly freed by Natsai and her friend
On their way out, they discovered two imprisoned Hippogriffs - one of them being Highwing .
The two freed them and escaped by riding the Hippogriffs out of the castle, while curses , including the Killing Curse , were hurled at them by the pursuing Ashwinders.
After the skirmish, Natsai brought the letter she retrieved to Officer Singer, but unfortunately, it was not sufficient evidence for the authorities to take action against Harlow.
Natsai became more determined than ever to bring Harlow down, recognising him as a significant part of Rookwood's criminal operations in Scotland .
In her gazelle Animagus form, she was able to safely spy on Harlow and Rookwood without being detected and continued to gather more evidence, which she delivered to Officer Singer.
However, as gazelles were not native to the British region , rumours began to circulate about a gazelle sighting.
These rumours eventually reached her mother's ears at Hogwarts, raising concern.
During one of her discussions with Singer, the officer mentioned Mr Bickle , a Scottish wizard who had also been collecting evidence on Harlow, hoping to dismantle his operation.
Johanna Bickle , grieving over the death of her husband and the disappearance of her son
After hearing this, Natsai and her new fifth-year friend visited Mr Bickle's house, only to find his wife Johanna in mourning.
Mr Bickle had been killed by Harlow, and their son Archie had gone missing.
Natsai and her friend tracked Archie down and found him imprisoned in the basement of one of Harlow's hideouts.
Archie revealed that he had witnessed his father's murder and had fled, only to be captured and held there until his rescue.

He was safely returned to his mother, who expressed her gratitude but also warned Natsai and her friend about the dangers of confronting Harlow, fearing they might suffer the same fate as her husband.
At the same time, Natsai's mother, having learned from Officer Singer about her daughter's efforts to take down Harlow, became alarmed.
She insisted that Natsai must stop and forbade her from leaving the castle for Hogsmeade in the future, much to Natsai's frustration.
Natsai, however, went against her mother's command.

Despite Mudiwa saying that she had foreseen Natsai's fall in her gazelle form, Natsai did not listen - believing it might not be true as her mother had claimed her Sight to control her many times before.

Determined to continue her path of stopping the criminals, Natsai had her friend visit Mr Bickle's associates: Daisy Rabe , Otto Dibble , Agabus Philbert ; in hopes of gathering more information, while she followed a few wizards from the Ashwinders to the Hog's Head .
Natsai, while spying on the Ashwinders at the Hog's Head, was soon discovered and captured by them.
She was imprisoned in their hideout alongside another detainee, Isko Rabe , the husband of Daisy Rabe.
Meanwhile, her friend, returning from visiting Mr Bickle's associates, found Natsai missing and began tracking her footprints.
The trail led to the Ashwinders' hideout, where they found and freed both Natsai and Mr Rabe, allowing them all to escape the cell.
Afterwards, the friend informed Natsai that from the visits, it had become clear that Rabe, Dibble, and Philbert had all been extorted by Harlow into carrying out his commands.
The two brought this information to Officer Singer and recounted everything that had happened.
Officer Singer said she would look into the matter, but also ordered them to refrain from further involvement with criminal investigations, insisting such matters were best left to the authorities.
Natsai, hoping for forgiveness, told her mother about the event.
Professor Onai supposedly shared the story with her colleagues , and word soon spread around the school.
Contrary to Natsai's hope, her mother may have grown even less forgiving.
Meanwhile, she came to realise that Officer Singer had taken no action against Harlow, who had only grown more powerful.
Determined to see justice done, Natsai resolved to put an end to his operations, whether the authorities acted or not.
Harlow, aware that it was Natsai and her friend who had freed the Hippogriffs, liberated Mr Rabe, and independently investigated his operation, began to take direct action to stop them.
Natsai received a letter , purportedly from Mrs Bickle, requesting a meeting at Manor Cape to share further information.
However, Natsai quickly discerned that the message had not come from Johanna Bickle, but from Harlow himself, intended to lure her into an ambush.
Natsai in her mother 's arms after taking the Cruciatus Curse
Despite this, Natsai and her friend proceeded to Manor Cape as instructed.
As expected, Harlow was waiting for them.
A fierce duel ensued, during which they ultimately gained the upper hand and subdued the criminal.
In a final act, Harlow rose and cast the Cruciatus Curse at Natsai's friend.
Reacting instinctively, Natsai transformed into a gazelle and leapt into the curse's direction, taking it herself.
This was witnessed by two witches who had followed Natsai to Manor Cape: her mother and Officer Singer.

Professor Onai immediately rushed to her daughter, now collapsed on the floor and returned to her human form, while Officer Singer, having witnessed the illicit use of an Unforgivable Curse , promptly arrested Harlow.
Following the incident, Natsai required a period of rest and recovery, during which she used a wheelchair .
She was on the mend, according to Nurse Noreen Blainey , and stayed indoor as her mother insisted.
Physical description
Natsai Onai had deep brown skin and dark brown eyes.
Her hair was styled in short, neat twists.
She had an oval-shaped face with high cheekbones and her eyebrows are gently arched.
Personality and traits
Natsai was described as a fierce competitor and a gifted student.
According to Lenora Everleigh, she had a knack for solving riddles.

She was also brave and stood for what was right and for protecting what she loved, even if it meant breaking the rules, as seen when she continued to fight against Theophilus Harlow despite warnings and prohibition from her mother and Officer Singer.
Her bravery also shone through when she instinctively put herself in the path of a curse to protect her friend.
Magical abilities and skills
Notes and references

title: Otto Dibble
paragraphs: Otto Dibble was a wizard who lived in the late 19th century .
Biography
He worked as an associate in Hogsmeade.
One day, he had been working as an associate in Gladrags Wizardwear when Theophilus Harlow entered.
He went to the back to check upon a non-existent order, and when he came out, Harlow had taken the letter from his fiancé Rosie Hill .
Dibble was told that his relationship with Rosie Hill and his continued employment was contingent with his co-operation.
As a result, he resorted to "creative bookkeeping" to cover the thefts by Harlow from his boss Augustus Hill .
Weeks later, a student asked him for information, and he told the student to look for the letter and destroy it.
After the letter was destroyed, Rosie and Otto eloped.
Notes and references

title: Augustus Hill
paragraphs: Augustus Hill (fl.
1890s ) was the shopkeeper of Gladrags Wizardwear in Hogsmeade during the late 19th century .
Augustus was unrelenting and always responded with positive feedback to any choice of attire.
Notes and references

title: Rosie Hill
paragraphs: Rosie Dibble (née Hill ) was a witch who lived in the late 19th century .
Biography
Rosie Hill had been engaged to Otto Dibble , her father, Augustus Hill 's, employee, for six months by 1890 .

However, their engagement was kept a secret from her father, as Dibble feared that, despite Hill's kind demeanour, he would lose all perspective regarding his daughter and would fire him in addition to preventing him from ever seeing Rosie again due to his "grave betrayal."
Dibble hoped that he could earn enough money to secure himself a stable lifestyle before they told Hill of their engagement, although Rosie longed to be able to share their love with her father.
In response to a letter that Dibble had sent her, Rosie sent a letter on her monogrammed pink stationary expressing her love for Dibble and her hopes that they could reveal their relationship soon.
Dibble was reading this letter at Gladrags Wizardwear when Theophilus Harlow entered.
Although Dibble managed to hide the letter behind the counter, Harlow distracted him by sending him to the back in search of a non-existent order before stealing Rosie's letter for himself.

Harlow blackmailed Dibble into letting him steal luxurious clothing every now and then for his " lady friend " or else he would tell Mr Hill about Dibble's engagement, putting his employment and relationship in jeopardy.

Weeks later, a Hogwarts student learned of Dibble and Rosie's situation, with Dibble telling them to look for the letter and destroy it so that it couldn't be used to blackmail him or expose his and Rosie's relationship before they were ready.

After the letter was recovered and destroyed by the student, Rosie and Otto eloped, although Dibble claimed in a later owl to the student that they had decided to inform Mr Hill of their engagement first, to which he was supportive.
Notes and references

title: Theophilus Harlow's lady friend
paragraphs: This witch was a romantic partner of Theophilus Harlow who lived in the late 19th century .
Biography

In the hopes of being allowed to steal luxurious clothing every now and then for his "lady friend," Theophilus Harlow blackmailed Gladrags Wizardwear employee Otto Dibble by distracting him by sending him to the back in search of a non-existent order before stealing a letter written by Dibble's secret fiancé Rosie Hill .
Harlow threatened that, if Dibble refused to let him steal the clothing, he would tell Rosie's father, Augustus Hill , about Dibble's engagement, putting his employment and relationship in jeopardy.
Notes and references

title: Agabus Philbert
paragraphs: Agabus Philbert was a Scottish wizard who lived in the late 19th century in Hogsmeade .
Biography
Agabus Philbert lived in Hogsmeade in the late 19th century with his wife Dulcibella .
Before her death , she wrote him a book of poetry , that he had plated in gold .
He intended to gift her the plated book before her birthday, but was unable to do so as she died before then.
Agabus vocally spoke out against the Rookwood Gang , having grown tired of them terrorising the villagers of Hogsmeade.
In response, Theophilus Harlow raided his house and froze him, taking the poetry book with him.
His friends, the Bickle family , hoped he would come forward and report the gang to Magical Law Enforcement Officer Ruth Singer , but fearing for his life, he refused.
Physical description
Agabus had short brown hair with bushy eyebrows and a moustache, light skin, and brown eyes, along with glasses .
Notes and references

title: Dulcibella Philbert
paragraphs: Dulcibella Philbert was the wife of Agabus Philbert who lived in Hogsmeade in the late 19th century .
Biography
Before her death , Dulcibella wrote a book of poetry .
For her birthday, her husband, Agabus Philbert , had the book plated in gold .
However, she died shortly before her birthday and never received the gift.
When her husband spoke out against the Rookwood Gang , Theophilus Harlow retaliated by breaking into his house and stealing the poetry book while laughing at him.
He later told the story to a Hogwarts student who located it in an Ashwinder hideout.
Notes and references

title: Isko Rabe
paragraphs: Isko Rabe was a wizard who lived in the late 19th century .
Biography
In 1890 , Isko worked for Gringotts Wizarding Bank , a job for which he travelled the world, and was married to Daisy Rabe .
Hoping to use Daisy's job as a security guard at Gringotts to break into the bank, Theophilus Harlow continuously asked her to help him break into Gringotts vaults in exchange for a few valuables.

However, Daisy refused Harlow's demands until she returned home one day and found Isko gone and a note affixed to her door saying that she had a few days to help the Rookwood Gang so that her husband would be returned safely.

After confirming that Isko had been kidnapped by noticing that his prized flowers had been trampled, which he would have never normally allowed, Daisy informed a fifth-year Hogwarts student about her situation, who offered to help her out.
After the student's friend, Natsai Onai , had also been kidnapped by the Ashwinders , the student found her wand and realised that she was in trouble.

After following her trail into an Ashwinder hideout beneath the Hog's Head Inn , the student located both her and Isko Rabe, who were both trapped in cells with cursed locks and an Anti-Disapparition Jinx strong enough to prevent Natsai's wandless magic from working.
Isko revealed to the student that his wand had been taken from him and hidden, with Natsai unable to summon his wand for him.
The student offered him the use of their wand , but Isko feared that a wand he hadn't connected with wouldn't work as well and could prove dangerous, asking the student to find his wand for him.
The student eventually managed to locate Isko's wand in a locked chest and returned it to him, enabling him to remove the enchantments on both his and Natsai's cells and allowing them to escape.
Although he was still weak, Isko offered to Disapparate out of the hideout with both the student and Natsai.
However, Natsai told him to go ahead of them and inform Officer Ruth Singer about what had happened in the hideout, as she and the student could fight their way out on their own.
Isko agreed, but warned them to be careful before Disapparating away.
Isko contacted Officer Singer and let her know about the events that had transpired before returning safely home to his wife.
Magical abilities and skills
Notes and references

title: Johanna Bickle's husband
paragraphs: Mr Bickle (d. 1890/1891 ) was an individual who lived in Lower Hogsfield in the late 19th century .
He was the husband of Johanna Bickle and the father of Archie Bickle .
Biography
Mr Bickle was known for his investigation into the criminal activities of Theophilus Harlow during the late 19th century .
He gathered substantial evidence with the intent to expose Harlow and provided it to Officer Ruth Singer .
His actions eventually attracted Harlow's attention.
He was murdered by Harlow as retribution for his attempts, and his death was witnessed by his son Archie, leading to the abduction of the boy.
Archie was imprisoned in one of Harlow's hideouts, until discovered and freed by Natsai Onai and her friend .
Notes and references

title: Archie Bickle
paragraphs: Archie Bickle (fl.
1890 ) was the son of Mr and Johanna Bickle .
He lived in Lower Hogsfield in the late 19th century with his parents.
Biography
Following the murder of his father by Theophilus Harlow , Archie became a key witness to the event and was subsequently abducted by him.
He was imprisoned in a basement within one of Harlow's hideouts, where he remained until he was rescued by Natsai Onai and a fifth-year Hogwarts student .
Upon his rescue, he was safely reunited with his mother who had feared the worst.
Notes and references

title: Manor Cape
paragraphs: Manor Cape was a region in the Scottish Highlands that connected to Marunweem Lake and Cragcroftshire .
The Lord of the Manor had lived in this region.
Notes and references

title: Mudiwa Onai
paragraphs: Professor Mudiwa Onai was a witch of African origin who taught Divination at Uagadou and later Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry during the late 19th century .
She was the mother of Natsai Onai , a Gryffindor student that transferred to Hogwarts from Uagadou following her job change.
Biography
Mudiwa was a gifted Seer and taught Divination at Uagadou .
She was also an Animagus , having taken the form of an African fish eagle .
As a mother, she sent her daughter, Natsai, to Uagadou to begin her magical education.
Natsai later became an Animagus herself, taking the form of a gazelle .
Mudiwa regarded her daughter's Animagus form as an reflection of her adaptability, but Natsai disagreed, seeing it as a representation of her awareness of danger.
When Natsai was nine years old, Mudiwa had failed to foresee her husband's death .
The trauma led her to refuse further Animagus transformations.

Seeking a fresh start and to be closer to her daughter, Mudiwa accepted an invitation from Professor Weasley to teach Divination at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in the 1889-1890 school year .
Subsequently, she arranged for Natsai to transfer from Uagadou to Hogwarts so they could be together.
1890-1891 school year
During the 1890-1891 school year , Mudiwa learned that Natsai was actively involved in efforts to dismantle the criminal activities of Theophilus Harlow .
Natsai had been using her Animagus form to secretly observe and gather information on Harlow, passing intelligence to Officer Singer .
However, rumours about a gazelle in Hogsmeade eventually reached Mudiwa, causing her concern for her daughter's safety.

After being informed by Officer Singer of Natsai's direct involvement, Mudiwa firmly forbade her from continuing these dangerous activities and restricted her from leaving Hogwarts to visit the village.
Mudiwa Onai in the battle for the final repository

At the end of the school year, Mudiwa played a critical role in defending Hogwarts against an invasion led by Ranrok , who sought to claim the final repository and replace wizardkind with goblinkind .
Mudiwa fought alongside others to protect the school and the wizarding community from Ranrok's forces, which included Loyalists and trolls .
Her courage and determination were instrumental in ensuring the safety of Hogwarts.
After the conflict, Mudiwa attended the memorial ceremony for Eleazar Fig , commemorating Ranrok's defeat and honoring those who had fought.
Personality and traits
Mudiwa was strict and had high expectations of her students and her daughter.
She had a commanding presence in any room she entered and demanded respect from all with whom she interacted.
Magical abilities and skills
Possessions
Notes and references

title: Magical Law Enforcement Officer
paragraphs: A Magical Law Enforcement Officer (style: " Officer ") , was a law-keeper in the wizarding world.

Working for the Department of Magical Law Enforcement of the British Ministry of Magic , their job was to stop crime and catch criminals guilty of an offence within the scope of the legislation they were tasked with upholding.
Functions

Magical Law Enforcement Officers were given a badge featuring the insignia of their Department, which identified them as vested by the Ministry with the authority to issue formal warnings , hand out fines , seize private property, make investigative inquiries, confiscate contraband and other illegal items, detain suspects, carry out arrests and use other appropriate means of policing wizarding Britain within his or her jurisdiction.
Cerberus Langarm of the British Auror Office , and Myra Curio , of the Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office , were known examples of Officers.
Known Officers
Notes and references

title: Greg Ellis
paragraphs: Greg Ellis (born Jonathan Rees , 21 March 1968) is an English actor, who voices various roles in Hogwarts Legacy .

These include Lodgok , Theophilus Harlow , Fastidio , Timothy Teasdale , Thaddeus Travers , Finley Grimes , Albie Weekes , Crispin Dunne , Edmund Hawkwright , Hans Hoode , Silvanus Selwyn and Sir Nestor Amset , as well as a ghost , a Dark wizard , a townsperson, the Zonko's Shopkeeper , a prisoner, a centaur , and the Hogsmeade town crier .

title: Anne Sallow
paragraphs: Anne Sallow (b. 1874/1875 ) was a Scottish witch and the twin sister of Sebastian Sallow .
Before her fifth year as a Slytherin student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , her home in Feldcroft was attacked by Victor Rookwood , Ranrok , and Ranrok's Loyalists .
She was cursed and developed a debilitating illness.

Her life was dictated by her feuding brother and uncle, as Sebastian wished to cure her by any means through the Dark Arts , while her primary caregiver and guardian Solomon Sallow only wanted to keep her comfortable and protected from the greater suffering Anne might experience from the Dark Arts.
Though Anne herself agreed with her uncle, Sebastian went to desperate means to save her, eventually resulting in their uncle's murder at Sebastian's hand and the breaking of the Sallow family .
It is unknown what happened to Anne afterwards.
Biography
Early life
Anne was born in 1874 or 1875 alongside a twin brother, Sebastian.
They were raised by two professors who worked at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .

Their parents died when they were young after a lamp in their cellar poisoned them with an undetectable toxin , after which they were taken in by their uncle Solomon Sallow who lived in a home in Feldcroft .
Hogwarts years
At the age of eleven, Anne and Sebastian began attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, where she was sorted into Slytherin .
Anne developed a close friendship with Ominis Gaunt , a Slytherin student in their year, who introduced her to the Undercroft , a secret area within Hogwarts Castle .
There, the three of them would often play Gobstones and hang out.
With Ominis not being particularly close to his own family, he would often visit Anne and Sebastian at their home in Feldcroft.
At one point during a school year, she wrote a letter to Sebastian, telling him to stop touching her Potions set.
Sometime before the start of her fifth year , Anne was attacked and cursed when Feldcroft was raided by Victor Rookwood , Ranrok , and Ranrok's Loyalists .
She had rushed out to help the wounded villagers and was told " children should be seen and not heard " before being cursed by Rookwood.
That was then unknown to the Sallows , and they assumed it to be a goblin who had cursed her.
She developed constant pain after this and was unable to attend school.
While the guilty party was initially assumed to be Ranrok's Loyalists, it was eventually discovered to have been Victor Rookwood by one of her brother's friends .
The Sallow family at Feldcroft
After the raid, Anne lived in constant agony, cared for by her uncle in Feldcroft.
They tried everything to cure her, from Noreen Blainey to St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries , to no avail.
By the end, Solomon simply wanted to keep her comfortable, though Sebastian was more desperate to untap the mysteries of the Dark Arts with the hope of finding a cure.
As Sebastian's interest in the Dark Arts only grew, Solomon grew suspicious of him.
Their rivalry reached a climax when, after performing the Imperius Curse on a goblin during a skirmish at Feldcroft , he was forbidden by Solomon from seeing Anne or visiting their home.
Anne Sallow with her uncle's corpse
Sebastian's journey into the Dark Arts culminated in the discovery of a dark relic that required a dark sacrifice to use.
He attempted to cure a reluctant Anne, who baulked and informed their uncle on what Sebastian was doing.
Solomon arrived to the Feldcroft Catacomb , where Sebastian had used the relic to control Inferi , and urged him to stop.
Sebastian attacked his uncle , engaged in a duel with him, and eventually murdered him.

Anne discovered her uncle's body and, after destroying the remaining Inferi and Slytherin's Spellbook, telling her twin in the process he had chosen his path, tearfully knelt over the motionless form of Solomon, before Apparating away with it.
Regardless of whether Ominis and his friend turned in Sebastian, Anne informed villagers in Feldcroft , such as Bernard Ndiaye , that Solomon had died in his sleep.

She left a letter for Sebastian, stating that she left to have time to herself, and while she would always love him, she may never forgive him for what he had done to their uncle and half-felt that he must face justice for his crimes.
Anne was the only participant at the funeral of Solomon Sallow.
After Solomon's murder, Anne moved elsewhere.
Her exact location was never disclosed in her letter to Sebastian, and her eventual fate is unknown.
Personality and traits
Prior to being cursed, Anne was described as being very similar in personality to Sebastian, having the same fearlessness and charisma, though was much more mischievous.
After being cursed, Anne maintained a largely kind and patient demeanour, though this was greatly tempered by an underlying (yet tangible) air of exhaustion due to the constant strain of the curse.

Anne also displayed a considerable level of precociousness and maturity towards being cursed, accepting that she may eventually succumb to it one day and that her return to Hogwarts will likely never come to pass.
Compared to Sebastian, Anne had a far more positive relationship with Solomon and shared her uncle's disdain towards the Dark Arts.

When Sebastian sought the Dark Arts as a means to protect and cure her, Anne became increasingly reprehensive towards his behaviour and would side with Solomon, eventually alerting Solomon to Sebastian's worsening activities.
After the strife culminated in Solomon dying by Sebastian's hand, Anne became furious with her brother and swiftly cut all ties with him, fleeing to a undisclosed destination.
However, she would maintain that she would always love Sebastian, but may never forgive him and desired for him to face justice for his actions.

title: Feldcroft
paragraphs: Feldcroft was a wizard hamlet located south of Hogwarts Castle , in the Feldcroft Region of the Highlands of Scotland .
Though small, the hamlet was home to a number of important wizarding families, such as the Rookwoods , the Morganachs , the Ndiayes , and the Sallows .
The town existed since the Middle Ages and formed an important part of the Feldcroft Region.
History
Middle Ages
Rookwood Castle overlooking the village
The Feldcroft Catacomb was built prior to 993 AD , where it held a peculiar Dark relic .
This relic was accessed by a medieval student of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry as part of an assignment by Salazar Slytherin .
At some point before or within the Tudor period , the Rookwood family took control over the village, constructing Rookwood Castle .
This castle was eventually inhabited by Charles Rookwood .
He was also a member of the Keepers , an organisation tasked to protect the knowledge of ancient magic .
A repository of this ancient magic rested below Rookwood Castle, which would later become the envy of Ranrok .
Tudor period
In the Tudor period, a drought occurred and the well dried, resulting in the deaths of many people, one of which was a boy whose father refused to speak for years.
The Keepers revived the drought-plagued hamlet in a matter of moments.
They were observed by a young Isidora Morganach , alongside her father and brother .
During her time as a professor at Hogwarts, Isidora lived in a house in Feldcroft, to which she frequently invited her colleagues.
19th century
In 1889 or 1890 , the goblin Ranrok , Victor Rookwood , and their followers launched an attack on Feldcroft, resulting in Anne Sallow being cursed .
Rookwood and Ranrok's presence in the town also became more pronounced, as they ransacked Rookwood Castle in search of the repository within.
The increasing number of goblin raids caused the residents of Feldcroft to acquire practice dummies so they could train to defend themselves against goblin raids.
Sebastian trying to help his sister Anne in Feldcroft
At some point during the 1890-1891 school year , Ranrok's Loyalists attacked the hamlet again, resulting in a skirmish .
Sebastian Sallow used the Imperius Curse on a goblin on a field just outside of the Sallow home , causing him to be evicted from his home by his uncle .

Later that year, after Sebastian discovered the same relic hunted by Salazar Slytherin's student, he summoned and controlled a mass of Inferi within the Feldcroft Catacomb , nearly endangering the town.
He was stopped by his uncle Solomon, resulting in Solomon's murder .
After a solitary funeral , the villagers of Feldcroft were told by Anne Sallow that Solomon had died in his sleep.
Locations
Residents
Notes and references

title: Victor Rookwood's curse
paragraphs: This curse ( incantation unknown ) caused the victim considerable pain , agony, and illness for years afterwards.
It could not be cured by any ordinary means, as both healing magic and Shrivelfigs had no impact.
It was suggested that it could be cured through a Dark relic , though this was never attempted in practice.
Known uses

It was used by Victor Rookwood on Anne Sallow during his and Ranrok 's raid on Feldcroft in the 1880s , leaving Anne in considerable pain for years after, and forcing her to leave her studies at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
Notes and references

title: Sallow family
paragraphs: Sallow was the surname of a wizarding family that existed from at least the 19th century .
The family had a troubling secret.
They lived in the Sallow home in Feldcroft .
Family members
Family tree
Notes and references

title: Sallow siblings' parents
paragraphs: Professors Sallow (d. between 1874 and 1882 ) were the parents of Sebastian and Anne Sallow .
They were deceased by 1890 , when their children were young.
Biography
They were dedicated professors as they spent nearly every waking moment in their cellar library, but died before 1890 , after a lamp in their cellar poisoned them with an undetectable toxin.
After Sebastian's father died, Solomon Sallow often referred to him as "his father's son", a remark Sebastian felt was meant as an insult.
Personality and traits
They were regarded as optimistic, open-minded, and eager for more knowledge: traits which Sebastian wished to emulate.
Their brother/brother-in-law, Solomon Sallow , told Sebastian that his father would be ashamed of his use of the Dark Arts .
Therefore, it is likely that these individuals, like Solomon, held a strong aversion to Dark Magic.
Notes and references

title: Sallow home
paragraphs: The Sallow home was a house in Feldcroft that belonged to Solomon Sallow , a former Auror who worked for the British Ministry of Magic .
After his death , it was seemingly inherited by his niece Anne .
History
Solomon lived in the house with his orphaned niece and nephew, Anne and Sebastian Sallow in the late 19th century .
Anne and Sebastian would regularly bring their school friend, Ominis Gaunt , to the house due to Ominis's dislike of his own family .
Likewise, Sebastian brought his new friend here during the 1890-1891 school year , introducing them to his family before exploring the rest of the village.
The friend was well-received by Anne, but Solomon treated them with suspicion.
Around this time, the home was filled with potions and ingredients for the debilitated Anne.

During a skirmish between Ranrok's Loyalists and the citizens of Feldcroft during the 1890-1891 school year, Sebastian used the Imperius Curse to force a goblin to kill himself just outside of the house.
For this, he was evicted by his uncle, who despised dark magic , and was told never to return.
After Solomon's death, the Sallow home seemingly passed into Anne's possession.
She left a letter to Sebastian, saying that she had left the house and needed time.
Thus, the future of the house-whether Anne continued to be the legal owner, had sold it, or who inherited it after she likely succumbed to her curse -is unknown.
As Solomon was buried in a grave in the house's garden, it is likely that his funeral happened here as well.
Notes and references

title: Ominis Gaunt
paragraphs: Ominis Gaunt (c. 1875 - pre- 1925 ) was a pure-blood wizard and a member of the House of Gaunt .
He was a Slytherin student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry from 1886 into the 1890s .

Despite being born into a family of dark wizards , he developed a deep distrust towards the Dark Arts , and often found himself in conflicts with his friend Sebastian Sallow over how they should be used.
Quick Answers
Biography
Early life
He was a descendant of Salazar Slytherin , born into the pure-blood House of Gaunt to a Mr and Mrs Gaunt , two Dark wizards .
He was born blind , and no spell was able to reverse it.
After this, he took to using his wand , which was " almost sentient ", to navigate his way around.
His upbringing resulted in trauma that made him pessimistic, distrusting of people, and sarcastic.

He disagreed with his family's use of the Dark Arts , which aligned him with his favourite aunt, Noctua Gaunt , who herself wished to change the family's traditions and uncover more about Salazar Slytherin's legacy.
Ominis was dismayed to find out that she had died in her attempt to navigate Slytherin's Scriptorium .
When he was a child, he refused to perform the Cruciatus Curse , which his older siblings and parents often performed on Muggles " for sport ".
This resulted in his own family using the curse on him, creating a division between him and his family that never healed.
When told to cast the curse again, he relented to avoid further anguish to himself, and found it difficult to forgive himself ever since.
Hogwarts years (1886-?)
Ominis Gaunt in a particularly boring History of Magic class at Hogwarts
Ominis started attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry at the age of eleven.
On 1 September 1886 , he was sorted into Slytherin (a house he " most certainly " expected to be sorted into due to his heritage), and became friends with Sebastian Sallow and his twin sister, Anne .
The three of them would often go into the Undercroft , a secret room only known to the House of Gaunt , to play Gobstones and hang out.
Ominis considered this place very special to him, and he was disappointed when Sebastian later revealed the existence of the Undercroft to another student .
When not at Hogwarts, Ominis would retreat to the Sallow home at Feldcroft , shying away from his own family, but developing a strong connection to the Sallows .
The first time Sebastian and Ominis practised the Blasting Curse , they singed their eyebrows.
Ominis had quite a playful nature, often taunting first year students by pretending that mermaids could be seen outside the Slytherin common room windows, keeping them " on the lookout for hours ".
Ominis Gaunt (left) in the Slytherin common room in his fifth year
He also became more acquainted to a new student who had joined late in their fifth year due to their ability to see and use ancient magic .

If this student was a Slytherin , then Ominis would have met them in the Slytherin common room on 2 September ; otherwise, they had a thorny introduction when Ominis caught them sneaking out of the Undercroft .
Sebastian often wanted to enlist Ominis's help with Dark Magic to help his sister Anne , which he was deeply uncomfortable with due to his intense childhood experiences.
Later in the year, when the new student disguised themselves as Phineas Nigellus Black using Polyjuice Potion , they accosted Ominis Gaunt in the hallways, demanding to know where he was going.
Ominis made a quick exit by stating that he was headed to the Hogwarts greenhouses to research for his essay on dittany and its uses , afterwards murmuring that the Headmaster was acting strangely.

Eventually, he was pressured into breaking into Slytherin's Scriptorium under Sebastian's promise that it would be their last encounter into Dark Magic, though Ominis was distressed throughout the whole venture, especially as he came face-to-face with the bones of his late aunt Noctua .
Ominis confronting the new student in the Feldcroft Catacomb

Sebastian did not stop his journey into the Dark Arts; by the winter of 1890 , he followed Sebastian and the other fifth-year student to the Catacomb outside Feldcroft , which they had just infiltrated , and was disgusted to find they had not only been practising the Imperius Curse , but also looking for a lost relic , infused with Dark Magic, to cure Anne's illness.
Ominis did not even register Sebastian's existence in this encounter, finding it too uncomfortable to see him as a friend anymore.
The fifth-year either persuaded Ominis to let them go, or went so far as to use the Imperius Curse to force Ominis to stand aside.
Later that year, Ominis was present at the Feldcroft Catacomb again, as Sebastian used the relic to summon Inferi .

Solomon Sallow had sworn to alert Headmaster Phineas Nigellus Black the next time Sebastian used dark magic, so Ominis ran to the Headmaster to tell him that the event was simply an exaggerated argument.
In his absence, Sebastian murdered Solomon, which convinced Ominis that he could no longer stand by and watch his friend's descent into darkness, and that it was time to turn Sebastian in.
Ominis asked their mutual friend to turn him in, which the friend possibly did.

After this, Sebastian was possibly expelled and put on trial at the Ministry of Magic ; likewise, it was possible that the friend refused to turn him in, and the incident in the catacombs was kept a secret, with Ominis being tasked to convince Anne to keep quiet.

After the defeat of Ranrok in the battle for the final repository , Ominis's friend possibly informed him at the memorial ceremony for Eleazar Fig that it had been Victor Rookwood that cursed Anne Sallow, not the goblins as they had originally believed.
After receiving this information, Ominis possibly informed both Anne and Sebastian.
Alternatively, if Sebastian was given the chance to amend on his own, their mutual friend told him directly about Rookwood being the one who cursed Anne.
Later life
It is known that the last living Gaunts by the summer of 1925 were Marvolo and his children Morfin and Merope .
It follows that Ominis had already passed away by that date; he either did not have any offspring or, if he did, they must also have already died by that date.
Magical abilities and skills
Possessions
Ominis's wand
Relationships
Family
Ominis had a strained relationship with his father , mother , and older siblings as they were all Dark wizards with a history of brutally torturing both himself and countless innocent Muggles.
He was additionally disgusted by their pure-blood supremacy .
On the other hand, Ominis stated that his father was friends with the headmaster , and threatened to exploit this if he wished on at least one occasion.
It is therefore unclear exactly how fragile their relationship was.
Sebastian Sallow
Sebastian Sallow, Ominis's oldest friend
Sebastian Sallow was Ominis's oldest friend.
However, their relationship became more tenuous in their fifth year with Sebastian's continued exploration of the Dark Arts, which Ominis regularly advised against.
In the end, their relationship suffered so badly that Ominis found it difficult to consider Sebastian a friend anymore, even though he did continue to worry about him greatly.
Unidentified fifth-year friend
This student was Ominis's new friend, who started late in their fifth year .
They had a rocky beginning when Ominis caught them outside of the Undercroft , which they had been shown by Sebastian.
Ominis attempted continuously to convince this student to help curb Sebastian's descent into the Dark Arts , and had come to trust their wisdom a great deal.
By the conclusion of the 1890-1891 school year , he considered this student a friend: a rare honour, as Sebastian had been his only true friend before.
Etymology
Although Ominis is not a name, the word ominous is an adjective which means "of ill omen, inauspicious; indicative or suggestive of future misfortune."
His name may be a reference to the twelfth verse of Edgar Allan Poe 's " The Raven ", in which the Raven is described as "this grim, ungainly, ghastly, gaunt , and ominous bird of yore".
Notes and references

title: Undercroft
paragraphs: The Undercroft was a secret hall within Hogwarts Castle accessible through a hidden passage on the ground floor of the Hogwarts Turris Magnus staircase , as well as via an ancient magic passageway to Isidora Morganach's house at Feldcroft .
History
Knowledge of the existence of this room passed through the House of Gaunt for generations.
It was shown to Sebastian Sallow by Ominis Gaunt , the latter of whom named it the Undercroft.
Before Anne Sallow left Hogwarts , she, Sebastian, and Ominis would often play Gobstones in this room.
In his fifth year , Sebastian showed a fellow student the Undercroft, teaching them the Blasting Curse .
This irritated Ominis, who felt his secret had been betrayed, though as the school year advanced, the trio became closer friends.
The triptych in the Undercroft
Sebastian and the student, meanwhile, discovered an ancient magic link between the Undercroft and Isidora Morganach's house in Feldcroft .
After travelling through, a triptych opened which depicted a torn scene of the Highlands , tempting Sebastian to explore the area and learn more about Morganach .
When the two finished the triptych, a Pensieve appeared which showed Morganach's life in the Tudor period.
In the later part of the school year, following the murder of Solomon Sallow by Sebastian, Ominis Gaunt brought the student to the Undercroft to ask them to turn Sebastian in.
Notes and references

title: Raid on Feldcroft
paragraphs: This raid was an early event within Ranrok's goblin rebellion that saw the invasion of Feldcroft , a hamlet in the Highlands of Scotland , the wounding of countless residents, and the cursing of Anne Sallow , a fourth year Slytherin student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
The raid was organised by Ranrok and Victor Rookwood with the purpose of acquiring more information about Isidora Morganach and the source of ancient magic that was stored beneath Hogwarts Castle .
Following the raid, Victor allowed the Loyalists to dig beneath his family home, Rookwood Castle , in a search for a repository of ancient magic.
Notes and references

title: Goblin killed by Sebastian Sallow
paragraphs: This goblin was one of the loyalists serving Ranrok , the goblin rebel leading a rebellion against wizardkind , in the late 19th century .
Biography

The goblin was killed by Sebastian Sallow during a skirmish at Feldcroft in the 1890-1891 school year , after the latter used the Imperius Curse to force the goblin into committing suicide by stabbing himself with his own sword to protect his twin sister Anne , who was horrified despite having been nearly killed by this same goblin beforehand.
After this incident, their uncle Solomon Sallow told Sebastian to stay away from them.
Notes and references

title: Skirmish at Feldcroft
paragraphs: This skirmish occurred at Feldcroft shortly after the infiltration of the Feldcroft Catacomb by Sebastian Sallow and his friend .
It involved a number of Ranrok's Loyalists attacking the town, which was defended by ex- Auror Solomon Sallow .
Events
While Solomon Sallow led the defence of the town, he was aided by a Hogwarts student and his nephew, Sebastian Sallow .
During the onslaught, Anne Sallow fell over into a field just outside the Sallow home , and was about to be attacked by an unidentified goblin .
Sebastian intervened, casting the Imperius Curse on the goblin and forcing him to commit suicide , thus saving Anne.

As the number of Loyalists dwindled, Solomon expressed his disgust at Sebastian's actions and urged him to stay away from them, or else he would report his meddling with the Dark Arts to the Headmaster , Phineas Nigellus Black .
Notes and references

title: Relic
paragraphs: This relic , located in the catacombs of Feldcroft , was a Dark artefact that had the ability to summon Inferi as well as heal those who had been afflicted by Dark Magic by way of a sacrifice.
History
Drawing of the relic by Slytherin's student
It was first discovered by a student of Salazar Slytherin in the first millennium A.D. , who recorded it in his notes.
These notes were discovered centuries later by Sebastian Sallow , who wished to use the relic to save his sister, Anne , from a debilitating curse that she had been put under.
In 1891 , Sebastian seized the relic, summoning Inferi within the catacomb and endangering the town of Feldcroft , much to the shock of Anne, his friend , and Ominis Gaunt .
Sebastian's friend fought their way through the Inferi, reaching Sebastian and begging him to stop.
Just then, the relic was seized by Sebastian's uncle Solomon , who disintegrated it with a nonverbal spell , much to Sebastian's horror.
Notes and references

title: Feldcroft Catacomb
paragraphs: The Feldcroft Catacomb was an underground burial place located in Feldcroft , Scotland .
It was populated by spiders and Inferi .
History
Medieval period
At some point within the early medieval period, a student of Salazar Slytherin ventured into the Catacomb, where they discovered a dark relic .
They were not permitted to take the relic out of the Catacomb, so they locked it in using human bones .
1890-1891 school year

After discovering Slytherin's Spellbook in his secret Scriptorium at Hogwarts , Sebastian read about this student's travels and learned about the existence of the relic, which he was determined could help cure his cursed sister, Anne .
He invited his friend into the Catacomb to find the relic, where they fought countless spiders to pass into its resting chamber.
Sebastian took the relic, but was stopped by Ominis Gaunt , who refused to let them get away with practising the Dark Arts .
Sebastian's friend either persuaded or used the Imperius Curse on Ominis to let them past.
At a later point in time, Sebastian invited Anne to the Catacomb by sending her his crest - a coded signal.
Using the powers of the relic, Sebastian controlled the Inferi within the cave, which his friend had to battle through to reach him.
When they finally met, they were interrupted by Solomon Sallow , Sebastian and Anne's uncle, who summoned and destroyed the relic, much to Sebastian's anger.
The murder of Solomon Sallow
Sebastian nonverbally attacked his uncle, leading to a duel between Solomon, Sebastian, and Sebastian's friend, while also being attacked by countless waves of Inferi.
Sebastian performed the Killing Curse on Solomon, murdering his uncle in cold blood.
Shortly after, Anne arrived, destroyed the remaining Inferi, and then destroyed Slytherin's Spellbook , before Disapparating with their uncle's corpse.
Notes and references

title: Skirmish in the Feldcroft Catacomb
paragraphs: This skirmish took place in the Feldcroft Catacomb in 1891 .
The confrontation was marked by the murder of Solomon Sallow , a former Auror for the British Ministry of Magic , by his nephew, Sebastian .
Background
A drawing of the relic by Salazar Slytherin's student

After the break-in of Slytherin's Scriptorium at Hogwarts Castle , Sebastian read in Slytherin's Spellbook about a student who had discovered a relic in the Feldcroft Catacomb - one with the power to heal cursed individuals with a required sacrifice.
Sebastian was intrigued by this, as his sister, Anne Sallow , had been cursed by Victor Rookwood two years prior, and he had become desperate for a cure ever since.
Sebastian invited his friend to the Catacomb to scout for the relic .
They defeated various waves of spiders before reaching and securing it.
However, they were stopped by Ominis Gaunt , who had followed them and demanded they stop meddling with the Dark Arts .
Sebastian and his friend refused, either persuading or using the Imperius Curse on Ominis to stop him from following them as they hurried out of the Catacomb.
After leaving the Catacomb, Sebastian and his friend found Feldcroft attacked by a large number of Ranrok's Loyalists .
They fought off waves of goblins together before an unidentified goblin rushed at Anne, axe in hand.
Sebastian used the Imperius Curse to force the goblin to kill himself - an act that his uncle Solomon was disgusted by, and evicted Sebastian from their house for.
Since that day, Sebastian rued that his sister Anne was forced to live with an uncle who he believed did not have her interests at heart.
He sent Anne a coded message, using his crest , to invite her to the Catacomb, where he was determined to heal her curse once and for all.
Events
Arrival of Sebastian's friend
Sebastian brought Anne Sallow and Ominis Gaunt to the Catacomb to show them his newfound power to control Inferi via the Dark relic he had acquired.
They left in distress, barricading the Catacomb and waiting for the arrival of their mutual friend .
Sebastian surrounded by loyal Inferi
When Sebastian's friend arrived at the Catacomb, they were greeted by Ominis and Anne, the latter of whom was pacing around, unnerved by the incident.
Both were visibly distressed.
Ominis claimed the entire Catacomb was overriden with Inferi that Sebastian had managed to control.
He stressed that the whole village was in danger and that Sebastian had clearly gone mad with the power the relic had given him.
Ominis and his friend entered the Catacomb and fought off waves of Inferi.
Meanwhile, Anne went to get her uncle, Solomon Sallow .
As Solomon had promised to report any instances of Dark magic to the Headmaster , Phineas Nigellus Black , Ominis rushed off to tell Black that the incident was just an overblown family argument.
Sebastian's friend found him in the Great Room surrounded by Inferi loyal to him, with Sebastian happily expressing how nice it felt to have so much power.

Before their conversation could go much further, they were interrupted by the arrival of Solomon, who attacked an Inferius - much to Sebastian's surprise - before summoning the relic and nonverbally destroying it.
Duel of the Sallows
Sebastian shot a nonverbal spell at his uncle and a three-way fight ensued, with Sebastian and his friend fighting the now free horde of Inferi and Solomon.
The fight ended when Sebastian shot the Killing Curse at Solomon, ending his life.
Sebastian dropped his wand at equal surprise and shock at what he had done.
The destruction of Slytherin's Spellbook
Anne Sallow arrived, aghast at the scene.
In a rare demonstration of her magical power, she knocked Sebastian against the wall, incinerated the remaining Inferi, and destroyed Slytherin's Spellbook , much to Sebastian's horror.
Anne then Disapparated away with Solomon's corpse.
She was the only person present at his burial some days later.
Aftermath
After the events that took place in the Feldcroft Catacomb, Ominis Gaunt felt that they had to turn Sebastian in for his crime.
If Sebastian and Ominis's friend agreed, then Sebastian would have been expelled from Hogwarts and faced trial at the Ministry .
However, they might have also kept the event secret, with Ominis persuading Anne to keep quiet for Sebastian's sake.
Regardless, Sebastian showed great remorse at his actions.
Notes and references

title: Bernard Ndiaye
paragraphs: Bernard Ndiaye was a Scottish wizard who lived in the late 19th century and was a father to twin daughters.
He operated a shop in Feldcroft .
Biography
Ndiaye was born and raised in the Scottish village of Feldcroft .
He attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , where he met a fellow student, Eddie Thistlewood , who became one of his closest friends.
After Hogwarts, having always adored magical creatures , he operated a shop in his home village that sold material by-products of beasts.
At one point, he fathered twin daughters.
In 1891 , one of his fellow Feldcroft inhabitants, Solomon Sallow , was killed by his nephew, Sebastian .
Despite the truth, Sebastian's sister Anne lied to Ndiaye, among other villagers, claiming that Solomon died in his sleep.
Notes and references

title: Anne Sallow's letter to Sebastian Sallow (II)
paragraphs: This letter was left by Anne Sallow in her home in Feldcroft after the murder of her uncle, Solomon Sallow , during a skirmish in the Feldcroft Catacomb .
It was addressed to Sebastian Sallow , Anne's brother and Solomon's murderer.
Whether the letter ever reached its addressee is unknown.
Contents
Sebastian,
Too much has happened.
I needed to get away from here for a while.
I miss Uncle Solomon.
I need time .
I will always love you, but I don't know if I can ever forgive you.
Anne
