He also suggested that witches and wizards whose Patronus took the form of their favourite animal were obsessive or eccentric, as they were wizards who could not hide their essential self in common life, in effect parading tendencies that others would prefer to conceal.

In addition to his masterwork, Professor Spangle also wrote an article on techniques for improved Spell Energy distribution, a hand-written manuscript , and a series of manuscripts that were left unpublished.

During the Calamity in the late 2010s or early 2020s , a Calamity Investigator working for the Statute of Secrecy Task Force read through the article and, despite Spangle's methods being incredibly unorthodox, found that applying them increased the amount of Spell Energy produced through their Inn Charm at wizarding inns.

They also later found and read through the unpublished manuscripts, finding that one contained an informative short instructional on how to access one's secret inner reserve of determination, which they used to increase the number of times they could cast the Trace Charm in quick succession.

A member of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force training to be a professor also discovered and read Professor Spangle's hand-written manuscript, increasing the amount of damage they could deal in combat, before turning it over to Madam Irma Pince for storage in the Hogwarts Library .
Magical abilities and skills
Etymology
Notes and references

title: Patronus spellbook
paragraphs: The Patronus spellbook was a book with instructions and information on the Patronus Charm .
A copy of this book was owned by Remus Lupin .
Notes and references

title: Powering-up spells
paragraphs: Garrick Ollivander casting a charged version of the Knockback Jinx
A wizard or witch could increase the power of a spell by waving their wand around in circular motions before casting a spell.
The spell, once its power had been increased, would change colour from its ordinary colour to a different colour.
A spell reaching the maximum amount of charged power was referred to as a Perfect Cast .
If one attempted to charge a spell more than this, it will backfire in mid-air, and cause minor damage to them.
Powering-up spells was covered in Miranda Goshawk 's The Standard Book of Spells .
Notes and references

title: Backfiring Jinx
paragraphs: The Backfiring Jinx ( incantation unknown ) was a jinx that backfired spells onto their casters.
History

In July 1996 , the Office for the Detection and Confiscation of Counterfeit Defensive Spells and Protective Objects got wind of a "nasty" example of this jinx in Elephant and Castle , but it was sorted out by the Magical Law Enforcement Patrol before they arrived on the scene.
Notes and references

title: Magicus Extremos
paragraphs: Magicus Extremos was the incantation of a partnership-based charm that temporarily increased the casters' spell power.
In order to activate this effect, at least three wizards and/or witches were needed to cast the charm simultaneously, which then invoked significantly increased power for a short while.
Known practitioners
Etymology
From the latin " magicus ", meaning " magical " and " extremus " meaning "extreme".
Notes and references

title: Maggot
paragraphs: A maggot , also known as a fly larvae , is the larval form of some varieties of fly , including houseflies, cheese flies, and blowflies .
They can be found in decaying meat and other foods.
History
The Dark wizard Raczidian being consumed by maggots as a result of attempting to cast the Patronus Charm

If an unworthy Dark wizard or witch attempted to cast the Patronus Charm , rather than summoning a spirit guardian, as the charm normally should, a horde of maggots would burst out of the caster's wand and start to consume him or her.
The first recorded instance of this happening was with the Dark wizard Raczidian .
The Aquavirius Maggot , a creature believed to exist by the Lovegoods , was described as a maggot resembling a brain .
Kreacher sent a package of maggots to Harry Potter for Christmas in 1996 as a means of showing his dislike for his new master.
Notes and references

title: Aquavirius Maggot
paragraphs: The Aquavirius Maggot was supposedly a magical creature that resembles a brain .
Xenophilius Lovegood believed they were bred by the British Ministry of Magic .
History

On 18 June 1996 , while in the Department of Mysteries in the British Ministry of Magic , Luna Lovegood incorrectly identified the pale blobs floating in the brain tank in the Department of Mysteries as being Aquavirius Maggots, though they were in fact just brains .
The Aquavirius Maggot was one of the many strange creatures in which Luna Lovegood and her father Xenophilius Lovegood believed, though many others did not.
Notes and references

title: Aardvark
paragraphs: The aardvark is a burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa .
It was one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Adder
paragraphs: An adder is a species of snake .
It was also one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History
In the summer of 1925 , Morfin Gaunt held a live adder when Bob Ogden visited the Gaunt Shack .
Notes and references

title: Morfin Gaunt's second snake
paragraphs: The second pet snake of Morfin Gaunt was the replacement of another late snake , which was killed and nailed to the Gaunt Shack door.
The snake was an adder .
Biography
When Bob Ogden from Magical Law Enforcement Patrol came to visit the Gaunt Shack in 1925 , Morfin was twisting it in his fingers, singing to it in Parseltongue .
The snake's final fate is unknown, but the day it heard the song was the same day Morfin was placed under arrest by Ogden, along with his father Marvolo .
It was evident that the arrest was beneficial for the snake, as it was spared the gruesome, inhumane fate of being nailed.
Notes and references

title: Albatross
paragraphs: An albatross is a species of bird .
It was one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Badger
paragraphs: The badger is an omnivorous mammal of the Mustelidae family, distinguishable by the white stripe that runs down its snout.
It was a known corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Badgers in the wizarding world
The badger was the mascot of Hufflepuff House at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .

Like the house it represented, the badger was often underestimated and deemed non-threatening because it was not generally aggressive unless provoked, at which point it could and would viciously fight off threats even larger than itself.
This symbolism was perhaps showcased best in the Battle of Hogwarts , where many Hufflepuffs stayed to fight and defend their school, with only Gryffindor outnumbering them.

Uric the Oddball once turned up for a presentation before the Wizards' Council wearing nothing but a toupee that turned out to be a dead badger, after listening to a Fwooper 's song continuously for three months.
There was a spell that could transfigure a cauldron into a badger.
One could turn a human into a badger .
Notes and references

title: Uric the Oddball
paragraphs: Uric the Oddball was a medieval wizard , who became famous for his eccentric behaviour, such as wearing a jellyfish as a hat, and sleeping in a room with fifty pet Augureys .
He is considered to be one of the most unconventional and weirdest wizards in history, and, as such, is often the punchline of wizarding jokes.
Biography
Early life
Uric was born in the Middle Ages, no earlier than 982 , somewhere in the British Isles .
In his youth, Uric attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , where he was Sorted into Ravenclaw .
He was possibly taught by Rowena Ravenclaw herself.
Adulthood
Uric the Oddball in his trademark jellyfish hat
At some point, Uric became famous for wearing a jellyfish for a hat.
This, among other things, is still what Uric is best remembered for.
Uric was known to have slept in a room with fifty pet Augureys .
The Augurey's distinctive low and throbbing cry was once believed to foretell death, although the bird actually cries at the approach of rain .
On a particularly rainy winter, the moaning of his Augureys convinced Uric that he was dead , and had returned as a ghost .
He constantly attempted to walk through the walls of his house, which resulted in a ten-day long concussion .
At one time, Uric the Oddball attempted to prove that the song of the Fwooper was actually beneficial to one's health.
After listening to it for three months without a break, he presented his findings to the Wizards' Council .
The Council was left unconvinced, as Uric arrived at the meeting wearing nothing but a toupee that, on closer inspection, proved to be a dead badger .
Death and post-mortem
Uric's depiction on a Chocolate Frog Card
Uric died sometime in the Middle Ages.
In honour of his eccentricity, a small biography of him was recorded on a Chocolate Frog Card .
At some point, Radolphus Pittiman studied Uric's life, and became his biographer.

In the 1989-1990 school year at Hogwarts, Uric the Oddball was the subject of a sixth-year History of Magic lecture, and one of the very few delivered by Binns to evoke any interest from the students; Charlie Weasley thought he seemed like a laugh and wanted to meet him, Andre Egwu respected his questionable but creative fashion sense, Ben Copper respected his courage to be whatever he wanted to be, and Tulip Karasu , herself often considered eccentric and chaotic, called him an artist ahead of his times.

On 1 September 1991 , Prefect Robert Hilliard welcomed the Ravenclaw first-years to Ravenclaw Tower with a short speech in which he mentioned eccentric Uric the Oddball as one of the many notable Hogwarts students who had been Sorted , like them, into Ravenclaw.

In the 1991-1992 school year , students of History of Magic at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry would scribble down names and dates, and mix up Uric the Oddball with Emeric the Evil , while Professor Binns droned on.
Notes and references

title: Cauldron to badger spell
paragraphs: This spell ( incantation unknown ) transformed a cauldron into a badger .
It was taught at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry sometime during or before the fifth year in Transfiguration .
Harry Potter practised this spell for his Ordinary Wizarding Levels during the 1995-1996 school year .
Notes and references

title: Badgering
paragraphs: Badgering ( incantation unknown ), was a transfiguration spell that turned a target into a badger .
History
In late 1992 , a student in Transfiguration class accidentally performed this spell on a classmate , earning a shouting from Professor McGonagall as consequence.
Notes and references

title: Hagrid's Hut
paragraphs: Hagrid's Hut served as the home of Rubeus Hagrid and some of his pets , including Fang , during his years as Hogwarts gamekeeper and later as a teacher at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
It was also used by other gamekeepers prior to Hagrid's tenure.
The hut was a small wooden cabin located outside Hogwarts Castle , on the edge of the Forbidden Forest .
Harry Potter , Hermione Granger , and Ron Weasley were among the Hogwarts students who regularly visited there during Hagrid's time.
History
The hut of unknown name stood for centuries and was already present by the 1890s , when it was inhabited by a gamekeeper .
A pumpkin patch was located behind it.
When Rubeus Hagrid became the gamekeeper of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry later in the mid- 20th century , he was given the hut - thereafter known as Hagrid's Hut - as his residence.
At some point in or before the 1980s , Hagrid tried using the Fire-Breathing Potion , and his hut nearly burned down.
Between the wars
Hagrid and the newly hatched Norbert
The 1991-1992 school year was Harry Potter 's first year in Hogwarts, along with Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger .
They visited Hagrid's hut occasionally and in April of 1992 , the trio saw a female dragon , a Norwegian Ridgeback , for the first time which hatched from an egg.
Hagrid, having mistaken the dragon for a male, named it Norbert .
On the same night, they noticed Draco Malfoy sneaking by the window of Hagrid's Hut and listening to their conversation.
After informing Professor McGonagall , Malfoy, along with the three students, received detention for being out of bed late at night.
As punishment, the caretaker Argus Filch escorted the four from the castle to Hagrid's Hut, where they split into two groups and were sent to the Forbidden Forest with Hagrid.
Malfoy and Fudge visiting the hut

In late 1992-1993 school year , Cornelius Fudge , the Minister for Magic , and Draco's father, Lucius Malfoy , along with Headmaster Dumbledore , visited the hut to discuss the incident of the re-opening of the Chamber of Secrets .
The Ministry of Magic decided to send Hagrid to Azkaban , assuming he was responsible for reopening the Chamber.
Unnoticed by the Minister and Lucius, Harry and Ron hid under the Cloak of Invisibility during the visit.
Before his departure, Hagrid secretly instructed them to "...follow the spiders " to learn the truth about the Chamber from Aragog in the forest, and reminded them to feed Fang.
Shortly before Buckbeak 's scheduled execution, Walden Macnair , Albus Dumbledore , Cornelius Fudge , and an elderly Committee member approach Hagrid's Hut

In late 1993 , Headmaster Dumbledore revisited the hut to inform Hagrid that he would replace Professor Kettleburn as the teacher of Care of Magical Creatures following his retirement - a job Hagrid had always wanted.

Around the end of the 1993-1994 school year , Cornelius Fudge, still Minister for Magic at the time, also returned to the hut, this time accompanied by Walden Macnair , Albus Dumbledore , and an elderly committee member from the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures , to oversee the planned execution of Buckbeak the Hippogriff after the creature had reportedly injured Draco Malfoy's arm.

Shortly after, when Harry and Hermione from the future saved Buckbeak, they, along with the creature, took refuge in Hagrid's empty cabin for safety while Remus Lupin transformed into a werewolf , remaining there until it was safe to return to the Forbidden Forest.
A lesson focused on Blast-Ended Skrewts in front of the hut

In one Care of Magical Creatures lesson during the 1994-1995 school year , Hagrid introduced the Gryffindor and Slytherin students to his newly bred beasts , the Blast-Ended Skrewts , in front of his hut.
Hundreds of these creatures were kept in several open wooden crates.
The Skrewts resembled deformed, shell-less lobsters -horribly pale, slimy, and with legs sticking out at odd angles.
They had no visible heads and measured about six inches in length, crawling over one another and bumping blindly into the sides of their boxes.
They also emitted a strong stench of rotting fish.
During the lesson, Draco Malfoy questioned Hagrid about the purpose of breeding such creatures .
Second Wizarding War
Dolores Umbridge in Hagrid's hut
In the first quarter of the 1995-1996 school year at Hogwarts, the Ministry appointed Dolores Umbridge as the new Defence Against the Dark Arts professor.
Around this time, Professor Dumbledore sent Hagrid to seek out the last colony of giants , leaving the hut deserted.
Upon his return, Harry, Ron, and Hermione were among the first to notice, spotting smoke rising from the hut's fireplace.
Umbridge soon visited Hagrid's hut, questioning him about his absence and the mission he had been sent on.
With her strong prejudice against half-breeds , particularly half-giants , she was intent on having Hagrid dismissed from Hogwarts.
Umbridge succeeded in this when she became Headmistress, replacing Professor Dumbledore.
Near the end of the school year, Hagrid was forcibly removed from the Hogwarts grounds by Umbridge with the help of several corrupt Ministry Aurors , including John Dawlish .

However, following Umbridge's removal from Hogwarts and Dumbledore's reinstatement as Headmaster, Hagrid was welcomed back to his roles as Care of Magical Creatures teacher and Keeper of Keys and Grounds .
Hagrid and Harry attempting to douse the flames engulfing his hut
In early 1997 , Aragog died of ill health.
Hagrid held a funeral for him outside his hut, attended by himself, Harry Potter, Horace Slughorn , and Fang.
Slughorn delivered a eulogy and buried Aragog, after which they all went inside to share some alcohol .
Under the influence of Felix Felicis , Harry successfully persuaded Slughorn to give him his memory of informing a young Tom Riddle about Horcruxes.
Before the end of the 1996-1997 school year , Death Eaters infiltrated Hogwarts Castle with the assistance of Draco Malfoy .
Professor Snape , as a Death Eater, escorted them to carry out the mission assigned to him.
After casting the Killing Curse on Professor Dumbledore, Harry pursued Snape and the Death Eaters, joined by Draco Malfoy, until they reached the grounds outside the castle.
During the confrontation, Death Eater Thorfinn Rowle used the Fire-Making Spell , setting Hagrid's hut ablaze with an explosive bang.
Hagrid rescued his dog Fang, trapped inside the hut, and then, together with Harry, used the Water-Making Spell to extinguish the flames.
Hagrid's Hut was repaired after the fire.
During the 1997-1998 school year , in which Hogwarts was under the control of the Death Eaters, Hagrid held a "Support Harry Potter" party in his hut which forced him into hiding.
After the war
After the Second Wizarding War ended following the Battle of Hogwarts , Hagrid returned to his hut and continued living there with Fang.
He remained there into the 2010s , still serving as the Hogwarts gamekeeper, the Keeper of Keys and Grounds, and the Professor of Care of Magical Creatures.
Interior
There was only one room inside, with hams and pheasants hanging from the ceiling.
There was also a fireplace where, most of the time, a copper kettle was used to boil water.
In the corner stood a massive bed with a patchwork quilt over it.
Sometimes, when Hagrid did not use his personal belongings, including his pink umbrella , his moleskin coat, and his crossbow, he kept those items inside the hut.
Other items found inside the hut were ingredients for foods and items used by him in teaching Care of Magical Creatures .
Notes and references

title: Bay horse
paragraphs: A bay horse is used to describe the type of horse with reddish-brown body coat with black point coloration.
Both the female and male bay horses, the Bay mare and Bay stallion, are possible corporeal forms of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Beagle
paragraphs: The beagle is a small breed of dog that originated in England and bred to hunt hare .
The beagle is a very intelligent and popular pet.
It is a known corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Hare
paragraphs: Hares are leporids belonging to the genus Lepus .
Overview
The hare was a possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
One was depicted among other animals in the wall illustrations at Platform Nine and Three-Quarters .
Known types of hares included Brown Hares , Mountain Hares , and Spotted Hares .
History
On 1 September 1993 , after the Dementor incident on the Hogwarts Express , the wrapper of the chocolate bar Remus Lupin handed out had a pattern of three conjoined hares as its design.

The Patronus of Luna Lovegood was a hare; she first conjured it late in her fourth year during the lessons taken by Dumbledore's Army , taught by Harry Potter in 1996 and employed in the Battle of Hogwarts on 2 May 1998 .
Nymphadora Tonks also had a hare patronus, specifically in the form of a Jack Rabbit , until her growing love for Remus Lupin , a werewolf , in 1996 resulted in it changing to a wolf .
Notes and references

title: Black cat
paragraphs: A black cat is a type of cat , commonly recognised by of its black fur.
It is not a particular breed of cat and may be mixed or of a specific breed.
Some believed black cats were evil and brought bad luck.
A black cat was one rare possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History
Black cat was one of several species of cats available at Magical Menagerie on Diagon Alley .
One could purchase one for 9 Galleons .

During her childhood, Merula Snyde 's aunt taught her that black cats were inherently evil, leading to her later attempting to banish a Matagot from Hogwarts due to the creature's resemblance to a black cat.
At least one black cat lived in the Sphinx Club.
Millicent Bulstrode owned a black cat at Hogwarts in the 1990s .
Daniel Page 's corporeal Patronus assumed the form of a black cat.
Notes and references

title: Matagot who befriended Mrs Norris
paragraphs: This Matagot befriended Mrs Norris in the 1980s .
Biography
During the 1988-1989 school year , this Matagot met and befriended Mrs Norris , playing with her repeatedly over several days.

Eventually, Mrs Norris's owner, Argus Filch , noticed that she was seemingly being followed by a mysterious beast while they were leaving the Hogwarts Library after a visit with Madam Irma Pince , with the creature continuing to follow her over the following days.
Filch reported this situation to Rubeus Hagrid , who asked Jacob's sibling to meet up with them in the Three Broomsticks Inn in order to ask for their help.

Jacob's sibling initially assumed that Filch was still upset about their having previously turned Mrs Norris pink temporarily for the Valentine's Day Ball , but, upon being informed of the situation, asked Filch to try to describe the creature.

Filch's description, combined with Madam Rosmerta 's mention that she had seen several black cats lurking behind the pub, led Hagrid to suggest that Mrs Norris was actually being stalked by a Matagot, surprising Jacob's sibling, who had previously bonded with another Matagot at the Magical Creatures Reserve .
Hagrid explained that Matagots were usually friendly but, if they felt threatened or if someone tried to cast a spell against them, they could be very dangerous.

Hagrid claimed that Filch was therefore right to meet them far away from Hogwarts , to which Filch affirmed, stating that he wouldn't let Mrs Norris out of his sight until the creature was dealt with.
Jacob's sibling offered to track down the Matagot and keep Mrs Norris safe from it, hoping to keep Hogwarts safe for all who lived within it.
They asked Filch where he had last seen the Matagot, with Filch claiming that he had seen it hiding at the Training Grounds during his morning patrol of the area.
Jacob's sibling suggested that Filch and Mrs Norris should wait in the Clock Tower Courtyard until the matter had been dealt with and then headed out in search of the rogue Matagot.
Upon arriving at the Training Grounds, Jacob's sibling encountered Ben Copper practising Anteoculatia and other offensive spells on a set of Mechanical Death Eaters .

After both explained to the other what they were doing on the Training Grounds, Ben offered his help in tracking down the stray Matagot, with Jacob's sibling asking if he saw anything unusual in the area where the creature was last seen.
While Ben claimed that he had seen Chiara Lobosca heading towards the Forbidden Forest , he hadn't seen or heard any mysterious creature lurking around the area despite being there all night.
At that moment, the pair heard a loud sound seemingly coming from somewhere nearby.
The pair searched the area to try to find the source of the sound, hearing it again from somewhere behind an entrance way.
At that moment, a black cat emerged from the entrance way and entered the Training Grounds.
Thinking the cat was harmless, Ben attempted to approach it despite Jacob's sibling's warnings, leading to the cat morphing into its spirit form in response, revealing that it was the rogue Matagot.

Jacob's sibling and Ben quickly moved out of this Matagot's way as it ran away from the Training Grounds and towards the Clock Tower Courtyard, with Jacob's sibling rushing after it to ensure that it didn't harm Mrs Norris.
Upon reaching the courtyard, Jacob's sibling encountered Mrs Norris seemingly fighting with this Matagot, now back in its black cat form, much to the anger of Filch.
Jacob's sibling successfully managed to scare this Matagot away from Mrs Norris, with it transforming once again as it escaped, leading to a rare moment of gratitude from Filch.
Liz Tuttle suddenly arrived at the courtyard, saddened that Jacob's sibling had chased away this "cute" Matagot.

After Jacob's sibling explained the situation to her, Liz claimed that this Matagot attacking Mrs Norris didn't make any sense based on her observations, suggesting that the situation might be due to a misunderstanding.

Liz suggested that this Matagot was actually trying to play with Mrs Norris, explaining that she had observed them playing together repeatedly and claiming that the two were actually friends, with the situation reminding Jacob's sibling of Mrs Norris befriending a Chimaera previously.
Filch, now furious that Jacob's sibling had made Mrs Norris upset by chasing away this Matagot, demanded that they find it and reunite the two.
Jacob's sibling agreed to try to find the creature, but claimed that it would take time and effort to earn its trust after having just chased it off.
Jacob's sibling decided to locate this Matagot and then bring it to Hagrid, hoping that he could help them bond with the creature.
Hagrid soon informed Jacob's sibling that this Matagot had fled to his garden , where Jacob's sibling met up with him and explained their misunderstanding.

Hagrid agreed to help Jacob's sibling gain this Matagot's trust, but suggested that they needed to calm down the agitated Matagot first, claiming that Matagots were very dangerous when they felt threatened, especially in their spirit form.

Hagrid suggested that Jacob's sibling should try to revert this Matagot back to its friendlier form by showing it that they meant no harm through a friendly gesture, with Jacob's sibling realising that they could try offering it some food.
Jacob's sibling managed to convince this Matagot to return to its friendly form as a result of the food offering, with Hagrid claiming that it was now safe to try to befriend it.
Jacob's sibling attempted to approach this Matagot to give it a friendly pat, but Fang suddenly ran into the garden and began to bark at this Matagot, scaring it away once again.
Hagrid explained that Fang used to be scared of cats , with his aggressive reaction to this Matagot appearing to be overcompensation for his previous fear.

However, Jacob's sibling realised that this Matagot's reaction to dogs , in combination with other feline-like behaviours it had displayed that resembled those of Jacob's sibling's pet cat , meant that speaking with another magical feline owner might help them understand how to best befriend this Matagot.
Hagrid agreed and suggested that Jacob's sibling should speak with Hogwarts' Quidditch announcer Murphy McNully , as he owned a Kneazle named Kneil and would surely be willing to help.
After rounding up this Matagot, Jacob's sibling met with Murphy and Kneil in the Care of Magical Creatures classroom and explained the situation to them.

Jacob's sibling claimed that, while they did own a cat, it wasn't a magical creature like Kneil was, asking Murphy to help teach them some tricks to try to appeal to this Matagot's cat-like instincts.

Murphy agreed to help and suggested that Jacob's sibling could use a bright light and allow the Matagot to chase it, leading to Jacob's sibling suggesting that they could illuminate the tip of their wand with the Wand-Lighting Charm and allow this Matagot to chase after it.
Jacob's sibling quickly cast the spell , resulting in this Matagot happily playing with them.

However, at that moment, Merula Snyde , mistakenly believing that the "hideous black cat" was trying to attack Jacob's sibling, charged at this Matagot, which immediately transitioned back into its spirit form in fright.
Jacob's sibling attempted to explain the situation, but Merula quickly cast a Stunning Spell at this Matagot, hitting it and causing it to split into two Matagots.
Both Matagots quickly ran away from the scene, with Merula following after them, swearing to find them and drive them away from Hogwarts once and for all.
Jacob's sibling followed after them, finding Merula threatening both Matagots in the Forest Grove of the Forbidden Forest.
Jacob's sibling finally managed to explain the situation to Merula, revealing that this Matagot was not attacking them and that it was actually friends with Mrs Norris.

Merula agreed that she had jumped to conclusions about the Matagot, explaining that her aunt had raised her to believe black cats were evil and that she had assumed the worst when she saw this Matagot, although she continued to deny that she was superstitious or that she believed in bad luck.
Merula agreed to allow the newly duplicated Matagots to remain on Hogwarts grounds, although she claimed that she was doing so for Mrs Norris, not Jacob's sibling.
Jacob's sibling offered some treats to the Matagots, calming them both down.

Upon hearing that Jacob's sibling was taking these Matagots back to Hagrid's garden to reunite with Mrs Norris, Merula decided to join them there, sheepishly claiming that she would be there for security purposes rather than getting the opportunity to watch adorable creatures play.
Jacob's sibling brought both of these Matagots back to Hagrid's garden, where they met up with Filch, Mrs Norris, Hagrid, Merula, Liz, Murphy, and Kneil.

As the two Matagots played with Mrs Norris and Kneil, Filch thanked Jacob's sibling for helping make Mrs Norris happier, but was confused as to why there were now two Matagots, to which Jacob's sibling jokingly offered to explain what happened to Filch over some Butterbeers at the Three Broomsticks, to Filch's slight annoyance.
The group then watched the two Matagots happily playing with Mrs Norris and Kneil, with Hagrid thanking Jacob's sibling for all of their help.

After the Matagots allowed Jacob's sibling to pet them, Hagrid claimed that Jacob's sibling had proven that they were a true friend to these creatures, suggesting that they should be allowed to stay at Hogwarts so that Jacob's sibling and Mrs Norris could visit them whenever they liked, to which Jacob's sibling happily agreed.

Hagrid affirmed that Jacob's sibling should also keep inviting their older friends to these play-dates, with Jacob's sibling happily confirming that they would even invite Merula to watch the creatures playing once again.
Notes and references

title: Millicent Bulstrode's cat
paragraphs: This black cat was owned by the Slytherin student Millicent Bulstrode at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry as a pet.
Biography
Hermione having partially transformed into this cat
On 17 December 1992 , Hermione Granger plucked a small hair of the cat from Millicent Bulstrode's robes in the Great Hall , thinking it was from her.

She unknowingly added the cat's hair to the Polyjuice Potion after completing it on 25 December 1992 in Moaning Myrtle's Bathroom , hoping to turn into Millicent so she could infiltrate the Slytherin common room with Harry Potter and Ronald Weasley .

However, as Polyjuice Potion was not meant for non-human transformations, Hermione was instead partially transformed into a cat; Harry and Ron later found Hermione hiding in a bathroom cubicle with the face and tail of a cat, with Moaning Myrtle laughing at her.
Notes and references

title: Black and white cat
paragraphs: A black and white cat is a type of cat , commonly recognised by its black and white fur.
It was one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Calico cat
paragraphs: A calico cat is a type of cat , the colouring of which is a combination of tortoiseshell and white .
It was one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History
The 19th-century Auror , Patricia McManners , was an unregistered calico cat Animagus .
Calico cats could be found in Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Hogsmeade and other wizarding villages.
Notes and references

title: Ginger cat
paragraphs: A ginger cat is a coat-colour of cat , commonly recognised by its ginger fur.
It was a possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Ginger was one of several colours of cats available at the Magical Menagerie in Diagon Alley .
One could be purchased for 9 Galleons .
History
The ginger cat was one of several cat coats that could be found in Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Hogsmeade and other wizarding villages in the late 1890s .
Notes and references

title: Siamese cat
paragraphs: Siamese cat is one of the first distinctly recognised breeds of oriental cat.
The breed originated in Thailand (formerly known as Siam).
History
Siamese cat was one of several species of cats available at Magical Menagerie in Diagon Alley .
One could purchase it for 11 Galleons .
In the late 1890s , in Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Hogsmeade and other wizarding villages, Siamese cats were one of several breeds of cat that could be found.
During the 1980s , at least one Siamese cat lived at the Sphinx Club alongside other cat breeds.
Notes and references

title: Tabby cat
paragraphs: A tabby cat is any cat that has a distinctive coat that features stripes, dots, lines or swirling patterns, usually together with a mark resembling an "M" on its forehead.
Tabbies are sometimes erroneously assumed to be a cat breed.
History
During the 1890s , grey tabby cats could be found living in Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Hogsmeade and other witching villages.
Tabby cat was one of several types of cats available at Magical Menagerie on Diagon Alley .
One could purchase it for 9 Galleons .
Minerva McGonagall , former Transfiguration teacher and Headmistress at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , was an Animagus that could morph into a tabby cat.
At the end of the 20th century , grey tabby cats lived in the Sphinx Club and Hippogriff Club , as well as in the Egyptian Marketplace .
Notes and references

title: Tortoiseshell cat
paragraphs: A tortoiseshell cat is a type of cat , the coat of which consists of two of the fur colours black , brown and orange .
It was a possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History
In the 19th century , cats with this coat could be found living at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , as well as in Hogsmeade and other wizarding villages in Scottish Highlands .
At least one tortoiseshell cat lived in the Brazilian wizarding village of Rio Escondido in the 1990s .
Notes and references

title: White cat
paragraphs: The white cat is a type of cat , commonly recognised by its pure white fur.
Some white cats suffer from congenital deafness caused by degeneration of the inner ear.
White cat was one of several species of cats available at Magical Menagerie on Diagon Alley .
One could purchase it for 9 Galleons .
Notes and references

title: Black Bear
paragraphs: A Black Bear is a species of bear and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Bear
paragraphs: A bear is a large dog -like mammal, and one of the largest carnivores living on land.
History
Harry Potter once described Rubeus Hagrid in his overcoat as looking similar to an overgrown bear on its hind legs.
Hagrid also owned a coat that was actually made of bearskin.
A teddy bear is a type of stuffed toy that more-or-less takes the appearance of this animal.
Hagrid packed a teddy bear for Norberta when sending her off to live in Romania .
Notes and references

title: Blackbird
paragraphs: A blackbird is a species of bird and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Black Mamba
paragraphs: A Black Mamba is an extremely venomous species of snake and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Black horse
paragraphs: A black horse is used to describe the type of horse with the entire hair coat black.
Both the female and male black horses, the Black Mare and Black Stallion, are possible corporeal forms of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Black Swan
paragraphs: A Black Swan is a species of swan and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Bloodhound
paragraphs: A Bloodhound is a breed of dog and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Borzoi
paragraphs: A Borzoi is a breed of dog and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Brown Bear
paragraphs: A Brown Bear is a species of bear and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Brown Hare
paragraphs: A Brown Hare is a type of hare and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Brown owl
paragraphs: The brown owl is a species of owl , noted for its superb binocular vision and directional hearing, making them excellent hunters towards rodents and voles .
It was also a corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History
The brown owl was one of several species of owls sold at Eeylops Owl Emporium .
One could purchase it for 10 Galleons .

On 22 January 1995 , Harry Potter sent Sirius Black a brown owl to deliver a letter informing him about the events that he had seen and overheard the night that he visited the Prefects' Bathroom to work out his golden egg clue.
A brown owl was amongst the owls that delivered hate mail to Hermione Granger in February 1995 following the publication of the article "Harry Potter's Secret Heartache" in Witch Weekly .
Notes and references

title: Vole
paragraphs: A vole is a small rodent resembling a mouse but with a stouter body and a shorter, hairier tail and a slightly rounder head.
History
The Owlery floor was covered in regurgitated skeletons of these creatures, indicating that they are a favourite food of owls .
An Aged witch near Knockturn Alley warned Harry Potter in 1992 not to go from Diagon Alley to Knockturn Alley, and threatened him with turning him into a vole.
Jarveys are known to eat these.
A vole is one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Eeylops Owl Emporium
paragraphs: Eeylops Owl Emporium was a chain of shops that sold owls and supplies to care for them, such as food .
It had three locations in Glasgow , Leeds , and London .
An Owl Post Office , owls were also hired to deliver letters and parcels.
Description
The front of the emporium
The London store was located at 521 Diagon Alley , on the North Side of Diagon Alley .
It was described as being relatively small, and dark inside, likely because owls were nocturnal creatures.
On the outside of the shop, many different colours and species of owls hung in cages, watching all of the passers-by.
There was also a sign which read "Eeylops Owl Emporium - Tawny, Screech, Barn, Brown and Snowy" .

Professor Zorble , also called the Postmaster, operated the emporium during the early 21st century and had at least five types of owls available during that time: the scops owl , Brown Fish owl , barred owl , barn owl , and eagle owl .
History
On 31 July 1991 , Rubeus Hagrid brought Harry Potter into Eeylops Owl Emporium to buy him his pet owl, Hedwig for his eleventh birthday present.
During the Christmas holidays in 1992 , Eyelops Owl Emporium was closed, as the owner went bird-watching in Wales .
In August 1996 , Harry and Ron Weasley bought large boxes of owl nuts at Eeylops Owl Emporium for Hedwig and Pigwidgeon respectively.
Before September 2008 , Rubeus Hagrid brought a new Hogwarts student to the Owl Post Office to choose their first owl .
After speaking to the postmaster Professor Zorble and picking an owl, Hagrid purchased it for them as a gift.
Sales
Known employees
Notes and references

title: 22 January
paragraphs: 22 January is the 22nd day of the year.
There are 343 days remaining (344 in leap years).

title: Harry Potter's letter to Sirius Black (1995) I
paragraphs: This letter was written by Harry Potter to his godfather, Sirius Black , on 22 January 1995 .
The letter described the events of the previous night, when Harry had sneaked out of the Gryffindor Tower to work on the golden egg .
Content
Harry wrote about Barty Crouch appearing on the Marauder's Map in the Potions Storeroom , as well as his encounter with Alastor Moody , Snape , and Argus Filch on the staircase.
However, in the excitement of recounting these events, Harry forgot to mention what he had discovered about the Second Task of the Triwizard Tournament .
As a result, when Sirius replied, he was unable to offer any advice.
Response
Sirius, in response to this letter, sent a letter of his own, simply saying " Send date of next Hogsmeade weekend by return owl. "
Notes and references

title: Tawny owl
paragraphs: The tawny owl is a species of owl , noted for its excellent hearing and their famous 'twit-tawoo' call between males and females.
The tawny owl was one of several species of owls sold at Eeylops Owl Emporium .
One could purchase it for 10 Galleons .
History

Early in the morning on 1 November , 1981 , a large tawny owl, one of several owls that would be traversing the skies that day due to Voldemort 's recent downfall, passed by the windows of 4 Privet Drive .
It was unseen by the Dursley family , who were busy with their morning routine.

Harry Potter 's third year supply list and Hogsmeade permission form , as well as a letter and birthday present from Rubeus Hagrid , were delivered to him by a tawny owl from Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
This owl was very professional, "ruffling its feathers importantly" and leaving immediately after delivering its load.
Neville Longbottom 's grandmother, Augusta , had a tawny owl that she sometimes used to send him things that he forgot.
A tawny owl was amongst the owls that delivered hate mail to Hermione Granger in February 1995 following the publication of the article "Harry Potter's Secret Heartache" in Witch Weekly .

Later that year, on 26 May , another tawny delivered her a copy of the morning's Daily Prophet , which she scanned and her to her delight discovered that Rita Skeeter had not uncovered the strange events regarding Bartemius Crouch Snr that happened two nights past.
Notes and references

title: Barn owl
paragraphs: The barn owl is a species of owl , common in Europe , distinct for its acute sense of hearing.
The barn owl was one of several species of owls sold at Eeylops Owl Emporium .
One could purchase it for 10 Galleons .
History

An unidentified 19th-century Hogwarts student with the rare ability to see traces of ancient magic owned a barn owl during their fifth year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in the 1890-1891 school year .

Augusta Longbottom owned a barn owl, which she used to send her grandson Neville a Remembrall in 1991 , and a Howler in 1994 , though by the start of the 1994-1995 school year , she was using a tawny owl instead.
On 31 July 1992 , Mafalda Hopkirk sent a barn owl to deliver a warning letter to Harry Potter for "his" illegal use of magic at 4 Privet Drive .
The owl dropped the letter on Mrs Mason 's head, causing her to scream and run out of the house due to her extreme fear of birds.

At least four barn owls were amongst the owls that delivered hate mail to Hermione Granger in February 1995 following the publication of the article "Harry Potter's Secret Heartache" in Witch Weekly .

During the summer holidays of 1995, a barn owl delivered Harry Potter a letter from Arthur Weasley telling him that Albus Dumbledore was trying to sort things out with the British Ministry of Magic regarding his usage of underage magic and to not do any more magic or leave 4 Privet Drive .
On 2 September of that year, Hermione received her copy of the morning's Daily Prophet from a barn owl.
Notes and references

title: Screech owl
paragraphs: Screech owls are a species of owl known for their agility.
Their diet consists of rabbits , voles , rats , mice and reptiles.
The screech owl was one of several species of owls sold at Eeylops Owl Emporium .
One could purchase it for 15 Galleons .
History
On 24 June 1995 , one of these owls delivered Hermione Granger her morning's copy of the Daily Prophet .

This was "as usual", so it is possible that this paper was always delivered to her by one of these birds, though on 2 September of that year at the start of the new school year , the paper was delivered to her by a barn owl instead.
Just a bit later in the year, however, she had another copy delivered to her by a screech owl.

During the summer holidays of that year, another of these owls sent Harry Potter an official letter from Mafalda Hopkirk telling him that he had been expelled from Hogwarts and that Ministry representatives were coming to destroy his wand .
Notes and references

title: Buffalo
paragraphs: A buffalo is a brown-haired herbivore with horns, and was a possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History

Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry Charms Master and Professor Filius Flitwick told his first-year class in 1991 that a wizard named Baruffio once mispronounced f as s and he and his wife ended with a buffalo on top of them.
A portrait of a buffalo sitting atop Baruffio could be found in Hogwarts Castle by 1890 .
Notes and references

title: Baruffio
paragraphs: Wizard Baruffio was a wizard with a speech impediment .
Biography

On account of his condition, he did not seem to have been able to perform particularly satisfactory magic , as he would mispronounce the incantations : once he said 's' instead of 'f' and conjured a buffalo on top of him,
Baruffio was also known for the invention of the potion Baruffio's Brain Elixir .
A portrait of Baruffio being sat upon by a buffalo could be found in Hogwarts Castle by 1890 .
Notes and references

title: Unidentified buffalo spell
paragraphs: This spell ( incantation unknown ) was unintentionally used by the wizard Baruffio sometime before 1991 when he mispronounced the letter "f" as "s" while reciting the incantation for another spell and ended up with a buffalo on his chest.
He also accidentally used the same spell to conjure a buffalo instead of a mink onto his wife 's shoulders.
Notes and references

title: Baruffio's wife
paragraphs: This individual was the wife of wizard Baruffio .
Notes and references

title: Jean-François Ménard
paragraphs: Jean-François Ménard (b. 10 July , 1948 ) is a French author and translator.
He translated the Harry Potter books written by J. K. Rowling into French, for the Gallimard publishing house.
He also has written some books, and translated the Artemis Fowl series into French as well.

title: Buzzard
paragraphs: A Buzzard is a medium-to-large bird of prey which has a large range.
A member of the genus Buteo , it is a member of the family Accipitirdae.
The buzzard is one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Capuchin Monkey
paragraphs: The Capuchin Monkey (binomial name Cebus) is a New World member of the primate family Cebinae.
It is a possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Cheetah
paragraphs: The cheetah is a species of big cat that is native to to Africa .
It is characterised by its incredible running speed (up to 114 kilometres/71 miles per hour) and its light orange coat spotted with black dots.
It was one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History

At an International Symposium of Animagi held circa 2016 , students from Uagadou , a school located in Uganda , transformed into their Animagus forms (which included elephants and cheetahs) in a synchronised display.
Notes and references

title: International Symposium of Animagi
paragraphs: The International Symposium of Animagi is an international gathering of Animagi held at unknown intervals.
History
The most recent symposium (as of 2016 ) attracted a lot of press after a synchronised demonstration of Animagus transformations staged by the Uagadou School Team nearly provoked a riot.
Many older, more experienced attendees felt threatened by the sight of teenage witches and wizards turning at will into elephants and cheetahs .
Adrian Tutley even lodged a formal complaint with the International Confederation of Wizards .
Notes and references

title: Uganda
paragraphs: Uganda is a landlocked nation located in East Africa .
The grey crowned crane is the national bird of Uganda.
Magical games and sports
A 1994 Quidditch World Cup attendee waving a Ugandan flag
This country had its own national Quidditch team .
They beat Wales at the 1994 Quidditch World Cup .
The country also had another team called the Patonga Proudsticks , from the town of Patonga .
Magical education
Uagadou was located in Uganda, but it took students from all over Africa .
Notes and references

title: Elephant
paragraphs: The elephant is the largest land mammal on earth, characterised by its long trunk, tusks, big, flat ears, column-like legs, and greyish to brown skin.
There are two main extant species of elephant as of the 20th century , one ( Loxodonta africana ) native to Africa , the other ( Elephas maximus ) native to south and south-east Asia .
An elephant was one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History
Hedley Fleetwood had a Patronus that took the form of a woolly mammoth , an extinct species of elephant, a rare example of someone having an extinct animal as a Patronus.
Elephant on a Bicycle was the name of a magical sweet produced by Honeydukes that enabled the consumer to produce animal noises, including those of an elephant.
In 1943 , Horace Slughorn was said to shake his head an old elephant bothered by mosquitos while Tom Riddle was goading him about the nature of Horcruxes .

After graduating from Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Glenna Golding worked at the British Ministry of Magic in the Department of Magical Accidents and Catastrophes as part of the Muggle-Worthy Excuse Committee .

She enjoyed making up excuses for magic, but felt that the Ministry didn't appreciate some of her more creative efforts, with her frequent attempts to blame magical incidents on a herd of African elephants being usually nixed straight away.

In the summer of 1991 , Harry Potter though that he would look like he was wearing bits of old elephant skin with his school uniform at Stonewall High , which his aunt Petunia 's had made by dying pieces of Dudley 's old clothing.
Aragog , an Acromantula spider , was said to be the size of a small baby elephant by 1993 .
A painting of an elephant hung in the Grand Staircase at Hogwarts .
The Abraxan Winged horses owned by the Beauxbatons Academy of Magic were said to be the size of elephants.
In early 1995 , Draco Malfoy cruelly referred to Rubeus Hagrid , a half-giant , as the "elephant-man" to Harry Potter in order to provoke him.
Elephant and Castle was the name of an area around a major road junction in London .
In December 1995 , Harry Potter witnessed wizards and witches at St Mungo's Hospital with elephant trunks.
In the last battle of the Battle of Hogwarts on 2 May 1998 , Lord Voldemort 's giants were said to charge at Grawp , a fellow giant like bull elephants.

At an International Symposium of Animagi held circa 2016 , students from Uagadou School of Magic , a school located in Uganda , transformed into their Animagus forms (which included elephants and cheetahs ) in a synchronised demonstration.
Notes and references

title: Chestnut horse
paragraphs: A chestnut horse is used to describe the type of horse with a reddish-to-brown coat with a mane and tail the same or lighter in colour than the coat.
Both the female and male Chestnut horses, the Chestnut Mare and Chestnut Stallion, are possible corporeal forms of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Chow Dog
paragraphs: A Chow Dog is a species of dog and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Crow
paragraphs: The crow is a passerine member in the order of birds and is native to Great Britain .
A crow was one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History
Morrigan , a famous Irish witch, was an Animagus and could turn into a crow.
Crows could be seen at the ruins of Percival Rackham 's house, as well as in the Highlands of Scotland .
Some crows resided in Rubeus Hagrid 's pumpkin patch in the 1993-1994 school year .
One of them acted like a guard by sitting on a wood-marker that was holding Buckbeak , waiting for execution.
This crow bit Harry Potter when he tried to free Buckbeak.
They all flew away when the executioner Walden Macnair cut an enlarged pumpkin in half with his axe .
One of them also sat on then- Minister for Magic Cornelius Fudge 's bowler.
Crows were also often seen hanging out on the top of the Bell towers near the bells.
At least from 2017 , crows were allowed as pets at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , as some students were seen with crows.
Notes and references

title: Morrigan
paragraphs: Morrigan was a famous Irish pure-blood witch , notable for being an Animagus who could turn into a crow .
Morrigan was an ancestor of William Sayre .
William nicknamed his daughter, Isolt , "Morrigan" due to her affinity for all things natural when she was young.
Magical skills and abilities
Etymology

According to Irish mythology , the Morrígan ("phantom queen") or Mórrígan (moe-ree-gan) ("great queen") was a Celtic goddess associated with fertility, war, death, and fate, especially with foretelling doom and death in battle - in this capacity, she would take the shape of a crow, flying above the battlefield.
The Morrígan was often portrayed as a trio of sisters, (the three Morrígna) which can explain the many different things she was associated with.
Notes and references

title: Ruins of Percival Rackham's house
paragraphs: These ruins were the remains of a house belonging to Percival Rackham .
Once thriving, it had been abandoned and left for nature to destroy it.
The building was in partial ruin and the bridge to it had collapsed.
Description
The ruin was perched on a rock and connected to the mainland via a bridge.
The main hall had a statue of Rackham who was once the owner of it.
One part of the wall had a mural on it that suggested the owner was a Seer .
Another had an enchanted, crystallised stone on it.
History
In Tudor times, Charles Rookwood and Percival Rackham used the building to create a private entrance to Gringotts Wizarding Bank behind a wall with an enchanted , crystallised stone on it.
They protected the entrance with ancient magic so only those with the ability to detect it could follow their path.
They also enchanted a key to serve as a Portkey to the ruins.
Mural of Percival Rackham
Long before 1890 , the building was abandoned and over time, destroyed by nature and left in ruin.
The path which led to a bridge had an enchanted wall of ice protecting it.
The bridge to the building had collapsed.
Miriam Fig sent her friend George Osric a container with the key inside.
Eleazar Fig and his new student opened the container and travelled to the ruin via the Portkey.
In order to reach the ruin, the student used a spell to break the ice.
Eleazar fixed the bridge.
They began exploring the ruin which led the student to the enchanted stone on a wall glowing with ancient magic.
Behind the wall was a glowing room which revealed itself when they used magic on it.
Upon touching it, they were transported to Gringotts.
Notes and references

title: Hogwarts gamekeeper's pumpkin patch
paragraphs: This pumpkin patch was owned and cared for by two gamekeepers at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry : an unidentified gamekeeper in the 1890s , and Rubeus Hagrid .
It was located behind Hagrid's Hut on the Hogwarts grounds .
History
An 1890s gamekeeper tending to the pumpkin patch
In the 1890-1891 school year , a pumpkin patch was grown in the same spot by one of Hagrid's predecessors .

At some point around Christmas between 1983 and 1990 , Greywing was distraught because he felt protective of Hagrid's pumpkins, which were no longer growing due to the winter, and was visibly distressed.
Albus Dumbledore gave her a pot of Leprechaun gold to protect instead, which cheered her up.
In 1986 , when Fang was a puppy, he was in the pumpkin patch when he found a fairy in it which scared him.
Fang then ran away and Hagrid couldn't find him, thus he asked for Jacob's sibling 's help towards finding him.
The pumpkin patch in 1994
In 1993 , Hagrid used his pumpkin patch to tether the hippogriff Buckbeak while awaiting its sentence of death.

With help from the Time-Turner , Harry Potter and Hermione Granger were able to successfully remove Buckbeak out of the pumpkin patch before his execution by pulling him with rope into the forest , take him back inside Hagrid's hut after everyone had else had left it, and let Sirius take him to be free.
In 1996 , the pumpkin patch was where Aragog 's funeral took place.
With the aid of Harry and Horace Slughorn , Hagrid dug a grave for the Acromantula and laid the enormous spider to rest with Slughorn saying a eulogy celebrating his memory.
Usage
The pumpkin patch was where the gamekeeper grew enormous pumpkins for the school's Hallowe'en feast every year on 31 October .
These pumpkins were usually carved into Jack-o-Lanterns and enchanted to hang from the ceiling in the Great Hall or in the corridors.
Notes and references

title: Crow
paragraphs: The crow is a passerine member in the order of birds and is native to Great Britain .
A crow was one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History
Morrigan , a famous Irish witch, was an Animagus and could turn into a crow.
Crows could be seen at the ruins of Percival Rackham 's house, as well as in the Highlands of Scotland .
Some crows resided in Rubeus Hagrid 's pumpkin patch in the 1993-1994 school year .
One of them acted like a guard by sitting on a wood-marker that was holding Buckbeak , waiting for execution.
This crow bit Harry Potter when he tried to free Buckbeak.
They all flew away when the executioner Walden Macnair cut an enlarged pumpkin in half with his axe .
One of them also sat on then- Minister for Magic Cornelius Fudge 's bowler.
Crows were also often seen hanging out on the top of the Bell towers near the bells.
At least from 2017 , crows were allowed as pets at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , as some students were seen with crows.
Notes and references

title: Pumpkin
paragraphs: A pumpkin is a gourd-like squash that grows on vines.
It is cultivated for its large pulpy round orange fruit with firm orange skin, and numerous seeds.
Overview
The Pumpkin-Head Jinx encased the victim's head in a pumpkin; the Pompion Potion also had this effect.
Pumpkin Pasties , Pumpkin juice , pumpkin tea , and pumpkin bread were made from pumpkins.
Pumpkin fizz was a pumpkin-flavoured drink.
The outer rind of pumpkins was used as a potion ingredient.
The wizarding shop Pumpkins R Us specialised in pumpkins.
The owner Dagbert Pips cultivated luminous pumpkins , flying pumpkins , exploding pumpkins and singing pumpkins , which were sold in the shop to wizards at Hallowe'en time.

In 1992 , Pips wrote to the Daily Prophet in order to express his dismay at proposed British Ministry of Magic restrictions on how wizards could celebrate Hallowe'en, saying that he had spent the last five years cultivating his magical pumpkins for a living.
Hogwarts legend had it that Pumpkin Johnny was a Hogwarts student with a fondness for pumpkins until a malicious peer targeted him with a Pumpkin-Head Jinx one Hallowe'en .
With his head trapped inside the gourd, he fled into the Forbidden Forest and vanished forever.

According to the myth, summoning him required chanting his name three times on Hallowe'en; he supposedly returned to terrorise the castle until the students learnt that cruel pranks carry consequences.
History

In a 1913 Defence Against the Dark Arts at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry concerning Boggarts , an unidentified student used the Boggart-Banishing Spell to change a Boggart in the form of a Zombie into having the head of a pumpkin.
Talbott Winger 's mother grew pumpkins in her garden.

During the 1986-1987 school year , students Merula Snyde and Ismelda Murk adopted the persona of the Pumpkin Johny to frighten their classmates, though they were not behind the simultaneous pumpkin-smashing, graffiti, or the plague of nightmares that struck the school.
That same year, someone costumed as Pumpkin Johnny during Rubeus Hagrid 's Pumpkin Party .
Pumpkins as candle holders were among the Hallowe'en decorations used at Hogwarts .
It was said that " hundreds of carved pumpkins leered from every corner " at Hallowen'en in 1994 .
Rubeus Hagrid maintained a pumpkin patch outside his hut , which produced the pumpkins used to decorate the Great Hall for the Hallowe'en Feast .
Although the plants are not inherently magical , Hagrid gave them some "help" so that the pumpkins swell to the size of garden sheds by the time the feast rolls around.
Though Hagrid did not say so directly, Hermione Granger deduced that he had used an Engorgement Charm upon them.
The common rooms were also decorated with pumpkins at least once in the 1980s .

Preceding the Hallowe'en Feast in 1988 , many students - Rowan Khanna , Penny Haywood , William Weasley , Wilfred Levi Kidd , and another - volunteered to help Headmaster Dumbledore prepare decorations for the feast, which included carving pumpkins.
Buckbeak , a Hippogriff , lying amongst some pumpkins
In Harry Potter 's second year , these pumpkins were carved into lanterns large enough for three men to sit in and displayed during the Hogwarts Hallowe'en festivities.
Pumpkin tart was served at the Start-of-Term Feast in 1993 .
Later in school year , Harry, Hermione and Ron hid behind some pumpkins in order to not be seen by Professor Dumbledore , Cornelius Fudge and the Executioner .
Later that same night, Harry and Hermione went back to the pumpkin patch to rescue Buckbeak.
In frustration, following Buckbeak's rescue, Walden Macnair used his axe to slash one of the pumpkins.

In 1996 , following Albus Dumbledore 's escape from Hogwarts, Harry Potter heard a second year girl assuring another that Cornelius Fudge was lying in St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries with a pumpkin for a head.
The destroyed pumpkins
Around Hallowe'en 2010 , some of Hagrid's pumpkins were destroyed by a Blast-Ended Skrewt .
Some students, including Cassandra Vole and an unidentified student , then helped him grow new ones.
Notes and references

title: Bell Towers
paragraphs: The Bell Towers were two square towers that rose over the main entrance to the greenhouses of Hogwarts Castle .
Between the two towers were a set of double wooden doors which led to the Bell Tower Entrance Hall .
Notes and references

title: Cheyenne
paragraphs: Cheyenne

Cheyenne (hatched c. 2001 ) is a female Pied Crow who appeared as an unidentified crow in the pumpkin patch outside Rubeus Hagrid 's hut in the film adaptation of Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban .
Although her species is native to Africa , she was raised in captivity in California.
Notes and references

title: Dapple grey horse
paragraphs: A Dapple Grey horse is a variant of the general grey horses , being an intermediate stage not seen on all grey horses, consisting of a dark hair coat with "dapples," which are dark rings with lighter hairs on the inside of the ring, scattered over the entire body of the animal.
Both the female and male Dapple Grey horses, the Dapple Grey Mare and Dapple Grey Stallions, are possible corporeal forms of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Deerhound
paragraphs: A deerhound is a breed of dog and one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Dolphin
paragraphs: The dolphin is an aquatic mammal, part of the toothed whale family.
It was one possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Rubeus Hagrid , the Keeper of the Keys and Grounds of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , had feet in leather boots that were described as resembling a pair of baby dolphins.
Notes and references

title: Leather boots
paragraphs: Leather boots are boots which are made out of leather .
They can be worn in any type of weather.
This type of boot was used as a Portkey to get to the 1994 Quidditch World Cup at Stoatshead Hill in Devon , England .
Notes and references

title: Dan Fogler
paragraphs: Daniel Kevin "Dan" Fogler (b. 20 October , 1976 ) is an American stand-up comedian, actor, musician, playwright, filmmaker, and voice artist.
He portrayed Jacob Kowalski in the Fantastic Beasts film series .
He also narrated the audiobook Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald - Makers, Mysteries and Magic .
Notes and references

title: Dragonfly
paragraphs: The dragonfly was a type of insect, notable for its large wings and long body.
Description
Known species of dragonfly included the Imperial Dragonfly , which was stronger than the common variety.
Dragonflies were particularly susceptible to the Knockback Jinx , the Fire-Making Spell , the Full Body-Bind Curse , the Softening Charm , and Freezing Spell .
Like most winged creatures, they could resist the Levitation Charm .
The thorax of the dragonfly was used by wizards as a potion ingredient.
It was a possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
History
In 1982 , Elspeth MacGillony went to a lake with her father and watched as dragonflies flew close to the lake, tapping the water with their tails.
She counted the dragonflies and noticed that every time they flew near the surface, they reduced in number.

As Professor Trelawney arrived at the Hogwarts Christmas feast on 25 December 1993 , it was described that her green sequined dress made her "look more than ever like a glittering, oversized dragonfly".
Notes and references

title: Imperial Dragonfly
paragraphs: The Imperial Dragonfly was a species of dragonfly , having approximately twice the stamina as a normal dragonfly.
Description
Originally from the Far East , the species had spread worldwide by 1993 , making its native habitat in streams.
Compared to other similar Creatures , Imperial Dragonflies were particularly susceptible to the Knockback Jinx , the Fire-Making Spell , the Full Body-Bind Curse , the Softening Charm , and Glacius .
Being winged creatures, however, they were immune to the effects of the Levitation Charm .
History
Hogwarts Castle had an infestation of Imperial Dragonflies during the 1993-1994 school year .
Notes and references

title: Dragonfly thorax
paragraphs: The thorax of the dragonfly , when toasted, could be used as an ingredient in potion -making.
A required ingredient of the Girding Potion and the dragon dung fertiliser , these thoraxes could be purchased at the Apothecary in 1991 .
Notes and references

title: Elspeth MacGillony
paragraphs: Professor Elspeth MacGillony was a witch who attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in the late 20th century and returned to the school to teach Study of Ancient Runes as a substitute teacher during the 2010-2011 school year , while attempting to find a magical object in the Great Lake that could supposedly rid her of fears.
Biography
Early life
MacGillony was born into a family of unknown wizarding descent sometime around the year of 1976 .
In 1982 , her father took her to a lake, and they sat under a tree for a long time, gazing into the lake.
She watched as sunlight was reflected off the surface and dragonflies flew close to the lake, tapping the water with their tails.
She counted the dragonflies and noticed that every time they flew near the surface, they reduced in number.
She wanted to go near the lake, but her father stopped her.
A kelpie rescuing MacGillony
Nevertheless, she still approached the lake, but got into contact with something cold and dark .
She was grabbed by some kind of waterweeds, and felt like they were pulling her into the darkness, when in fact, it was exactly the kelpie that rescued her and lifted her out of the lake.
After she got out, she was determined to never go near the lake, or any lake ever again.
The traumatic experience would go on to haunt her for the rest of her life.
Hogwarts years (1988-1995)
MacGillony attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry from 1988 to 1995 .
On the eve of her arrival, she rode on a boat across the Great Lake with other first-year students and was scared by the waterweeds within.
Due to this incident, she was made fun of for several months.
Some claimed she was afraid of Flobberworms too, and some even put Cornish pixies into her pockets and laughed as she tossed the robes away.

MacGillony struggled with her studies during the first three years at the school, during which she came to resent students who were more accomplished than herself, whom she called " proud, righteous and always looking down on the weak and the fearful ".
In 1993 , as a fifth-year student, her magical abilities improved considerably, and she thought about retaliating against her bullies with the use of potions , hexes and curses .
She read about the Imperius Curse and was fascinated by it.
As students were forbidden from learning such curse, she went into the Forbidden Forest and practised it secretly.
She felt it was hard to master, but was getting the hang of it, as she successfully cast it upon several Nifflers , which walked by the lake as she wanted.
Quest for the crown of courage
In 2009 , she dreamt of being pulled towards the bottom of the lake again, during which she was unable to call for help, despite the magic she had mastered.
In order to end her suffering, she intended to go back to Hogwarts to find an object that could supposedly rid her of her fears.
MacGillony with McGonagall and students

During the 2010-2011 school year , MacGillony was invited back to the school by Headmistress Minerva McGonagall to serve as the substitute teacher of Study of Ancient Runes while Professor Clodagh Dromgoole was on leave.
Upon arrival, MacGillony met several third-year students by the Great Lake and talked with them about the beauty and danger of it.
McGonagall then approached them and greeted MacGillony, noting that she expected her in her office to get settled in for an hour.
for which MacGillony apologised and explained that she missed the place and wanted to walk around.
She formally introduced herself to the students and allowed them to call her by her first name.
She then left with McGonagall to see whether there was something else needed in her office.

MacGillony knew that the object she sought was in the Great Lake, and so not only did she frequently went to the lake and look into its depth, but she also began using the Imperius Curse on students to make them go into the lake and retrieve the object for her.

When an unidentified student who was investigating creatures in the lake by themself encountered her, she advised them to be careful and said that curiosity, while valuable, was a double-edged sword, since some secrets in the lake could be very dangerous.
MacGillony talking to the student in the library
At one point, MacGillony was found by the same student in the library and briefly talked to them about her next lesson, the topic of which would be basic runic numbers.
She had a hard time recalling what was used to represent the number "4" and came up with the Diricawl , but was corrected by the student with the Fwooper , the right answer.
She then left in a hurry to allegedly prepare more for her lesson.
Eventually it was Daniel Page who succeeded in getting what she needed, and after he got out of the lake, MacGillony came, summoned the chest that he had found and revealed a magical crown inside.

Stating that the crown was imbued with great power and would make its wearer fearless, she started to use the crown, but a kelpie who lived in the lake interrupted her with jets of water and knocked the crown away from her.
The two students also got into a duelling stance, and a duel then erupted among them.
MacGillony incarcerated by McGonagall
After she cast a spell that blasted the student into the lake, the kelpie raised to defend them against her.
She then confronted it directly, and did not realise she had successfully overcome her fear without the crown's help until she bumped into the dropped crown.

Before anything further could happen, however, McGonagall arrived and used the Incarcerous Spell to restrain her, stating that her probationary period had ended and she had become a true monster the moment she decided to take advantage of the students.
The crown was then taken from her to Gringotts Wizarding Bank for examination, and she was imprisoned in Azkaban for using an Unforgivable Curse .
Physical description
MacGillony had medium-length red hair , green eyes, light skin and freckles.
She wore green robes , adorned with black feathers, with much jewellery, such as earrings and a necklace.
Personality and traits
MacGillony was a lonely and timid individual for the most part of her known life.
Her first encounter with a kelpie left her with traumatic memories, which led to her fear of the creature and waterweeds.
Hostility grew inside her during her years at Hogwarts due to the constant bullying, which induced her thought of using the Dark Arts to pay the bullies back.
Mastery of the Imperius Curse along with her maniacal desire for the crown of courage had made her unscrupulous.
Ultimately, she appeared to have overcome her fear without the crown's help, but it was at the cost of the health of students and her own career.
Magical abilities and skills
Possessions
Notes and references

title: Elspeth MacGillony's father
paragraphs: Mr MacGillony was the father of Elspeth MacGillony .
Biography
In 1982 , he took Elspeth to a lake.
They sat under a tree for a long time and looked at the lake.
At one point, Elspeth became curious and wanted to go near the lake, but her father stopped her.
Notes and references

title: Christmas feast
paragraphs: The Christmas feast was held on Christmas Day .
It was attended by the Professors and any students that have chosen to remain at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry over the Christmas holidays .
Overview
1980s Christmas feast

The feast was prepared by the house-elves in the kitchens , and consisted of a hundred fat, roast turkeys , mountains of roast and boiled potatoes , platters of fat chipolatas , tureens of buttered peas , silver boats of thick, rich gravy and cranberry sauce .
For dessert, flaming Christmas puddings were served, with silver Sickles hidden within the pudding.
Also on the tables were Wizard Crackers .
Unlike their Muggle counterparts that contained plastic toys and paper hats, Wizard Crackers exploded with a blast, like a cannon going off, and engulfed the pullers in blue smoke.
Inside could be found such delights as live mice , Wizard's Chess sets, and Grow-Your-Own-Warts kits , as well as real-sized hats and jokes.
Because of the small number of students that stayed for Christmas during Harry's third year, the house tables were put to one side and a table for twelve set up in their place.
The Christmas feast was the only one which took place during the school holidays.
As such, the other feasts were usually attended by all students, with the exception of the 1997 Leaving Feast .
Known participants
Notes and references

title: Devil
paragraphs: The devil is an entity believed in many religions (notably Christianity and Islam ) to be the embodiment of evil and the enemy of humankind .
History
In certain Christian traditions, the devil was said to have once been an angel named Lucifer, cast out of heaven for disobeying God .
The story of Lucifer's fall was covered in the book The Hierarchie of the Blessed Angells .
The devil was mentioned in various idioms used by both Muggles and wizards .

Examples include "speaking of the devil", which Professor Weasley used when Professor Fig arrived in the middle of her conversation about him with a student , "what the devil are you doing", said by Vernon Dursley when he thought his nephew Harry Potter was making loud noises (though, in fact, it was Dobby ), and the term "devil-may-care", used to describe cheerfulness and recklessness.
On 31 October 1981 , Hallowe'en night, one of the celebrating Muggles in the costume parade in Godric's Hollow was dressed up as the devil.
The Fat Lady described Sirius Black as having "eyes like the devil" after he attacked her portrait in October 1993 .
Notes and references

title: Dun horse
paragraphs: A dun horse is used to describe any bay , black , or chestnut -based horse affected by the dilution gene that brightens both red and black pigments in its coat colour , lightening the base body coat and suppressing the underlying base colour to the mane, tail, legs, and primitive markings.
Both the female and male dun horses, the dun mare and dun stallion, are possible corporeal forms of the Patronus Charm .
Notes and references

title: Eagle
paragraphs: An eagle is any large bird of prey belonging to the family Accipitridae .
The eagle was the mascot of Ravenclaw House at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
It was a possible corporeal form of the Patronus Charm .
Eagle feathers were sometimes used for quills .
The body of a Hippogriff was half-eagle and half- horse , while the body of a Griffin was half-eagle and half- lion .
History
Talbott Winger could transform into an eagle as an Animagus .

After Severus Snape left the room following the questioning of Harry Potter and Ronald Weasley about the Flying Ford Anglia on 1 September 1992 , Minerva McGonagall was said to be eyeing them like a wrathful eagle.
On Christmas in December 1992, Hermione Granger presented Harry Potter with a luxury eagle-feather quill as a Christmas present.
Harry later used that quill do his homework during the summer holidays in 1993 and also when writing a letter to Sirius Black during the summer holidays in 1994 .
In May 1996 , Luna Lovegood wore a hat that took the form of a lifelike eagle to the Gryffindor vs Ravenclaw Quidditch match .
Notes and references

title: Griffin
paragraphs: The Griffin was a magical beast which originated from Greece .
Description
A Griffin guarding treasure
It had the front legs, wings and head of a giant eagle , and the body, hind legs, and tail of a lion .
The main diet of the Griffin was raw meat .
Griffins were known as fierce creatures ; however, despite this, skilled wizards and witches were able to befriend them.
Griffins had a natural instinct to protect treasure and as such were often used by wizards for that very purpose, like Sphinxes .
The treasure they guarded could be anything from gold to the plants in a garden.
If for some reason they didn't have any treasure to guard, they became very distraught.
This could be taken care of by simply giving the Griffin a new treasure to guard.
History
There were stone carvings of griffins on Solomon Sallow's grave in Feldcroft .
Newton Scamander kept a Griffin in his basement at 9 Sherringford Square in 1927 .

During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , during the Outdoor celebration of magic , Madam Hooch and Professor Silvanus Kettleburn gave a combined Care of Magical Creatures and Flying class to fifth-year students on the Training Grounds about how to fly Griffins.
Jacob's sibling was chosen to fly the Griffin present, and found the experience exhilarating.
