Notes and references

title: Guardian
paragraphs: A Guardian was an animated statue, bewitched by the Keepers as sentries.
History

In the late fifteenth century , numerous Guardians were created by the Keepers , consisting of four Hogwarts professors , to protect their secret vaults and dungeons and tested a wizard with rare capability to see and wield ancient magic .

From 1 September 1890 toward the end of the school year , one in particular, a Hogwarts student destroyed them and passed the Keepers' tests and trials, proving their worthiness to protect the knowledge of ancient magic.
Known Guardians
Guardian in Vault 12

These Guardians were created by Percival Rackham and Charles Rookwood to protect Vault 12 , before being destroyed by an unidentified 19th-century Hogwarts student during his/her and Eleazar Fig 's Gringotts exploration in 1890 .
The Guardians were only seen, as reflections on the ground, by wizards or witches who possessed the ability to perceive and use ancient magic when they were invisible .
They had to cast the Revelio Charm to reveal the statues, armed with swords, which would stand up and call their Guardian fellows to fight intruders.
Pensieve Sentry
Pensieve Sentries were made by the Keepers to protect their memories and Pensieve .

The sentries, armed with mace weapons, were guarding the Athenaeum , a secret chamber under the restricted section of Hogwarts Library , for centuries before being destroyed by an unidentified 19th-century Hogwarts in 1890.
Pensieve Guardian
Pensieve Guardian
Pensieve Guardians were created by the Keepers to guard their memories and Pensieves in their trial.
These animated statues were very much larger than the Guardians in Vault 12 and the Pensieve Sentries.
In the 1890-1891 school year, an unidentified 19th-century Hogwarts student destroyed all of them during the trials.
Pensieve Sentinel
Pensieve Sentinels were bewitched by Charles Rookwood to protect his memory and Pensieve at Rookwood Castle .
Ancient magic ensured that their weapons will always re-form after being thrown or disarmed away.
During Charles Rookwood's trial, an unidentified 19th-century Hogwarts student destroyed them all and reached the Pensieve .
Pensieve Protector
Pensieve Protectors were created by the Keepers to aid in the protection of ancient magic .
Just like Pensieve Sentinels, ancient magic ensured that their weapons would always re-form after being thrown or disarmed away.
Notes and references

title: Pensieve Guardian
paragraphs: A Pensieve Guardian was a guardian , an enchanted suit of armour powered with ancient magic , that guarded the final chamber of Percival Rackham 's trial.
It could only be defeated by the very magic that powered it.
Notes and references

title: Matilda Weasley
paragraphs: Professor Matilda Weasley (fl.
19th century ) was a pure-blood witch who lived during the 19th century .
In her youth, she attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , before going on to work for the British Ministry of Magic as a Curse-Breaker .
Later, she returned to her old school, becoming the professor of Transfiguration and, eventually, Deputy Headmistress .
Biography
Early life
Matilda was born into the wizarding Weasley family and attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , where she was Sorted into Gryffindor House .
Noted to have been an " exceptionally talented witch ", she was presumably a gifted pupil.
In her second year , she met and befriended Deek , an old house-elf employed in the school's kitchens , and together, they discovered the Room of Requirement .
She would visit the room many more times throughout her schooling, even once forgetting her school bag there.
She only recovered it years later, during the 1890-1891 school year , while showing the room to a new student in her time as a professor - much to her delight.
Ministry career
After graduating, Matilda joined the British Ministry of Magic as a Curse-Breaker .
Her calming presence and extraordinary wandwork allowed her to rise quickly through the ranks.
Around this time, Matilda also befriended Chiyo Kogawa , a Mahoutokoro -educated witch of the Japanese Ministry of Magic , whom she stayed in touch with over the years that followed.
Freelancing career

At some point during her Ministry career, Matilda met and fell in love with a Curse-Breaker named Paul , who reciprocated her feelings, and before long, Matilda had resigned her position at the Ministry in favour of travelling the world with him as freelance Curse-Breakers.
With time, however, Matilda began to miss her family, the stability of a settled life, and the camaraderie of working with a talented group of witches and wizards.
As Paul had no desire to "stop moving", their romance ended, and Matilda settled back down in Britain by herself.
At some point, she worked with Chiyo Kogawa in Yokohama , a time described as "eventful".
Hogwarts career
Matilda Weasley at her desk in the Transfiguration Classroom
At some point before 1889 , Matilda took over from an unidentified predecessor .

Matilda became the professor of Transfiguration at Hogwarts, and proved herself to be a stern yet fair-minded instructor regarded for her ability to combine a good sense of humour with an air of authority.
She was also eventually promoted to the position of Deputy Headmistress , in which capacity her students found her to be " slightly intimidating ".
During her tenure, she maintained two separate offices - one for her professorial duties, and another , presumably as part of her Deputy Headmistress responsibilities.

In her role, she took great care to supervise and discipline her nephew, Garreth Weasley , who was a student at the school in her care, though Garreth felt his aunt was too overbearing and protective.

As Headmaster Phineas Nigellus Black had delegated her the job of handling staff appointments, she recruited Chiyo Kogawa as the school's new Flying Instructor and Quidditch referee after learning about a bad experience she had had during a try-out for the Toyohashi Tengu .

Matilda had also befriended Mudiwa Onai , a gifted Seer and educator at Uagadou , with whom she was friendly enough that when she learned of the unexpected death of the latter's husband , she offered words of consolation and successfully persuaded Professor Black to let her invite Mudiwa to teach at Hogwarts instead.

In 1890 , a new student was to be enrolled at the school to start as a fifth-year , and Matilda wrote them a unique acceptance letter informing them of their unusual situation and the preparation required.
Around the time the letter was dispatched to the student, a strange magical disturbance took place at the school that greatly concerned the student body.
Professor Weasley joined Professor Hecat in Classroom 3C to address the fourth-year students, where she admitted that the staff had no knowledge of what had caused the disturbance to happen.

To help the future student catch up with their classmates, Matilda discussed with Professor Black and officers from the Department of Magical Education , who lent the school a copy of the Wizard's Field Guide to give to the student.
She additionally organised for them to receive extracurricular assignments from their professors.
Matilda placing the Sorting Hat onto the new fifth-year student's head
Matilda met the student in person on 1 September , the first day of the school year .
The student arrived late at the Sorting Ceremony held in the evening, and Matilda placed the Sorting Hat onto the student's head.
After they were sorted, Matilda introduced herself to them and guided them to their common room .
The next day, Matilda gave the Wizard's Field Guide to the student and showed them how to make use of it.
They travelled to the Central Hall via Floo Flames , where Matilda informed the student of their schedule of the day that included two classes and a trip to Hogsmeade to replenish their supplies.
Professor Eleazar Fig then ran into Matilda and the student, and they talked briefly about the dragon attack Fig and the student had experienced.
She asked the student to see her in her classroom after they completed the classes.
When they arrived, she was talking to Deek about letting the student use the Room of Requirement .
After Deek left, she turned to the student and let them know that Professor Ronen was ready to give them their first assignment.
She also explained what the student should need from Hogsmeade, and asked them who they would like to go with to the village after completing the assignment.
They chose between Sebastian Sallow and Natsai Onai , the two choices Matilda gave them, and she sent the desired student an owl to give them the task.
When it was time for the new fifth-year student to learn about the Room of Requirement, Matilda sent them an owl asking them to meet her in the seventh-floor corridor .
However, she was dealing with Professor Black when the student went there, and when she arrived, she saw that the student had already discovered the entrance to the room by themself.
They then went in, and Matilda found that the room presented itself to the student as the Room of Hidden Things, in which she finally spotted her old school bag .
When a pile of chairs blocked their way forward, Matilda taught the Vanishing Spell to the student, and noted the moonstones the spell produced.
After they found Deek, he asked the student to imagine the room as the way they liked it, which transformed it into a commodious space free to customise.
Matilda then taught the student Conjuration spells, which required spellcrafts as recipes and used moonstones to conjure various kinds of workstations and decorations.
Matilda was kept mainly in the dark about the quest pursued by the student and their mentor Professor Fig as they worked to combat the rise of Ranrok's goblin rebellion and the Rookwood Gang .
However, she was told the full story by the end of the school year, by which point Ranrok was making significant gains to capture the final repository beneath Hogwarts Castle.
Matilda and the other professors rushed to defend Hogwarts in an ensuing battle within the Keepers' Caverns , in which the defenders were victorious, after the new student subdued and killed Ranrok.
Matilda and the other professors arrive at the battle beneath the school
The battle, however, saw the death of Fig, to whom Matilda led a heartwarming eulogy at his memorial ceremony soon after.
Matilda also checked up on the new student and their progress.

When the new student completed their Ordinary Wizarding Level examinations, Matilda led a speech at the Leaving Feast that comemmorated the student's triumphant achievements and their defence of Hogwarts.
Magical abilities and skills
Etymology
Matilda is a feminine name deriving from the Old High German words "maht" (meaning might and strength) and "hild" (meaning battle).
The name itself, thus, means "Mighty in battle".
Notes and references

title: Wizard's Field Guide
paragraphs: The Wizard's Field Guide was a book owned by the British Ministry of Magic .
It was bewitched to help young witches and wizards advance in their studies faster than usual if they fell behind.
It could be loaned to the teachers of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry to help late arrivals to the student body catch up to their classmates.
Usage
The Wizard's Field Guide was imbued with the power to look out into the world and help the one using it to discover different opportunities to learn and grow.
It also possessed the Charmed Compass spell, which helped its owner find certain destinations.

It filled itself out with new pages as the student learned new things, and there were over a hundred potential field guide pages to be found in Hogwarts Castle and throughout the surrounding grounds alone.
History
At some point shortly before the 1890-1891 school year , the school learned of the existence of a young individual who would be admitted to Hogwarts as a fifth-year .
Headmaster Phineas Nigellus Black worked with the Department of Magical Education to figure out a way to help the student catch up with their peers during their studies for the O.W.L.s .
They loaned Professor Black the Wizard's Field Guide .
On their first day, Professor Matilda Weasley gave the student their Field Guide .
The book was nearly empty at first, but it expanded throughout their explorations and with the progression of their knowledge.
Field Guide Pages
There were different types of Field Guide Pages which were revealed by using a specific charm on an object.
The Field Guide Page had a short paragraph with information related to the object.
There were over two hundred pages.
Known content included:
Collection Page
These type of Pages could be revealed using the Revelio Charm .
Notes and references

title: Gerbold Ollivander
paragraphs: Gerbold Octavius Ollivander (fl.
19th century ) was a pure-blood wizard and famously accomplished wandmaker .
He was the father of Gervaise Ollivander , and, through him, the paternal grandfather of Garrick Ollivander .
Biography
Early life
Gerbold Octavius was born into the wizarding Ollivander family in or prior to the 19th century .
He reaped the benefits of growing up in the family's wandmaking business .
Having taken up the family business in London , Gerbold studied further into wandlore and became highly regarded as an excellent wandmaker .
At some point, he also fathered a son, Gervaise , who went on to provide his father with a grandson, Garrick , both of whom continued the family tradition of wandmaking .
Career as a wandmaker
Gerbold believed that fir produced "the survivor's wand", as he had sold wands of this wood to three different wizards , each of whom found himself in mortal danger and came out unharmed.
He was also fond of saying, "If you seek integrity, search first among the poplars ," which his grandson Garrick found correct based on his own experience with poplar wands and their owners.

During the nineteenth century , at a time when wands made of silver lime were in vogue, the wandmaker Arturo Cephalopos claimed that the wood 's reputed connection with powers of Divination was "a falsehood circulated by merchants like Gerbold Ollivander, who have overstocked their workshops with silver lime and hope to shift their surplus".
According to Gerbold's grandson Garrick , however, Cephalopos was "an ignoramus" who predictably went out of business.
By the time of the 1890-1891 school year , Gerbold had been maintaining the branch in the village of Hogsmeade in Scotland .
There, he continued to make and sell high-quality wands to his customers.
This included a Hogwarts student that curiously enough started their schooling five years late.

Gerbold was determined to recover the Ollivander family's heirloom wand , an apple and fairy wing wand that had been in the possession of his family until the 1790s , when it had been stolen and hidden by Richard Jackdaw .
It was never recovered because it was later destroyed.
Gerbold was notified by Professor Eleazar Fig of an upcoming visit from the new fifth-year student that involved the making of a special wand .
He suspected that it could only serve a unique purpose and would not be of much use otherwise.
When the student visited, they provided him with the materials they had gotten from the Keepers , and Gerbold successfully crafted a wand using them.
Magical abilities and skills
Notes and references

title: Troll attack on Hogsmeade
paragraphs: This attack occurred in 1890 when two Armoured Trolls were unleashed onto Hogsmeade .
They smashed multiple buildings and damaged the places, causing enormous chaos.
The Ministry officer Ruth Singer and others lured one away, while a student and their friend (either Sebastian Sallow or Natsai Onai ) defeated the another.
The attack was sent by Ranrok as a distraction as part of a greater plan.
Notes and references

title: Eleazar Fig's office
paragraphs: The office of Professor Eleazar Fig was located on the fourth floor of the Astronomy Wing , adjacent to Class 67 , the classroom of Magical Theory .
History
In the 1890-1891 school year , this office was used by Eleazar Fig.
He met the new fifth-year student here to discuss how the locket they had found in Vault 12 had produced a map of Hogwarts which led to the Map Chamber .
Eleazar was about to bring the student to the chamber before they were interrupted by Phineas Nigellus Black , who called Eleazar away.

Later in the year, they met again to disguise the student as Professor Black with Polyjuice Potion , so that the student could retrieve the password to the Headmaster's office in order to speak with Niamh Fitzgerald 's portrait .
Notes and references

title: Aesop Sharp
paragraphs: Professor Aesop Sharp (b. circa 1858 ) was a wizard who worked as an Auror for the British Ministry of Magic , and later as a Potions Master at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in the 19th century .
Biography
Early life
Aesop was born into a family of unknown wizarding descent in or before the 19th century .
He attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , where he was Sorted into Slytherin House .
Career as an Auror
After leaving Hogwarts, Aesop joined the British Ministry of Magic and landed a position in the Auror Office .
On 31 December 1875 , Aesop was issued a memorandum from the office about Borgin and Burkes 's suspicious activities and the decision for Aesop to join the Aurors who were watching the shop.
At some point in his career, he and his partner were working an assignment when they were ambushed, resulting in a severe leg injury to him and death to his partner.
When it became clear that his injury meant he would have to give up being an Auror, Aesop decided to retire from the Office.

The Ministry would have been happy to keep him, working in the Auror recruitment programme , but Aesop believed that if he was to be relegated to a desk and tedious paperwork for the rest of his career, then his time would be better spent passing on what he knew to the next generation of young witches and wizards at his old school.
He also planned to use the resources at Hogwarts in hopes of finding a way to heal his injuries.
This was also part of his motivation to apply to the job of Potions Master .
Career at Hogwarts
Professor Sharp teaching a class

His wish of sharing his extensive experience involving battleworthy draughts and elixirs with the students came to fruition when he was offered the job of Potions Master at the school, at which point he was granted a classroom down in the dungeons to teach in.
In time, he became widely known for his challenging lessons and lack of patience with misbehaving students, but also for his genuine pride in those who exceeded in the class.
Professor Sharp was teaching at the school during the 1890-1891 school year , when a new student started school as a fifth-year , something highly unusual.

As the school year advanced, Professor Sharp gave extracurricular assignments to this student to help them catch up on their magical knowledge, asking them to brew and use certain potions and teaching them how to cast the Banishing Charm and the Severing Charm .
He was also known to have assigned students of unknown year an essay on invisibility , as well as one comparing potions of the Middle Ages to those of the Black Death .
Aesop Sharp in the battle for the final repository

At the end of the year, when Ranrok invaded the Keepers' Caverns with the aim of obtaining the final repository and supplanting wizardkind with goblinkind , Aesop Sharp defended Hogwarts Castle against his army of Loyalists and trolls , ensuring the safety of not only the school, but also the wizarding world as a whole.
He fought two trolls alongside his colleague, Eleazar Fig , who died to Ranrok later in the battle.
Aesop Sharp was present at the memorial ceremony for Eleazar Fig which took place after Ranrok's final defeat at the hands of the late-coming student he had helped to teach that year.
Physical description
He had long brown hair , and a beard.
He wore a three-piece suit with a brown overcoat, light brown vest, a white shirt with a brown tie, and brown trousers.
He walked with a very noticeable limp in his left leg.
Personality and traits
Sharp had a gruff and keenly acute nature, who was not easily impressed by his students and was a difficult taskmaster.

Although he was wholly unwilling to suffer fools in his class, he was by no means entirely unreasonable in his methods, as he was known to take genuine pride in students who excelled in his class in spite of his challenging curriculum.
Magical abilities and skills
Possessions
Aesop Sharp's Auror Badge , which he kept on his desk at Hogwarts in the 1890-1891 school year
Notes and references

title: Athenaeum
paragraphs: The Athenaeum was a cavernous series of chambers located directly beneath the Restricted Section in the Hogwarts Library , constructed through some form of ancient magic .
It was created by the Keepers , and was accessible only by a secretive portal at the very base of the Restricted Section.
History
The portal to the Athenaeum at the base of the Restricted Section , accessible only through ancient magic
The Athenaeum, accessible through an ancient portal in a chamber located beneath the Restricted Section, was clandestinely constructed by the Keepers during the Tudor period .
During the 1890-1891 school year , the new fifth-year student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry discovered the portal beneath the library and passed through it, entering the Athenaeum.
When the student reached the end of this chamber, they found a book above a Pensieve which opened to release a memory of the Keepers .
Within the memory, the Keepers met the young Isidora Morganach , a witch who, like this student, had the rare ability to see traces of ancient magic .
Notes and references

title: Faris Spavin
paragraphs: Minister Faris Spavin , also known as Spout-hole , (fl.
1756 - 1903 ) was a British wizard who served as the twentieth Minister for Magic of the British Ministry of Magic , in office from 1865 to 1903 .
Biography
Tenure as Minister for Magic (1865-1903)
Faris Spavin was born in 1755 or 1756 .
He became Minister for Magic in 1865 at 109 years old, and was known for being the longest-serving holder of the position.
Over the course of his career, he was elected at least six times, as elections for the office of Minister for Magic needed to be held at a maximum interval of seven years.
He survived an assassination attempt made by a centaur who took offence to the punchline of his infamous " a centaur , a ghost and a dwarf walk into a bar " joke .
In the 1870s through to the 1880s , the Muggle government made plans to flatten the Leaky Cauldron with the creation of Charing Cross Road .
Faris Spavin made a melancholy seven-hour speech before the Wizengamot explaining why the Leaky Cauldron could not be saved.

During the course of his tedious speech, however, the wizarding community rallied and performed a mass of Memory Charms (and possibly also the Imperius Curse , though it had never been proven) on several Muggle city planners so that the Leaky Cauldron could be accommodated in the revised plans for the new road.
After his speech, Spavin's secretary presented him with a note describing the developments that had just invalidated his words.
The largest poaching ring in eastern Wales formed during his tenure, culminating in the Great Poacher Raid of 1878 .
The ring was single-handedly taken down by a Ministry official, Dinah Hecat , who confiscated a Hebridean Black skeleton from the event.
Spavin's time in office saw the introduction of an important piece of wizarding legislation, the Decree for the Reasonable Restriction of Underage Sorcery , in 1875 .
This law made it illegal for an underage wizard to perform magic outside of school .
The Ministry of Magic detected breaches of the Decree by means of the Trace .
Spavin's term was also notable for introducing some reforms to the game of Quidditch (and the commotion they originated).
In 1883 , a riot broke out at the Ministry Headquarters after the Department of Magical Games and Sports decided to get rid of "goal baskets" in favour of the modern goalposts in Quidditch .
One year later, on 21 June 1884 , a similar riot erupted after the department decreed the institutionalisation of the Stooging Penalty in Quidditch .

This announcement caused widespread discontent among British Quidditch players and fans, who again demonstrated at the Ministry headquarters, bombarded a Department representative with Quaffles and threatened to stooge Minister Spavin himself.
Wizards from the Department of Magical Law Enforcement were duly dispatched and the crowd reluctantly dispersed.

In the 1890s , Faris Spavin received a request from Phineas Nigellus Black , the Headmaster of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , to change the school's admissions process, very likely to restrict Muggle-born access to the school while favouring pure-bloods , though this was declined.
In 1890, a witch claimed her son was attacked by a Dementor .
Spavin commented on the matter saying 'Dementors are under strict Ministry control.'
and 'They are and have always been stationed at Azkaban prison .
The idea that they are running rife amongst the populous, kissing random wizards is nothing but utter delusion.'
The witch was proven wrong, as his son's gormless look actually came from long hours of paperwork from his job as a Ministry intern and not a Dementor's Kiss.
Ranrok's goblin rebellion
During the 1890s , Spavin oversaw the Ministry's response to Ranrok's goblin rebellion as well as the rising threat of the Rookwood Gang .

When Eleazar Fig went to the Ministry to explain the events surrounding George Osric 's death and tried to express his concerns about Ranrok , Spavin hardly allowed him to talk, preferring to "rant" about dragons instead.

When Eleazar Fig sent Faris Spavin a letter about Ranrok's rebellion, Spavin wrote back accepting that it was an issue, but appeared to disregard it, focussing more on his new Stooging Penalty and inviting Fig to the upcoming Quidditch Final .
In 1901 , Spavin attended Queen Victoria 's funeral in an admiral's hat and spats.
Two years later, in 1903 , the Wizengamot gently suggested he step down as Minister for Magic .
He was 147 when he resigned due to advanced age.
Personality and traits
According to Eleazar Fig , the Professor of Magical Theory in the 1890s , Minister Spavin talked more than he listened.
Etymology
Notes and references

title: Richard Jackdaw
paragraphs: Richard Jackdaw was a wizard who was decapitated seeking adventure.
He returned as a ghost and was invited to join the Headless Hunt .
Biography
Hogwarts years
Richard Jackdaw started at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry at some point in the 19th century and was Sorted into an unknown house .
During his schooling, he was known as a heartbreaker; he attempted to woo Apollonia Black , who seemed to want nothing to do with him.
At some point, he picked up some yellowed old pages of a map that Peeves had left behind after a particularly aggressive riot through the library.
Apollonia thought the pages were worthless, but Richard thought the map might lead to something she would be interested in.
At the same time, Richard also wooed another girl, Anne Thisbe , by promising her adventure following the map, but only after she solved a series of puzzles.
At some point, he served as an assistant at Ollivanders in Hogsmeade , and there stole the prized heirloom wand that belonged to the Ollivander family .
He fled his job afterwards.
After discovering that the wand was only special for sentimental reasons, he had every intention of returning it, but died before he got the chance.
He also stole and sold the Black family ring at some point.
While seeking adventure in very dangerous places, circumstances led to Richard Jackdaw being decapitated in a cave near Upper Hogsfield .
He did not see what killed him; the last thing he remembered before dying was feeling a slight breeze and then he felt "light headed".
Post-mortem
Jackdaw's skeleton
After death , he returned as a ghost , but without any knowledge of the cause of his death.

Without Richard's body or any evidence, along with a vindictive and fraudulent testimony from Apollonia Black whose family was well connected at the Ministry of Magic , combined with the fact that she was Muggle-born , Anne was ultimately convicted of his murder and sentenced to life in Azkaban .
Some time after becoming a ghost, Richard Jackdaw was invited to join the Headless Hunt with other ghosts who died by decapitation.
Richard Jackdaw possibly Nearly Headless Nick 's five-hundredth Deathday Party on Hallowe'en in 1992 .
He may have also participated in the Battle of Hogwarts on 2 May 1998 with other members of the Headless Hunt.
Personality and traits

Richard was headstrong, daring, reckless, ambitious, and unafraid of breaking the law, as evidenced by his seizure of the Ollivander family's heirloom wand , as well as his love triangle with Apollonia Black and Anne Thisbe .
His determination to seek adventure eventually resulted in his own demise, and his carelessness also led to him not learning of how his fate affected Anne's possibly until some time during the 1890s.
Notes and references

title: Map Chamber
paragraphs: The Map Chamber was a chamber that was located deep below Hogwarts Castle that held the portraits of the Keepers , the four guardians of ancient magic .
Description
The Map Chamber was located deep within a large, light-filled cavern .
The architecture of the Map Chamber reflected the era of the Keepers , the Tudor era , with its Tudor-style trefoil arches.
The Map Chamber featured a water wall and a tower of flame with a statue of an elemental being standing watch.
A Pensieve was set on a podium and at its base was a silhouette of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry carved in wood.
There were fours portraits for each of the Keepers.
If book was put the podium, it would release ancient magic to reveal a spectral map of the area.
It would signal the location of four trials for a student who could perceive ancient magic.
Finding the chamber
In order to lead a wizard to it, the Keepers created a trail.
They opened a vault at Gringotts for which the key was put in a special casing.
It could only be opened by someone who could perceive ancient magic .
Once they entered the vault, they would find a pensieve with a locket levitating above it.
The locket had a memory inside of two Keepers creating the vault.
If the inscription on the locket was read, it opened to reveal a map.
The map led to the Restricted Section where there was a hidden entrance to the Athenaeum .
Its Antechamber had a pensieve with a book levitating above it.
The book contained a map to the Map Chamber.
History
The chamber was built in the Tudor period by the Keepers .

During the 1890-1891 school year , a student of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry with the ability to find ancient magic found the Map Chamber with the help of Professor Eleazar Fig and the ghost of Richard Jackdaw .
Notes and references

title: San Bakar's Tower
paragraphs: San Bakar's Tower was the residence of San Bakar , a member of the Keepers , during the Middle Ages .
Over the centuries, it eventually fell into disrepair.
Description

The tower was the location where former Hogwarts Professor of Divination and leader of the Keepers , Percival Rackham set up his test for a potential successor to the secrets and role of guardianship of ancient magic .
The trial was accessible through a secret, ancient magical doorway within the tower on the ground floor.
Only someone with the same innate ancient magic ability that Rackham himself possessed was able to access it.
The trial consisted of exploring and navigating an underground labyrinth filled with enchanted architecture and magical puzzles.

There were two common themes in the labyrinth; a magical archway in which the room was different depending on which side of the arch on was on, and floating platforms one could stand on and move across the room by using the Summoning Charm to pull themselves and the platform to an outstretched handle that matched those on the platform.
The labyrinth was also guarded by suits of enchanted armour that attacked anyone who passed through.

The Pensieve Sentinels were regular sized suits of armour with no noteworthy abilities, the Pensieve Protectors were larger suits capable of fast and powerful attacks, and the final armour, the Pensieve Guardian , was gigantic and capable of magic attacks.
Only after this final armour was defeated was one able to reach the Pensieve at the end of the labyrinth and view the memories Professor Rackham left behind.
History
During 1890 , the place was put under the investigation of Ranrok's Loyalists , who, under Ranrok 's leadership, were searching for information on the final repository .

The tower was infiltrated by Eleazar Fig and his student as they needed to unlock Percival Rackham 's trial, the first of the four trials that the student would be given in their quest to prove their worth to the Keepers .
Notes and references

title: Memorial ceremony for Eleazar Fig
paragraphs: The memorial ceremony for Eleazar Fig was held during the 1890-1891 school year of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
The memorial feast was held following his death in the battle for the final repository after he had been grievously injured by debris caused by Ranrok 's transformation into a dragon .
He had lived just long enough to see Ranrok's death himself before collapsing from his injuries.

Headmaster Phineas Nigellus Black and Deputy Headmistress Matilda Weasley both gave eulogies within this memorial ceremony, honouring Eleazar's life, his dedication to his wife as well as to Hogwarts.
History
Background information
Concurrent to Ranrok's goblin rebellion , Eleazar tutored and mentored a Hogwarts student who possessed the rare ability to perceive and use ancient magic .
Determined to hone this student's power, they embarked on a number of trials set by the Keepers to unlock the deeper mysteries of ancient magic as well as its storied history.

The student individually discovered that Isidora Morganach , a Hogwarts professor from the 15th - 16th century , also possessed the same ability, but had been using it to extract negative emotions from students.

She stored this corrupted form of ancient magic in the final repository in the Keepers' Caverns beneath Hogwarts Castle : a giant storage unit made of goblin silver , constructed by Bragbor the Boastful .
Eleazar Fig and the student reaching the final repository
In the 1890s , Bragbor's descendant Ranrok was determined to re-acquire the Repository, for goblins believed that the creator of an item had a claim to it, not its purchaser.
Meanwhile, Fig and his student were determined to stop him.
This culminated in the battle for the final repository , where Fig, the student, and several Hogwarts professors fought Ranrok's Loyalists and several invading trolls .
Ranrok reached the Repository first, and was able to harness the ancient magic contained therein and transformed into a near-invincible dragon .
Eleazar Fig was crushed by the debris caused by Ranrok's transformation.
Ranrok's dragon form was defeated by the student after a hard-pressed duel , which Fig lived long enough to witness before collapsing from his wounds.
Remembering Eleazar
The Enchanted Ceiling during the event
Eleazar Fig received a school-wide ceremony in the Great Hall , hosted by Phineas Nigellus Black , commemorating his life and achievements.

Torn between his personal dislike for and newfound, grudging respect for his departed colleague for his heroic sacrifice in laying down his life to protect Hogwarts, however, his eulogy was somewhat awkward, having seemingly found it difficult to find the right words to honour somebody whom he had only ever treated as an inferior in life.

Nevertheless shaken by the loss, however, as Professor Matilda Weasley approached to take over the speech to do Fig proper justice, the Headmaster had very nearly lost his composure, and seemed relieved to have the Deputy Headmistress there to offer a far more heart-warming eulogy on Eleazar's life than he was capable of giving himself.

After Professor Weasley made a stirring speech about how the best way Hogwarts could honour her late co-worker was by " wisely , resourcefully , justly , and bravely facing all that lies ahead", Professor Black, who had regained some of his usual prim manner, nodded in agreement and ended the assembly by leading the students and staff in a toast for the late professor.
Notes and references

title: Descending Charm
paragraphs: The Descending Charm ( Descendo ) was a charm that made objects fall or move downwards.
It could also be used to stop the victim of a Billywig sting from floating, although the effect was only temporary.
History

During the 1988-1989 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry , Professor Filius Flitwick taught this charm to fifth-year students in Charms class , in preparation for their Ordinary Wizarding Levels .
Known uses
Known practitioners
Etymology
Descendo is Latin for "I descend".
Notes and references

title: Levitation Spell
paragraphs: The Levitation Spell ( Levioso ) was a charm that levitated objects.
However, it did not also allow one to move said objects (unlike a similar spell ).
It could also be used to levitate people in duelling .
Levitated Diricawls could not disappear and reappear as usual.
History
The Levitation Spell was one of the earliest recorded spells of the wizarding world , having been created in ancient England .
During the 1890s , the spell was used in duelling .
It was taught in fifth-year Defence Against the Dark Arts classes by Professor Hecat at Hogwarts .
Known uses
Known practitioners
Etymology
Levioso probably derives from Latin levo , meaning to "raise, lift up", or levis , meaning light (of weight).
Notes and references

title: Troll
paragraphs: A troll was a magical beast of prodigious strength and immense stupidity.
In fact, they were so synonymous with stupidity that wizards actually had the lowest wizarding exam failing grade named after them.
Trolls were grouped in the taxonomical genus Troglodytarum .
There were three known breeds of trolls: the mountain troll , the river troll , and the forest troll .
Each possessed unique physical characteristics and inhabited distinct areas, as indicated by their names.
Trolls also possessed rudimentary magic , although how they applied it is unknown.
Description
Physical appearance
A diagram of a troll
Trolls generally reached a height of about twelve feet and weighed up to a tonne.
Their feet had two toes, both with giant toenails.
Skin colours and overall appearances varied by breed; mountain trolls were grey and somewhat lumpy, while river trolls were purple and forest trolls were green.
Troll whiskers had magical properties, and were sometimes used as wand cores , though they were considered inferior to the Supreme Cores .
A troll brain was tiny.
Behaviour
Trolls were dangerously violent and incredibly aggressive, and they engaged in unpredictable behaviour, comparable to giants .

They were also incredibly low in intelligence when compared to other species; to give at least one example, giants seemed to have more intelligence than the troll, despite their otherwise similarities.
They were particularly attracted to unpleasant smells, such as Dungbombs .
They tended to avoid Puffapods , since the entire species was highly allergic to the plant.
Diet
Trolls, similar to Acromantulas , had a taste for human flesh.
They enjoyed it raw, but were not exactly fussy about what they ate.
They were also fond of fish .
Society and culture

Troll language was supposedly nothing more than simple grunts that only trolls seemed to be able to interpret, though skilled magical multi-linguists such as Bartemius Crouch Senior could understand them.
Trolls understood only a limited number of human words, and some of the smarter ones who knew English could be skillfully trained as security trolls .
Professor Quirrell had a gift for communicating with trolls, having used it to set one loose in Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in 1991 in an effort to steal the Philosopher's Stone .
Mountain trolls had been known to tame and ride Graphorns , or at least try to ride them.
However, the Graphorns didn't seem to be very keen on the idea.
Trolls did not usually wear armour and would usually be prone to smashing it in confusion or anger.
This makes it all the more surprising that a fully intact suit of Troll Armour was on display in the Armoury during the 1890s .
Trolls participated in wizarding society to some extent; some witches and wizards made a career out of training security trolls .
These were evidently a different type of troll than the mountain variety, since they seemed considerably more intelligent and less smelly.
History
Early history
Trolls originated in Scandinavia , but were later found all across Europe .

Trolls were not recognised as magical beings , but instead classified as beasts by the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures of the British Ministry of Magic , most likely due to their aggressive natures.

Pierre Bonaccord , the first Supreme Mugwump of the International Confederation of Wizards , wanted to stop troll-hunting and give them rights, but his appointment to that office was contested by Liechtenstein , since they were having problems with a tribe of very dangerous mountain trolls at the time.
19th century
In the end of the 19th century , Ranrok 's followers had enlisted trolls among their ranks.
In 1890 , they sent two of them to attack Hogsmeade in an attempt to create a diversion so that Victor Rookwood could abduct the new fifth-year student that had previously encountered Ranrok.
However, the first troll was repelled by officer Ruth Singer and other villagers, while the second one was killed by the student with ancient magic .

During the final battle for control of the final repository located beneath Hogwarts , no less than four trolls were mobilised by Ranrok's troops; three of them were disposed of by the student and Professor Eleazar Fig , while the last one was taken out by Professor Aesop Sharp .

Throughout their exploration of the region, the student would frequently encounter trolls (including ones that were not in Ranrok's army), such as when they went to find Bubotuber pus for Sacharissa Tugwood .
They also took out the troll that Alexandra Ricketts had unsuccessfully attempted to train to help defend Brocburrow , and the troll guarding the Dale Family Tomb .
20th century
The House of Black kept an umbrella stand made out of a troll's leg in their front hall.

After the details of the Sorting Ceremony were revealed to him in 1991 , Ron Weasley stated that he was going to kill his brother Fred , who had scared him earlier by suggesting that the test to get into Hogwarts involved wrestling a troll.
A troll was Quirrell 's contribution to guarding the Philosopher's Stone in the Underground Chambers , during the 1991-1992 school year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
To create a diversion so he could go after the stone, Professor Quirrell let another troll into the castle on Hallowe'en 1991 , appearing in the dungeon .
It wandered around the corridors until Harry Potter and Ron Weasley locked it in a girls' bathroom, only to realise soon after that Hermione Granger was also in that particular bathroom.

With a combination of using the Levitation Charm and what Minerva McGonagall would cite as " sheer dumb luck ", Ron managed to knock it by levitating its club and dropping it on its head, incapacitating it and saving Hermione.

The wizarding author and celebrity Gilderoy Lockhart wrote about his supposed adventures with trolls in his book Travels with Trolls , which was a mandatory Defence Against the Dark Arts textbook for his classes in that subject for the 1992-1993 school year when he was that year's Professor .

As Lockhart was, in reality, a con artist who took the credit of the achievements of far braver wizards and witches and used the Memory Charm to erase their memories of their deeds, Lockhart in reality had no actual experience with these creatures.
Albus Dumbledore hired security trolls to guard the Fat Lady after Sirius Black broke into the castle and attacked her portrait.
They spent all their time pacing the corridor in front of the Fat Lady 's portrait, giving dirty looks to everyone who happened by and comparing the sizes of their clubs.
They left at the end of the year, when Sirius was deemed to have left the country.

When Ron Weasley was captured by Snatchers in 1997 , he told them he was Stan Shunpike , due to them not looking very intelligent, and even speculated that one of them might have been part-troll , judging by his odour.
By 1999 , Artemius Lawson became an outspoken advocate for the strict restraint of trolls.
He thought it was wrong to allow them to roam free, stating that "they were creatures who weighed a ton, but had brains the size of a bogey" .
21st century

During the Calamity , several trolls started randomly appearing throughout the wizarding world guarding various magical Confoundables , with volunteer members of the Statute of Secrecy Task Force having to incapacitate them with spells such as the the Ebublio Jinx and the Knockback Jinx , in order to overpower the Confoundables and return them to their rightful place.
Known breeds
There were three known different types of trolls, each with its own highly unique set of physical differences.
Notes and references
